Status: implemented in erp-security. The compiler described here turns the domain column of your security/ir.access.csv rows into the predicate the ORM puts in every statement. Loading the rows from the database (ir.access, res.groups) and the erp access report command come with the same slice. Design: ADR 0035 decision 2 and docs/design/m3-access-engine.md §3.1. How rows combine (permissions OR, restrictions AND, _inherits parents) is in [security.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/security.md) §1. This page is about the domain column.

Odoo evaluates a rule's domain in Python for each user, with user, company_ids, company_id and time as values. ERPForAll compiles it once per policy: those names are *symbols* that become statement parameters (the user id, the allowed companies, the transaction's start time) or sub-selects (a path from the user's row). One compiled predicate then serves every user with the same groups, and nothing is evaluated in memory. The price: a rule can only use the forms below. Everything else is refused with a message that says what to write instead. Most Odoo rules need no change.

| You write | It means | |---|---| | Literals: 1, -1, 2.5, 'text', True, False, None, lists and tuples | The value (None is False) | | user.id | The user's id | | user, user.ids as a value | The list of the user's id (('user_id', '=', user)) | | user.partner_id.id, user.partner_id.commercial_partner_id.id | One id along a path of stored many2one fields from the user's row; False when a link on the path is empty | | user.employee_id.ids, user.all_group_ids.ids, user.partner_id | The ids along a path of stored relational fields; an empty list when a link is empty | | company_ids | The ids of the companies the user works in now (the company switcher) | | company_id | The current company | | company_ids + [False], user.partner_id.child_ids.ids + [3] | A list holding those ids and the literals | | time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d'), context_today(), fields.Date.today(), datetime.date.today() | Today (a date), when the transaction started | | time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'), datetime.now(), datetime.datetime.now(), fields.Datetime.now() | Now (a timestamp), when the transaction started | | ('f', 'in', user.env['m'].search([...]).ids) (also not in, =, !=, without .ids) | A sub-query: f must hold ids of m; the search domain must be literal; archived records of m are left out unless the domain names its active field, as search does | | ('f', 'access', 'read') (write, create, unlink) on a many2one or id | The record that f points to (or the record itself for id) must pass the rules of that operation for the same user | Conditions use Odoo's list syntax with the prefix operators '&', '|', '!'. Paths such as ('partner_id.country_id', '=', 5) and any conditions are allowed; inside a rule they never apply the related model's own rules (Odoo's any!). The internal operators any! and not any! are not accepted in a rule string, as in Odoo. A search *by* a user does apply the related model's rules: ('product_tmpl_id', 'any', [...]), ('product_variant_ids.standard_price', '>', 0) or a one2many or many2many condition keeps only the related records that user may read. A related model's rule may use child_of and parent_of (the product rules' ('company_id', 'parent_of', company_ids)): it is resolved before the search runs, the same way as the searched model's own rule, and the search stays one statement. Examples, as they appear in security/ir.access.csv: id,name,model_id,group_id/id,operation,domain library_book_own,own books,library.book,library.group_library_user,crud,"[('user_id', '=', user.id)]" library_book_company,books of my companies,library.book,,crud,"[('company_id', 'in', company_ids + [False])]" library_book_partner,books of my company's partner,library.book,base.group_portal,r,"[('partner_id', 'child_of', user.partner_id.commercial_partner_id.id)]" library_loan_book,loans of readable books,library.loan,library.group_library_user,r,"[('book_id', 'access', 'read')]"

Some access decisions cannot be written with the forms above because the record to test is chosen by data: a message points at its document by a model name and an id (mail.message.model and res_id, a many2one_reference field), and the documents are of many models. An addon can declare a **rule operator** for such a case. It is a spelling that is valid in the domain text of ir.access rows only, and the policy compiler expands it when it builds the predicate. erp_sdk::rule_operator!(pub THREAD_ACCESS = "thread_access" { addon: "mail",              // ignored while this addon is not installed model: "mail.message",       // the only model whose rows may use it field: "res_id",             // the many2one_reference field the condition names inherits: "mail.thread",     // the models it ranges over operations: [Read],          // the values a row may give }); A row then writes ('res_id', 'thread_access', 'read') next to ordinary conditions: access_mail_message_user,mail.message.user,model_mail_message,base.group_user,r,"['|', ('author_id', '=', user.partner_id.id), ('res_id', 'thread_access', 'read')]" What the compiler does with it, for each group set and company shape (once, memoized with the rest of the predicate): one branch per concrete model that inherits inherits (abstract, transient and the declaring model itself are left out) and that the principal may read at model level, each model = M AND res_id pointing at a record of M that passes M's own rules for that operation. The branches hold parameters, never the id of a user or a company, so one predicate serves every user. A model the principal cannot read has no branch; no branch at all is FALSE. A record of M that no longer exists matches nothing, also where M allows everything. What it refuses, each as a rule error that denies the rows concerned (like any rule that does not compile) or, for a declaration, as a refusal to build the policy: | Refused | Message or effect | |---|---| | The spelling outside ir.access row text (an RPC, search or list-syntax domain) | The ordinary Invalid operator in condition ('res_id', 'thread_access', 'read'): it is not a domain operator | | Another model, another field, or a value the declaration does not list | The 'thread_access' operator works only on mail.message in condition ..., ... only on the field 'res_id' ..., Invalid value for 'thread_access' operator in condition ... | | A negation over it: '!', or the operator inside the sub-domain of a not any | a declared rule operator cannot be negated: ... | | A cycle through the access operator (M's rule needs the message again) | the rules on the cycle fail with the usual access cycle error | Blast radius: the expansion needs the combined read predicate of every model it ranges over that the principal may read at model level. A rule that does not compile, or an access cycle, on any such model therefore fails the reads of the declaring model (for thread_access, every mail.message read) for every group that reaches that model, with that rule's error. It is never skipped. A declaration of an addon that is not installed in the database is ignored (the spelling is then an invalid operator); one of an installed addon whose model or field is missing refuses to build. | A declaration with a malformed or duplicate name, the name of a core operator, a field that is not a many2one_reference, or a model the registry does not have | rule operator '<name>' (declared in <module>): <reason> (ADR 0032 Amendment 1); the policy does not build | The first declaration is thread_access of the mail addon (read only; posting and writing map to the document's operations in a later slice). Design: ADR 0032 Amendment 1, docs/design/m4-mail-core-a1-access.md. The declaration must be linked into the server (the addon crate is linked), or the spelling is an invalid operator in the rows that use it.

| Refused | Why | Write instead | |---|---|---| | user.has_group('x.group_y') | A group check is the rule's group | Two permission rows: one for x.group_y with the wider domain, one for the other group with the narrower one. Permissions OR, so members of x.group_y get both | | user.name, user.login, any non-id value of the user | Rules compare record ids | A path ending in .id or .ids | | user.env.companies..., user.env.ref(...), user.env['m'].search(<domain with user or company>) | Computed from the environment in Python | company_ids; a literal search; a path from user | | Arithmetic and string formatting (user.id + 1, '%s' % x, datetime.now() - timedelta(days=1)) | Computations are not compiled to SQL | A literal, a path, or the plain now/today forms | | .id after a one2many or many2many (user.employee_ids.id) | It names several records | .ids | | Names Odoo addons add to the rule context (website) | Not supported until an addon can declare a rule symbol | — | | A domain on a rule of ir.access itself | The table that repairs a broken policy is governed by permissions only (Odoo refuses it too) | A permission without domain | Example of the has_group rewrite. In place of one row sale_order_rule,orders,sale.order,sales_team.group_sale_salesman,r,"[] if user.has_group('sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads') else [('user_id', '=', user.id)]" ship two: sale_order_own,own orders,sale.order,sales_team.group_sale_salesman,r,"[('user_id', '=', user.id)]" sale_order_all,all orders,sale.order,sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads,r,

- **When the row is written** (ir.access create or write), the domain is checked against the model: an unknown field, operator or form is a ValidationError with Odoo's text, Invalid domain <domain>: <reason>. So a broken rule normally never reaches the table. - **When the policy is built** (after a module upgrade changed a model, or rows written with SQL), a rule that does not compile denies its model's operations to everyone it applies to (its group's members, or everyone for a restriction) with Access rule '<name>' (<id>) on <model> cannot be compiled: <reason>. It is never skipped and never turned into "everything". The build report lists it; erp access report prints the report and erp access disable-rule <xmlid> archives the rule. - **access cycles**: rules whose access conditions lead back to themselves (sale.order read needs res.partner read, which needs sale.order read) are rule errors of every rule on the cycle.

- "Today" and "now" are the transaction's start time; Odoo keeps the value in a cache until the next clear. - user.<path>.id and .ids are read in the statement itself, so a change of the user's partner or employee is seen at once. Every field on the path must be stored. - Rules that compute on user values are refused instead of evaluated (see above). - Write-time validation also checks the access conditions' field and operation; Odoo only checks them when the rule is used.

An access CSV is an input to authorization, not a complete acceptance oracle. For addon acceptance, author expected outcomes independently from the rows being tested. Reconcile the installed concrete and transient models (including extensions and auto-installed bridges) with an explicit manifest. Keep abstract models as named exclusions, never as silent skips. Use an ordinary authenticated administrator and ordinary internal users with verified groups and separate companies. A Full/System setup environment is not an administrative test subject. Anonymous HTTP denial does not test an authenticated public group's rules. Supply valid model-specific CRUD payloads; a validation error on bad input cannot prove authorization. Verify successful mutations by readback and refusals by absence of mutation, including mixed batches. Check generated company restrictions, field groups/runtime hooks, related fields, menu discovery and direct execution separately. Service-owned or immutable models need an explicit documented refusal and a supported positive control. Do not add blanket grants just to make their generic CRUD probes succeed. Attachments and chatter require a demonstrably unreadable parent; a foreign-company contact can still be shared under its declared policy. A staged source inventory and acceptance protocol exist; execution remains pending the multi-user fixture and test packages. Their eventual oracle must fail on unknown models or unresolved expected policy, never update its baseline automatically.

Inventory declares role permissions in its addon data. Move-line read is granted to the roles that can read moves; line create, write and delete are granted to the roles that can write moves. The same role mapping covers line serial children and correction records. An ordinary employee has no move-line grant. This mapping deliberately allows an operator to remove an editable line while retaining the move itself. These are explicit group rows, not automatic inheritance of a parent record's domains. A bridge adding a sales, purchasing, portal, barcode or quality role must declare its corresponding line permissions and any required record restrictions. In particular, portal access to a transfer must not become unrestricted line access. Other addon grants remain additive. Company confinement comes from model company_access declarations and their generated rules. Required-company balances and lines use exact scope with empty company denied. Explicitly shared locations, lots and routes permit empty company. Do not insert a sentinel company or duplicate the generated restrictions in an access CSV. Parent-owned location-policy and serial child rows use their declared parent scope. Lot-name scope and topology-version records have no ordinary permission rows, which means refusal rather than unrestricted access. Group and privilege defaults are editable records. The inventory light-group override composes with the inherited classification; its manifest invokes reclassification after loading the feature identities. Normal upgrades preserve group customization. The privilege category field is not available in the base model yet. Package permissions are intentionally withheld until the package model supplies a company declaration.

sections.text: Status: the access engine of ADR 0035 (design note docs/design/m3-access-engine.md §2.2, §3.3, §3.4). The rules themselves are ir.access rows (security.md §1), loaded and compiled into the policy described here by erp-security (erp_security::source::PolicySource, with erp_security::resolver::Resolver for the users' groups and companies). Engine tests also use erp_testkit::DomainPolicy. Field access by groups is described in [field-access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/field-access.md). Every Rust example on this page is compiled and run as a doctest of erp-test-models, like the examples of models.md.

Access has two levels, as in Odoo: 1. **The model check**: may this user read (write, create, delete) records of this model at all? Answered from the policy snapshot, no query. 2. **The record predicate**: which records? A domain over the model (Odoo's _access_domain), compiled to SQL and evaluated by PostgreSQL, never record by record in Rust. The engine applies them on every ORM operation, in Odoo's order: | Operation | What is checked | |---|---| | search, search_count, read_group, name_search | the model check, then the read predicate as one more condition after your domain, in the same statement | | reading fields of records | every record must match the read predicate, else erp.access | | write | the write predicate on every record, before the change | | create | the create predicate on the new records: decided by the INSERT itself when it reads only the new row's own columns, otherwise one statement after the create (the row must exist to be matched) | | unlink | the unlink predicate on every record, before anything is deleted | | x2many values | only the related records the user may read are listed | | many2many commands that link records | the linked records must be readable | | onchange | the write check of the edited record | A record check is one SELECT id … WHERE id = ANY($1) AND <predicate> per batch of ids. The read and write results are remembered for the rest of the transaction, until the transaction writes a field one of the predicates reads, so reading the same records again costs no query. Superuser mode (sudo(true)) passes every check. A new record that is not yet in the database and has no origin keeps field checks only; a new-record shadow of a database record (one with an origin) requires read access to that origin record. Cached values are shared within a transaction, including across with_user and sudo environments. A value in that cache grants no permission: scalar reads (cell, value, cells, values) and row/fetch APIs use the current environment's model, record and field checks. Reading as sudo and then dropping sudo cannot carry that permission into the next read. The permission memo is keyed separately by principal and policy. ADR 0084 proposes this deliberate strengthening of Odoo's direct cached field access; lead acceptance is pending. Raw SQL that writes ORM tables (tx.execute, tx.batch) is invisible to these memos and to the record cache: follow it with tx.invalidate_model(..) or tx.invalidate_records(..) (or tx.invalidate_all()), which ends both the cached values and the remembered access checks. A refusal is an erp.access error (ErrorKind::Access) with Odoo's texts: at model level Your access rights do not let you modify 'Book' (library.book) records. and the groups that would allow it; at record level Access rules protect some of these records. …, which in debug mode (an internal user with base.group_no_one) lists the denied records and the rules to blame. The record-level text costs one statement on the error path (two in debug mode).

A compiled predicate never holds the user's values: user.id, the companies and "now" are **parameters**, bound by each statement for the user it runs for. One predicate, and one SQL text, serves every user with the same groups. In Rust a parameter is a PrincipalParam (crates/erp-domain/src/param.rs, not part of the published documentation), used as the value of a condition: use erp_sdk::access::{NowKind, PrincipalParam, UserPath}; use erp_sdk::domain::Value; use erp_sdk::prelude::*;

// Odoo: [('user_id', '=', user.id)] let mine = Domain::condition("user_id", Operator::Eq, PrincipalParam::Uid)?; assert_eq!(mine.to_string(), "[('user_id', '=', user.id)]"); // Odoo: [('company_id', 'in', company_ids + [False])] let my_companies = Domain::condition( "company_id", Operator::In, Value::List(vec![PrincipalParam::CompanyIds.into(), Value::Bool(false)]), )?; assert_eq!( my_companies.to_string(), "[('company_id', 'in', [company_ids, False])]" ); // Odoo: [('partner_id', '=', user.partner_id.id)] let own_partner = Domain::condition( "partner_id", Operator::Eq, PrincipalParam::UserPath(UserPath::parse("partner_id.id")?), )?; assert_eq!( own_partner.to_string(), "[('partner_id', '=', user.partner_id.id)]" ); // Odoo: [('deadline', '>=', context_today())] on a date field let open = Domain::condition("deadline", Operator::Ge, PrincipalParam::Now(NowKind::Date))?; assert_eq!(open.to_string(), "[('deadline', '>=', context_today())]");

| Parameter | Odoo | Value | |---|---|---| | PrincipalParam::Uid | user.id | the user's id | | PrincipalParam::CompanyId | company_id | the current company | | PrincipalParam::CompanyIds | company_ids | the allowed companies (a list: in an in list it adds all of them) | | PrincipalParam::Now(NowKind::Date) / Now(NowKind::Timestamp) | context_today() / datetime.datetime.now() | the transaction's start, compared with date or datetime fields | | PrincipalParam::UserPath(path) | user.partner_id.id, user.employee_ids.ids | a field path from the user's res.users row, ending in id (one id, False when a link is empty) or ids (the ids reached) | | PrincipalParam::GrantIds { .. } | link grants | not available yet; binding one is refused | Rules for parameters: - Only Rust code builds them. No client domain, JSON value or data file can contain one. - They are decided in SQL only. A search binds them like an access predicate does; filtered_domain and other in-memory evaluation refuse a domain with a parameter (erp.programming). - Rewrites that need the value refuse them with a message naming the parameter: like/ilike, =?, a boolean field, a Now of the wrong kind (NowKind::Date on a datetime field).

Most access is data (ir.access rows). When a model needs a rule that rows cannot express, an addon overrides the predicate with an #[access_domain] function in a #[methods] block, the Rust form of Odoo's _access_domain override. It receives the predicate of the rest of the chain through sup and returns the new one; it narrows with & or widens with |:
use erp_sdk::access::{AccessCtx, AccessSuper, Operation, PrincipalParam}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*;
pub struct Book { #[field(char, required)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(many2one, comodel = "res.users")] pub owner_id: Option<RecId>, #[field(boolean)] pub restricted: bool, }

impl Book { /// Restricted books are read by their owner and by librarians only. #[access_domain] fn _access_domain(ctx: &AccessCtx, op: Operation, sup: AccessSuper) -> Result<Domain> { let policy = sup.call(ctx, op)?; if op != Operation::Read || ctx.has_group("library.group_librarian")? { return Ok(policy); } let open = Domain::condition("restricted", Operator::Eq, false)?; let owned = Domain::condition("owner_id", Operator::Eq, PrincipalParam::Uid)?; Ok(policy & (open | owned)) } }

- **Signature**: fn(ctx: &AccessCtx, op: Operation, sup: AccessSuper) -> Result<Domain>, synchronous, no self. The macro refuses an async fn, another signature, or a function that is also a #[method], #[compute], #[constrains], #[onchange] or #[rpc]. - **No user values, no I/O.** The function runs while the policy compiles a predicate, and the result is reused for every user with the same groups. AccessCtx tells it the groups (has_group), the kind of principal (class(): internal, portal, public …), the elevation kind and the model; the user's id, companies and context are not there. Use parameters for them, as owned does above. - **has_group("module.name")** answers for the user's effective groups. A malformed or unknown external id is an erp.programming error, never false: a typo must not silently deny or allow. - **Chain order**: each addon contributes at most one override per model; the overrides run in the model's method resolution order, the most recently loaded addon first, exactly like #[method(override)] chains (models.md). The bottom of the chain is the predicate the policy computed from the rows. - **Your addon must declare the model**: an override in an addon without a #[model] or #[extend] of that model, or a second override of one model by the same addon, stops the server at startup (example below). - **An error denies**: returning Err refuses the operation with that error. - **Superuser mode** never calls the chain (it passes every check).

pub mod library_extra { use erp_sdk::access::{AccessCtx, AccessSuper, Operation}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use super::Book; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "library_extra", depends = ["library"]); pub struct Rules; /// Wrong: this addon has no #[extend(Book, addon = "library_extra")]. #[methods(Book, addon = "library_extra")] impl Rules { #[access_domain] fn _access_domain(ctx: &AccessCtx, op: Operation, sup: AccessSuper) -> Result<Domain> { sup.call(ctx, op) } } }

let err = erp_testkit::Harness::builder([&ADDON, &library_extra::ADDON]) .check() .unwrap_err() .to_string(); assert!(err.contains( "(addon 'library_extra') has no declaration of model 'library.book' in addon \ 'library_extra': add an #[extend] (or #[model]) for it in that addon" ));

The override applies wherever the predicate does: searches, record checks, the access operator and filtered_access. A related field read as the user, or a search through a non-sudo relation, sees the override of the related model.

A model that delegates to a parent (inherits = [("parent.model", "field")]) is reachable only where its parent is: the parent's predicate is ANDed into the model's own, and a parent the user may not touch at all denies the model too (Odoo's _check_inherits_access). A model whose own rules should decide alone, like Odoo's mail.mail over mail.message, says inherits_access = false:
pub struct Message { #[field(char)] pub body: Option<Arc<str>>, } /// An outgoing mail of a message: its own rules decide who sees it.

name = "library.mail", description = "Outgoing Mail", inherits = [("library.message", "message_id")], inherits_access = false )] pub struct Mail { #[field(many2one, comodel = "library.message", required, ondelete = "cascade")] pub message_id: Option<RecId>, }

let registry = erp_testkit::Harness::builder([&ADDON]).registry_only()?; assert!(!registry.model("library.mail").unwrap().inherits_access); assert!(registry.model("library.message").unwrap().inherits_access);

The default is true; the newest declaration that sets it wins, so an addon's #[extend] can change it. Whom the error message names as allowed groups still intersects with the parents' (Odoo's _get_groups_with_access does too).
Recordsets have Odoo's three access helpers (erp_sdk::access::Operation names the operation):
use erp_sdk::access::Operation;

// erp.access unless every book may be written (Odoo check_access('write')) books.check_access(&mut tx, Operation::Write).await?; // the same as a boolean (Odoo has_access('unlink')) let can_delete: bool = books.has_access(&mut tx, Operation::Unlink).await?; // the books the user may read, in order (Odoo _filtered_access('read')) let readable: Records = books.filtered_access(&mut tx, Operation::Read).await?;

In a domain, the access operator asks the same question: ('id', 'access', 'write') keeps the records the user may write, ('partner_id', 'access', 'read') the records whose partner the user may read (a many2one or id field, and read, write, create or unlink as the value). **Changing data with SQL.** The memo of record checks follows ORM writes. After changing with SQL data that predicates read, call tx.invalidate_model(..), tx.invalidate_records(..) or tx.invalidate_all(), as you would for cached values: they also forget the memoized checks that read the invalidated fields.

Where Odoo code calls sudo() to read or write one thing the user may not, open a named block that names exactly that (ADR 0164; ADR 0035 decision 5). Transaction::elevated takes the caller's environment, a reason (a dotted name, ElevationReason), an ElevationScope (models, operations and, optionally, fields) and the body. The body gets an environment of the same user carrying the scope: use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use erp_orm::audit::ElevationReason; use erp_orm::{ElevationScope, Operation, OperationSet, ScopeItem}; async fn author_names(tx: &mut Transaction, env: &Env) -> Result<Vec<Value>> { let users = tx.registry().model_id("res.users") .ok_or_else(|| Error::programming("res.users is missing"))?; let scope = ElevationScope::new([ScopeItem::new(users, OperationSet::of([Operation::Read]))?])?; tx.elevated(env, ElevationReason::new("library.author.read_name")?, scope, async |tx, env| { env.records("res.users")?.search(tx, &Domain::TRUE).await?.values(tx, "name").await }) .await } What the runtime guarantees today: - **The environment lives only as long as the block.** When the body returns, fails, panics or its future is dropped, the block closes. Using its environment or its recordsets afterwards, or in another transaction, is refused with Programming ("elevated environment of block … (reason '…') used outside it"), whatever the cache already holds. Return plain values from the body, not environments or recordsets. A panic or a dropped future also cancels the transaction (as an interrupted savepoint does): writes the body left pending are never flushed, and the transaction must be rolled back. - **The elevation is audited before the body runs.** Entry records the reason, the scope and who acted in the transaction's audit row; equal blocks are one entry with a count. When the audit store is not ready the body does not run. - **A scope never reaches superuser mode.** sudo(true) or with_user of the superuser on a block environment gives an environment that refuses every use ("… cannot be widened to superuser mode"), and so do the audited escape hatches (unscoped sudo, a superuser server action). Other derivations (with_context, with_company, sudo(false), with_user of another user) keep the block's lifetime; a with_user of another user is admitted only when the block's user itself holds principal.impersonate (a scope never carries a capability; SPEC-PRIN-029). The engine's own privileged steps keep working inside a block: the body of a compute_sudo field, for example, runs in superuser mode bound to the block, which grants nothing beyond what that compute already runs with outside any block, and ends with the block. - **Library code that calls sudo(true) fails inside a block** until it is migrated (the mail, base and web libraries are planned): for example base's decimal precision lookup (a write of a field with a named precision that this transaction has not resolved yet), and mail posting and followers. Such calls get the "cannot be widened to superuser mode" error. Resolve or prepare those values before the block, or wait for the slice that moves that library code to its own block. - **Nested blocks do not add up.** A block opened inside another carries only its own scope, so library code that opens its own block (mail posting, numbering) works from inside yours. The outer environment stays valid until the outer block closes. - **Pending writes are flushed before the block closes**, also when the body returned an error; if that flush fails as well, one error carries both messages. A read-only API key stays read-only inside a block. What is refused before the body, with Programming unless said otherwise: - a transaction that must be rolled back: cancelled, aborted or released ("cannot open an elevation block: the transaction is aborted or released; roll back" for the last two), or poisoned, which is refused with the poison's own error (its kind and message, for example the Validation error that poisoned it); - a read-only transaction without a read-audit owner ("scoped elevation requires an audited transaction: this read-only transaction has no read-audit owner"); RPC read-effect calls are opened by the server with an owner, which writes one read_ok attempt row before the result is released (an addon does not declare an owner: the P6 lint will enforce that, and until then core review does); - a model or field id that is not in the transaction's registry; - a lifted rule the access policy refuses (see below). A refused entry takes no block identity and records no evidence. What a scope grants (ADR 0164 D3): - **For each (model, operation) the scope names**, the permission rules count as granted: the user needs no ir.access permission row for it. Every restriction (group-less rule) still applies, including the generated company restriction and rules that reach the company through a relation. An access condition or rule operator inside such a restriction is decided for the user without the block, so naming its target model too does not widen it. An _inherits child keeps its parent's predicate: the scoped one when the scope names the parent for that operation, the user's ordinary one otherwise. - **Everything the scope does not name** (another operation of the same model, another model) is decided exactly as for the user without the block, with the same error kind and message. - **A rule that bears the company.** For a scope, a rule bears the company when it does not compile, is the generated company restriction, names company_id, company_ids or the company parameters (company_ids, company_id), is a rule of res.company, or reads (directly, through a relational path, an any sub-domain, a literal search or a user.<path>) a field of res.company, a many2one, one2many or many2many whose comodel is res.company under any name (ir.job's run_as_company included), or a reference or many2one_reference field (it cannot be proven not to point at a company). The check sees company relations only through field types (relations to res.company, reference fields, rules of res.company): a plain integer or char field holding a company id, or a many2one to a model that _inherits res.company, is not detected, so do not rely on the check for those. - **Lifting a restriction:** ScopeItem::lift names restrictions to drop for the item's operations. A lift is accepted only for a restriction of the item's model that compiles, does not bear the company, holds no access condition or rule operator, and applies to at least one operation the item names. Anything else (a permission, another model's rule, an unknown external id) is refused at entry with Programming naming the rule and the reason, for example "cannot lift restriction rule 'my_addon.rule_x' (Rule X) on my.model: it bears the company (it reads my.model.owner_company, a relation to res.company), and a scope never lifts a company restriction". A policy without restriction rules (a fixed or test policy) refuses every lift. - **A named operation whose company confinement is only in permissions** is refused at entry with Programming, before the block takes an identity or records anything: when a permission rule of the model for that operation bears the company and no restriction of the model for that operation confines to companies, naming it would drop the model's only company filter. Only the generated company restriction counts as company confinement: a handwritten restriction never does, even one naming company_id or the company parameters ([('company_id', '!=', False)] or ['|', ('public', '=', True), ('company_id', 'in', company_ids)] confine nothing to the user's companies), nor a rule of res.company or one reading a reference field. A permission with an access condition or a rule operator bears the company too: it brings in the target model's whole predicate, company restriction included, so a line confined only through its document ([('order_id', 'access', 'read')]) is not nameable. To keep a model with a company_id nameable in a scope, give it a company_access that generates its company restriction (res.company takes no declaration, and every permission of it bears the company, so an operation of it with a permission is never nameable). All permission rules of the model count, not only those of the user's groups, so the answer does not depend on who opens the block. Example: "the scope names read on 'res.company', which keeps no generated company restriction and whose permission rules (base.access_company_system, base.access_company_internal) may bear the company: scoped elevation cannot open it (ADR 0164 A6)". In the shipped rules of base, mail, uom and product this refuses every operation on res.company, Read on mail.message, and Read, Write and Unlink on mail.activity (their document rules read the res_id reference); models with a generated company restriction, such as res.currency.rate, stay nameable. This fail-closed rule is accepted (ADR 0164 D3). - **Not changed:** field access. A field restricted by groups stays closed inside a block until field masks for scoped blocks exist (planned). The company set never grows, and a read-only API key stays read-only. Scoped elevation is never the way to act in a company the user is not in (ADR 0164 A6).

The policy snapshot is compiled from the access tables, and a user's groups and companies are resolved from the user tables. When a transaction changes them through the ORM, the engine flushes what is pending, rebuilds the policy for that transaction alone and resolves the users again before its next decision (design note §3.4), so a transaction sees its own access changes. base registers its tables for this. An addon whose table feeds the policy or the resolution of users registers it with policy_source!; a table that predicates only *read* (a project's members, a document's followers) needs no registration:
use erp_sdk::access::{PolicySourceWrite, SourceKind};

pub struct Role { #[field(many2one, comodel = "res.users")] pub user_id: Option<RecId>, #[field(boolean, default = true)] pub active: bool, } erp_sdk::access::policy_source!( /// Roles put users in groups: a membership the resolver reads. pub ROLES = PolicySourceWrite::new("library.role", SourceKind::Membership) .fields(&["user_id", "active"]) );

SourceKind::Policy marks a table the policy is compiled from, SourceKind::Membership one the users' groups and companies are resolved from. Every create and unlink counts; a write counts when it touches one of the listed fields (all fields without .fields(..)). The server checks the listed fields at startup. Core code that changes such tables with SQL (data loading, uninstall, migrations) calls tx.mark_policy_dirty() instead.

Import DOM controllers from @erpforall/elang. Create them after mounting, and release them when the owning view closes. Controllers do not infer roles, labels, selection or business actions. Native controls keep their own Enter/Space behavior. import { createFocusTrap, createRovingTabindex, LiveRegion, createTranslator } from "@erpforall/elang"; const trap = createFocusTrap(dialogElement, { onEscape: closeDialog }); // The modal owner also makes the background inert and removes it on close. const tabs = createRovingTabindex(tablistElement, { items: () => [...tablistElement.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('[role="tab"]')], orientation: "horizontal", }); // Call after the caller changes the item collection or availability. tabs.refresh(); const announcements = new LiveRegion(appElement); announcements.announce("Saved"); // polite by default; assertive for urgent errors // Snapshot the user's language and trusted catalogue at app/session creation. const { _t } = createTranslator({ language: userLanguage, catalogue }); const label = _t("Hello %s", displayName); // On disposal: trap.dispose(); tabs.dispose(); announcements.destroy();

For role="menu" dropdowns (such as action menus, cog menus, navbar overflow lists, breadcrumbs collapsed trails, and debug menus), attachMenuDropdown manages roving focus across menuitems with arrow keys (ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End), Escape dismissal returning focus to the trigger button, Tab key closing, outside click dismissal, and aria-expanded synchronization. Only en_US is admitted in B0. Other languages fail with an error saying language selection is not available yet. Missing catalogue terms fall back to their source text. Module-scoped lookup uses translator.forModule("my_addon"). Named substitutions use _t("Hello %(name)s", {name: displayName}). Catalogue data is snapshotted and bounded; missing substitution values fail. Returned plain strings must render as text. If an argument is genuine Markup, the result is Markup and all other text, including the format string, is escaped. Never insert plain translation strings as HTML. Compiler extraction/translation and RTL remain UI5-DONE sibling deliveries. For Vitest import auditComponent from @erpforall/elang/testing and await it with a connected mounted component root. It runs axe-core with color contrast disabled because jsdom cannot measure rendering. Use await auditPage(page) with a Playwright Page for a complete rendered document audit including active overlays and contrast. Run audits after opening each hidden menu/dialog. Both helpers throw on serious or critical violations and return the complete engine result for other findings. Injection/engine errors propagate. The testing entry point and axe-core are dev-only; never import it from a view or runtime module. Automated audits do not prove screen-reader speech, keyboard correctness or complete WCAG conformance. LiveRegion is also a canonical service class: register with env.services.add(LiveRegion) before startup, then resolve with env.services.get(LiveRegion) or useService(LiveRegion). Its default service root is document.body. The app owner calls destroy() during teardown; the container does not implicitly dispose service instances. Catalogue admission permits at most 1024 modules (names of 1–256 UTF-16 units), 100000 terms and a 16 MiB aggregate charge. The charge is twice each term's source and translation lengths plus 64 per term; twice each module name's length plus 128 per module. These are admission accounting units, not measured heap bytes. Source strings are limited to 65536 units and formatted output to 1048576 units.

createHotkeyController(root, {bindings, blocked, report}) registers a disposable view owner. Supply a synchronous array of HotkeyBinding declarations; it is validated on creation, refresh and dispatch. A DOM binding focuses and clicks its existing target. A callback binding runs run() and reports throws and rejected promises through report. Keep that error sink alive after view disposal. import { createHotkeyController, createHotkeyBoundary } from "@erpforall/elang"; const shortcuts = createHotkeyController(appElement, { bindings: () => [{kind: "dom", chord: "alt+x", target: executeButton}], blocked: () => operationPending, report: reportError, }); const overlayKeys = createHotkeyBoundary(dialogElement, { onEscape: closeDialog, report: reportError, }); // After replacing controls, drop obsolete hints and validate the new collection. shortcuts.refresh(); // On close/unmount (both operations are idempotent): overlayKeys.dispose(); shortcuts.dispose(); Chords use optional modifiers in order ctrl+alt+meta+shift+ and a lowercase letter/digit or escape/enter. Invalid options and declarations throw UIError with code: "value"; refreshing a disposed controller is a usage error. Controllers allow at most 256 bindings each, with 128 controllers and 32 exclusive boundaries per document; chord/hint text is at most 32 UTF-16 units. These are admission limits, not measured heap figures. Targets must belong to the root's document. A dynamic supplier failure reports to its owner and aborts the event. Only the active exclusive overlay receives shortcuts. An unmatched or blocked modal does not pass commands to the page behind it. A duplicate eligible chord reports one error and activates nothing. Element/document handlers may consume keys before shared dispatch at window bubbling; Escape belongs to one scope per event. Boundary Escape is allowed in editable controls, is nonrepeating and is suppressed during composition. An explicit conflicting Escape binding is an error. Default bindings exclude editable targets and repeats; a declaration can explicitly set allowEditable or allowRepeat. Composition sessions, isComposing, AltGraph and consumed events always win. DOM eligibility excludes hidden, inert, disabled, aria-disabled, disconnected and collapsed controls. Alt hints are text-only, aria-hidden and cleaned on release, blur, visibility loss, mutation and disposal. Native Enter/Space and editor-local keyboard behavior remain with their controls.

Status: implemented. Addon base has the action models (ir.actions.act_window, act_url, client, server), their key table ir.actions.actions, the contextual-action lookup get_bindings and the menu model ir.ui.menu; server actions run (see "Running server actions"), including code actions. The web client's /web/action/load and load_menus are not served yet. Design: docs/design/m2-s3.md §3, §6; ADR 0058 (the shared id sequence). Specs: SPEC-DATA-062, 063, 064 in docs/specs/data/data-views-api.md. Field names are Odoo's, so the data files you port from Odoo load unchanged: <record id="action_partner" model="ir.actions.act_window"> <field name="name">Contacts</field> <field name="res_model">res.partner</field> <field name="view_mode">list,form,kanban</field> <field name="path">contacts</field> </record> <menuitem id="menu_contacts" name="Contacts" action="action_partner" sequence="10"/>

Each action type has its own table (ir_act_window, ir_act_url, ir_act_client, ir_act_server), and all of them draw their ids from one sequence, ir_actions_id_seq (#[model(..., id_sequence = ACTIONS_ID_SEQUENCE)], see [models.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/models.md)). So an action id names exactly one action of any type, as in Odoo. The key table ir_actions (ir.actions.actions) has one row per action: its id, type (the typed model, e.g. ir.actions.act_window), name, path and the binding columns. The typed models' create and write keep it in step in the same statement batch, and a follow-delete trigger on every typed table removes the key rows of every deleted action, also of the ones a foreign key deletes by cascade (a multi action's children, the actions of a deleted model or field). Writing ir.actions.actions directly is refused with Programming "ir.actions.actions rows follow their typed action; write the typed action instead", and so is upsert on any action model (it does not run create). A new action type of your addon inherits ir.actions.base, names the same sequence and declares the trigger; create refuses an action model without both, and so does the final registry (erp_addon_base::ir_actions::check_action_model):
use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use erp_addon_base::ir_actions::{ACTIONS_CACHE, ACTIONS_ID_SEQUENCE, IrActionsBase}; /// An action that opens a dashboard.

name = "actions_guide.dashboard_action", description = "Dashboard Action", table = "actions_guide_dashboard_action", inherit = [IrActionsBase], id_sequence = ACTIONS_ID_SEQUENCE, follow_deletes = [("_keys_follow", cache = ACTIONS_CACHE, key_table = "ir_actions")] )] pub struct DashboardAction { /// The dashboard to open. #[field(char, required = true)] pub dashboard: Option<Arc<str>>, }

type is set from the model on create; a different value is a Validation error. To find which type an id belongs to, erp_addon_base::ir_actions::action_by_id(tx, id) reads the key table (one statement) and returns an ActionRef whose model is checked against the registry. Inserts and updates that go around the ORM (migration SQL on an action table) must keep ir_actions in step and invalidate the actions named cache themselves; deletes are followed by the trigger, but the deleting transaction itself sees the change only when the ORM made it. get_bindings refuses a key row whose typed row is missing, naming both tables. run_as_superuser is set only by an administrator on an action with groups (see "Running server actions").

path is the URL segment the web client shows for an action. It must match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*, must not start with m- or action-, must not be new, and is at most 128 bytes; each rule has Odoo's message, checked before anything is written (erp_addon_base::ir_actions::check_path, typed error ActionPathError): use erp_addon_base::ir_actions::{ActionPathError, check_path}; fn main() { assert_eq!(check_path("contacts"), Ok(())); assert_eq!(check_path("Contacts"), Err(ActionPathError::Format)); assert_eq!(check_path("action-7"), Err(ActionPathError::ReservedAction)); } An empty path is a format error (leave the field unset instead; Odoo would store ''). A path is unique across **all** action types: the unique index _path_unique of ir_actions decides, so two transactions saving the same path on two types cannot both commit. The second waits for the first and then fails with Validation "Path to show in the URL must be unique! Please choose another one." (Odoo checks with a count query, which two transactions can pass together.)

views is computed: first one (view, type) per view_ids row, then each type of view_mode that no row gives, the action's view_id first when its type is one of them, the others with false. With view_mode = "list,form,kanban", view_id a form view F and a view_ids row for a kanban view K, views is [[K, "kanban"], [F, "form"], [false, "list"]]. view_mode must not repeat a type ("The modes in view_mode must not be duplicated: [...]") and must not contain whitespace or an empty type ("No spaces allowed in view_mode: “[...]”"). Odoo lets "list, form" and "list,,form" through (BUG-072); we do not. At most 32 types and 256 bytes. Unknown types are accepted, as in Odoo. res_model and the binding model must be models of the registry ("Invalid model name “x” in action definition."); without a name, the action takes its model's description.

A window action opened in the web client may carry default values for the records created from it: <record id="action_move_out_invoice_type" model="ir.actions.act_window"> <field name="name">Invoices</field> <field name="res_model">account.move</field> <field name="view_mode">list,form</field> <field name="context">{'default_move_type': 'out_invoice'}</field> </record> The web server (erp_load_web_action, erp_load_web_action_views, erp_load_web_action_ref) admits the context only as a literal dictionary of at most 16 keys, each default_<field> naming a field of res_model, each value a text, a boolean or an integer within the browser's safe range. The client adds it to the session context, so the list's New button and a form opened from the menu start with those values; a dashboard card's own context comes after it, and a session key always keeps the session's value. Everything else is refused by name when the action is loaded: an expression (uid, context.get(...)), a list or a negative number as a value, a key that names no field, a repeated key, session keys such as allowed_company_ids, and search_default_<name> (default search filters of an action are not delivered yet). A default must also be one the field can take. A key that names a readonly, computed or related field, a one2many or many2many field, or a field of a type without a literal form here (binary, json, reference and the like) is refused. The value must fit the field's type: | Field type | Value | |---|---| | boolean | True or False | | integer | an integer | | many2one | a record id: an integer above zero | | float, monetary | an integer (the context admits no decimal literal) | | char, text, html | a text | | selection | a text; one of the declared values when the selection is a static list | | date | a text of the form YYYY-MM-DD | | datetime | a text of the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS | For dates only the form is checked when the action is loaded. An empty {} is the same as no context.
An action with binding_model_id shows in that model's action menu (binding_type = "action") or print menu ("report"), in the view types of binding_view_types:

use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn menu_entries(tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<Vec<String>> { let env = tx.env(); let bindings = erp_addon_base::ir_actions::get_bindings(tx, &env, "res.groups").await?; Ok(bindings .action() .iter() .map(|b| format!("{}: {:?}", b.id(), b.values().get("name"))) .collect()) }

Each binding's values are id, name, binding_view_types, and sequence and domain where the action type has them (an empty domain is left out). action bindings are sorted by sequence (absent: 0), then id. A binding with group_ids shows only to members of one of them (base.group_no_one only in debug mode); a binding with a res_model shows only when the user may read that model. The part that is the same for everyone is cached per model in the named cache actions, which every action write invalidates, in every process (the signal generations); a cold call costs one statement on ir_actions plus one per action type present, a warm call none. Group membership is checked per call, so joining a group needs no invalidation. A model name the registry does not have is a Validation error.

ir.ui.menu has Odoo's fields: name, active, sequence (default 10), parent_id (ondelete = restrict: a menu with children cannot be deleted), child_id, group_ids (ir_ui_menu_group_rel), web_icon and action, a reference "<action model>,<id>" over the four action models. The tree is a parent store: a cycle is refused with "This parent would make a loop in the 'Menu' records: ...". The <menuitem> shorthand of data files writes these records ([data-files.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/data-files.md)). Which menus a user sees is decided by the web client's menu loading, which is not available yet.

A report is an ir.actions.report record plus a QWeb view whose key is the report's report_name. Both load from your data files; the action shares the id space of the other action types and shows under **Settings > Technical > Reporting > Reports**. Paper formats (report.paperformat) are under **Paper Format** next to it. my_addon.report_order qweb my_addon.report_order

Order my_addon.order qweb-pdf my_addon.report_order 'Order ' + object.name report | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | model (required) | the model printed; must be in the registry | | report_type | qweb-pdf (default), qweb-html or qweb-text | | report_name (required) | the key of the QWeb template | | paperformat_id | a report.paperformat; empty: the company's, then base.paperformat_euro | | print_report_name | expression over object and time giving the download name; empty: name | | binding_model_id, binding_type=report | lists the report when printing records of that model; create_action and unlink_action (the form's "Offer when printing" and "Stop offering when printing") set and clear it | | binding_view_types, multi | where the Print menu offers it; multi hides it on a form | | group_ids, domain | who and which records see it in the Print menu | | save_as_attachment, attachment, attachment_use | keep the printed file as an attachment named by the attachment expression, and print it again instead of rendering | | allow_attachment_group_fields | acknowledges that a kept attachment shows group-restricted fields as the first printer saw them | Base ships three paper formats: base.paperformat_euro (A4), base.paperformat_us (US Letter) and base.paperformat_batch_deposit. Checked when the action or its template loads, each refusal naming the report: - print_report_name and attachment must parse as expressions; save_as_attachment needs an attachment expression. - For qweb-pdf and qweb-html, the template and every template it calls by a literal t-call must stay inside the print profile (crates/erp-report/src/profile.rs). - With an attachment expression, a template that prints a field limited to groups is refused unless allow_attachment_group_fields is set. - At the end of the install or upgrade, a template (or called template) that is not an active QWeb view of the database is refused: `Report 'Order' (my_addon.report_order): template '...' is not an active QWeb view of this database`. Printing: a list with selected records and a record form each show a **Print** button before the **Actions** menu. It lists the reports of the model (erp_print_reports) by name, a model without a report shows "No report available", and the Actions menu never holds reports. On a form, picking a report saves unsaved changes first and then prints that one record. report_action returns the client action (type, name, report_name, report_type, context.active_ids, data).

Actions and menus live in PostgreSQL only. The bindings cache is per process and rebuilt on demand; another process's action write reaches it through the cache:actions generation, read by the opening flight of each transaction before any cached value is used.

erp_addon_base::server_action::run_server_action(tx, env, &RunRequest::new(action_id, active_model, &active_ids)) runs one ir.actions.server action and returns the action it asks the client to open, if any (ActionResult). It runs **as the caller**: the access check, every child of a multi action and every write use the caller's environment, never superuser, unless the action carries the administrator-only run_as_superuser flag (ADR 0009 §10; Odoo checks the caller and then runs as superuser). An action with groups needs the caller in one of them; one without needs write access on its model and the active records. A flagged action's run is audited: see [the audit trail](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/audit.md). Before the first runner starts, the action and its whole tree of children are read in one statement and checked: at most 8 levels (MAX_DEPTH) and 256 actions (MAX_ACTIONS), no warnings (a child on another model, children with other groups, a sequence on a non-text field, …), a runner for every type, and every stored selection set (evaluation_type on object_write, update_m2m_operation on an x2many target). An error after that point (a child's access check, a write) can come after an earlier child wrote: **roll back the transaction on every error.** Stored action data is bounded before it reaches the client driver: each selected text field may contain at most 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, each action at most 256 group IDs, and the tree at most 1,048,576 logical payload bytes (text plus eight bytes per group ID). Exceeding a bound returns a typed Limit error; group lists are never truncated. An update path may contain at most 16 dot-separated steps. The runner's active_model, active_ids and active_id describe the current request. An empty request removes active_id, including a value inherited from the caller's context, while preserving unrelated context keys. The caller's original environment is unchanged. Outside superuser mode, the guard for mutations of a flagged action tree permits at most 256 distinct actions across the affected ancestor/descendant set. Larger sets are refused before locking; unlink checks the caller's model and record permissions first. Stored parent chains are checked after create, including links supplied by default_parent_id in loader or sudo contexts. Built in: object_write, object_create, multi, and sandboxed Luau code/equations ([script API](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/luau-scripts.md)). object_copy and webhook (both planned) return ServerActionError::Unsupported. run_as_superuser = true is written only by an administrator, on an action with groups; changing the tree of a flagged action also needs base.group_system. Running a flagged action records the elevation in the audit trail before the elevated body runs: the caller's right to run it is checked first, then the node and its subtree run with superuser mode, and a run whose audit row cannot be written does not start.

An addon adds a value to ir.actions.server.state with selection_add and declares its runner (Odoo's _run_action_<state>[_multi]): use erp_addon_base::server_action::{ActionResult, RunnerCtx}; use erp_sdk::{BoxFuture, Result, serde_json::json}; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "action_demo", depends = ["base"]); fn open_record(ctx: RunnerCtx<'_>) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Option<ActionResult>>> { Box::pin(async move { let id = ctx.records().ids()[0]; Ok(Some(ActionResult::new(json!({ "type": "ir.actions.act_url", "url": format!("/record/{id}"), }))?)) }) } erp_addon_base::server_action_runner!( OPEN_RECORD = { state: "x_open_record", multi: false, run: open_record } );

multi: false runs once per active record (its id in the context as active_id), multi: true once for all. The declaration belongs to the declaring crate's ADDON (or addon: OTHER_ADDON) and counts only when that addon is installed. Registry setup (check_runners, from _register_hook of ir.actions.server) refuses two runners for one state and a runner whose state is not in the selection, naming each declaration's file:line, and a state without a runner, naming the state. A runner writes only through ctx.env() and ctx.tx(), never sudo.

Implementation acceptance for this new contract is pending. An exposed main-form object method can return a literal action such as: { "type": "ir.actions.act_window", "name": "Related records", "res_model": "my_addon.line", "target": "current", "views": [[false, "list"], [false, "form"]], "domain": [["parent_id", "=", 42]], "context": {"default_parent_id": 42} } In real code derive the parent id from the authorized singleton. The numbers above illustrate syntax; they are not a shipped provider or real count. Check the source record's read permission in your method. The normalizer admits the target model and domain fields under the caller, and every later ORM read enforces current record rules and company selection. A domain filters the action; it is not a grant and does not replace model security. Admission uses ordinary read-only search planning, including registered search-domain hooks. Those hooks can run during normalization and again during later searches; keep them read-only and do not treat normalization as a single execution of a business action. Only literal domains, list optionally followed by form, and default_<field> values naming real target fields are supported. A current-window result may also carry the booleans active_test and create; create: False hides New in the opened list, as Odoo does. The opened list's breadcrumb leads back to the record whose button opened it. Company/user/locale/server context, expressions, services, res_id, view_mode aliases and current-list results from a dialog are refused. Integral numeric literals must fit the browser's safe integer range; use the field's supported string representation for exact decimal values. Existing target: "new" form dialogs keep their existing syntax. The source is saved and validated before its object method runs. A destination failure is reported without repeating that method; the source is refreshed. The base domain survives list search clearing, paging and form/list navigation. Field defaults and caller context travel with that action, including new-record creation. The URL contains only a page-lifetime action identity. Back/forward in the same page can reuse it. Reload, copying the URL into another tab, state eviction or authority/metadata lifetime changes can expire it; an explicit error asks the user to reopen the originating menu, with a recovery link on an initially expired route. No raw action JSON or domain is placed in the URL, and expired state never opens an unfiltered list. The page keeps at most 64 entries, each bounded to 32 KiB serialized state. This framework change does not add a sample Library loan counter. A correct related count must use a separately admitted aggregate under the caller's rules, including target-model Read when zero rows match. Historical event counters and relation-id materialization are not substitutes for that provider.

The web client loads the menu tree via ir.ui.menu.erp_load_web_menus (JSON-2 endpoint, Read access). Every returned menu node includes module: string | null, including application roots. This is the nonempty namespace of the oldest ir.model.data row (lowest row ID) whose model is ir.ui.menu and whose res_id is that menu. No provenance, or an empty namespace on that selected row, returns explicit null. A child uses its own provenance; it does not inherit the root's module. Later external-ID aliases do not replace the selected namespace. Names, icons and action targets do not determine the module. This read never generates an external ID. An ordinary user can receive module metadata for an authorized menu without direct access to ir.model.data. The value grants no permission and does not prove that an addon is installed. Existing menu, action and target-model access still determines the returned forest. Module text shares the request budget and is limited to 4096 bytes. Settings-rail rendering is delivered separately. Key capabilities on ir.ui.menu: - complete_name: Computed breadcrumb path of the menu (e.g. "Sales / Configuration / Settings"), computed hierarchical path joined with " / ". - _visible_menu_ids(debug): ORM method returning the set of menu IDs visible to the calling user based on: - Active flag (active = true) - ACL read permissions on ir.ui.menu - Group membership in group_ids - Deep visibility: a menu with an action is visible if the user has access; a parent folder menu is visible only if at least one of its children or descendants is visible.

Menu trees (wire::MenuTree) are evaluated directly per request within the caller's authenticated transaction and REPEATABLE READ snapshot. Ad-hoc in-memory caching was removed (ADR 0060 D3/D5, review WM-01/02) to eliminate authority collisions across principals, group revocations, company context, and database snapshot boundaries. Evaluation invariants: - **Bounded capacity**: Enforces MAX_MENU_ROWS = 4096 and MAX_TREE_DEPTH = 32. - **Cycle detection**: Fails loudly on menu hierarchy cycles. - **Action access reachability**: Replaces raw SQL with authenticated ORM record checks (ir.actions.act_window record rules and target model Read permissions). - **Descendant pruning**: Menus without an accessible action and folder menus with no authorized action descendant are pruned from the returned tree. - **Budget enforcement**: Response payload serialization is metered through ResponseAdmission and DescriptionEncoder, sharing the request's DescriptionBudget under the 8 MiB ceiling.

The core framework has no HTTP client for AI and never needs a model to run. A provider (a hosted service or a local server) is an addon that implements the traits of erp_sdk::ai: - ModelProvider: text completion, streaming and token counting with CompletionRequest and CompletionResponse. Every completion and embedding call reports a UsageRecord (tokens, cost, latency). - EmbeddingProvider: vector embeddings. - ToolModelProvider: tool turns, on top of ModelProvider. A provider that cannot call tools does not implement it, so code that needs tool calling does not compile against it. Design: docs/design/m3-ai0-iface.md (text and embeddings) and docs/design/ai1-sdk-tools.md (tool calling); decision record ADR 0188.

Call erp_addon_ai_base::catalog::find_models_spec() for the static provider tool declaration. Pass the caller's existing transaction and a typed ToolCall to catalog::find_models. The sole argument is query, a string. An empty query looks across all concrete installed models. Names and bounded descriptions match case-insensitively. The result carries the original call ID and labelled JSON data containing models in technical-name order and a has_more flag. Each row contains name, description and description_truncated. Narrow the query when has_more is true. Hidden models are omitted before deciding whether more results exist. The tool requires an ordinary user and a current company. A future HTTP turn handler must also establish an interactive session and verify CSRF. The native tool does not open an endpoint. No fields, business records or record counts are returned. The database's technical System Parameters govern each search: | Parameter | Default | Allowed range | |---|---:|---:| | ai_base.catalog_query_bytes | 256 | 1–1024 UTF-8 bytes | | ai_base.catalog_result_rows | 20 | 1–80 readable models | | ai_base.catalog_help_chars | 160 | 1–2000 Unicode scalar values | | ai_base.catalog_result_bytes | 32768 | 4096–65536 labelled JSON bytes | If the first model's description alone would exhaust the byte budget, the result keeps its technical name and marks its description as truncated.

The native erp_cli::assistant_read::search_records entry accepts the configured RPC service, Auth service, browser session secret, selected company, and a typed tool call. It executes web_search_read against the target model using that session. The host owns the trusted company selection. The provider cannot supply a session, context or company override. For example, {"model":"purchase.order","domain":[["state","=","draft"]],"fields":["name","state"],"limit":5,"order":"id desc"} asks for five recent draft orders visible in the chosen company. The required domain is a nonempty AND list of direct scalar comparisons. Operators are =, !=, >, <, >=, <= and ilike. Dates use the ordinary RPC field format. Specify one simple sort field and optional asc or desc. Direct stored scalar fields are supported. Relation paths, computed and delegated values, secret, binary and group-masked fields are excluded. A refused filter or sort field fails the call. The explicit projection omits ineligible fields and requires at least one readable field. Each output row carries an ID. The truncated flag covers count, text or payload limits. When the first complete row exceeds the byte limit only its ID is returned. Technical System Parameters under ai_base.search_ set the admissible maximum rows (20; 1–80), fields (16; 1–64), conditions (12; 1–64), operand bytes (256; 1–2048), characters per returned string (512; 1–2000) and labelled result bytes (32768; 4096–65536). Reads follow the database's installed record rules and the RPC service's read-audit policy.

A tool turn is a ToolTurnRequest: a model name, the conversation as TurnMessages and the ToolSpecs the model may call. Each message is a role (TurnRole::System, User, Assistant) and a list of ContentParts: | Part | Who sends it | What it is | |---|---|---| | Instruction | system | text built from &'static str pieces and typed values | | UserText | user | what the user typed | | Data (LabelledData) | user side | a value a tool read, labelled with its DataSource (tool, model, record ids) | | ToolResult | user side | the answer to one tool call, tied to it by id, holding LabelledData | | ToolCall | assistant | a call as the model produced it: id, name and arguments, kept as received | | AssistantText | assistant | the model's own prose, resent with the history (any String) | TurnMessage::new refuses a part its role may not carry and an empty message. ToolTurnRequest::new refuses two tools with one name, a repeated tool call id, a tool result for a call no earlier assistant message made, and a second result for one call. A provider answer is a ToolTurnResponse with assistant parts only, and finish_reason is FinishReason::ToolUse when the model waits for tool results. Instruction has no conversion from a runtime String, no parsing, no deserialization and no default; LabelledData has none from any string, and its only constructor is LabelledData::new(source, value). Compile-fail cases and a compile-time probe pin this (SPEC-AIA-001, partial). The types do not close every path. Three are review rules for ai_base: - A leaked String (String::leak) is a &'static str and passes Instruction::from_static. Only string literals go there. - Any crate can call LabelledData::new. Only the tool executor builds it. - ContentPart::AssistantText holds any String. Only provider responses supply assistant parts. use erp_sdk::ai::{DataSource, Instruction, LabelledData, ToolName}; let instruction = Instruction::from_static("You answer questions about ") .then_integer(3) .then_static(" records; read only: ") .then_flag(true); assert_eq!(instruction.render(), "You answer questions about 3 records; read only: true"); let source = DataSource::new(ToolName::new("search_read")?, Some("res.partner".to_owned()), vec![7, 9])?; let data = LabelledData::new(source, serde_json::json!({"name": "Azure Interior"})); assert_eq!(data.source().ids(), &[7, 9]);

| Value | Rule | |---|---| | ToolName | 1 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - (the common subset of the hosted providers' rules) | | ToolSpec description | not blank, at most 1,024 characters | | ToolSpec input schema | a JSON object whose top-level "type" is "object" | | ToolCallId | 1 to 256 bytes, no control or Unicode format (Cf) characters | | ToolCall name | at most 256 bytes; it need not be a valid ToolName, so the executor can answer "unknown tool" | | DataSource model | not empty when present | Each refusal is a ToolTypeError variant naming the value or position. An adapter that cannot represent a provider's answer (an empty id, an oversized name) returns ProviderError::InvalidResponse, never a guessed value.

Implement ModelProvider first, then ToolModelProvider::complete_turn. For the configured Anthropic Messages or OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions route, create one encoder with ConfiguredRoute::request_encoder() at the start of the assistant turn and reuse it for each encode(&request). It uses the route's exact provider family and model. It builds a JSON body without credentials, and returns ProviderError::InvalidRequest for histories or options it cannot represent. Instruction renders in the system channel. A ToolResult carries its call ID and labelled JSON in the provider's tool-result block or tool-role message. Unpaired LabelledData uses a separate user-role text block with a random per-turn delimiter since it has no call ID. Tool results must immediately follow their assistant call batch, before additional user text. Anthropic requires a positive max_tokens and leading instructions. OpenAI-compatible schemas must already describe closed objects with all properties required. Declare optional inputs as required nullable values. The encoder preserves schema semantics and refuses unsupported keywords. The route applies ai.max_request_bytes before building the JSON and checks the final compact body size. Both providers share the same structural entry and nesting limits. Call decode_response(&body) on the same encoder with the complete JSON body from a successful non-streaming exchange. The decoder preserves assistant text and tool calls as typed parts. It retains the returned model and validated token counts for metering. Unsupported provider blocks, malformed JSON, inconsistent tool finish reasons and unusable usage records return ProviderError::InvalidResponse without echoing the response. Duplicate tool argument keys are detected directly from the response JSON before conversion to SDK values. JSON bodies are capped at 1 MiB. A transport must separately enforce its read limit before buffering any response. Provider transport, retry and streaming belong to the provider transport implementation. A decoded tool call still needs normal executor validation, access checks and any required user confirmation.

erp_testkit::ai::ScriptedModelProvider answers each tool turn with the next queued reply and records every request: use erp_sdk::ai::ToolModelProvider; use erp_testkit::ai::{ScriptedModelProvider, ScriptedReply}; let provider = ScriptedModelProvider::new("scripted-llm"); provider.push_reply(ScriptedReply::tool_call("call_01", "search_read", serde_json::json!({"model": "res.partner"}))?); provider.push_reply(ScriptedReply::text("There are 5 customers.")?); // provider.complete_turn(&request).await? returns the replies in order; // provider.recorded_requests() returns the requests it received. push_error queues a ProviderError. When the script runs out, complete_turn returns ProviderError::Backend naming the call number, never a default answer. Text-only requests (complete, stream, count_tokens) behave like MockModelProvider, which echoes the prompt. The scripted name and arguments are kept as given, so a test can script a call to a tool that does not exist. The round trip is tested in crates/erp-testkit/tests/ai_tools.rs (SPEC-AIA-002). The native ai_base addon can now send a typed non-streaming turn to a node-bound Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The configured route controls the provider and allowed model. See [native HTTP exchange and limits](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/ai-configuration.md#sending-a-non-streaming-turn-from-native-code).

Status: stages A and B (ADR 0039, ADR 0151). Optional chain seals, retention and the audit reader are separate planned work; there is no audit screen yet. ADR 0167 specifies the reader and additive read policy. The typed reader engine, database authority and successful-read selection are in place. Dedicated serving APIs remain pending. Odoo Community has no framework audit trail; this is ERPForAll's own design.

| What happened | Row | When it is written | |---|---|---| | A JSON-2 call that changes data commits | one change row | in the same transaction, by one INSERT before COMMIT | | That call is denied, fails, ends with an unknown COMMIT, or is a replay of an idempotent call | one attempt row | on its own connection after the call ended | | An unselected read by a user | nothing | no audit statement | | A successful read selected by model, elevation or operator policy | one read_ok attempt | independently, before releasing the buffered result | | A server action flagged run_as_superuser runs | an elevation entry in the transaction's row | before the elevated body runs | A bulk call over a thousand records is still one row. A call retried after a serialization failure writes only the row of the attempt that ends the call, with its attempt number. If the audit row cannot be written, the change is rolled back and the caller gets 503 erp.audit_unavailable: audit is never skipped. A row holds who acted (principal kind, subject, the key that was used as an id, the delegating user), the model, the method and its effect, the ids the call named (consecutive ids as ranges), a SHA-256 digest of the redacted arguments, the correlation and operation ids, the company set, the policy generations, the outcome and a bounded error class. It never holds a key, key name, password, hash, token, cookie, login, address or error message. Record values are digested after redaction (redaction version 2): a field marked secret (#[field(char, secret = true)], or FieldDecl::secret(true)), restricted fields, binary and image fields and unknown fields are replaced by their reason, for example {"$redacted":"secret"}, before anything is hashed, so the digest of two different passwords is the same. A method that takes no record values contributes only the names of its arguments. Mark every field that holds a password or another credential secret: the base addon marks res.users.password and the password wizards' fields. The marker also applies inside x2many create and update commands (triples, and a plain list of value maps), because each nested record is redacted with its own model's declarations; a shape the redaction does not recognise, or a many2one given a list or map, is replaced whole by {"$redacted":"unparsed"}. An extension cannot switch secret off once an addon set it (the registry refuses with a programming error naming the field), a related field whose path ends at a secret field is secret too, and ir.config_parameter.value is marked secret. A field that is not marked keeps its value in the digest, so a reader of the rows can still confirm a guess about a low-entropy value there (a PIN, a phone number); the digest is evidence that a call happened, not a place to hide such data. Fields declared at runtime (ir.model.fields custom fields) cannot be marked secret yet.

Authentication code records a lifecycle change in the transaction that makes it. The event is written with the change or not at all, and is dropped if a savepoint around it rolls back: use erp_sdk::audit::{ApiKeyRevoked, AuthEvent, KeyRouteScope, RevokeCause}; use erp_sdk::{ApiKeyId, KeyKind, Transaction, UserId}; fn revoke_recorded(tx: &mut Transaction) -> erp_sdk::Result<()> { let event = ApiKeyRevoked::new( ApiKeyId::new(91).map_err(erp_sdk::Error::from)?, UserId::new(7).map_err(erp_sdk::Error::from)?, KeyKind::User, KeyRouteScope::Rpc, RevokeCause::Owner, ); tx.audit_auth(AuthEvent::ApiKeyRevoked(event)) } audit_auth refuses before any statement when the audit store is not ready, in a read-only transaction and after the commit preamble froze the buffer. When the audit store is unavailable the revocation fails too: revocation is atomic with its audit row. The one exception is the operator's emergency revocation on the owner connection, described below.

erp auth emergency-revoke ([cli.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/cli.md#auth-emergency-revoke)) ends API keys and sessions on the owner connection when the runtime role cannot write audit rows. It still writes its own row in the same transaction, with origin cli and the core System principal.
