Every field has name and type. type is one of boolean, integer, float, monetary, char, text, html, selection, date, datetime, json, many2one, one2many, many2many. | Key | Types | Meaning | |---|---|---| | string, help, required, readonly, store, copy, groups | all | as in Odoo | | index | all | true, false, or "btree", "btree_not_null", "trigram" | | default | all | a static value that fits the type: boolean for boolean, integer for integer, number for float/monetary (finite), string for char/text/html/selection/date/datetime; relational and json fields take none. false fits every type: on a field that is not boolean it is Odoo's "no value" (default=False) | | related | all | a related path; the only computed field allowed here | | size | char | at least 1 (leave it out for no limit; Odoo reads size=0 as no limit) | | digits | float | [precision, scale], scale at most 1000 | | currency_field | monetary | | | selection, selection_add | selection | [[value, label], …]; selection_add also takes [value] to position an existing value | | comodel | relational | required | | inverse | one2many | required | | relation, column1, column2 | many2many | all three or none | | ondelete | many2one, many2many, selection | many2one/many2many: "set null", "restrict", "cascade"; selection: "set null", "cascade", "set default", "set <val>" | | domain, context, check_company | relational | domain in JSON list syntax, context a JSON object |

- Field names are free: TOML fields are declared fields, so they need no x_ prefix. - Unknown keys, values of the wrong type and keys that do not apply to the field type are errors naming the file and line, e.g. Model file 'models/test.toml:7': unknown field widget, expected one of name, …. - compute and depends are refused: in a model file a computed field is related. reference and many2one_reference fields belong in a native addon. - Files are read in file-name order (prefix them 10_, 20_ to control it); inside an addon, declarations apply in file, then line order. - Only regular *.toml files may sit in models/; anything else (other files, directories, symlinks) is an error. - Limits: 1 MiB per file, 256 files and 16 MiB per addon, 1000 models per file and 10 000 per addon, 1600 fields per model, 64 parents, 4096 selection entries, names up to 128 bytes, texts up to 16 KiB. Files must be UTF-8.

use erp_modules::{addon_descriptor, read_manifest_from_dir, read_model_files, ModuleName}; use erp_registry::{Overlay, RegistryBuilder}; let name = ModuleName::new("test_data_only")?; let manifest = read_manifest_from_dir(&dir, &name)?.expect("manifest.toml"); let addon = addon_descriptor(&manifest)?;           // &'static AddonDescriptor let mut overlay = Overlay::new(); overlay.add_addon_defs(read_model_files(&dir, &name)?)?; let registry = RegistryBuilder::new([addon]).overlay(&overlay).build()?;

Custom models and fields (Odoo's ir.model and ir.model.fields with state = 'manual') belong to one database. They are applied through an Overlay, after every addon: use erp_registry::{FieldDef, KindDef, ManualModel, Overlay}; let mut overlay = Overlay::new(); overlay.add_manual_model(ManualModel::new("x_bananas").description("Bananas"))?; overlay.add_manual_field("x_bananas", FieldDef::new("x_name", KindDef::Char { size: None }).string("Name"))?; overlay.add_manual_field("res.partner", FieldDef::new("x_foo", KindDef::Char { size: None }))?; - Names follow Odoo's rules, checked when added: models start with x_ and use [a-z0-9_.]; fields start with x_ and are PostgreSQL names of at most 63 bytes; each model and each (model, field) pair is unique. The messages are Odoo's (The model name must start with 'x_'., Custom fields must have a name that starts with 'x_'!, …) followed by what was refused. - A custom field on a delegation parent (_inherits) shows up on every child, at any depth, with its column only on the parent. - A custom model whose only name field is x_name uses it as _rec_name (its display_name); an x_active field archives its records. - Custom fields only add: one may not redefine a field an addon declares. A custom model needs a table of its own (x_a.b and x_a_b cannot both exist). - A static default must fit the field type, as in model files. - A required custom field needs a default when its model's table already has rows (or, when an optional field becomes required, while its column holds empty values). Without one the schema update stops with `cannot update the schema: required field 'test_rel.unit.x_code' has no default and table "test_rel_unit" has rows; …` and nothing changes. Odoo only logs a warning there. - A custom field on a model that does not exist, or pointing at a comodel that does not exist, makes the registry build fail with the model or field named, unless the database is loaded with ManualFieldPolicy::DropBroken (next section). - A custom related field is checked when the registry is built: every step of the path must exist (fields of _inherits parents included), the steps before the last must be many2one, one2many or many2many fields, and the target must have the field's type (`Type of related field res.partner.x_name_len (integer) is inconsistent with res.partner.name (char)`).

Custom fields live in the database, addons change under them. After an upgrade a custom field can be broken: a newer addon version declares a field with the same name, the model the field extends is gone, its comodel is gone, or its related path no longer resolves. By default (Strict) the registry build fails, naming the field. A server loading a database after an upgrade can choose to leave such fields out instead, as Odoo does, and gets them back as a typed report: use erp_registry::{Databases, DropReason, ManualFieldPolicy, RegistryCache}; let dbs = Databases::new(RegistryCache::new()); let registry = dbs.load_with("db_a", &addons, overlay, ManualFieldPolicy::DropBroken)?; for dropped in registry.dropped_fields() { // e.g. res.partner.x_code: DeclaredByAddon { addons: ["sale"] } report(dropped.model(), dropped.field(), dropped.reason(), dropped.error()); } - Only custom fields are dropped, and only for a reason of their own (DropReason): DeclaredByAddon (the addon field wins, as in Odoo), UnknownModel, UnknownComodel, Related (path or type), Refused (any other check of that field: one2many inverse, many2one or many2many rules, parameters such as a monetary field without a currency field). error() is the error a strict build gives for that field. - Fields that depend on a dropped one go too: a related field through a dropped many2one, a one2many whose inverse was dropped, the inherited copies on _inherits children. - Everything else still fails the build: addon declarations, custom models, the same custom field declared twice (in two overlays, or on a model and on a model inheriting it under a new name), broken or not, and quotas (ResourceExhausted). - Nothing is logged instead of reported: read dropped_fields() and show it (health check, admin notice). The columns of dropped fields are never deleted: they stay in the database, with their data, until the field is fixed or deleted by an administrator. - The policy is kept for the database: set_overlay builds with it too, so a database with a broken field can still change its other custom fields. Only the fields dropped already carry over: an overlay change that would drop any other custom field (a new broken field, or a field the change breaks, e.g. by removing its comodel) is refused with that field's strict error, before the schema is touched: // db loaded with DropBroken; res.users.x_old_tag_id is dropped already let mut changed = dbs.overlay("db_a").expect("loaded"); changed.add_manual_field("res.users", FieldDef::new("x_new_id", KindDef::Many2one { comodel: "x_new_nowhere".into(), ondelete: None, }))?; let err = dbs.set_overlay("db_a", changed, sync).await.unwrap_err(); assert_eq!(err.message(), "Field res.users.x_new_id refers to unknown model 'x_new_nowhere'"); - RegistryBuilder::manual_fields(ManualFieldPolicy::DropBroken) does the same for a registry built directly (tests, tools).

RegistryCache shares one immutable registry between databases with the same installed addons (names and dependencies) and the same overlay; Databases keeps the registry of each database. Another database never sees your custom fields. use erp_orm::{Orm, StaticPolicy}; use erp_registry::{Databases, Overlay, RegistryCache}; let dbs = Databases::new(RegistryCache::new()); let a = dbs.load("db_a", &addons, Overlay::new())?;   // server start: schema already matches let b = dbs.load("db_b", &addons, Overlay::new())?;   // same Arc as a // custom fields changed: sync the schema with the new registry, then swap let a2 = dbs .set_overlay("db_a", overlay, |registry| async move { let orm = Orm::builder(registry, pool).policy(policy).build()?; let report = orm.sync_schema().await?;        // committed before it returns show(report.kept_comments());                 // usually empty, see SchemaStepReport Ok(()) }) .await?;                                          // on any error db_a keeps a dbs.cache().drop_unused();                            // free registries nobody holds - set_overlay is the only way to install a changed overlay: the new columns exist before any request sees the registry that uses them. load on a loaded database with a different overlay is refused (`database 'db_a' is loaded with another overlay; change it with Databases::set_overlay, …). One set_overlay` runs at a time per database: a second call while one is applying is refused before it builds anything (`an overlay is being applied to database 'db_a' already; wait for it to finish and apply this one again, kind Concurrency). If a load` replaced the registry while yours synchronized the schema, yours fails with a Concurrency error too (the schema was already changed): apply your overlay again. - set_overlay is not cancel-safe: run it in its own spawned task (tokio::spawn), never inside a request future that a client disconnect or timeout can drop. Between the committed schema change and the swap, requests still on the old registry can fail; M3 makes the swap live across workers. - Registries come only through Databases, which charges each database's own intern quota. - Databases::set_overlay is async and not cancel-safe: run it in its own tokio::spawned task, never inside a request future that can be dropped. Composing a registry is CPU work, so build the overlay value itself (and call the synchronous Databases::load) from tokio::task::spawn_blocking, not on a runtime worker thread. - Schema updates run with lock_timeout at most 10 s and statement_timeout at most 5 min (each statement), set before the update waits for anything (a transaction's lower values are kept, e.g. a module operation's): a busy table, or another schema update of the same database running longer than the lock timeout (`another schema synchronization of this database is running; gave up waiting for it after 10s …, kind Lock`; the message names the value in force), makes the update fail instead of blocking every request behind it. Try again later. If the commit itself fails because the connection dropped, the outcome is unknown: run the update again. Runtime definitions are interned for the life of the process (ADR 0026 §2): editing custom fields many times grows memory a little each time (one chunk of at most 32 fields per edit). Each database has its own quota (InternAccount, 32 MiB by default, Databases::set_account lowers it before the first load); a refused change charges nothing. A database over it gets `the runtime model declarations of this database use more than … bytes (its intern quota); … (kind ResourceExhausted`) while other databases are unaffected. The process intern budget bounds the whole process: INTERN_BUDGET_BYTES (256 MiB) by default, room for 8 databases at their full quota. A server with more databases raises it at start: // each database's full quota on top of the default, for 40 databases erp_registry::set_intern_budget(erp_registry::intern_budget_for(40)?)?; Over the budget, a definition is refused with `runtime model declarations use more than … bytes in this process (its intern budget); … (kind ResourceExhausted`). Overlay equality depends on order (it is the field order): load custom models and fields in ir.model/ir.model.fields id order so equal databases share a registry.

Status: data parsing and loading are complete (crates/erp-data, crates/erp-modules). The loader turns your XML and CSV data files into transactional operations, assigns external IDs (ir.model.data), enforces noupdate and forcecreate semantics, executes <function> calls and <delete> statements, registers views and templates, and automatically cleans up obsolete records on module upgrade and uninstallation. ERP data files retain Odoo input compatibility: an addon written for Odoo reads the same way, with the stricter checks below (ADR 0019). Every rule here is enforced when the file is read, before anything reaches the database.

Per project rules (AGENTS.md "Default data for every model"), every model defined by a base addon (including uom) ships default records like Odoo in its data files (data/*.xml or data/*.csv), with an install test confirming the records exist after erp module install. Default data files are marked with noupdate="1" in XML files (<erp noupdate="1">) or # noupdate: 1 as the first line of CSV files so that tenant modifications are preserved across module upgrades without creating duplicate rows or resetting operator changes.

The canonical root is ; legacy , and roots remain accepted input aliases. Containers nest and take noupdate, auto_sequence, uid and context. Inside: record, template, asset, menuitem, delete, function. VIP 3 What the reader checks, beyond well-formed XML: - **Allowed elements and attributes only**, per element, as in Odoo's import_xml.rng. A typo (, modle=) stops the file with "does not fit the required schema" and the line. - **One value source per field**: ref, eval or search, or a type with text or file. model goes with eval/search, use with search. Text next to eval is refused. - **File values**: type="bytes" file="path" (binary, preferred; type="base64" still read), type="file" with the path as text (stored as module,path), file="path" without type (the file's text). - **Markup**: put view architectures in type="xml" and HTML in type="html"; markup in a field without a type is refused (it would lose its structure). HTML void elements (
, ) must be empty. - **Booleans** (noupdate, forcecreate, menu active, …): 1/0, true/false, yes/no, on/off in any case. On

The file name gives the model (ir.model.access.csv, res.partner-extra.csv → res.partner). The first line holds the field paths for load() (id, name, group_id:id, model_id/id, …), kept exactly as written. Columns with @ (translations) are skipped, as are rows whose cells are all empty. An empty or repeated header, a row with a different number of cells, or an invalid external ID in the id column stops the file with its line. On upgrade, a file without an id column is skipped with a reason.

Errors name the file, the line and what is wrong, for example: The XML file 'my_addon/data/tags.xml' does not fit the required schema! my_addon/data/tags.xml:12: unknown attribute 'modle' on <record>; allowed: id, model, forcecreate, uid, context Value errors also show the operation they occurred in (up to 2 KiB of it): while parsing my_addon/data/tags.xml:14, somewhere inside <record id="tag_vip" model="res.partner.category">…</record> invalid integer 'three' in <field>: invalid digit found in string

The module system loads the files of data (and, for modules with demo data, demo) in the operation's transaction, through the default ErpDataLoader. An error anywhere rolls the whole operation back. **File kinds** (by extension, case-insensitive): .xml and .csv are loaded; .sql is run as written (one round trip, development-folder addons only; a COMMIT in it fails the operation); .js is listed and ignored (not even read); anything else fails with `can't load unknown file type … (expected .xml, .csv, .sql or .js)`. A file listed twice in one list loads twice. **Modes.** Install and reinit load in init mode (every record is written); an upgrade loads in update mode, which leaves records under noupdate alone: - A record under noupdate (its <data noupdate="1"> or <erp noupdate="1">) that already exists is not written, and neither are the <record id=…> sub-records inside it; their external ids still count as loaded. A noupdate record without an id is skipped. A noupdate record the user deleted is created again (its external id is re-pointed), unless it says forcecreate="0". - The noupdate flag of an external id is fixed when the id is created; loading never changes it. - An external id of another module (<record id="other.x">) updates that module's record; the module must be part of the install step (The ID "other.x" refers to an uninstalled module), and the record must exist (Cannot update missing record 'other.x') unless the record says forcecreate="1". - A ref="x" that does not resolve fails the load (External ID not found in the system: m.x); on a record with forcecreate="0" the record is skipped instead and the skip is returned as a notice. - <field name="lines"><record …/></field> on a one2many field creates the parent first, then each sub-record with the inverse field set, depth first. - auto_sequence="1" on <erp> or <data> numbers the records of a model with a sequence field that give none: 10, 20, 30, … within one top-level record and the sub-records nested in it, restarting for the next top-level record (as Odoo does); a skipped record does not take a number. - At the end of an operation the records of the updated modules whose external ids the data no longer names are deleted (a record that another external id still names only loses this one; noupdate ids and the schema records of the module system are never touched). Consecutive records of one model are written together: a file of 1,000 records costs a handful of statements, not thousands. A failure of such a write is reported at the first record of the batch and says how many records were written together. **<record>.** Fields convert by the field's type: text to integer, float, boolean (0, false, off are false) and many2one ids; ref="x" gives the id of an external id (the model and id, model,id, for a reference field); eval runs the expression language (ref(), Command, dates, version). The record gets an ir.model.data row module.id (flag noupdate from the enclosing <data noupdate>), and a field named xmlid is filled with it unless the file sets it. uid="ref" runs the record as that user; the context of enclosing elements and of the record are evaluated outer to inner and merged key by key, and data files never carry lang. **Value forms.** Besides text, ref= and eval, a <field> takes: search="[domain]" (with model="…", or the comodel of a relational field; use="field" picks the value read from the match): the first match for a many2one or plain field, every match for a many2many (as Command.set), False when nothing matches; type="file" (stores module,path after checking the file exists in the addon); file="module/path" (text), type="bytes" file="…" and the deprecated type="base64" file="…" (base64 text, plus a DeprecatedBase64 notice); type="list" / "tuple" of <value> elements (a None inside stays null); and type="xml" / "html", where %(xid)d and %(xid)s are replaced by the record id and %% is a literal %. A search= on a plain field without model fails with Odoo's text Define an attribute model="..." in your .XML file!. A context that sets lang fails until translations exist. **Menus and templates.** <menuitem> writes ir.ui.menu records (parent from the enclosing menu or the parent attribute, sequence, web_icon on top-level menus, action as model,id, the name from the action when the menu has none, groups="a,-b" as link and unlink); a menu tree costs a fixed number of statements per tree level. <template> writes an ir.ui.view record (a theme.ir.ui.view record in a module named theme_*); a root active= is applied on install or for a view that does not exist yet and never on an upgrade of an existing view. Both need the real models (ir.ui.menu, ir.ui.view), which the base addon provides: a module that does not depend on base fails loading with an error that names the missing model and says to add base to depends. **Demo data.** A module gets demo data only when every module it depends on has it. All demo files of a module load inside one savepoint; if one fails on its data (a parse error, a refused value, a missing reference), the savepoint rolls back, the module installs with demo = false, and the failure is returned in OperationOutcome::data_notices as DemoFailed (and written to ir.demo_failure when that model exists). Failures of the database itself still fail the install. An administrator can load demo data into a database created without it: see [Load demo data](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/load-demo-data.md). **Notices.** Things Odoo only logs are returned in OperationOutcome::data_notices: a file listed twice (RepeatedFile), a .js file (IgnoredFile), a CSV file skipped because an upgrade found no id column (SkippedFile), a record skipped for an unresolved ref with forcecreate="0" (SkippedUnresolvedRef), a failed demo (DemoFailed). let outcome = system.button_immediate_install(&caller, &[module]).await?; for notice in &outcome.data_notices { eprintln!("{notice}"); } <function>, <delete> and CSV files, and #[data_callable]: [Calling methods and deleting from data files](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/data-functions.md). ModuleSystem::reinit(&caller, &[module]) reloads the data of installed modules (and their installed dependents) in init mode without running migrations.

docs.title: Calling methods and deleting from data files (<function>, <delete>, CSV)

sections.text: Status: loading is in place. The reader checks the files (see [Data files](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/data-files.md)); this page is about what the loader does with <function>, <delete> and CSV files, and how a method opts in to being called from a data file.

Odoo lets a <function> call any attribute of a model. ERPForAll lets it call only methods that say so (ADR 0009 §8): a method is **data-callable** when it carries #[data_callable] or #[rpc(effect = …)] (every RPC method is data-callable). Nothing else can be reached from a data file, so an addon that is only read cannot call a private helper that skips an access check.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;
pub struct Book { #[field(char, required)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(integer)] pub copies: i32, }

impl Book { /// Called as <function model="library.book" name="restock"><value eval="[ref('book_a')]"/>…. /// A records method: the first argument of the <function> is the ids. #[method] #[data_callable] async fn restock(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, count: i64) -> Result<bool> { for book in this.iter() { let copies = i64::from(book.get(tx, Book::COPIES).await?); let total = i32::try_from(copies + count) .map_err(|_| Error::validation("too many copies"))?; book.set(tx, Book::COPIES, total).await?; } Ok(true) } /// A model method (Odoo's @api.model): no ids. #[method] #[data_callable(model)] async fn seed(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, name: String) -> Result<RecordSet<Book>> { this.create(tx, vec![this.vals().set(Book::NAME, name.as_str())]).await } /// Private by name, still callable from data (Odoo calls such methods from data files too); /// the _ prefix keeps it out of RPC, which needs #[rpc]. #[method] #[data_callable(model)] async fn _migrate(_this: &RecordSet<Book>, _tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<bool> { Ok(true) } /// Not declared: a <function> naming it fails the load. #[method] async fn recount(_this: &RecordSet<Book>, _tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<bool> { Ok(true) } }

#[data_callable] takes model for a model method, like #[rpc]. It has no effect class: a <function> runs inside the module operation's transaction, and effects belong to the RPC transport. A method may carry #[rpc(hide)] and #[data_callable] together; #[rpc(hide)] only removes RPC. A method with #[rpc(effect = …)] must not also carry #[data_callable] (it already is). A chain of overrides is data-callable when any implementation along it declares the level; the oldest declaration's parameter table and binder are used, as for RPC.
Both #[rpc(effect = …)] and #[data_callable] on one method:
impl Book { #[method] #[rpc(effect = read)] #[data_callable] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }
An unknown parameter, or a reserved parameter name (ids and context are keys of the call):
impl Book { #[method] #[data_callable(records)] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }
impl Book { #[method] #[data_callable] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, context: i64) -> Result<i64> { Ok(context) } }

<function model="library.book" name="seed" eval="['Dune']"/> <function model="library.book" name="restock"> <value eval="[ref('book_a'), ref('book_b')]"/>   <!-- the ids --> <value type="int">5</value>                       <!-- count --> </function> <function model="library.book" name="restock" uid="base.user_admin" context="{'tracking_disable': True}"> <value eval="ref('book_a')"/> <value name="count" eval="3"/> <value name="context" eval="{'lang': 'fr_FR'}"/>  <!-- merged into the call's context --> </function> - Positional arguments come from eval (a list or tuple) or from the <value> and nested <function> children in order; <value name="…"> gives a keyword. eval and children cannot be mixed (the reader refuses it, as Odoo's schema does). - They bind to the method's parameters in declaration order, keywords by name, with the typed conversion of RPC arguments (an i64 parameter takes an integer, not "5"). Failures are load errors: takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given, got an unexpected keyword argument 'x', got multiple values for argument 'x', missing a required argument: 'x', argument 'count': expected an integer, got string. - A records method takes the ids first: a list (falsy ids dropped), or one id. A model method takes none. - A nested <function> runs first and its result is the argument; a recordset result is its ids. - uid and context on the <function> (or an enclosing element) set the acting user and the context, as for <record>. A context keyword is merged into that context and is not passed on. - A method's own error stops the load with its kind (a Validation error stays one). - Under noupdate (the element or an enclosing <data noupdate="1">) a <function> runs on install and is skipped on upgrade. Method names with __ are refused by the reader.

<delete model="library.book" id="book_old"/> <delete model="library.book" search="[('copies', '=', 0)]"/> It runs in every mode, also under noupdate. The records are the search result, or the record of the external id, in one unlink. An id that does not exist, or whose record is already gone, is not an error: the load goes on and returns a DeleteTargetMissing notice in OperationOutcome::data_notices. Two differences from Odoo, both toward failing loudly (ADR 0018): a search that does not evaluate or does not run fails the load (Odoo logs a warning and deletes only the id target), and an id that belongs to a record of another model than model is refused (Odoo would unlink whichever record of model has that number).

A CSV file is loaded through the importer (load() with the id column), so a row with an existing external id updates its record and a new one creates it. The model is the file name up to the first - (res.partner-extra.csv loads into res.partner). The context carries mode (init or update), module, noupdate and the install_* keys, and never lang. If any message of the importer is an error, the install stops with all the messages: Module loading library failed: file data/library.book.csv could not be processed: No matching record found for external id 'nope' in field 'Author' On upgrade, a file without an id column is not loaded (it could only create duplicates): the operation goes on and returns a SkippedFile notice with the reason. One2many lines declaring their own external ids (field/id) are lifted to their own ir.model.data entries in the same load session; subsequent imports update the existing child records.

docs.title: A data-only addon: no Rust, no compilation

sections.text: Prompt-authored customization is planned and is not available through a runtime API yet. Its output uses the same data-only declarations as a manually authored addon: stable external IDs, dependencies, inherited views and admitted safe action recipes. Base addon files are not edited. Immutable customization releases add preview, explicit confirmation, checked activation, export and reversal; adding reflection rows alone does not activate a supported custom field. The proposed contract is ADR 0224, extending ADR 0033. A custom selection value does not implement a business transition. Domain addons must expose a validated transition/policy capability before conversation can configure it. Custom action bodies retain the normal safe runtime and current-user access rules; no generated native code or arbitrary SQL is admitted in such a release. A generated release also carries no install hooks, no SQL migrations and no migration text written by the model; its only migrations are the ones the customization compiler emits and shows in the diff. A behaviour that needs code beyond that is planned as a generated WebAssembly package, built, signed and installed through the package lifecycle (proposed ADR 0229).

Status: addons/sample_library is the worked example and is covered by crates/erp-cli/tests/sample_library.rs (install, use through the ORM, upgrade with a schema change, uninstall, demo data, a broken model file) and, for the browser Addons screen, by crates/erp-cli/tests/human_data_only_install.rs. A data-only addon is a folder with a manifest, model declarations in TOML and data files in XML or CSV. It has no Cargo.toml and no src/, so there is nothing to compile: put the folder in an addons path and install it (ADR 0009 §1). addons/sample_library/ manifest.toml models/10_author.toml  15_genre.toml  20_book.toml  30_loan.toml security/ir.access.csv views/sample_library_views.xml demo/sample_library_demo.xml

name = "Sample Library" summary = "Books, authors and loans: a sample addon with no Rust code and no compilation" version = "1.0.0" license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0" author = "ERPForAll" category = "Sample" application = true depends = ["base"] data = ["security/ir.access.csv", "views/sample_library_views.xml"] demo = ["demo/sample_library_demo.xml"] The module name is the folder name. data files load in the order listed (access rows first, then views, actions and menus); demo files load only when the database was created with demo data. Unknown keys are refused.

Files are read in file-name order (hence the 10_, 20_ prefixes: book points at author). One file can hold several [[model]] tables. A new model and its fields: [[model]] name = "sample_library.book" description = "Library Book" order = "title, id" rec_name = "title" [[model.field]] name = "title" type = "char" required = true [[model.field]] name = "author_id" type = "many2one" comodel = "sample_library.author" ondelete = "restrict" [[model.field]] name = "available" type = "boolean" default = true To add fields to a model of another addon, write extend = "res.partner" instead of name, as the fixture crates/erp-modules/tests/fixtures/test_data_only/models/20_users.toml does. A selection field takes selection = [["draft", "Draft"], ["out", "On Loan"]]. A one2many needs comodel and inverse (an author's book_ids, a book's loan_ids); a many2many needs comodel and may name its table with relation, column1 and column2 (a book's genre_ids uses the default sample_library_book_sample_library_genre_rel). In a form, a one2many shows its lines as a list taken from the comodel's own list view and edits a line in a dialog built from the comodel's form view; the inverse field is set from the parent and not shown. A many2many shows tags. The tables and columns are created at install and altered at upgrade. A mistake in a file stops the install with the file name and line, and nothing is changed. A model file cannot declare SQL objects: sql_function, sql_trigger, sql_condition, sql_grant and persistence, on a model or at the top of the file, are refused with an error saying that the SQL object key is native-only for now. Database functions, triggers and grants are declared by native (Rust) addons only (proposed ADR 0166, SPEC-ORMX-039).

These are ordinary data files, exactly as in a native addon (data-files.md, views.md, actions-menus.md, access.md): ir.ui.view records with list and form architectures, ir.actions.act_window records, and menuitem elements. Access is a CSV of ir.access rows; the sample gives every internal user (base.group_user) full rights on its four models. Without a row nobody but the superuser can read or write a model.

For a database that already exists, with the addons folder on the path: export DATABASE_URL="postgres://erp@db.internal/postgres" erp module install -d mydb sample_library --addons-path ./addons (cli.md). The install operation registers an addon that was copied into the folder after the database was created; no separate refresh is needed (tested). The erp module command line itself was not run against sample_library in the slice that added the sample; the module-system calls it makes were. **Browser Addons screen.** A system administrator can install the addon from the Addons screen (POST /web/module/install with {"modules":["sample_library"]}; the request carries names only). The server offers the data-only addons found in its configured addons directory (the one in server.toml, addons_path; the human release copies addons/ there), so a new folder shows up without rebuilding the binary. ADR 0066, "D3 amendment (2026-10-27)". A folder may hold only manifest.toml, models/*.toml, .xml and .csv files under views/, data/, demo/ and security/, and README* text files. An addon with anything else (a .sql file, migrations/, static/, a Rust crate, a symlink, another file kind, or a manifest data/demo path outside the folder or not .xml/.csv) is **not offered** and is refused. The server logs the path and the rule on standard error; check the log when an addon you expected is missing from the list. A broken manifest.toml anywhere in the directory makes the catalogue fail with an error rather than list partially.

A data-only addon can declare models, extend models, ship views, menus, access rows, data and demo, related fields, Luau formulas and Luau hooks. It cannot: - add Rust methods, overrides with super, #[rpc] endpoints, constraints written in code or computed fields beyond related/Luau formulas: use a native addon today, or the WASM track (M2b) once it lands; - add client-side widgets or JavaScript/TypeScript code: those need an addon with a client build (see human-client-extensions.md). Starting from a native addon later is mechanical: the same models/, views/ and security/ folders are kept and a Cargo.toml plus src/ is added.

Sample Library 1.0.4 adds fields so that most shipped field widgets appear in its views: a book's summary (text), website, cover_color (char), color (integer), rating and book_format (selection), member_discount (float) and favorite (boolean), and an author's email and phone. The widgets are chosen in the views with widget="…", as in Odoo; the model files only declare plain fields. The upgrade adds the columns and keeps existing rows; demo values for the new fields come only with a fresh install of the demo data. The list of widgets and where they appear is in the user guide page "Editing fields and field widgets", section "Where to try the widgets". Not yet shown in the samples: password, boolean_checkbox, boolean_icon, label_selection, badges_selection, filterable_selection, many2many_tags_avatar, many2many_tags_color_dot, daterange, code and monetary.

Sample Library 1.0.2 displays its existing editable loan state selection in the header using widget="statusbar". Its model choices, required flag, default draft, access rows and optional demo records remain unchanged. The widget is part of web; this sample still has no compiled client or Rust code. State edits use normal Save/Discard. When sample_library_wasm is installed, upgrade it to 1.3.5 in the same maintenance/release train as Sample Library 1.0.2. The newer package adds its loan buttons inside the base header; older versions create another header and their combined view is refused. Copying the new source alone does not update a database's installed views or stored WASM package. Rehearse both installed addon upgrades, including any sample_library_wasm_policy, before opening the new client for human testing. No new record data or approvals are installed by this presentation change.

addons/contacts is a data-only application that adds no model. It shows the usual split between an addon that owns a model's views and an addon that offers the way to reach them: - base owns the res.partner and res.partner.category views (addons/base/data/partner_views.xml: base.partner_list, partner_form, partner_search, partner_category_list, partner_category_form). Every addon that opens a contact from a relational field gets these as the default views. - contacts (depends = ["base"]) declares two window actions (contacts.action_contacts, contacts.action_contact_tags) that name those views with ir.actions.act_window.view records, and a top-level menu with web_icon="lucide:contact" whose Configuration branch is limited to base.group_system. Views are referenced across addons by their external id (ref="base.partner_list"). - Demo contacts (demo/contacts_demo.xml: two companies with child contacts, two tags) load only with demo data. The addon defines no model, so it has no further default records. To add a field to the contact form from your own addon, do not edit partner_views.xml: declare an inheriting view record (inherit_id = base.partner_form, see [views](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/views.md)) in your addon. The install test crates/erp-cli/tests/contacts_install.rs lists every record of the addon by external id and checks that the views validate when installed; a view that names a field the model does not have fails the install.

An addon can ship demo data: example records that make a fresh database look used, so lists, forms, reports and tests have something to show. Demo data is optional and is loaded only when the database is created with demo data.

Put the files in the addon's demo/ folder and list them in the manifest next to data: data = ["views/book_views.xml"] demo = ["demo/book_demo.xml", "demo/loans.csv"] Demo files use the same formats as data files ([data-files.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/data-files.md)): XML with <record> elements, or CSV. They load after all data files of the module, in the order listed. Two rules differ from data files: - **noupdate by default.** A demo file loads as if it were wrapped in <erp noupdate="1">, so an upgrade never rewrites demo records a user has edited. - **All or nothing.** The demo files of one module load inside one savepoint. If one fails on its data (a missing reference, a refused value), the module installs without demo data and the failure is reported as a DemoFailed notice; the rest of the install goes ahead.

base takes the database's demo flag, chosen once when the database is initialized: erp db init --with-demo (the default is --without-demo; InitOptions::with_demo(true) in code). The flag stays on the database; erp db init refuses to change it later, and erp module install --with-demo on a database without demo data loads the demo data of every installed addon first ([cli.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/cli.md#installing-modules)). Every other module gets demo data only when each module it depends on has it. A module with no demo list passes the flag on, so an addon without demo files does not stop its dependents from loading theirs. Without the flag, no demo record exists in any addon. A demo file may refer to the external ids of the module's dependencies, because those are loaded first: the product demo prices the vendor partners that the base demo creates (base.partner_demo_mitra_kayu).

- Invent the content: company names, people, products, notes. Use example.com-style addresses and fictional phone numbers. Never copy real customers or another project's demo records. - Give every record an external id (partner_demo_..., product_demo_...) so tests and other demo files can refer to it. Most demo ids carry a _demo_ infix; attribute values (pav_…) do not, so check a new id against the addon's default data ids before you use it. - A company partner is a root partner with a tax ID (vat): is_company is computed from it. People are child partners with parent_id. - Do not create demo users with passwords. Demo data never ships credentials. - Default data (categories, units, currencies, the record sets an addon needs to work) belongs in data, not in demo. - Test it: initialise a test database with and without demo data and assert that the records exist, and that none exist without the flag (crates/erp-cli/tests/demo_data.rs).

| Addon | Demo files | Records | |---|---|---| | base | res_currency_demo.xml, res_currency_rate_demo.xml, res_partner_demo.xml | EUR, IDR, SGD and GBP made active; 7 spot rates for them against the company currency; 6 company partners (4 vendors, 2 customers) with 9 contacts | | product | product_attribute_demo.xml, product_category_demo.xml, product_demo.xml, product_supplierinfo_demo.xml, product_pricelist_demo.xml | 17 attribute values (some with a default extra price); 7 subcategories; 15 product templates (12 goods, 3 services; 28 variants after the attribute lines); 11 vendor price rows on the base demo vendors; 2 pricelists with 4 rules; 3 combos with 6 items | | contacts | contacts_demo.xml | 2 companies with contacts and 2 tags | | account | account_account_demo.xml, account_journal_demo.xml | 3 reporting tags; a small generic chart of 20 accounts of the main company (one or more per account type group, codes 101100 to 691000), some tagged with the demo tags or the cash-flow tags of the default data; 1 extra ledger (Management Reporting); 6 journals on those accounts (sales, purchases, bank, cash, general, and a general journal in the extra ledger) | | sample_library | sample_library_demo.xml | authors, genres, books and loans | The account demo names the company of every account (company_ids) and journal (company_id): base.main_company. An account code is stored per company, so naming it keeps the records independent of the company the loader happens to work in. Fiscal periods have no demo records: they are created when a dated document needs them, and the record API refuses them. Taxes come later, with the fiscal country of the company: a tax needs a country, and the main company has none. Combo items point at single-variant products. A variant that an attribute line generates has no external id, so a demo file refers to it with search="[('product_tmpl_id', '=', ref('...'))]", which finds the first variant of the template. acceptance_notes ships no demo. Its notes need an owner user in the same company as the note, and demo data creates no users (no passwords), so the company-consistency check refuses a note owned by the system user.
Status: implemented. A runtime (WASM) addon ships as one .erpaddon file, a ZIP archive. This page is what an addon author needs to build one, and what an administrator's install step checks.

manifest.toml            # required; same keys as a native addon, plus an optional [wasm] section wasm/<name>.wasm         # required when the manifest has [wasm]; <name> is the technical name data/ views/ security/ i18n/ migrations/   # as for native addons static/dist/             # optional pre-built client code (needs an explicit administrator ack) SHA256SUMS               # required; one line per file except itself SHA256SUMS lines are <64 lowercase hex> + two spaces (or a space and *) + the path, separated by \n. No blank lines, comments or duplicates; paths follow the archive path rules below. It detects corruption and tampering of individual files. It travels inside the archive, so it does not prove who made the package; pin the archive digest (archive_sha256) where authenticity matters.

Paths must already be canonical: no leading /, no \, no : (drive letters), no control characters, no empty, . or .. segment, at most 512 bytes (255 per segment). There is no normalisation, so two entries can never resolve to one name. Duplicate names, names that differ only by case, a name that is both a file and a directory (also case-folded, on every directory prefix) and symlink entries are refused. Anything whose lowercase form is under static/dist/ must be spelled exactly static/dist/, so client code cannot dodge the acknowledgement gate.

Read under hard bounds, enforced while inflating (header sizes are never trusted for allocation): archive 64 MiB, 4096 entries, 32 MiB per entry, 128 MiB total uncompressed. PackageLimits lets a caller tighten them. Exceeding one gives Error::PackageLimitExceeded naming the bound.

[wasm] capabilities accepts only: migrations-sql; filesystem:temp:<N>(kb|mb|gb) with 1 <= N <= 4096; network:outbound:<http(s)-url> where the host is an exact DNS name or IP literal (no userinfo, no percent-encoding, no wildcard in the host, strict dotted-quad IPv4 only), the port is explicit if present, and * may only be the whole last path segment (/*). The stored form is normalised (lowercase host), and consent compares that form. Unknown names are an error.

erp addon package <addon> -o <name>.erpaddon after erp addon build <addon> --target wasm (see wasm-addons.md). The packer writes technical_name = "<name>" as the first line of the archived manifest when the source manifest has none, so a display name such as "Shop (WASM)" is fine.

let package = ErpAddonPackage::open("shop.erpaddon")?; let mut consent = AdminConsent::new(package.name().clone()); consent.approve_capability("migrations-sql");        // exactly what the manifest requests consent.set_client_dist_digest_ack(package.client_dist_digest().unwrap()); // only if it ships static/dist/ let consented = package.consent(&consent)?;           // the only way to get a ConsentedPackage store_package(&mut tx, &consented).await?;            // stores the verified archive bytes Consent must match the request exactly: missing approvals, approvals for capabilities the package does not request, another addon's name, and a wrong or unneeded client acknowledgement are all refused. Storing never overwrites: the same archive returns the existing row, a different archive under an existing (name, version) is a conflict. Not yet done: ir_module_package is created by init_package_table only and is not part of the schema-migration path; the acknowledgement is not yet written to an audit trail; an upgrade does not yet compare the previous client digest.

Status: implemented. ERPForAll only: Odoo checks overlapping periods in Python after the write (hr.version._check_dates), so two concurrent transactions can both pass, or takes a row lock (resource.calendar.attendance). Here the database enforces the rule. Every Rust example in this guide is compiled and run as a doctest of erp-test-models (cargo test --doc): the declarations go through the registry and ORM checks a server runs at startup. Lines starting with #  are hidden setup.

An exclusion says: no two records whose equal fields are equal may have overlapping periods. The period is two stored date or two stored datetime fields, period = ("from", "to"), with bounds: - bounds = "[)": the start is included, the end is not, so a booking that ends at 11:00 and one that starts at 11:00 do not overlap (the usual choice for datetimes); - bounds = "[]": both ends are included, so two stays that share a day overlap (the usual choice for whole days). bounds has no default. A NULL end is unbounded: a booking without a stop is open-ended and overlaps every later booking of the same resource. A filter (a constant domain) limits the rule to the records it matches, here the ones that are not cancelled. A NULL in an equal column never conflicts (PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct), so two records without a resource may overlap. Make the field required, or add a filter such as [('resource_id', '!=', False)] to state that records without one are outside the rule on purpose.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;
pub struct Resource { #[field(char, required)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, }

name = "booking.booking", description = "Booking", exclusions = [exclude( name = "_no_double_booking", equal = ["resource_id"], period = ("start", "stop"), bounds = "[)", filter = "[('state', '!=', 'cancel')]", message = "This resource is already booked for an overlapping period." )] )] pub struct Booking { #[field(many2one, comodel = "booking.resource", required)] pub resource_id: Option<RecId>, #[field(datetime)] pub start: Option<DateTime>, #[field(datetime)] pub stop: Option<DateTime>, #[field( selection, selection = [("confirmed", "Confirmed"), ("cancel", "Cancelled")], default = "confirmed", required )] pub state: Option<Arc<str>>, }

What the user sees when a booking overlaps another one — in the same transaction or in a concurrent one that committed first — is a validation error with the declared message: The database refused the change: This resource is already booked for an overlapping period. The server's DETAIL (the other row's key values) is never shown: it can name a record the user may not read. **Empty and inverted periods** would overlap nothing and slip past the rule, so they are refused too. create, and write when the other end of the period is already in the transaction, refuse them before any statement; schema sync also adds a CHECK (named <constraint>_period_check) that refuses them in the database, for raw SQL and for writes whose other end was not loaded. Both give the same message, naming the fields' labels and the model's description: The database refused the change: 'Start' must be before 'Stop' on 'Booking' ('Arrival' must not be after 'Departure' for [] periods, where a period of one day is valid.) The period check applies to every row, whatever the exclusion's filter says: an inverted period is always invalid, even on a record the rule leaves out (for example a cancelled booking).

EXCLUDE USING gist ("resource_id" WITH =, tsrange("start", "stop", '[)') WITH &&) WHERE (...) (daterange for date periods), with the canonical definition in the constraint's comment, plus the period CHECK. A changed declaration is dropped and re-created on the next sync; an unchanged one is left alone. Equality inside a GiST index needs the btree_gist extension: schema sync installs it (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist, a trusted extension the owner role may create) in the same transaction, before the constraint. When the server does not have it, or the role may not create it, the install fails and names the model, the extension and the object.

Building the GiST index takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table for the whole build and has no online form. When the table already holds more than large_table_rows rows, the install or upgrade therefore refuses to add (or change) an exclusion or a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key and says so: cannot add exclusion '_no_double_booking' to 'booking.booking' during the install: table 'booking_booking' has more than 1000 rows and an exclusion constraint has no online build. Run erp db build-object -d <db> --model booking.booking --object _no_double_booking in a maintenance window (it holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table for the build), then retry the install Run the command in a window you chose, then retry the install; it finds the object present and does nothing for it: DATABASE_URL="postgres://erp@db.internal/postgres" \ erp db build-object -d prod --model booking.booking --object _no_double_booking --lock-timeout 60 - --object is the declared name (_no_double_booking), --lock-timeout the seconds to wait for a lock (1 to 3600, default 30; 0 and larger values are refused at argument parsing). While the build waits for its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, new readers and writers of the table queue behind it: choose a short timeout. --build-timeout (60 to 86400, default six hours, longer than the lock timeout) stops a statement that runs too long. - It runs as the role in DATABASE_URL (the owner role), takes the schema lock that schema sync takes, and in one transaction creates btree_gist when needed, adds the period CHECK and the constraint and stores the canonical definition in the comment. Reads and writes of the table wait while it runs. It does not put a running server into maintenance mode. - Rows that already break the rule fail it with cannot add exclusion '<name>' to '<model>': existing records conflict, e.g. (<id>, <id>), ... (up to 20 id pairs); nothing is left behind. Fix the rows and run it again. A lock that is not granted within the timeout fails it with a message naming the table and the timeout. - An object that is already there with the canonical definition is left alone (the report says so), so running it twice is safe. - The registry is composed from the addons linked into the erp binary; from Rust, Orm::build_object(model, object, &BuildObjectOptions) does the same work and returns a BuildObjectReport.

A filter is a domain in list syntax over the model's own stored scalar, selection, boolean and many2one fields, with =, !=, in, not in (False meaning "not set") and &, |, !. Its values are literals: no paths (partner_id.country_id), no uid, no context, no ref, no arithmetic. It means exactly what the same domain means in a search, NULL rules included. A filter outside these rules fails the ORM's startup: exclusion '_no_double_booking' on 'booking.booking': filter [('resource_id', '=', uid)]: only literal values are allowed, found the name 'uid'

Exclusions compose by name like the other table objects: an addon adds one with #[extend], and a later declaration with the same name replaces an earlier one. A model file (models/*.toml) or an overlay never replaces an object a Rust declaration made: the registry refuses the build naming both sources, so choose another name.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use booking::Booking;

Booking, exclusions = [exclude( name = "_one_guest_per_room", equal = ["room"], period = ("arrival", "departure"), bounds = "[]", message = "This room is already taken on one of these days." )] )] pub struct BookingRooms;

date_range and datetime_range store a period in one column (daterange, tsrange). The Rust types are Option<DateRange> and Option<DatetimeRange>; a Range has a lower and an upper end, each optional (None is unbounded), read with the field's bounds, which every range field declares. A [] date range is stored by PostgreSQL as [lower, upper + 1 day) and read back as declared. A key(..., without_overlaps = "<range field>") is PostgreSQL 18's temporal key: `UNIQUE (fields..., range WITHOUT OVERLAPS)`, here one rate per product for any date. It is a rule, not an upsert key.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;
pub struct Product { #[field(char, required)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, }

name = "pricing.rate", description = "Rate", keys = [key( name = "_rate_key", fields = ["product_id"], without_overlaps = "validity", message = "A product has one rate for any date." )] )] pub struct Rate { #[field(many2one, comodel = "pricing.product", required)] pub product_id: Option<RecId>, #[field(date_range, bounds = "[)", string = "Validity")] pub validity: Option<DateRange>, #[field(float)] pub amount: f64, }

let jan = Date::from_ymd(2026, 1, 1).expect("a date"); let rates = tx.env().model::<Rate>()?; // open-ended: from January on let rate = rates .create( &mut tx, vec![ Vals::new() .set(Rate::PRODUCT_ID, product) .set(Rate::VALIDITY, DateRange::new(Some(jan), None)) .set(Rate::AMOUNT, 9.5), ], ) .await?; let validity: Option<DateRange> = rate.get(&mut tx, Rate::VALIDITY).await?; // the rates valid on a day, and those overlapping a period (false: unbounded) let on_day = rates .search(&mut tx, &Domain::field("validity")?.contains("2026-03-01")) .await?; let from_march = rates .search(&mut tx, &Domain::field("validity")?.overlaps("2026-03-01", false)) .await?;

On the dynamic surface (JSON-2, Luau, data files, read), a range is [lower, upper] with false for an unbounded end: ["2026-01-01", false]. Writing anything else (a string, a list of three) is a validation error that names the field and the expected shape. An empty or inverted range is refused with the field's label: The database refused the change: 'Validity' (pricing.rate.validity) is an empty range: its lower end must be before its upper end Domains on range fields: overlaps takes a range [lower, upper] (with the field's bounds), contains a date or datetime, and = False / != False test whether the field is set. Other operators are refused, and so is grouping by a range field. In-memory filtering (filtered_domain) gives the same answers as the database.

A native addon can still write raw SQL table objects (`constraints = [("_name", "EXCLUDE ...", "message")]`, the Odoo port path). Schema sync does not read raw SQL to guess what it needs: state it with extensions = [...] ("btree_gist", "pg_trgm" or "unaccent"), and schema sync installs them first.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;

name = "legacy.booking", description = "Legacy booking", extensions = ["btree_gist"], constraints = [( "_no_overlap", "EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, tsrange(start, stop) WITH &&)", "This room is already booked." )] )] pub struct LegacyBooking { #[field(integer)] pub room: i32, #[field(datetime)] pub start: Option<DateTime>, #[field(datetime)] pub stop: Option<DateTime>, }

Data-only addons declare the same typed objects: they name fields, never SQL, so a database-stored package can use them. Unknown keys and raw SQL are errors naming the file and line. [[model]] extend = "booking.booking" [[model.exclude]] name = "_no_double_booking" equal = ["resource_id"] period = { from = "start", to = "stop", bounds = "[)" } filter = "[('state', '!=', 'cancel')]" message = "This resource is already booked for an overlapping period." [[model]] name = "pricing.season" description = "Season" [[model.field]] name = "product_id" type = "many2one" comodel = "pricing.product" required = true [[model.field]] name = "dates" type = "date_range" bounds = "[]" [[model.key]] name = "_one_season" fields = ["product_id"] without_overlaps = "dates" message = "Seasons of a product may not overlap." Partitioning is declared by native addons only, and business keys without without_overlaps (the keys an upsert uses) are planned.
A range field without bounds:
pub struct Rate { #[field(date_range)] pub validity: Option<DateRange>, }
An exclusion without bounds:

name = "broken.booking", exclusions = [exclude(name = "_x", period = ("start", "stop"), message = "taken")] )] pub struct Booking { #[field(datetime)] pub start: Option<DateTime>, #[field(datetime)] pub stop: Option<DateTime>, }

Registry errors (at startup) name the object, the model and the reason: a field that does not exist or is not stored, a field type = cannot compare (JSON, x2many), period fields of different types, a field listed twice, an empty message, a without_overlaps key on a field that is not a range or without any other field.

@erpforall/expr evaluates a ValidatedAst from the bounded AST reader/decoder. Host record and context bindings use tagged ExprValue values, not raw JS primitives. Use intVal, strVal, listVal and the other value constructors. Integers crossing the evaluator boundary must fit i64; use bigint for exact values instead of converting through JavaScript number. Names, resolver values, registered host attribute results and host call results are admitted under the current evaluation budget. Admission validates the data, checks depth/work/logical bytes, charges the copy, then snapshots it. Container wrappers/arrays are frozen and byte buffers are isolated from their source. Replacing a field/context signal is how hosts publish changes. Treat returned values as read-only; changing a source container cannot change a cached result. Budget.admit(value) now returns the admitted snapshot. A low-level caller that uses this method must retain the returned value; ignoring it keeps the original host reference. Evaluator-owned producers reserve their output and work under the invocation budget before returning; their results use checkValue without charging them again. Internal capability provenance belongs to one evaluation, so exporting a bound method and reintroducing it as a host value admits its captured receiver under the new evaluation budget. Native objectVal/callableVal constructors register explicit trusted capabilities. A structural cast to those tags does not register a capability. The sandbox never derives a callback from a data property. Malformed tags/payloads, holes, cyclic data and data accessors fail explicitly. Quota errors are sticky for the evaluation. Proxies are not a supported data transport; native callback implementations remain trusted host code. Errors from those callbacks propagate rather than becoming successful expression values. The reactive adapter validates context data once per evaluation, while charging each expression reference. It indexes primitive keys with Python numeric key equivalence; compound-key equality uses an explicit work budget. Container structure is normalized once; each reference snapshots its leaf data. A trusted native callback that changes a source leaf between references can therefore publish a newer value to the later reference; earlier admitted values remain isolated. A fresh signal reevaluation validates the source again with a new budget. This cache does not survive disposal or a later evaluation. Known integration limitation: FORMAT R2-11's string/bytes/dict * unpacking and call-error precedence remain open and do not block this delivery. This repair does not declare the full interpreter or Odoo behavior accepted. Product performance remains deferred to milestone end.

Rust owns the expression syntax and wire declarations. The AST transport in erp_expr::wire is schema version 1: an ordered node arena with the root last. An edge refers to an earlier node, every other node has exactly one parent, and no unused node is admitted. Literal integers use canonical decimal strings; floating-point literals use hexadecimal binary64 bits. Do not convert integer payloads through JavaScript number. On the producer, parse source with erp_expr::parse, then serialize with erp_expr::wire::encode. Both can fail. ValidatedAst::from_json validates received transport bytes before exposing an immutable Rust AST through as_expr(). A raw WireDocument deserialized by serde is still untrusted; convert it through ValidatedAst::try_from before evaluation. Encoding checks public AST values too, including trees constructed without the source parser. The crate's wire rustdoc contains an executable roundtrip example. JSON numbers used for schema versions, child indices and bytes have value semantics: 0, 0.0 and 0e0 are equivalent. After binary64 rounding, the number must be an integer within the field's range. Literal integer payloads remain canonical strings. To match browser Number rounding, erp-expr enables serde_json's float_roundtrip feature. Cargo feature unification also enables that decimal-parsing behavior in other workspace consumers of the same serde_json dependency. Its performance impact outside expression transport has not been measured. In the browser, @erpforall/expr supplies readResponseJson for a streamed response and parseBoundedJson for bounded text or UTF-8 bytes. The parser rejects duplicate keys throughout the response, malformed Unicode, excessive depth, and byte/allocation-ledger limits. Its returned containers are frozen. After the owning view decoder validates its description's shape, create one DescriptionBudget for that parsed description subtree and pass that same budget to each decodeAst call in the description. This counts expressions and nodes together and includes nonexpression wrapper bytes in the byte cap. decodeAst accepts only containers authenticated by the bounded reader; a handwritten object or TypeScript cast is insufficient. Check isValidatedAst when accepting a handle across another runtime trust boundary. Limits may be lowered, never raised or disabled by zero. AST rejection returns an InvalidAst kind, JSON path and diagnostic; it is distinct from a Python evaluation exception. A schema-version mismatch requires reloading/upgrading compatible client/server code. Consumers must surface the failure, rather than rendering a partial view or substituting a false modifier. The AST child supplies decoding, not the client evaluator. Evaluation and signal adapters remain the later UIX children; production view descriptions and response integration belong to WEB-SERVER-BASE and the view slices. Schema maintainers enable the nondefault Rust schema-gen feature only in tooling. scripts/gen-ui-types.sh --write refreshes the complete managed declaration set; --check detects missing, extra or changed declarations without editing them. The test-only nested response proves the derive path; it is not a production view description. Import the generated wire declarations through the package's type-only @erpforall/expr/wire export.

The generator pins optional ts-rs to 11.1.0. Its [documented export API](https://docs.rs/ts-rs/11.1.0/ts_rs/trait.TS.html) exports the registered roots and their dependencies to .d.ts files; the [version's licence is MIT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aleph-Alpha/ts-rs/v11.1.0/LICENSE). Run generation through the authorized remote build workflow. Enabling schema-gen in production or wasm dependencies is not supported. ts-rs reports that it ignores serde's deny_unknown_fields and custom deserialize_with admission attributes. These warnings remain visible. The declarations describe JSON shape: they cannot enforce duplicate rejection, integer bounds, canonical integer strings, float-bit syntax or mandatory-field admission. For example, slice bounds and keyword names are **required nullable fields**, and integer/float literal payloads remain strings. Keep the Rust and browser runtime validators; do not remove fields with ts(skip) or disable warnings globally to conceal an admission mismatch. examples/support/schema.rs contains a test-only nested producer with to_json_with_limits. It validates each raw expression, checks the expression and aggregate-node counts, and serializes through a bounded writer that includes description wrapper bytes and the complete response. Limit overrides must be positive and may only lower the current limits. Failures return a typed error; no partial response is returned. This helper encodes each expression once for validation and again in the nested output. It proves the transport contract, not the production view serializer's performance; the owning view slice must supply that implementation. The ui_fixtures tooling example has separate goldens and differential modes. goldens includes the authoritative Rust golden table and copies its ordinal, source, success flag and expectation unchanged alongside its parsed AST. differential labels a bounded seeded Rust oracle with its context and limits, retaining source-parse failures as rows. The generated corpus also records operation family, case and seed. web-expr-fuzz-smoke compares the browser's actual repr or PythonError class and complete text against Rust for every parsed row; parser outcomes are replayed by the Rust exporter harness. The browser has no source parser. Seeded fast-check properties shrink failures within the finite row index domain; hostile wire properties shrink their generated fields/indices. Ignored logs/uix-fuzz/ artifacts record the seed, shrink path, row or wire, limits and context. Committed replay files are read-only regression inputs. Neither generated mode changes the authoritative CPython expectations.

Expression and human-view DTOs run their Serde derives before the optional erp_macros::wire_ts attribute. The schema tool passes serialized names, tags, optional fields and flattening through to ts-rs. Input validators such as deserialize_with and deny_unknown_fields are enforced by Serde even when schema-gen is enabled. A scalar newtype can use Serde conversion into its stored wire type. A different outgoing type requires a schema that describes that type. Run scripts/gen-ui-types.sh --check and compare the human_ui_schema output with addons/web/static/src/generated/human-ui.ts after changing either wire contract.

docs.title: Python Expressions in Data and Views

sections.text: Status: complete (crates/erp-expr). Implements: ADR 0004 (language selection), ADR 0009 §9 (expression evaluator), ADR 0020 (Python expression sandbox). Specs: docs/specs/data/data-views-api.md (SPEC-DATA-012, SPEC-DATA-054). The erp-expr crate provides a pure, zero-I/O sandboxed expression evaluator for the subset of Python syntax used throughout Odoo data files and views. It evaluates XML eval="..." attributes, search="..." domains and context dictionaries under fixed resource limits and checked arithmetic. View modifiers (invisible, readonly, required) are combined as text during view inheritance (see below). ---

Expressions are evaluated when data files are loaded (install and upgrade) and wherever a host evaluates an expression it stores: 1. **XML data files (<field eval="...">)**: computed values, relational commands, dates and configuration tuples: <field name="active" eval="True"/> <field name="sequence" eval="10 + 5"/> <field name="date_deadline" eval="(datetime.today() + relativedelta(months=1)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')"/> <field name="tag_ids" eval="[Command.set([ref('tag_urgent'), ref('tag_review')])]"/> 2. **Context dictionaries**: default values or flags for actions and relational fields: <field name="context" eval="{'default_partner_id': ref('base.main_partner'), 'search_default_my': 1}"/> 3. **Search domains (domain="[...]")**: Odoo domain lists of (field, operator, value) tuples: <field name="partner_id" domain="[('is_company', '=', True), ('parent_id', '=', False)]"/> 4. **View modifiers (invisible="...", readonly="...", required="...")**: conditions on the record's values in forms and lists: <field name="reason" invisible="state != 'rejected'" required="state == 'rejected'"/> ---

The evaluator implements a subset of Python expression grammar; it never executes statements or imports code: - **Literals**: True, False, None; 64-bit signed integers and floats; single- and double-quoted strings with escape sequences; f-strings; lists, tuples and dictionaries. - **Operators**: - arithmetic +, -, *, /, //, %, **, unary +, - and ~; - comparisons ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, including chained comparisons (0 < x < 10); - identity and membership is, is not, in, not in; - boolean and, or, not (short-circuiting); - bitwise &, |, ^, <<, >>. - **Access**: subscripts and slices (items[0], name[:3]), attribute and method access on the values the host binds (dates, Command, records the data loader provides). - **Conditionals and comprehensions**: a if condition else b, list comprehensions ([x * 2 for x in values if x]), generator expressions (sum(x for x in values)), and :=. **Not supported** (refused with a parse error that names the construct): set literals, set and dict comprehensions, ** unpacking in dict displays, lambda, import and other statement keywords. ---

EvalContext::standard() binds the Python builtins and the names of Odoo's data-loader context. It deliberately binds nothing that reads host data: - **Builtins**: str, repr, int, float, bool, len, list, tuple, dict, min, max, sum, abs, round. - **Relational commands (Command)**, matching Odoo's Command namespace for x2many writes: - Command.create({'name': 'Item'}): create a child record (triple (0, 0, values)) - Command.update(id, {'name': 'New'}): update a child record (triple (1, id, values)) - Command.delete(id): delete the record (triple (2, id, 0)) - Command.unlink(id): remove from the relation without deleting (triple (3, id, 0)) - Command.link(id): add an existing record (triple (4, id, 0)) - Command.clear(): remove all relations (triple (5, 0, 0)) - Command.set([id1, id2]): replace the relation set (triple (6, 0, [ids])) - **Date and time**: datetime (also bound as DateTime) is the datetime class: call it to build a value (datetime(2026, 1, 2)) or use datetime.now() and datetime.today(); it has no other attributes, so datetime.date(...) and datetime.timedelta(...) are refused. timedelta(days=1) and relativedelta(months=1) are top-level names, and time.strftime('%Y') formats the current time. now(), today() and time.strftime() need a clock; the standard context has none and refuses them with a ValueError that says so. The data loader supplies the clock. - **Host-provided names**: the data loader (crates/erp-data/src/load/expr.rs) adds the clock, version, and host hooks that resolve ref('module.xmlid') through its XML-id resolver (which reports a missing id) and answer record, search and group lookups. Record access through obj and env needs EvalContext::with_model. Where the host has not provided them, ref, obj, env, user, has_group and version raise a NameError that names the provider instead of returning an empty value. ---

An inheriting view changes a modifier with position="attributes". To add or remove a condition without restating the whole expression, use add, remove and separator on <attribute>: <!-- Base view --> <field name="due_date" readonly="state in ('done', 'cancelled')"/> <!-- Inheriting view --> <field name="due_date" position="attributes"> <attribute name="readonly" add="is_locked" separator="or"/> </field> erp_expr::combine_python_attribute combines the texts: add appends with the separator, remove drops a matching operand. It does not parse or check the expressions. The separator must be and or or; a missing or other separator fails with ExprError::Modifier (SPEC-DATA-054). See [views](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/views.md) for the other position values. ---

Expressions are untrusted input. The evaluator has no access to the operating system, files, environment variables or threads. Every parse-and-evaluate call gets a fresh budget (EvalLimits, ADR 0020 §1). The values below are a ceiling: the with_* methods can only lower them. | Limit | Ceiling | Error message (ExprError::LimitExceeded) | |---|---|---| | Source length | 64 KiB | refused before parsing | | Nesting depth (syntax tree, evaluation and produced values) | 100 | value nesting depth limit of N exceeded | | Evaluation steps | 1,000,000 | evaluation step limit of N exceeded | | Size of one produced value | 1 MiB | value of N bytes exceeds the per-value limit of N bytes | | Total bytes produced by one evaluation | 16 MiB | evaluation memory budget of N bytes exceeded | | Format width | 1,000 | refused when formatting | **Checked 64-bit arithmetic**: integer arithmetic is checked. An integer outside the 64-bit range fails with ExprError::Overflow (OverflowError: ...); division or modulo by zero fails with ExprError::ZeroDivision (ZeroDivisionError: ...). Nothing overflows silently and nothing panics.

docs.title: Field access: hiding and protecting single fields

sections.text: Status: implemented. The engine checks field access on every ORM path, and the policy erp-security compiles from the group tables decides it: which groups a user is in, and what groups='…' means for them. In tests the testkit's FieldPolicy can stand in for the tables. The design is in ADR 0035 and docs/design/m3-access-engine.md §2.2 and §3.3. Every Rust example in this guide is compiled and run as a doctest of erp-test-models.
Put groups = "…" on the field, as in Odoo:
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;

pub struct Employee { #[field(char)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, /// Only members of the HR managers group (a comma-separated list means "any of them"). #[field(integer, groups = "hr.group_hr_manager")] pub salary: i32, /// . is Odoo's "nobody": no user, whatever the groups; only superuser mode reaches it. #[field(integer, groups = ".")] pub legacy_code: i32, }
The group names are external ids (module.name). A field without groups is open to everyone who may use the model.

| Text | Who may use the field | |---|---| | a.x,b.y | members of a.x or of b.y (implied groups count: a member of a group that implies a.x is in a.x) | | a.x,!b.y | members of a.x who are not in b.y | | !b.y | everyone who is not in b.y | | a.x,!a.x | nobody (the negation is checked first) | | . | nobody, in any group; only superuser mode reaches the field | | base.group_no_one | members of the technical-features group, **in debug mode only** (in either position) | The text is parsed once when the policy is built, against the groups of the database. An external id that names no group (a typo, an uninstalled addon) is an error in the build report (PolicySnapshot::report, erp access report) and **closes the field** to everyone outside superuser mode: it is never skipped, so a typo cannot leave a field open. With the technical group, the denial error in debug mode names the broken text. Custom fields (x_…, created in the database) take their groups from the field's group list (ir.model.fields), and a list with several groups means "any of them". A custom field is also subject to a registry groups of the same name; both must hold.
Transaction::has_groups answers env.user.has_groups(spec) with the same texts, from the groups the transaction already resolved (no statement for the transaction's own user):
use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn can_see_salaries(tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<bool> { let env = tx.env(); tx.has_groups(&env, "hr.group_hr_manager,!base.group_portal").await }

On a user record, res.users.has_group(xmlid) asks about that user. A user who is not internal gets an AccessError when asking about someone else; internal users and superuser mode may. A **related field** that declares no groups takes the groups of the field it points to, along a chain of related fields; one that declares its own keeps them (SPEC-SEC-050). A field an _inherits child takes over from its parent carries the parent field's groups. A related path that does not resolve, or a cycle of related fields, stops the registry build with a Programming error naming model.field and the path (it would otherwise leave the field open).
