Odoo does the same, except that it stores email and phone on the company and computes the address from the partner. Creating a company with a name and no partner_id creates the partner and passes the contact values to it. country_id, state_id, logo and the report fields are not available yet; see docs/specs/base/company.md, section 4.7. An addon adds its own company contact field the same way: another related field plus an entry in the Settings > Companies form view. The company name does not follow the partner's name yet (SPEC-PARTNER-060 is not implemented). ---

Under the ERPForAll engineering standards, silent fallbacks, ignored errors, and permissive defaults are forbidden. The following table highlights common Odoo behaviors that fail loudly in ERPForAll: | Area | Odoo Behavior | ERPForAll Fail-Loudly Contract | Relevant ADR | |---|---|---|---| | **Manifest Parsing** | Broken __manifest__.py files or missing keys are logged at DEBUG or silently cause the module to vanish from the list. | Any syntax error, unknown key outside [extra], wrong value type, or invalid version stops startup with an error. | ADR 0018 §1–2 | | **Missing Dependencies** | Modules with missing dependencies are silently skipped or dropped from the installation graph. | Discovery reports an explicit error listing all missing dependency chains and cycles. | ADR 0018 §5 | | **Data File Schema** | Unrecognized XML tags or attributes are ignored; misspelled attributes (modle=, <feild>) pass silently. | Parser strictly enforces the element and attribute allowlist (RNG schema); unknown elements abort loading with file and line. | ADR 0019 §3 | | **Boolean Attributes** | Any arbitrary string in a boolean attribute (e.g. noupdate="unknown") evaluates to True via str2bool. | Only 1/0, true/false, yes/no, on/off are accepted; anything else fails loading immediately. | ADR 0019 §2 | | **Comments in Values** | XML comments inside text values (e.g. <field>A<!-- c -->B</field>) silently drop content after the comment. | Comments inside raw text field values are rejected loudly. | ADR 0019 §3 | | **Expression Evaluation** | Python expressions in eval can fail at runtime or invoke unmonitored builtins. | erp-expr parses expressions at build/install time; unexposed attributes or variables fail immediately (UnknownAttribute). | ADR 0020 §1–3 | | **RPC Exposure** | All public Python methods (not prefixed with _) are callable over RPC unless @api.private is added. | Methods are private by default; calling an unexposed method over RPC returns 403. Only explicit #[rpc] methods are callable. | ADR 0038 §1, ADR 0004 | | **RPC Effect Violations** | A @api.readonly method that writes to the database emits a warning and silently replays on a read/write cursor. | Calling a method marked #[rpc(effect = read)] that attempts a database write fails loudly with a transaction error. | ADR 0038 §2 | | **Translated View Selectors** | Extension views can match elements by translated strings (<button string="Save">), breaking under other locales. | Locating elements by translatable attributes (string="...") is strictly forbidden and rejected by erp-views. | ADR 0027, erp-views | | **Server Action Permissions** | Server actions for object_write, object_create, etc., silently run with superuser privileges. | All server actions run with caller rights unless an explicit, administrator-assigned run_as_superuser flag is present. | ADR 0001, ADR 0009 §10 | | **PostgreSQL Version Gate** | Server starts on older PostgreSQL releases (9.6+) and fails later with obscure syntax errors or degraded queries. | Connection pool post-create hook enforces PostgreSQL 18+ (server_version_num >= 180000), refusing older servers with a typed error naming ADR 0028 and warning on PG19+. | ADR 0028 §1 | | **Required Database Extensions** | Missing extensions (e.g. pg_trgm) silently cause trigram indexes to be skipped or fall back to sequential scans. | Schema sync and DDL require declared extensions: declaring a trigram index (index = "trigram") when pg_trgm is not installed fails loudly with MissingExtensionError (Programming error). | ADR 0028 §3 | | **Installation Atomicity** | Odoo commits after each module during multi-module install; a mid-way failure leaves a partially installed database. | Install, upgrade, and uninstall execute in a single PostgreSQL transaction (all-or-nothing rollback on any failure). | ADR 0009 §2 | | **Result Dictionaries** | values['x'] on a missing key raises KeyError; any code can add a key of any type to any row dict. | Result rows are batches with one shared layout (erp_fields::rows): reading a key the rows do not have, a key absent in that row, or a row past the end is a Programming error naming the key, the row and the model; get_opt and contains are the explicit tests. Read a row like a dict with value.dict() (get, get_opt, contains, keys, iter, len), for Value::Map and Value::Row alike. Value is #[non_exhaustive]: an addon's match on it ends with an arm that returns an error, never one that turns an unknown value into a normal one. The Rows override API (set, insert_key, remove_key, children_mut, from_maps) reaches web_read and read overrides in a later delivery. | ADR 0052 | ---

Features already functional on main for addon developers: - **Module discovery & CLI:** Addon discovery, dependency graph resolution, manifest validation, and developer CLI commands (erp module install, upgrade, uninstall, scaffold, dev). - **Module Lifecycle in DB:** Transactional install, upgrade, uninstall and dependency graph in PostgreSQL. - **Security & Access Policy:** Access policy compilation from ir.access into SQL predicates, group inheritance closure, and field-level groups enforcement (follow-up open).

The table below lists features that are designed or under active development on the board, with their current state and what is still to come: | Feature | Current State | Still to come | Description | |---|---|---|---| | **Database Data Loading** | Parser (erp-data) merged | planned | Loading XML/CSV records into PostgreSQL, external IDs (ir.model.data), noupdate tracking. | | **View & Menu DB Storage** | Arch engine (erp-views) merged | planned | Storing and resolving ir.ui.view and ir.ui.menu records in the database. | | **Migrations** | ADR 0009 §2 designed | planned | Migration execution engine, MOD-036..039. | | **Packaged Addons (.erpaddon)** | Native crates merged; plan done | in progress | Distributable ZIP archive packages and WASM component isolation (ADR 0001, ADR 0009). | | **HTTP JSON-2 RPC Server & Auth** | In-process dispatch merged; password login and session rows ([auth.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/auth.md)) | HTTP server and API key authentication (planned) | HTTP listener for /json/2/<model>/<method>, session cookies, API key authentication. | | **Web Client UI** | Specifications & plan defined | in progress | Core web client shell, reactive views (form, list, kanban, search, pivot, graph, calendar, gantt), widget registry. | | **Native Typst PDF Reports** | ADR 0031 accepted; specs done | implementation planned in ADR 0031 | High-performance QWeb-to-Typst PDF report generation engine with PDF/A-3 support. | ---

Unlike Odoo where upgrades between minor and major versions frequently break custom addon signatures, model field structures, and view inheritance without advance warning, ERPForAll enforces strict, machine-verified backward compatibility across minor releases (1.x): - **Additive Public APIs:** Core framework APIs (erp-sdk, erp-orm, erp-modules, erp-fields, erp-expr, etc.) must remain backward-compatible and additive within a minor series (1.x). Breaking method signatures or removing public API items within a minor series is strictly prohibited. - **Compiler-Driven Deprecation Lifecycle:** When an API is superseded, it must be annotated with #[deprecated(since = "1.X.0", note = "...")] directing developers to the preferred replacement. Deprecated APIs remain fully operational and tested for at least one complete minor release cycle before removal (or until 2.0). - **Automated CI Compatibility Matrix (scripts/ci-compat.sh):** A dedicated compat step runs in CI under scripts/ci.sh. It extracts the baseline two-addon extension suite from compat-baseline (which becomes v1.0.0 at the 1.0 release) and compiles and executes it against the current core codebase using an offline, local runner that reuses the workspace target directory. Deprecation warnings are emitted and reported in build logs, while any compiler error or runtime test regression fails CI loudly.

docs.title: PDF page operations, attachments, metadata and e-invoices

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

erp-pdf is a pure Rust framework leaf. Report composition code can merge byte buffers, extract or split pages, rotate selected pages, apply a one-page PDF overlay, embed files, edit Info/XMP metadata and turn a PDF/A-3 invoice into a Factur-X / ZUGFeRD container. Addons use the report integration; this is not a new addon dependency or a server endpoint. There is no new end-user print screen or deployment implied by this API.

Run foreign or uploaded PDFs inside an isolated report worker with operating-system memory and deadline limits. The library's byte, graph and work limits, and its caught Rust panics, do not contain allocator abort, stack exhaustion, upstream parser allocation or infinite loops. A caller with no isolated worker must refuse foreign input. The library opens no files, uses no database, clock or network, and keeps no shared state. No converter executable is needed. Every operation emits to a caller-owned FnMut(&[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()>. An error invalidates **all** emitted bytes, including earlier split documents. Buffer privately or use unpublished storage; publish only after the entire operation succeeds. A sink failure stops input consumption. Retry and cluster quotas belong to the caller, not a process-local singleton in this crate.

- merge(inputs, limits, emit) accepts a lazy iterator of byte buffers. It loads one document at a time, remaps object references and emits one plain PDF in input/page order. Xref and page bookkeeping grow with bounded output size; this is not a constant-memory claim. - PageSelection::new(vec![3, 1], limits) uses one-based page numbers and preserves this order for extract. Empty, zero, repeated and out-of-document selections fail explicitly. - split(input, ranges, limits, emit) requires consecutive inclusive ranges covering all pages exactly once. The consumer receives one complete PDF per call. Output bytes are counted across all results. - rotate composes a validated Rotation with inherited quarter-turn rotation on selected pages; siblings keep their original inheritance. - stamp imports a one-page overlay into an isolated Form XObject. StampPlacement supplies the six finite affine-matrix numbers in target default page coordinates. Crop origins remain source coordinates; the caller chooses translation/scale. The overlay is placed the way a viewer shows its page: a quarter-turn Rotate turns it clockwise about its crop box (the turned box keeps the lower-left corner of the crop box), and UserUnit keeps its physical size (overlay coordinates times the overlay's unit, divided by the unit of each selected target page; the translation of the placement stays in target units). A UserUnit that is not a positive number is malformed input, as is a resulting transform whose coefficients overflow or collapse to a singular matrix. Render labels/fonts in the caller's PDF renderer; this crate adds no text layout engine. Merge, extract and split are **plain reading copies**: catalog metadata, attachments, outlines, document structure and archival claims are not carried over; page annotations follow the policy below. Page associations and structural parent references are removed. This is not a general PDF sanitizer. Content streams and ordinary resources remain opaque unless stamping or form flattening needs to decode drawing operations. The profile refuses signed documents; page annotations, [forms](#forms) and [layers](#layers) have their own sections below. Unsupported cross-document page references fail instead of leaving broken references. Rotation/stamping also refuse output intents or PDF/A identification metadata; they do not certify archival conformance. Drawing operations must balance graphics and text scopes for stamping. Malformed page trees, dangling references, invalid geometry and malformed metadata fail explicitly.

Links, notes and highlights are page annotations. A reading copy has a fresh catalog, so an annotation can be carried only when it needs nothing from the old one. The caller chooses with ReadingCopy: let summary = ReadingCopy::new() .annotations(AnnotationPolicy::KeepOrDrop) .merge(inputs, &limits, &mut emit)?; if summary.annotations_dropped() > 0 { // Tell the user that some interactive elements are not in the printable copy. } | Policy | Self-contained annotations | Any other annotation | |---|---|---| | AnnotationPolicy::Refuse (default; what merge, extract and split use) | document refused | document refused | | AnnotationPolicy::KeepSelfContained | carried | document refused; the message names the reason, input and page | | AnnotationPolicy::KeepOrDrop | carried | left out and counted in the summary | Self-contained are: links to a URI; links with an explicit destination (direct or in a GoTo action) to a page of the same copy, meaning the same input document in a merge, the same selection in extract and the same range in split; and the markup types (Text, FreeText with its own appearance, Line, Square, Circle, Polygon, PolyLine, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly, StrikeOut, Stamp, Caret, Ink) with their popups and replies, as long as the parent is carried too. Carried annotations point at the copied pages. Form fields follow the [form policy](#forms). Not self-contained, and therefore refused or left out: any other annotation type (file attachments, media, 3D, redaction), named destinations, links to a page outside the copy, additional actions, chained actions, structure destinations and every action other than URI and GoTo (scripts, launch, remote go-to, form submission). The URI of a carried link is copied as it is; it is data of the source document, so show merged foreign documents with the same care as the originals. An annotation that belongs to a layer is carried with its layer (see [Layers](#layers)). Use KeepSelfContained for documents the system rendered itself (a failure there is a defect to see) and KeepOrDrop for uploaded documents that only need a printable copy. ReadingCopy::extract and ReadingCopy::split take the same policy; the summary of a split covers all its results. rotate and stamp write the whole document again and keep its annotations as they are; a reader draws them above the stamped overlay. Unsigned forms are preserved. An overlay page that has annotations is refused. Unsupported input returns a contextual error. PDF feature <feature> is refused by design marks a combination the library does not plan to process. Other unsupported features identify the missing capability.

A PDF can hide part of a page in a layer that is off by default, for example a draft mark or a print-only note. The state of a layer lives in the document catalog, not with the layer, so each operation treats it by what it writes: - rotate and stamp write the whole document again. Layers, their default state and alternate configurations stay as they are. stamp needs the marked-content sections of the target page and of the overlay page closed (PDF unbalanced marked content otherwise), so the overlay is never drawn inside a hidden layer. - merge, extract and split write a fresh catalog. The copy lists the layers its pages use and gives each one its default state explicitly, so a hidden layer stays hidden and a shown one stays shown. The layer panel order, automatic states, radio groups and locks are kept for the copied layers. Layers no copied page uses, alternate configurations and the configuration's name are not carried. A carried annotation that belongs to a layer keeps it: its layer is listed like one the page content uses. - An overlay with layers is refused (overlay optional content): draw the overlay without layers. - A document whose layer configuration is inconsistent is refused with a message that names the entry, for example a layer used by a page but missing from the catalog list. A default configuration with base state Unchanged or an intent other than View is refused by design. The exact rules and messages are in the specification, section 4.5 (docs/specs/reports/pdf-post-processing.md).

rotate and stamp keep an unsigned form as it is: the fields, their values and their appearances are written again and the result can still be filled in. A field annotation in a document that has no form in its catalog is refused. A reading copy has no form. By default a document with a form is refused. To put a filled-in form into a printable copy, flatten it: let summary = ReadingCopy::new() .forms(FormPolicy::Flatten) .annotations(AnnotationPolicy::KeepOrDrop) .merge(inputs, &limits, &mut emit)?; // summary.fields_flattened(): painted fields and intentionally invisible fields. // summary.annotations_dropped(): includes fields that could not be painted. Flattening paints each field of the copied pages into its page from the appearance the file stores for it, where a reader shows it. The values stay visible; the copy has no fields, no field actions and no field scripts. A field a reader does not show (hidden, no area, an unchecked box) paints nothing. Some fields cannot be painted from the file alone: a field without a stored appearance, a form that asks the reader to build all appearances (NeedAppearances, common after a library filled the form without redrawing it), a field that stays upright on a rotated page, and a widget directly carrying optional-content membership (a form field with optional-content membership, refused by design). Such a field follows the annotation policy: Refuse and KeepSelfContained refuse the document and name the reason, input and page; KeepOrDrop leaves it out and counts it. Check annotations_dropped() before you present a flattened form as complete: a dropped field is a value the copy does not show. Flattening XFA forms is refused. A stored appearance may itself use layers: its groups are carried with the configuration described in [Layers](#layers). A form can coexist with layered page content and ordinary layered annotations. A group missing from the catalog list is refused. Other annotations still follow the annotation policy. With AnnotationPolicy::Refuse a document whose only annotations are paintable or intentionally invisible form fields is accepted under FormPolicy::Flatten. Unsigned XFA content is preserved by rotation and stamping. Overlay documents containing forms are refused. A signed document is refused by merge, extract, split, rotate and stamp (also as overlay): writing it again breaks the signature, and a copy is not signed. Keep and send the signed original instead. Detection of signature markers does not verify a signature.

These edits are **incremental updates**: the input bytes are emitted unchanged and one update section follows, so the original is always a prefix of the output and identical inputs give identical bytes. Encrypted and signed (Perms) inputs are refused. - embedded_files(input, limits) reads every entry of the flat or nested EmbeddedFiles name tree: exact decoded bytes (all files together bounded by decoded_bytes), MIME type, description, AFRelationship, creation/modification dates and whether the catalog AF array lists it. Cyclic or malformed trees fail. Names are returned as data; nothing is written to disk. - `attach(input, data, &EmbeddedFileOptions::new(name, mime, Relationship::Alternative, modified, limits)?, Duplicate::Refuse, limits, emit) embeds a file with F/UF, EF`, MIME and the relationship, and lists it in the catalog AF. Other names stay. A name that exists fails unless Duplicate::Replace is given; then the same file specification object is revised so every reference follows the new payload. Names with path separators are refused. PDF/A-1 and PDF/A-2 inputs are refused (arbitrary attachments break those parts). - metadata(input, limits) returns Info and XMP values of Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator, Producer, CreationDate and ModDate (dates in ISO 8601 form), the pdfaid part/level and the raw packet. - update_metadata(input, &MetadataUpdate::new().text(MetadataField::Title, "…", limits)?.date(MetadataField::ModDate, date)?, limits, emit) writes the fields to both Info and XMP. Unknown XMP properties are kept byte for byte. A DTD or entity, malformed XML or an oversized packet fails instead of being dropped. Multiple RDF roots and qualified standard values are supported for an unambiguous document subject. Other subjects, nested resource fields and unknown qualifiers are preserved. Titles/subjects update x-default while retaining translations. Author sets one entry; removing qualified later entries is refused. Ambiguous subjects and conflicting standard or PDF/A identification values fail before any bytes are emitted, even when the edit changes a different field. A qualified value needs one consistent representation across its outer property and nested Description. PdfDate::new(…) takes an explicit date and UTC offset. - einvoice(input, xml, &EInvoiceOptions::new(EInvoiceName::FacturX, description, date, limits)?, limits, emit) needs an input whose XMP declares pdfaid:part 3. It reads the profile from the CII guideline identifier (MINIMUM, BASIC WL, BASIC, EN 16931, EXTENDED, XRECHNUNG), embeds the XML as factur-x.xml (or xrechnung.xml for XRECHNUNG) with relationship Data for MINIMUM/BASIC WL and Alternative otherwise, and adds the fx: properties (DocumentType, DocumentFileName, Version, ConformanceLevel from the profile) with their PDF/A extension schema. The producer's pdfaid level and every other property are kept, so Info and XMP stay equal. Existing extension-schema bags receive the new schema entry without changing earlier entries. An unknown profile, repeated Factur-X data/schema, ambiguous or malformed schema container, or non-PDF/A-3 input fails. einvoice_level(xml, limits) returns the profile alone. Merged downloads stay plain reading copies: merging two e-invoices yields no pdfaid packet and no embedded files. Structural success is not a PDF/A or Factur-X verdict: veraPDF and an e-invoice validator are not run by this crate, and producing the PDF/A-3 base document is the renderer's job.

PdfLimits::default().with(Limit::InputBytes, bytes)? changes a bound. All bounds have floor one and a hard ceiling; zero never means unlimited. The public get, name and ceiling methods expose the contract. The caller supplies these values from worker node configuration; this leaf cannot read administrator settings. An integration that adds business defaults must declare them at its owning settings scope. | Dimension | Default | Ceiling | |---|---:|---:| | Encoded bytes per input | 64 MiB | 256 MiB | | Emitted / copied-generated bytes (separate counters) | 256 MiB | 1 GiB | | Merge inputs / split results | 1,024 | 10,000 | | Pages | 10,000 | 100,000 | | Admitted source objects / emitted objects | 1,000,000 | 4,000,000 | | Graph nesting | 64 | 128 | | Traversal work units | 4,000,000 | 16,000,000 | | Decoded content bytes | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | | Metadata bytes | 1 MiB | 4 MiB | These are admission choices, not measured throughput or memory capacities. Source-object accounting includes unreachable objects across all merge inputs and new normalized/imported objects; emitted objects have a separate bound of the same value. Work is shared by library traversals within a public call. Parser-internal work remains subject to worker enforcement. Decoded content is bounded per page, with the completed stamped stream checked again; metadata is bounded per packet. Stamping also charges cumulative generated content and deep-copied resource payload/node storage against the output-byte setting before retaining each copy. This is conservative admission, separate from emitted bytes and actual allocator/RSS usage. Content decoding with non-null DecodeParms is refused rather than silently applying fallback parameters. Caller concurrency multiplies resource needs and requires caller admission. PdfError::kind() distinguishes invalid options, malformed documents, unsupported features, exceeded limits, consumer errors and caught panics. Display supplies stable contextual messages without document contents; std::error::Error::source retains a lower-level cause where available. No performance or PDF/A compliance claim is made by successful parsing or rendering.

docs.title: Query AST: saving a search and running it later

sections.text: Status: implemented. A saved search, a dashboard tile, an export or an agent tool describes its query as one JSON document, the **query AST**. Any code can parse it, check its shape, store its canonical text, and later run it as whoever is running it, with that person's rights. The decision is ADR 0045, the behaviour is docs/specs/orm/query-ast.md (SPEC-QAST), the design is docs/design/m3-qast.md. Odoo keeps saved filters as three Python-literal text columns and applies them with the rights of whoever opens them; nothing checks them until they run, and nothing bounds them. The AST keeps the second part (it always runs as the person who runs it) and fixes the rest: a versioned format, one canonical form, strict parsing, limits, a check against the current registry at every run.

A document is a JSON object with a version, a kind (search_read or read_group), a model, a domain, an optional context, an order and a page. Every object has a closed set of keys: an unknown key is an error, never ignored. {"version": 1, "kind": "search_read", "model": "account.move", "domain": [["state", "=", "posted"], ["invoice_user_id", "=", {"param": "uid"}]], "fields": ["name", "amount_total"], "order": [{"field": "invoice_date", "dir": "desc"}], "limit": 80} {"version": 1, "kind": "read_group", "model": "account.move", "groupby": [{"path": "invoice_date", "granularity": "month"}], "aggregates": [{"func": "count"}, {"func": "sum", "field": "amount_total"}], "having": [{"aggregate": "amount_total:sum", "op": ">", "value": 1000}], "order": [{"key": "amount_total:sum", "dir": "desc"}], "limit": 500} - limit is required: 1 to 2,000 rows for search_read, 1 to 10,000 groups for read_group. A larger value is an error, not a cap. offset (default 0) is at most 1,000,000. - fields is a non-empty list: there is no "all fields", because "all" changes meaning when the registry changes. - domain is Odoo's list syntax. A value can be a **principal parameter**, {"param": "uid"}, which stands for the person who runs the query: uid, company_id, company_ids, today or now. The document never holds a user id or a company of its own. - context takes one key, active_test (a boolean). lang, tz and allowed_company_ids come from the running environment, as they do for a live call; any other key is refused. - In a read_group document, order and having name a group-by (invoice_date:month) or an aggregate (__count, amount_total:sum) declared in the same document. array_agg, array_agg_distinct and recordset aggregates (unbounded output per group) are refused.

use erp_sdk::Granularity; use erp_sdk::query::{AggregateFunc, OrderDir, QueryAst, QueryLimits}; let limits = QueryLimits::default(); let ast = QueryAst::read_group("account.move") .group_by("invoice_date", Some(Granularity::Month)) .count() .aggregate("amount_total", AggregateFunc::Sum) .order("amount_total:sum", OrderDir::Desc, None) .limit(500) .build(&limits)?; assert_eq!(ast.limit(), 500);

The builder's domain(...) takes an erp_sdk::query::Json tree of the list syntax. A builder collects the same document the parser reads and runs the same validation in build, so a built AST and a parsed one accept and refuse the same things. A mistake is a QueryAstError with the path of the element: query AST $.model: invalid model name 'Bad Model': ....

use erp_sdk::query::{QueryAst, QueryLimits}; let limits = QueryLimits::default(); let ast = QueryAst::parse( br#"{"version": 1, "kind": "search_read", "model": "res.partner", "fields": ["name"], "limit": 20, "order": [{"field": "name"}]}"#, &limits, )?; // The canonical form: sorted keys, no spaces, every key written. Store it as text. let canonical = ast.canonical(); assert!(canonical.starts_with(br#"{"context":{},"domain":[],"fields":["name"]"#)); // It parses back to an equal query, and writes the same bytes again. let again = QueryAst::parse(&canonical, &limits)?; assert_eq!(again, ast); assert_eq!(again.canonical(), canonical);

Two documents that differ only in key order or in absent keys versus their defaults are the same query and have the same canonical bytes. Hash the canonical bytes if you need an identity. Store them as text, not jsonb: jsonb rewrites numbers and drops duplicate keys. QueryAst::parse takes bytes. A layer that already holds a parsed JSON tree (erp_fields::json::parse) passes it to QueryAst::from_json. Paging gives a new validated query: ast.with_page(limit, offset, &limits).

QueryLimits::default() holds the ceilings: 64 KiB of input, JSON depth 32, 512 domain conditions, domain depth 16, 128 fields, 6 group-bys, 32 aggregates, 8 order terms, 32 having conditions, 4 path segments. A host can lower any of them and never raise or disable them: use erp_sdk::query::QueryLimits; let limits = QueryLimits::builder().max_rows(100).build()?; // 0 and values above the default are errors, not "unlimited" assert!(QueryLimits::builder().max_rows(0).build().is_err()); assert!(QueryLimits::builder().max_rows(5000).build().is_err());

erp_sdk::query::run(tx, &env, &ast) checks the query against the transaction's registry and the environment's access, then runs it through Records::search_read or Records::read_group: the same statement, the same method chain, the same errors as the live call. check does the checks and fetches nothing. use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use erp_sdk::query::{QueryAst, QueryLimits, QueryResult, check, run}; async fn replay(tx: &mut Transaction, stored: &[u8]) -> Result<()> { // the text was checked when it was stored and is read again now, under the same limits let ast = QueryAst::parse(stored, &QueryLimits::default())?; let env = tx.env(); // the person running it: nobody else's rights are involved // does the query still fit the registry and this person's access? (no data statement) check(tx, &env, &ast).await?; match run(tx, &env, &ast).await? { QueryResult::Rows { rows, truncated } => { println!("{} rows; more rows exist: {truncated}", rows.len()); } QueryResult::Groups { columns, rows, truncated } => { println!("{columns:?}: {} groups; more exist: {truncated}", rows.len()); } _ => {} } Ok(()) }

- **No superuser mode.** check and run refuse an environment in superuser mode (sudo(), the System principal) with an Access error: a favourite saved by anyone must not read every record. Audited elevated replay is planned. - **The environment decides everything.** The document carries no user. A query saved by an administrator and run by a clerk uses the clerk's model access, record rules, field groups and company scope; {"param": "uid"} is the clerk's id. Nothing is remembered between runs: no compiled statement, no "this query was valid" flag. - **A field the person cannot read, or that no longer exists, fails the run** with an error that names it (Access or Validation). The query never runs with the field left out: a dropped fields entry would change what a report means, a dropped domain condition would broaden it. - **truncated** is true when more rows or groups matched than the query's limit. The ORM fetches limit + 1 in the same statement to know. - check follows the planning half of the code run uses. For plain conditions it sends no data statement; child_of / parent_of and access conditions are resolved through the database, so check may send statements for them. It does not call #[method(override)] implementations of _read_group; run does. - **Stable pages.** A grouped run adds the group-bys your order does not name, ascending, after your terms, so groups tied on an aggregate keep one order and offset paging does not repeat or skip groups. - **Time.** A query is bounded in size, not in running time. Run it under the host's statement_timeout (the HTTP server will set one per request); 2,000 rows of heavy x2many or computed fields cost what they cost.

| Error | Kind | When | |---|---|---| | QueryAstError | Validation | the document is refused: path and reason (query AST $.limit: limit is 2001; at most 2000 allowed) | | unknown or abstract model, unknown field, bad granularity | Validation | the registry no longer fits the document | | no read access to the model, an unreadable field | Access | the running principal's rights | erp_fields::Error::from(query_ast_error) gives the Validation error with the original as its source, so ? works in functions that return the shared Result.

The storage of saved queries and their UI, turning a natural-language question into a document, the RPC method and tool that run a document, the JSON Schema of the format and scheduled runs are all planned.

@erpforall/expr/restricted-host is a type-only entry point for the version 1 card host contract. It describes capabilities for the restricted JavaScript card language. The Python modifier evaluator remains a separate API. Declare the fields, context keys and registered helper signatures that a card can use. Names are closed: a declared field does not grant access to every record field, and a declared helper does not grant access to arbitrary JavaScript functions. Fields, Context and Helpers must have finite, explicitly declared key sets: broad string, number and symbol index signatures are rejected. The same restriction applies recursively to field data, context data and helper arguments and results. Open dictionaries are permitted only by the explicit JSON data type accepted by JSON.stringify; JSON.parse still returns unknown, which requires validation before use. This example is checked in web/packages/expr/tests/restricted-host.types.ts: import type { RestrictedCardHostV1 } from "@erpforall/expr/restricted-host"; type Fields = { title: string; total: number; tags: readonly string[] }; type Context = { lang: string; active_ids: readonly number[] }; type Helpers = { badge: (label: string, total: number) => string }; declare const host: RestrictedCardHostV1<Fields, Context, Helpers>; const title: string = host.record.title.value; const rawTotal: number = host.record.total.raw_value; const badge: string = host.badge(title, rawTotal); Field values are readonly wrappers: value is formatted text, raw_value retains the declared data type, and name is the declared field name. record.id is an id wrapper with numeric-or-false value and raw_value. The ADR's shorthand record.id includes that wrapper: the pinned Community card context and the extracted card corpus use record.id.raw_value. record.context and context retain only the explicitly declared context keys. Nested data and arrays are readonly. Addon helpers are registered code; they are never supplied as functions in template data, cannot replace a builtin host name, and cannot use prototype names. The contract names widget flags and selection/read-only mode flags, the specified Luxon DateTime construction and instance methods, duration results, JSON parse/stringify, pure Math members, Array.isArray, scalar conversions and the listed image, colour and formatting helpers. The Math list is explicit and omits random. The Luxon list is explicit, rather than importing the full library type. JSON.parse returns unknown, so a helper consuming its result must validate or narrow it. A host implementation must enforce its data and resource limits when parsing JSON; a TypeScript return type does not establish runtime admission. Keep the V1 contract stable. A later addon may add declared fields or helpers without changing existing signatures. An incompatible contract requires a new versioned type; editing V1 would break existing consumers. This slice adds no runtime registration service or shared state. These declarations provide authoring checks, not sandbox enforcement. TypeScript structural types and primitive/array methods cannot establish a secure member allowlist. A later delivery owns static and computed member admission, the runtime host membrane and quotas, unknown-member errors, the restricted grammar, and markup and URL sanitisation. Importing this type-only entry point does not activate those features or certify a card as safe. The compile contract tests are part of the web workspace typecheck; runtime enforcement has no acceptance result in UIX-DONE.

docs/specs/corpus/card-expr-corpus.json retains occurrences from the exact Community tree pinned in bench/odoo/ODOO_COMMIT. The extractor reads Git objects, so refreshing the source checkout does not silently change historical provenance. Run regeneration in a configured build environment: python3 -I scripts/card-expr-corpus.py --odoo-root /path/to/odoo-reference The docs CI lane regenerates and compares bytes. Its source checkout must contain the pinned commit; a missing object fails the check. Copy generated data back to the author branch and review the diff. After changing the corpus or Rust fixture tooling, regenerate scripts/ui-generated.py --write on the build host and preserve its source/output identity manifest with the generated oracle. The structural corpus includes card template roots in kanban views and standalone card/menu templates. Inherited xpath fragments outside those roots are excluded; it does not reconstruct effective database views. The Python-compatible expressions run against both expression implementations over 1,000 seeded fixture records. Named JavaScript-only exclusions are pinned visibly. Agreement does not establish restricted JavaScript behavior, sanitisation, or effective inherited-view coverage. UI2-DONE owns that admission gate.

The JSON-2 core (erp-rpc) runs in-process; the native HTTP route is /erp/json/2/<model>/<method>. ADR 0073 establishes the product namespace; ADR 0038 and docs/design/m3-rpc.md describe dispatch. Existing /json/2/ callers remain accepted as input aliases without redirecting or replaying POSTs. Use X-ERP-Database when selecting a database; a single legacy selector remains accepted, but sending both header names is refused. Domain errors emit erp.exceptions.*; session errors emit erp.http.session.*. Integrations matching exception names must use these canonical names. Status/body semantics are unchanged. In Odoo every public method (a name that does not start with _) is callable over RPC unless it is decorated @api.private. ERPForAll turns this around: a method is callable only when you mark it with #[rpc], and the mark must say what the method changes, its **effect**. Helpers you never meant to publish stay private, and the server knows which calls only read. Every Rust example here is compiled and run as a doctest of erp-test-models, like the rest of the guide.

| Effect | Use it when the method | A read_only API key | Transaction | |---|---|---|---| | read | changes nothing anywhere | may call it | READ ONLY (may go to a replica later) | | write | changes this database, reversibly | is refused | read/write | | destructive | deletes data or is hard to undo (unlink, posting) | is refused | read/write | | external | acts outside the database (mail, payment, HTTP) | is refused | read/write | Pick the widest effect of anything the method may do: a method that reads and sends an e-mail is external. The effect labels the whole call, including what the methods it calls do.
Put #[rpc(effect = …)] next to #[method]. Add model for a model method (Odoo's @api.model): the call's ids must then be empty.
use erp_sdk::prelude::*;
pub struct Book { #[field(char, required)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(integer)] pub copies: i32, }

impl Book { /// How many copies the selected books have in total. #[method] #[rpc(effect = read)] async fn total_copies(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { let copies: Vec<i32> = this.mapped(tx, Book::COPIES).await?; Ok(copies.into_iter().map(i64::from).sum()) } /// Add count copies to each selected book (10 when the call does not say). #[method] #[rpc(effect = write)] async fn add_copies( this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, #[arg(default = 10)] count: i64, ) -> Result<bool> { for book in this.iter() { let copies = i64::from(book.get(tx, Book::COPIES).await?); let total = i32::try_from(copies + count) .map_err(|_| Error::validation("too many copies"))?; book.set(tx, Book::COPIES, total).await?; } Ok(true) } /// Create a book by name: a model method. #[method] #[rpc(effect = write, model)] async fn quick_create(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, name: String) -> Result<RecordSet<Book>> { this.create(tx, vec![this.vals().set(Book::NAME, name.as_str())]).await } /// Not marked: callable from Rust, refused over RPC with Odoo's 403. #[method] async fn recount(_this: &RecordSet<Book>, _tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<bool> { Ok(true) } }
A client then calls POST /erp/json/2/library.book/add_copies with {"ids": [7], "count": 2}, or {"ids": 7} (a single id), or without count to get the default.

- Keyword names are your Rust parameter names. A missing required argument, an unknown one or ids on a model method answer 422 with Odoo's texts (missing a required argument: 'count', got an unexpected keyword argument 'cnt', cannot call library.book.quick_create with ids). - Option<T> makes an argument optional (absent or null is None); #[arg(default = expr)] gives a default. Conversions are lossless: an i64 takes JSON integers only, so 1.5 or "2" is a 422 naming the argument and the expected type. - Accepted types implement erp_sdk::rpc::FromRpc: bool, i64, u64, f64, String, Value, ValueMap, Vec<T>, Option<T>, Domain, web::Spec and rpc::Binary (standard padded base64, decoded strictly). Results implement erp_sdk::rpc::IntoRpc; a recordset is returned as its ids, as Odoo does. Implement the traits for your own types when you need more; FromRpc then needs a const SHAPE: ArgShape (erp_sdk::rpc::ArgShape) describing the JSON your binder accepts, or ArgShape::Open("why") when no closed shape describes it (see [Offering a method to the assistant](#offering-a-method-to-the-assistant)). - The parameter names ids and context are reserved (they are keys of the call body); using them is a compile error.
#[rpc] without an effect:
impl Book { #[method] #[rpc] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }
An unknown effect, or a reserved parameter name:
impl Book { #[method] #[rpc(effect = readonly)] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }
impl Book { #[method] #[rpc(effect = read)] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, ids: Vec<i64>) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }
An effect given twice (even the same one):
impl Book { #[method] #[rpc(effect = read, effect = write)] async fn total(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i64> { Ok(0) } }

An override in another addon may expose a method, widen its effect, or hide it with #[rpc(hide)] (Odoo's @api.private in a subclass). An override without #[rpc] keeps what is below it. It may not narrow the effect: the server refuses to start, naming both declarations.

impl Book { #[method] #[rpc(effect = write, model)] async fn import_catalogue(_this: &RecordSet<Book>, _tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<bool> { Ok(true) } } pub mod library_mail { use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use super::Book; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "library_mail", depends = ["library"]); #[extend(Book, addon = "library_mail")] pub struct BookMail {} #[methods(Book, addon = "library_mail")] impl BookMail { /// Now also e-mails the librarian: external. #[method(override)] #[rpc(effect = external, model)] async fn import_catalogue(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, sup: Super) -> Result<bool> { sup.call(tx, this.as_records(), ()).await } } } pub mod library_lite { use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use super::Book; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "library_lite", depends = ["library"]); #[extend(Book, addon = "library_lite")] pub struct BookLite {} #[methods(Book, addon = "library_lite")] impl BookLite { /// Wrong: read below write. #[method(override)] #[rpc(effect = read, model)] async fn import_catalogue(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, sup: Super) -> Result<bool> { sup.call(tx, this.as_records(), ()).await } } }

erp_testkit::Harness::builder([&ADDON, &library_mail::ADDON]).check()?; let err = erp_testkit::Harness::builder([&ADDON, &library_lite::ADDON]) .check() .unwrap_err() .to_string(); assert!(err.contains( "library.book.import_catalogue: addon 'library_lite' declares effect = read below effect = \ write declared by 'library'" ));

A read call runs in a read-only transaction. If the method (or anything it calls) creates, writes, deletes, locks rows, flushes pending values or sends a statement that changes data, the call fails with erp.programming naming the method: `'library.book.total_copies' is declared effect = read but tried to write 'library.book'; declare effect = write (or wider).` Odoo would quietly replay the call on a read/write cursor; ERPForAll does not, because read is what lets a read-only API key call the method.
Business methods are closed to the AI assistant unless you offer them (ADR 0188 D2 (a)). Add assistant = offer to the method's #[rpc]:

async fn set_priority(this: &RecordSet<Task>, tx: &mut Transaction, priority: String) -> Result<bool> The assistant may then use the method: a read method runs during the turn, a write or destructive one becomes a proposal the user confirms before it runs (ADR 0188 D5). The rules: - offer is the only value. It needs effect = read, write or destructive: with effect = external, or next to #[rpc(hide)], it is a compile error. - Every parameter needs a closed shape: bool, i64, u64, f64, String, Domain, and Vec<T> or Option<T> of those. Value, ValueMap, web::Spec, rpc::Binary and your own types with ArgShape::Open have no closed schema; offering such a method fails the ORM build with an error naming the model, the method and the parameter. - The offer belongs to your implementation. When another addon overrides the method, the method stays offered only if that override says assistant = offer too: an override without it withdraws the offer (it may add behaviour you never reviewed). A WebAssembly implementation in the chain also withdraws it. If an override widens the method to effect = external, or hides it, while your offer stands, the ORM build fails. - **Review rule.** Never offer a method that posts, notifies, or reaches an outbound delivery (mail, messages, webhooks, payments, anything queued for after commit). Those are external in effect even when the code path looks like a database write. Reviewers refuse an offer on such a method. The assistant reads the offered methods and their argument schemas from the exposure table (ExposureTable::assistant_offers, ExposureTable::assistant_offered); the schemas come from erp_registry::tool_schema.

The body's context replaces the context (nothing carries over from earlier calls). lang must be an active language, tz a known time zone and allowed_company_ids companies of the user, checked before the method runs. Keys only the server may set (the data loader's install_mode, module, install_filename, noupdate) are refused with 422. Every key beginning with __ is also reserved and refused with 422, including addon-defined keys: do not use that prefix for public context parameters. This is broader than the named server-only keys in ADR 0038 option (c). Other keys reach your method unchanged. If your addon adds a context key that relaxes a check, an audit or a constraint, it must be server-only (talk to the core team); the identity never comes from the context.

A client that may retry a write, destructive or external call sends the header Idempotency-Key: <uuid> (RFC 9562, v7 recommended). The server runs the call at most once per key and user: - the same request again replays the stored answer byte for byte (header Idempotent-Replayed: true); - the same key with a different request is 422 erp.idempotency_mismatch; - while the first request still runs, 409 erp.idempotency_in_progress with Retry-After; - after the user's access changed (companies, key scope, groups, the access policy), 409 erp.idempotency_access_changed: the first call did commit, but its answer is not sent again; - after rpc.idempotency_replay_secs (1 hour by default), 409 erp.idempotency_result_expired; the key still prevents a second execution for rpc.idempotency_ttl_secs (24 hours); - a call that failed stored nothing, so retrying with the key runs it again. If the server answers 500 erp.commit_unknown, the connection was lost while committing: retry with the same key to learn the outcome. Keys are refused on read calls and from public and link callers.

Error bodies keep Odoo's shape: name, message, arguments, timestamp, context, debug, in that order, with Odoo's statuses and texts for Odoo's exceptions and erp.* names for the server's own (the table is in docs/design/m3-rpc.md §11). debug is empty unless the operator turns on rpc.error_debug and the user holds the capability rpc.debug_errors; even then it shows the error chain, the SQLSTATE and the statement template, never values. A database error's message names only its SQLSTATE.

Link erp-data to contribute load, export_data, and get_import_templates through the existing erp_orm::rpc::RPC_IMPLS registration slice (ADR 0038). These are framework methods inherited by every model. The registration's base addon label is framework ownership: ERPForAll has no separate base_import addon yet. Odoo adds get_import_templates by extending base from that addon (odoo/addons/base_import/models/base_import.py:84-94). Its default result, and ours, is []. All three methods have effect write, so a read-only API key cannot call them. load and get_import_templates are model methods (empty ids); export_data takes record ids. This follows Odoo's model decorators and absence of @api.readonly on these methods (odoo/odoo/orm/models.py:924-964, odoo/addons/base_import/models/base_import.py:84-94). Export can create external identifiers, so callers must treat it as a write. JSON-2 bodies use keyword arguments: {"fields":["name"],"data":[["Example"]]} Send that body to /erp/json/2/<model>/load. Its result contains ids, messages, and nextrow; row-level import failures are reported in messages. The RPC contract deliberately requires string cells: a non-string cell fails binding before any row is read, with its zero-based row and column. The resource contract caps a call at 1,000 columns and 1,000,000 rows. The configured whole-request limits.rpc_body_bytes check runs before parsing and bounds both individual cells and aggregate string bytes (default 2 MiB, configurable from 64 KiB through 128 MiB); there are no additional fixed cell/matrix byte caps. Column and row limit refusals are validation errors; an oversized whole request is refused as HTTP 413. For /erp/json/2/<model>/export_data, send: {"ids":[7],"fields_to_export":["id","name"]} The result is {"datas": [...]}. At most 1,000 export fields are accepted. Export requires superuser mode, the export group base.group_allow_export, or the admin group base.group_erp_manager, as well as the model's read access. Group lookup errors propagate; user ids are not an authorization policy. These rights follow Odoo's export check and admin definition (odoo/odoo/orm/models.py:937-940, odoo/odoo/orm/environments.py:182-185, odoo/odoo/addons/base/models/res_users.py:1292-1294). For /erp/json/2/<model>/get_import_templates, send {}. The framework default returns an empty list; addons may override it through the existing RPC override mechanism.

The trusted native HTTP root attaches RpcCredential with RpcCall::credential. Each RPC attempt opens a fresh session transaction on the primary with the supplied CredentialOptions, exact context and read entry. Returning an elevated principal, another registry, a nonprimary transaction or a changed intent/context is a Programming error. Current resolved groups/companies govern gates, record access and idempotent replay; an earlier transport principal is only an identity precheck. Credential calls conceal error-debug details. Addon RPC methods continue using their supplied transaction and normal ORM access; they do not construct credentials or open nested transactions.

ir.actions.act_window.erp_load_web_action_views is a Read method (ADR 0100). Pass ids: [action_id], wire_major: 1, and options: {mobile: false} with normal caller context. It returns {action, views}: the same WindowAction and ViewDescription as the separate action and model get_views calls. The server derives the view requests from the authorized action and performs both reads in the caller's transaction. Action/model access, company and field restrictions, view admission and metadata bounds still apply. Any failure rejects the whole call; no successful action prefix is returned. Record data is requested separately. Existing erp_load_web_action and get_views calls remain available, including action-only related-record discovery. erp_load_web_action_ref (a model method, no ids) takes xml_id: "module.name" and returns the same window action after the same checks; an unknown XML id, a non-window-action XML id and an unreadable action get one identical refusal ([Dashboard cards](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/dashboard-cards.md#server-call)). The human client shares bundle loads for navigation and prefetch, seeds the page-local action/view cache and discards late seeding after metadata invalidation. Failed bundle loads are retried only by a subsequent explicit read/navigation. The Rust schema root is erp_views::wire::WindowActionViews. The existing crates/erp-views/examples/human_ui_schema.rs generator owns its TypeScript representation in addons/web/static/src/generated/human-ui.ts. Regenerate on an approved build host with: cargo run --locked -p erp-views --features schema-gen --example human_ui_schema -- addons/web/static/src/generated/human-ui.ts

The ordinary model Read methods search_panel_select_range and search_panel_select_multi_range accept field_name and optional search/category/filter/comodel domains. They are model calls: omit ids. Native clients use the ordinary authenticated JSON-2 route, for example POST /erp/json/2/<model>/search_panel_select_range with {"field_name":"state","expand":true,"enable_counters":true}. Range responses carry parent_field and values; multi-range responses carry values. With counters enabled, entries include __count. Categories can carry the comodel's parent link; relational filters can request a group_by field. Every source field, comodel field, category record and counted source record remains subject to the request's access and company policy. Native user API keys call these methods under their resolved subject authority. Native user keys currently inherit the subject scope; restricted/read-only native keys remain unavailable until scoped principals exist. A synthetic read-only RPC principal is a separate dispatcher-level contract. A missing, null, false or zero display limit means no display truncation. Reaching a positive limit returns {"error_msg":"Too many items to display."}. This is a display result, not a permission to disable request/work safety bounds. Counter queries apply the complete admitted domain; a display limit does not limit their input rows. For many2many grouping, group_domain keys encode JSON scalar group identities. Malformed maps, compound/null identities and equivalent duplicate keys are rejected; at most 64 map entries are admitted. Many2one grouping uses a domain instead. Unknown parameters, wrong types, inaccessible fields and malformed restrictions fail explicitly. Backend data availability does not imply that the current human client renders every panel section: its existing static selection subset and unsupported-feature notices remain documented separately.

ADR 0152 adds a top-level html_validation transport control. Omit it to preserve the ordinary success shape and use Strict HTML admission: policy removals refuse the write. Send "html_validation":"clean" to accept policy cleaning with diagnostics, or "strict" to request strict validation with the report envelope. This never changes a field's policy or access rights. Do not put the control in context or a model method signature. Explicit controls return {"result": <ordinary result>, "html_reports": [...]} on success. Consume the reports even when the operation succeeded. Each report identifies model, field, nullable language, total_count and entries; entries carry kind, name, reason, count, and sample node ordinals in sample_locations. No rejected body, URL or attribute value is included. Strict DisallowedContent errors use the normal error response with an additive html_reports member, not a successful result envelope. The envelope counts toward limits.rpc_result_bytes. Exceeding it rolls back the call. Reports include stored computations flushed before commit and are published only after a successful commit. Idempotent replay returns the original report bytes; changing the control with the same key is a request mismatch. Requests without the control retain their historical digest representation for recovery. Managed password operations refuse the control explicitly. This protocol is an integration candidate until its release notes record deployment. The [HTML field guide](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/html-sanitize-report.md#model-fields-and-transaction-reports) describes the host API and remaining preset, property, import and mail integration boundaries.

The bigint field type (ADR 0210) uses canonical signed decimal JSON strings on input and output: "0", "9007199254740993" or "-9223372036854775808". Use the string directly, or an exact bigint facility in the integration; converting it to JavaScript Number can lose information. Read/create/write/search_read and nested typed results preserve the string representation. Safe JSON integers in ±(2^53−1) are also accepted as field input. Larger numeric tokens, floats, noncanonical decimal text and values outside signed i64 receive a validation error naming the field. Existing integer and record-id contracts are unchanged. Domain operands for large bigint values are decimal strings and compare numerically. Metadata reports type = "bigint", sortable true and groupable false; grouping and aggregation are unavailable in this scalar delivery. Frozen WASM ABI1 refuses bigint operations rather than erasing the native type.

ADR 0086 remains Proposed until the designated lead merges it; the lead accepted the design in substance on 2026-10-31. A nonstored field can name search_method = "_search_flag" alongside its compute method. Declare the provider with #[search_method] inside the model's ordinary #[methods(Model)] implementation. The compiling example is ResPartner::_search_has_vat in addons/base/src/res_partner.rs; the independent fixture and override are in crates/erp-test-models/tests/search_method.rs. The synchronous signature is fn(&FieldSearchRequest<'_>, &mut FieldSearchContext<'_>) -> Result<Domain>. An override adds FieldSearchSuper<'_> as the third parameter and uses #[search_method(override)]. Call sup.call(req, ctx) to delegate. The request exposes operator() and operand(); it cannot be constructed or mutated by an addon. The context exposes the environment and original model/field through getters, plus charge_work(units) for cooperative calculation. Charge explicit iterative work with ctx.charge_work(1)? on each iteration. It supplies no transaction, cursor, commit hook or SQL API. Native addon code remains trusted Rust, not sandboxed executable code. Return a domain over stored fields or other searchable nonstored fields, with no database scan or filtering of loaded records. The complete returned predicate stays inside each relational path's existential scope. Ordinary field access and model/record/company rules still apply. Hierarchy and access operators enter ordinary preparation after expansion. Missing or duplicate providers, wrong types, unsupported operators, cycles and resource exhaustion return errors. Catching a failed continuation cannot recover an operation. Stored fields cannot declare this callback. Boolean requests accept equality, inequality and membership/nonmembership with Boolean values. Other scalar field types use typed comparison and membership operands; textual fields also accept pattern operators. JSON and range operands have no search-provider contract in this proposal and are refused. Domain null uses Value::Bool(false) for nullable scalar fields. The hard ceilings are 32 active provider expansions, 4096 expanded AST nodes, 8192 work units, 256 native AST/value depth and 1048576 copied text/value bytes per expansion operation. ORM configuration may lower positive provider/node/work limits, never raise or disable them. Returned custom nodes, opaque values and internal traversal operators (any!, not any!) are refused. Internal traversal operators are reserved for framework-generated predicates. No product performance claim is made; measurement stays deferred to milestone end. A malformed domain produced by a provider is a Programming error naming its method, model and field, including when a user supplied the original external search. Invalid original external operands remain Validation errors. Access refusals retain their Access kind; a provider does not gain permission through translation. Native relational predicates accept both Value::Domain and list-syntax operands for any/not any; providers expand before ordinary hierarchy and access preparation in either form. Framework callers that explicitly parse trusted native list syntax use Domain::from_list_native: it reports Programming errors and preserves nested provider contexts. External list constructors keep their Validation contract. This constructor does not grant a provider permission to return internal traversal operators; provider output admission still rejects them. Parsing a provider list and admitting its materialized AST consume the same operation-local budget as its raw values.

A provider can return ('id', 'child_of', Value::Domain(sub)) (or parent_of), where sub is a typed domain on the same model. This is the typed form of Odoo's [('id', 'child_of', self._search(domain))] (a tag name search that includes descendants). The sub-domain is searched with the caller's access rules when the hierarchy is resolved, exactly like a start record given by name, and the walk is unchanged (SPEC-DOM-091). The external JSON syntax has no such operand and still refuses a list of lists as a start value.

Status: model and record access are decided by the AccessPolicy (crates/erp-orm/src/access/mod.rs, not part of the published documentation) trait in erp-orm and enforced on every ORM operation by the access engine (ADR 0035; how addons work with it: [access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/access.md)). CSV access lists are parsed by erp-data (ADR 0019), and field-level permissions are declared via groups attributes in erp-registry. Compiling the ir.access rows into a policy, field access, capability resolution and authentication are delivered separately; see the sections below. ---

Odoo 20 keeps grants and filters in one table, ir.access, and addons ship its rows in security/ir.access.csv (loaded by erp-data like any CSV data file; the file name names the model). The columns are Odoo's own (odoo/odoo/addons/base/security/ir.access.csv): id,name,model_id,group_id/id,operation,domain access_library_book_user,library.book user,library.book,library.group_library_user,r, access_library_book_manager,library.book manager,library.book,library.group_library_manager,crud, library_book_own_company,books of my companies,library.book,,rwcd,"[('company_id', 'in', company_ids)]" | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | id | External id of the row within the addon. | | name | Human-readable label. | | model_id | Technical model name the row applies to (library.book). | | group_id/id | External id of a res.groups record. Empty means the row applies to everyone. | | operation | Letters for the operations the row covers, in c, r, u, d order: c create, r read, u write (update), d delete (unlink); the model accepts the non-empty subsets (crud, cr, ud, r, ...). w is not a letter. | | domain | Optional record filter (Odoo domain syntax); empty means all records. | How rows combine (Odoo 20, odoo/odoo/orm/models.py:3601-3647; ADR 0035): - A row **with a group** is a *permission*: members of that group may perform the listed operations on the records its domain matches. Permissions of all the user's groups are **OR**ed. - A row **without a group** is a *restriction*: it narrows every user's access to the records its domain matches, and restrictions are **AND**ed. A restriction never grants anything on its own: with no matching permission the access domain is empty (false). - The access domain for a model and operation is OR(permissions) AND AND(restrictions). erp-security compiles the rows into the installed policy: PolicySource loads them, the compiler turns each domain into a predicate and the ORM enforces it through AccessPolicy (section 3). What a domain may contain (user.id, company_ids, user paths, literal searches, the access operator) and what is refused, with the rewrites, is in [access-rules.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/access-rules.md). ---

Individual sensitive fields can be restricted to specific user groups directly in the model declaration. In model structs using the #[model] macro, specify groups = "..." on the #[field(...)] attribute: use erp_sdk::prelude::*;

pub struct EmployeeSalary { #[field(char, required = true)] pub employee_name: Arc<str>, // Field restricted strictly to HR Managers #[field(monetary, groups = "hr.group_hr_manager")] pub base_salary: Option<Decimal>, } Programmatic declarations configure this via FieldDecl::groups (crates/erp-registry/src/decl.rs, not part of the published documentation): FieldDecl::new("base_salary", KindDecl::Monetary(MonetaryField::new())) .groups("hr.group_hr_manager") The declared group string is stored in FieldSpec.groups (crates/erp-registry/src/spec.rs, not part of the published documentation) in the compiled registry. The engine checks it on every ORM path (read, write, create, commands, domains, order, group by, fields_get); see [field-access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/field-access.md). Which groups a user is in, and so what the text means for them, comes from the policy of erp-security, built from the group tables; the exact meaning of the text (!group, ., the technical group) is in [field-access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/field-access.md). ---

The ORM asks the installed AccessPolicy (crates/erp-orm/src/access/mod.rs, not part of the published documentation) (v2, ADR 0035), a synchronous, immutable snapshot. For a principal binding (the user, its interned groups and companies, its elevation) it answers the model-level check and returns the record predicate of an operation as an AccessDomain (crates/erp-orm/src/access/domain.rs, not part of the published documentation): a domain whose user values are parameters (user.id, company_ids, …) bound by each statement, so one predicate serves every user with the same groups: pub trait AccessPolicy: Send + Sync + 'static { fn check_model(&self, b: &PrincipalBinding<'_>, model: &ModelSpec, op: Operation) -> Result<()>; fn access_domain(&self, b: &PrincipalBinding<'_>, model: &ModelSpec, op: Operation) -> Result<AccessDomain>; // plus the snapshot's identity and generation, group interning and closure, // capabilities, explain and check_scope (the lifts and named operations of a scoped // elevation block) // (see the rustdoc) } A policy implemented outside erp-security keeps the default check_scope: it refuses every lifted rule of a scoped elevation block, since such a policy has no restriction rules to lift (what a block grants under the compiled policy: [access.md, scoped elevation blocks](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/access.md#scoped-elevation-blocks)). The engine pins one snapshot per transaction, applies the predicates in SQL on searches and record checks, memoizes record checks per transaction, and rebuilds the snapshot privately when the transaction changes the access tables (design note §3.3, §3.4). Addons change a model's predicate in code with an #[access_domain] override, and check access with check_access, has_access and filtered_access: see [access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/access.md).
The Operation enum identifies the model-level action: - Operation::Read ("read") - Operation::Write ("write") - Operation::Create ("create") - Operation::Unlink ("unlink")

- **Fail-closed**: If no AccessPolicy is installed, erp-orm installs StaticPolicy::DenyAll: every operation outside superuser mode is refused. - **SQL domain fusion (ADR 0002 §6)**: a search ANDs the read predicate into its statement, after your domain; record checks select the allowed ids with one statement per batch. Records are never filtered in memory. FALSE hides all records; TRUE restricts nothing. - **Bootstrap and test policies**: until erp-security compiles the ir.access rows, StaticPolicy (crates/erp-orm/src/access/static_policy.rs, not part of the published documentation) serves bootstrap and tests that do not exercise access: - StaticPolicy::AllowAll: permits all operations. - StaticPolicy::SuperuserOnly: permits operations only in superuser mode. - StaticPolicy::DenyAll: denies all operations. Engine tests use erp_testkit::DomainPolicy (record predicates per model and operation, group permissions, overrides) and erp_testkit::RulesPolicy. ---

base holds the policy in its own tables, Odoo's: ir.access (ir_access), res.groups (res_groups, with the implications in res_groups_implied_rel), res.groups.privilege, the groups of custom fields (ir_model_fields_group_rel) and ir.capability (ir_capability, which groups hold a named capability). Every process compiles them into one policy snapshot and re-reads them only when they change: - **Any write counts, however it is made.** A statement-level trigger on each of these tables records one policy change per transaction (the ORM, security/ir.access.csv loading, raw SQL, the cascade of a deleted model or group, TRUNCATE). Other processes rebuild their snapshot at their next transaction; nothing is cached past that. - **Your own transaction sees its own changes at once** (SPEC-SEC-018). Writing a rule or a group, or a user's group_ids, company_ids, company_id or active, makes the next operation of the same transaction flush those writes and decide with a private snapshot and the re-read groups and companies of the users acting in it. Removing yourself from the group that lets you read a model hides its records from your next search, with no explicit flush. - **Membership is read, not compiled.** A user's groups and companies are read when a transaction starts, so adding a user to a group changes nothing for other users and costs no rebuild. An addon that keeps rows the policy compiles (rare: share tables read by a grant need nothing, see models.md, signal triggers) declares the trigger on its model and registers the model, so a transaction that writes it re-reads its policy: use erp_sdk::access::{POLICY_SOURCE_WRITES, PolicySourceWrite, SourceKind}; // in Cargo.toml: linkme = "0.3" (the registration is a link-time slice)

static POLICY_ROWS: PolicySourceWrite = PolicySourceWrite::new("library.policy_row", SourceKind::Policy); SourceKind::Membership marks a model whose writes change who belongs where (re-read, no rebuild); .fields(&["..."]) limits the count to writes of those fields (creates and deletes always count). A registration naming a field the model does not have fails the server start. **Capabilities** (capabilities.md): base ships data/ir.capability.csv, which gives the core capabilities (policy.explain_others, policy.customize, principal.impersonate, audit.read, company.all, rpc.debug_errors) to base.group_system. An addon that declares a capability ships its own row in the same format; a declared capability without a row is an error of the policy build, and asking for it fails. **When a rule cannot be compiled** it denies the operations it covers and is listed by erp access report; erp access disable-rule <module.name> switches it off (see cli.md). ---

What base enforces on res.users and res.groups, and the hooks an addon has. **User types.** base.group_user (internal), base.group_portal and base.group_public are disjoint. A user may not hold two of them, directly or through implied groups, and a group may not imply two of them; both raise a Validation error naming the user or group. **Implied groups.** implied_ids is the direct implication; all_implied_ids and all_implied_by_ids are the reflexive transitive closures (cycles are allowed and closed). A user's all_group_ids is the closure of group_ids. Call _apply_group / _remove_group on a set of groups to add or remove an implied group on them and on every group they imply; members gain or lose it with the implication. A group name may not start with -. **Default groups and roles.** A user created without group_ids gets base.group_user plus the groups the group with external id base.default_user_group implies. Groups given are never completed, an explicit empty set stays empty, and a default_group_ids context key wins. The read-only role field is group_system, light_user, regular_user or false, computed from all_group_ids (typed as erp_addon_base::res_users::Role). Its search is a domain over group_ids (role_domain, four statements however many users there are) and users_with_role(tx, &env, &[Some(Role::System)]) runs it in **your** environment: record rules and active_test apply as for any search, and the result is not elevated. A group is light when its external id is in res.groups._get_light_group_xmlids: override that method to add the light groups of your addon, then every group of yours that is not light makes its holders regular users, and base.group_user_regular is kept implied by the least-privileged regular group of each privilege. The form's role toggle is an onchange on role. **The last administrator.** Taking base.group_system away from the last active administrator fails with "You must have at least an administrator user." whatever the way: a command, SET or clear on the user's group_ids or on the group's user_ids, archiving the user, deleting the user (deleting the group itself is refused too). Odoo guards only the user-side group_ids write; these are stricter on purpose. The check locks the remaining administrators' rows, so two transactions removing two different administrators at the same time cannot both commit: the loser gets a Concurrency error (SQLSTATE 40001/40P01), which Orm::run retries. Call erp_addon_base::res_users::ensure_an_administrator(tx) from your own code that changes administrators by raw SQL. **Missing groups are errors.** The rules look base.group_* up by external id. A database without base.group_system (or base.group_user for new users, or the three groups of the role onchange) is a Programming error, not a database where the rules do not apply; so is a registry without the ir.model.data model (compose erp_data::model_data::ADDON), and so is a database without base.group_user_regular when a group is created or rearranged (Odoo returns quietly there; we do not, because it would leave every regular user without the marker). The one exception is Odoo's "base is installing" state: the data loader calls Transaction::begin_base_install(&grant) with the module system's grant (ModuleSystem builds its ORM with it and lends it to the load session) around each of base's data files, and refuses a base file when its session has no grant (erp_modules::Error::BaseInstallGrantMissing). The state lives in the Rust transaction object, not in the database and not in the context (the client controls the context, a database-level SET could keep a setting on for good): turning it on needs the BaseInstallGrant of the Orm that opened the transaction (OrmBuilder::build_with_base_install_grant returns it next to the Orm; plain build() mints none, the module-install executor receives it from the build site before cron, hooks or RPC start, and it is never reachable from a Transaction or Env). Transaction::begin_base_install(&grant) is refused with an Access error for another Orm's grant or unless the transaction was opened as the System principal (the stage ORMs that Orm::rebuild makes for one module operation share the original's grant, so it holds after switch_orm), and turning it on is logged at warn; end_base_install is always allowed. A savepoint that rolls back restores the flag it had on entry. Lookups that only define sets (user types, light groups, the regular marker, internal groups) skip an absent group, as Odoo does. A group that is not saved (a new record without an origin) passed to the group helpers (_is_light_groups, _has_cycle, _reduce_to_light_groups, ...) is a Programming error; the empty set is light. **Roles.** The role onchange accepts light_user, regular_user, group_system or empty (no change); any other value is an error, not a no-op. **Two user types at once.** Two transactions that put the same user into the portal group and into the internal group would both pass the disjointness check under REPEATABLE READ (Odoo has the same gap). The check therefore updates the affected user rows first, in id order, so the second transaction fails with a Concurrency error (40001) that Orm::run retries. This covers group_ids writes on res.users and user_ids links on res.groups; a change of the group graph that merges user types is not serialised. **share.** True for users outside the internal user type; it follows the user's groups and is recomputed for all users, in one set-based statement, when the group graph changes. Without base.group_user in the database nobody is internal and every user is share = true. Stored fields that depend on share are not notified by the set-based recompute (the ORM has no public modified hook yet). **Self-service fields.** Mark the res.users fields an internal user may edit on their own record with user_writeable on the field (#[field(char, user_writeable)]). Users outside base.group_system (Settings administrators; superuser mode is also exempt) are denied writes on every other field with the field access error. This includes Access Rights users (base.group_erp_manager): they may save another user's self-service fields, but not password, login, groups or any other field (SPEC-SEC-033). The check costs no statement and fields_get reports those fields read-only. A field you add to res.users is therefore administrator-only unless you mark it. company_id is marked: an internal user changes their own default company, and _check_user_company keeps it among company_ids (below), so a self-write cannot lock the user out; company_ids stays administrator-only, so a self-write cannot widen access.
