A scoped elevation does not widen the mask. **Default company (ADR 0170, SPEC-COMPANY-025..031).** company_id is required by rule, not by a NOT NULL column (the bootstrap inserts the superuser before any company exists, and raw SQL can still write NULL): - default_get gives a new user the environment's company (tx.companies(env), first entry) for both company_id and company_ids. A System principal that names no company takes the database's only active company, and gets no default when there are several (the create is then refused, below). - Every ORM create, including sudo creates by signup/SSO addons, that passes company_id and no company_ids allows that company. Provisioning code sets both fields deliberately. - An active user's company_id must be one of its company_ids (`#[constrains("company_id", "company_ids", "active")], erp_addon_base::res_users::check_user_companies): Validation`, naming the user and the user's allowed companies (not the chosen company: a user who writes their own company_id may not read it). Inactive users and databases without any company are not checked. The relation rows are read, so an archived default company is still "allowed" and keeps its own refusal (SPEC-COMPANY-021). The check locks the membership and user rows it relies on, so two transactions that each remove a part of the same fact conflict: the loser gets Concurrency and Orm::run retries. - company_id is ondelete = "restrict": deleting a company that is some user's default company is a Validation error naming res.users; a company that is only in a user's company_ids can be deleted and the membership row goes with it. - An addon that creates users in code passes company_id (and company_ids) or creates them in an environment whose company is set. - The base 1.10 migration (assign_user_companies) fills existing rows or refuses before any fill. R1b never adds membership: active users with an out-of-set default and no active allowed company refuse; inactive users in that shape stay unchanged. R1a instead selects the lowest-id active allowed default, changing sign-in company and company-dependent values without changing memberships. See docs/user/users.md. - After 1.10, NULL defaults are legal only for the superuser and inactive users. Other NULLs come from a writer outside ORM enforcement. NULL alone is not a sign-in refusal when allowed companies exist. The idempotent assign_user_companies helper can be explicitly rerun in a supported migration transaction to repair those defaults or refuse with the affected ids. It cannot reverse historical R1b grants: see the operator guide. **_allow_sudo_commands.** res.users and res.groups set allow_sudo_commands = false: an x2many command (create, update, delete, link) from another model that targets them runs as the transaction's original user, even from sudo() or with_user(..). group.write({user_ids: [..]}) therefore cannot be used to bypass the access rules of users. Set allow_sudo_commands = false on your own models the same way when a sudo write on a parent must not reach them. Commands on these models run as the request's user in **both** directions: a command targeting res.users or res.groups always runs as the transaction's original user, so an administrator's request that works with_user(portal_user) runs those commands as the administrator again (Odoo does the same). Not yet: res.partner links (partner_id, partner_share), passwords and login (planned).

The My Preferences dialog (base.users_preferences_form, opened from the user menu) is an ordinary form view, so an addon adds its own preference without editing base: a user_writeable field on res.users, and a view that inherits the dialog and puts the field in one of its named groups. mail does exactly this for the notification choice (addons/mail/src/res_users.rs, addons/mail/views/res_users_views.xml, SPEC-PREFS-015 and SPEC-PREFS-016). The dialog has two named groups for this: other_preferences (right column of the Preferences page) and calendar_preferences (Calendar page). Inside the group, position="inside" appends after the fields already there.

pub struct UsersThread { /// How the user wants notifications delivered; their own choice, so it is user_writeable. #[field( selection, selection = [("email", "E-mail"), ("inbox", "Inbox")], default = "email", user_writeable )] pub notification_type: Option<Arc<str>>, } <record id="users_preferences_form_inherit_mail" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">res.users.preferences.form.inherit.mail</field> <field name="model">res.users</field> <field name="inherit_id" ref="base.users_preferences_form"/> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <xpath expr="//group[@name='other_preferences']" position="inside"> <field name="notification_type" widget="radio" string="Notifications" options="{'horizontal': True}"/> </xpath> </field> </record> Rules to keep in mind: - The field must be user_writeable. Without it a user outside base.group_system is refused on save with the field access error (SPEC-SEC-033), and the dialog would show a field nobody can save. Mark only what is the user's own business and what no other user's data depends on; each field of the dialog carries a one-line justification in its rustdoc. - A selection field can be a horizontal radio (widget="radio", options="{'horizontal': True}"); a short text field takes the plain widgets (email, phone, char). - Do not make a field required at the column unless every writer sets it: the database default exists only for booleans (ADR 0171), so a raw INSERT INTO res_users that omits a required column is refused. mail keeps default = "email" and refuses an empty value with a #[constrains] rule instead. Schema sync adds a new column with its static default, so rows that exist at upgrade are filled; only a row inserted by raw SQL afterwards holds no value, and that means the default. - The named groups are not on the wire: the client receives the combined form, and group names matter only for your xpath. The dialog accepts no other element than the form grammar of [human-form-layout.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/human-form-layout.md). - Test it with two addons: the dialog described with and without yours installed (crates/erp-cli/tests/user_preferences_mail.rs), and a self-write of the new field by a user outside base.group_system. ---

These arrive with the named board tasks; nothing below is on main yet: - **Access engine (ADR 0035):** the engine (record checks on every operation, the #[access_domain] chain, principal parameters) is in place, described in [access.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/access.md); still to come: ir.access compiled to SQL predicates per model, operation and group set; field access by groups and ir.capability; scoped, named and audited elevation blocks (sudo() stays in the core for parity and is refused in shipped addon code). - **Authentication:** login, credentials and API keys. - **RPC and server (ADR 0034):** JSON-2 over HTTP with request limits. - **Background jobs** ([background jobs](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/jobs.md)), **the event outbox and the realtime bus:** background jobs, the event outbox and the realtime bus. Each of these tasks adds its own page to this guide when it lands. ---

An approval policy says which RPC entry calls of users need a decision by another person before they run. It works on calls, not records (ADR 0169 D11): the writes a method makes on other models, jobs and System calls never consult it. Until the approval dispatch lands, the revisions can be drafted, checked and resolved, but no call is held for approval yet. The model refuses an active Approve or Deny revision for users with a validation error: creating, copying (with active = true) or activating one is refused ("requiring approval for or denying calls of users is not available yet in this release"; a copy of an already active revision is refused earlier, as a duplicate of its selector); a revision saved archived can be prepared, and archiving is never refused. Allow revisions and agent or service revisions are not fenced (SPEC-TRUST-026). **Who configures them.** Only members of base.group_system (Settings Administration) may create or archive revisions, and only for their active companies; a revision for every company is global administration. Every other user gets the ordinary access refusal. Each change made through RPC leaves the call's row in the audit trail. **Revisions.** One row is one revision: a selector, an outcome (allow, approve, deny) and, for approve, the people who may decide (named users and groups). A revision never changes after creation except active: to change a policy, create the new revision and archive the old one. Revisions are never deleted. The selector is: | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | company_id | one company, or empty for every company | | principal_kind | user (agent and service revisions are stored but not resolved yet) | | effect | the effect class of the method (read, write, destructive, external) | | model, method | an exact model and optionally an exact method; empty model means every model | **Which revision applies.** For a call, the most specific active revision wins: a revision of the call's company before one for every company; then model and method, then model, then every model. Two active revisions with the same selector cannot be written. The companies of a call on records that all have a company are the caller's active companies plus those companies. A create, a call on a record without a company and a call without target records (a model method) are resolved for every company the caller is allowed in, plus, for a create, the companies the new records get when known. All these companies must select the same revision, otherwise the call is refused: choosing the active company never passes over another company's revision. **Who may approve.** The eligible set is computed when the call is resolved: the named users and the current members of the named groups (through implied groups), never the user making the call or the user impersonating them, never archived, portal (share) or superuser accounts, and only users allowed in every company the call is resolved for (for a create, every company the requester is allowed in). A call whose set is empty is refused before anything is stored. **What is refused at write time.** approve for read calls; approve for external calls of users; an allow revision for agents or services; an unknown model; a method that the model does not expose over RPC with that effect; approvers on an allow or deny revision; an active user approve revision with no approver; more named users plus groups than the configured operating limit (default/hard ceiling 64); a named approver who is archived, a portal user or the superuser. Each message names the revision. **In code.** Addon code that needs the outcome of a call uses erp_addon_base::ir_approval_policy::resolve(env, tx, &call), where call states the facts of the call: ApprovalCall::on_records(model, method, &record_companies) (one Option<CompanyId> per target record, None for a record without a company), ApprovalCall::create(model, method, &known_companies) or ApprovalCall::model_level(model, method). resolve returns Unmanaged, Allow, Approve { revision, approvers } or Deny. The effect is the method's current effect in the registry; a method revision written for an earlier effect (an addon raised it) refuses the call until an administrator replaces it. Pass one entry for every target record: a record left out is not resolved for its company, while a record without a company widens the call. A caller who may not read the revisions involved gets "This action needs an approval that is not set up correctly; ask an administrator." instead of the detail; the detail goes to the server log (erp::approvals) only, never to the error's debug field. The default data ships two inert agent revisions (destructive and external calls need approval) and no user revision.

base.approval_max_approvers is an administrator-managed, database-global declared setting (default 64, inclusive range 1–64). Declared Settings storage is its only authority; an identically named system parameter has no effect. ir_approval_policy::MAX_APPROVERS remains the immutable hard ceiling. Native policy creation/reactivation and eligible-set resolution use the transaction-visible setting; a missing stored value uses the declaration default and corrupt storage refuses. Use ir_approval_policy::eligible_approvers when checking current eligibility. It bounds both named users plus groups and distinct eligible humans without truncation, retaining requester exclusions and company checks. A future decision or execution coordinator must reread eligibility and retain immutable invocation checks; this helper alone does not implement approval execution. Settings refuses a lower value while an active revision has too many named references or potential internal-human approvers. Without a requester at configuration time, the latter count excludes inactive, share and superuser accounts, applies a company-specific revision’s company, and counts the union for a global revision. Policy edits and Settings writes synchronize through the global scope row version. Ordinary read snapshots follow transaction admission semantics, without a process-local cache.

docs.title: Sequences: names, period keys and wait modes

sections.text: Status: implemented. The design is in ADR 0048 D2.2/D2.8 and docs/design/m3-base-a-seq-widen.md; the behaviour is specified in docs/specs/base/sequence-widen.md (SPEC-SEQ-001..014). ir.sequence draws numbers from a counter row (H21). An addon that keeps its own counter, such as the accounting chain table of the accounting numbering service, still needs two things H21 knows: how to **render** a document name such as INV/2026/00001, and which **period** a date belongs to, so the counter restarts at the right time. The erp_sdk::sequence module gives both as pure functions: no transaction, no database access.

use erp_sdk::Date; use erp_sdk::sequence::{SequencePattern, SequenceReset}; fn main() -> erp_sdk::Result<()> { let invoices = SequencePattern::builder(SequenceReset::Year) .prefix("INV/") .padding(5) .build()?; let date = Date::from_ymd(2026, 3, 12).expect("valid date"); assert_eq!(invoices.render(1, date, None)?, "INV/2026/00001"); // numbers wider than the padding widen; they never wrap assert_eq!(invoices.render(123_456, date, None)?, "INV/2026/123456"); // the reset period: the counter of the 2026 chain is separate from 2027's assert_eq!(invoices.period_key(date, None)?.as_str(), "2026"); Ok(()) } The five reset rules are Odoo's: Never, Year, Month, YearRange (fiscal year, 15-16) and YearRangeMonth (15-16/03). Their period keys are never, 2026, 2026-07, 2025-26 and 2025-26-07. Parts you do not set take Odoo's starting formats: four-digit years for Year and Month, two-digit years for the fiscal rules, / before the counter, - between the two fiscal years. Change them with year_digits, date_separator, month_separator and number_separator. build() refuses a pattern whose names would be misread later, for example a Never pattern with the prefix INV/2026/, which Odoo's grammar reads back as a yearly sequence. It also refuses padding above 64, more than 128 bytes of fixed text, line breaks, and digits in a separator or the suffix. Each error names the part that is wrong.

The fiscal rules need the company's fiscal year that contains the date. You compute it (Odoo: res.company.compute_fiscalyear_dates) and pass it in. There is no default, because a guessed fiscal year silently gives the wrong number: use erp_sdk::Date; use erp_sdk::sequence::{FiscalYear, SequencePattern, SequenceReset}; fn main() -> erp_sdk::Result<()> { let d = |y, m, day| Date::from_ymd(y, m, day).expect("valid date"); let bills = SequencePattern::builder(SequenceReset::YearRangeMonth) .prefix("BILL/") .padding(4) .build()?; // a fiscal year that ends on 15 April splits April into two periods let fy24 = FiscalYear::new(d(2023, 4, 16), d(2024, 4, 15))?; let fy25 = FiscalYear::new(d(2024, 4, 16), d(2025, 4, 15))?; assert_eq!(bills.render(1, d(2024, 4, 10), Some(&fy24))?, "BILL/23-24/04/0001"); assert_eq!(bills.render(1, d(2024, 4, 17), Some(&fy25))?, "BILL/24-25/04/0001"); // without a fiscal year the call fails and names what is missing assert!(bills.render(1, d(2024, 4, 17), None).is_err()); Ok(()) } A calendar fiscal year renders the same year twice (26-26), as Odoo does.

Imports and hand-typed names arrive without a declared pattern. SequencePattern::infer_from_name reads the pattern and reset rule the way Odoo's sequence.mixin does. It is tested against more than 700 names whose expected values come from Odoo's own code: use erp_sdk::sequence::{SequencePattern, SequenceReset}; fn main() -> erp_sdk::Result<()> { let p = SequencePattern::infer_from_name("MISC/15-16/01/0001")?; assert_eq!((p.reset(), p.prefix(), p.padding()), (SequenceReset::YearRangeMonth, "MISC/", 4)); // a store code is not a year and month let p = SequencePattern::infer_from_name("SHOP/0510/00042")?; assert_eq!((p.reset(), p.prefix()), (SequenceReset::Never, "SHOP/0510/")); // a name without digits keeps its text as the prefix let p = SequencePattern::infer_from_name("INV/ABC/")?; assert_eq!((p.reset(), p.prefix(), p.padding()), (SequenceReset::Never, "INV/ABC/", 0)); Ok(()) } Names longer than 256 bytes are refused. Only ASCII 0-9 count as digits.

A gapless ir.sequence (implementation = 'no_gap') locks its row for each draw. Its wait_mode field decides what happens when another transaction holds the row: | wait_mode | Lock | When the row is held | |---|---|---| | nowait (default, Odoo) | FOR UPDATE NOWAIT | the draw fails at once: Lock, SQLSTATE 55P03, not retried | | lock_timeout | FOR UPDATE | the draw waits, at most the unit of work's lock_timeout (10 s by default) | In lock_timeout mode, when the holder commits, the waiting draw fails with Concurrency/40001. This is how PostgreSQL reports it at REPEATABLE READ, because the row changed after the waiter's snapshot. Orm::run then runs your unit of work again, and the new attempt draws the next number. Keep such draws inside Orm::run and near the end of the unit, so a retry repeats little work. If the limit runs out first, the error is Lock/55P03 with Condition::LockTimeout, and its message names the sequence. Match on the condition, not on the SQLSTATE. The wait mode does not apply to standard sequences, which take no row lock. An unknown stored value is an error; the draw never falls back to nowait.

A standard sequence creates, changes and removes a PostgreSQL sequence object with its record. When the server's database role may not do that while it runs (as on a deployment, where only installs and upgrades create objects), the database refuses the statement for missing privilege. That refusal is a UserError, not a database error: it says the server cannot create (change, remove) database sequences while it runs and that the "No gap" implementation works. Every other database error of these statements passes unchanged. Only code meets this refusal: users, the administrator included, may read sequences but not create, change or remove them, so their request is refused by access first. Numbering an addon creates at run time should therefore be gapless (implementation = 'no_gap', usually wait_mode = 'lock_timeout'); numbering created by an install or upgrade may stay standard. Inventory does this for operation types (the Inventory topology guide, "Numbering made while the server runs").

A document that takes its number from an ir.sequence record (a sales order, a purchase order, a transfer) draws it with one of two calls of erp_sdk::sequence, inside the transaction that saves the document: | Call | Draws from | |---|---| | draw_by_code(tx, env, code, company, date) | the sequence with code of company; when that company has none, the shared one (no company) | | draw_by_id(tx, env, sequence_id, date) | the sequence record sequence_id, for a document that stores its sequence in a many2one | use erp_sdk::sequence::{draw_by_code, draw_by_id}; use erp_sdk::{CompanyId, Date, Env, Result, Transaction}; /// The name of a new order of company, dated date. async fn order_name( tx: &mut Transaction, env: &Env, company: CompanyId, date: Date, ) -> Result<String> { draw_by_code(tx, env, "sale.order", company, Some(date)).await } /// The name of a new transfer of an operation type whose sequence is record sequence_id. async fn transfer_name(tx: &mut Transaction, env: &Env, sequence_id: i64) -> Result<String> { draw_by_id(tx, env, sequence_id, None).await } fn main() { let _ = (order_name, transfer_name); } - **Who may draw.** The caller's environment needs read access on ir.sequence; internal users (base.group_user) have it, as in Odoo. Write access is not needed: the counter and a new date range are written by the framework. Without read access the call fails with Access. In superuser mode the check passes. - **Company.** Pass the document's company (CompanyId::new(id)? from its company_id). Its own record wins over the shared one. A company the environment may not use is refused with Access. draw_by_id draws a shared record for everyone and a company's record only when that company is one of the selected companies of the environment, as a read of the record would decide; otherwise Access "The sequence 42 belongs to a company that is not one of the selected companies." Superuser mode draws whatever the company. (Odoo has no company rule on ir.sequence and draws by id whatever the company.) - **Date.** None takes the context's ir_sequence_date, else today. A sequence with use_date_range that has no range for the date gets one for that year, between its neighbours, as Odoo creates it. - **Refusals.** No sequence for the code, neither the company's nor a shared one: UserError "No sequence with the code 'sale.order' exists for company 3 or for all companies." A missing record: UserError "The sequence 42 does not exist." Neither call returns an empty string or a placeholder, so a document is never saved without its number. (Odoo's next_by_code returns False here; erp_orm::sequence::next_by_code keeps that answer as None for parity, the draw_* calls refuse.) - **Concurrency.** Two transactions never receive the same number. A standard sequence draws from a PostgreSQL sequence without a row lock: the numbers of transactions that roll back are lost, so the series has gaps. A no_gap sequence locks its row (or its date range) until the transaction ends, so drawers take turns as described in [the wait mode](#gapless-sequences-the-wait-mode): nowait refuses the second drawer at once, lock_timeout makes it wait and Orm::run retries it. Draw near the end of the unit of work. There is no client route to draw a number: numbers are drawn by model code (the order's create), never by an RPC call from the web client.

Status: not yet released; this page describes the server lifecycle as built, with its scope and limitations. The native CLI remains the composition root: erp server --config /private/server.toml discovers addons, composes the registry and authorization policy, and opens the configured HTTP listener. erp-server uses framework services; addons do not become dependencies of the transport crate.

An application process registers in the tenant database through an ADR 0057 membership. Its node connection uses a role separate from both the request role and the schema owner. Role memberships, including NOINHERIT/SET/ADMIN paths, must not cross the request/heartbeat boundary; privilege admission examines reachable roles as well as directly effective grants. Publish that role's node-table grants through the operator command before starting the service. Request transactions must never use the heartbeat pool. Point serving configurations at prepared runtime addon trees. Release preparation excludes build tool dependencies and caches; a development tree containing package-manager links is not a runtime artifact. Node identity still checks the whole configured catalogue and refuses links in dev sources. The membership compares build, addon and shared-configuration identities. Replicas of the same service use the same canonical public_origin; their listener addresses may differ. A process becomes ready only after its settle interval and identity checks succeed. New requests check the membership's local lease fence at admission, including when the heartbeat task has not run recently. A listening socket alone does not establish readiness: probe GET /erp/health/ready and require HTTP 200; HTTP 503 means that lease, registry or required authentication-maintenance health is not ready. The GC health gate does not change the membership's separately authoritative lease fence. Registry and authorization changes use the existing SIGNAL path. A replacement publishes its complete service generation together, while work already admitted can finish on its previous generation. Failed publication remains visible as maintenance; a write is never replayed as recovery.

The interim authentication collector exists until the job scheduler owns scheduling. It uses the existing authentication collector for expired/idle sessions and old throttle state. Scheduling must preserve its sweep cursor in shared durable storage and coordinate work across replicas; an in-memory cursor that starts again at page zero after restart is insufficient. A partial failure still returns the cursor of committed work, which the scheduler must preserve before reporting the failure. A new WebApp starts with unknown collection health: HTTP readiness and both login methods are closed. Native composition publishes health through WebApp::set_login_available only from the supervised collector; an embedder must provide the same maintenance lifecycle. The server starts the collector before exposing login. A failure disables both GET and POST /erp/login while leaving HTTP and registry-refresh supervision alive. It retries with bounded 5/10/20/30-second backoff and exits on the fifth consecutive failure. A completed collection resets the failure count and reopens login. A successful privilege/state probe followed by validated NotDue may also establish or restore admission, because only successful collection advances the shared due time. Busy alone never heals a prior failure. Contention with a valid fenced batch returns Busy without waiting for its lock; it does not count as a failure of the healthy replica. Logs preserve error kinds and sanitized cause categories, and repeated lack of progress produces a warning. Node self-fencing and registry admission remain independently authoritative. A collector that stops or cannot maintain its required state must produce a visible failure instead of leaving login active without cleanup. Addon session-end hooks run under the collector's existing transaction restrictions; they must propagate errors and may not silently turn a refused operation into successful cleanup.

On the operator's termination signal the server stops admission, drains its membership, stops accepting connections and gives admitted requests the configured drain interval. HTTP cleanup, membership acknowledgements and runtime shutdown share one absolute deadline. Blocking jobs already started by Tokio cannot be cooperatively cancelled; runtime shutdown stops waiting at the remaining deadline, and CLI process exit reclaims unfinished blocking work. The drain setting is bounded; it never means an unlimited shutdown. The node lease protects admission after unexpected process loss, while scheduled exclusive work requires its own fencing at each effect.

The framework's signed anonymous preference cookie and CSRF tokens remain separate from session authentication. A per-response nonce primitive is available for shell page composition; consumers must obtain a new nonce for each response and propagate random-source failures. This slice does not claim that every page already consumes the primitive. D14 startup validation checks accepted values and cross-setting byte-budget relationships. A passing startup check does not establish runtime implementation of an otherwise pending upload, websocket, streaming or performance slice. Product performance evidence remains deferred to milestone end under ADR 0065. See [the CLI guide](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/cli.md) for command configuration and [authentication](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/auth.md) for the session lifecycle.

The SDK exports validated pure declarations in erp_sdk::settings. A native addon registers a factory: use erp_sdk::settings::{ScopeKind, SettingDecl}; fn settings() -> erp_sdk::Result<Vec<SettingDecl>> { Ok(vec![SettingDecl::boolean("my_addon.enabled", "Enabled", ScopeKind::Global, true)? .access(&["base.group_system"], &["base.group_system"])?]) } erp_sdk::setting_declarations!(settings); The macro binds the generated crate::ADDON descriptor, so its factory belongs to that actual addon. Base's base.attachment_max_bytes has a narrow canonical System Parameter binding (ADR 0193). Its declared Settings value is read from ir_config_parameter, not duplicated in the scalar value table. Both edit surfaces use the global scope lock, revision and transactional audit. Do not add a second independent value or bypass the checked services with SQL. This is a specific base policy binding, not a generic addon parameter-binding API. Only installed registry addons contribute; group references must resolve and belong to the addon's transitive dependency closure. Declarations are not generic parameter keys. Secret storage is excluded. Use the typed constructors for boolean, bounded string/integer/float and selection; no coercion occurs. A company declaration has exactly company scope, with no fallback to global values. A value of the wrong type or outside a setting's floor or hard bound is refused, by validate and by every write through it, with one sentence that names the setting and its accepted bounds. A stored value that no longer fits its declaration is refused on read as Stored setting <key> is invalid. Call ir.config.setting.erp_describe(scope), then erp_read_values(scope, keys). Read results carry a canonical decimal scope revision. erp_write_values(scope, expected_revision, changes) accepts a nonempty batch of unique {key,value} entries and checks both group policy and current allowed companies. Keep its observed revision; stale writers must reload. All values, revision and audit commit together. Native consumers can call erp_addon_base::ir_config_setting::{describe,read_values,write_values} inside their existing transaction. No node-local value cache exists; invalidation is queued on the transaction. The base Settings menu/action points at the ordinary ir.config.setting service form. Its narrow XML is <form record_mode="service"><widget name="web.settings" scope_kinds="global,company"/></form>. The metadata producer translates this into ADR 0066's typed web.form/web.settings nodes and must reject unknown attributes, duplicate/unknown scope kinds and service field children. XML source publication alone does not prove that producer or the browser integration is complete.

Settings group by the key prefix: my_addon.enabled belongs to the my_addon app on the Settings page. The sidebar uses the first authorized root menu in server order whose owning module matches the target app, including its name and icon; an app without a matching root retains a neutral initial tile, and the page shows one app at a time; a search reaches every app. To give your addon its own Configuration > Settings entry, ship a service form that opens the shared page on your app, then a menu for it: <record id="settings_form" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">my_addon.settings</field> <field name="model">ir.config.setting</field> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <form record_mode="service"> <widget name="web.settings" scope_kinds="global,company" app="my_addon"/> </form> </field> </record> <record id="settings_action" model="ir.actions.act_window"> <field name="name">Settings</field> <field name="res_model">ir.config.setting</field> <field name="view_mode">form</field> <field name="view_id" ref="settings_form"/> </record> <menuitem id="config_menu" name="Configuration" parent="my_addon_menu" groups="base.group_system" sequence="90"/> <menuitem id="settings_menu" name="Settings" parent="config_menu" action="settings_action" groups="base.group_system"/> An action that names an app opens settings for the current company when the app contributes company settings. Shared-only apps open their global scope. app must be an addon technical name (a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or _, at most 64 bytes); the view is refused at load otherwise, and web.addons does not accept it. When the page opens and no declared setting carries that prefix, the browser says so instead of showing another app. acceptance_notes ships this exact pattern under Notes > Configuration > Settings.

Secondary or integration addons (such as sale_stock or stock_barcode) often contribute configuration that belongs logically on an existing application's settings page rather than a standalone screen. In Odoo this is done with XML view inheritance on res.config.settings. In ERPForAll, addons configure this natively via the builder methods on SettingDecl: use erp_sdk::settings::{ScopeKind, SettingDecl}; fn settings() -> erp_sdk::Result<Vec<SettingDecl>> { Ok(vec![ SettingDecl::boolean("sale_stock.allow_returns", "Allow Spontaneous Returns", ScopeKind::Global, false)? .app("stock")? .block("Operations")? .sequence(20) .access(&["base.group_user"], &["base.group_system"])?, ]) } erp_sdk::setting_declarations!(settings); - **Namespace ownership**: Setting keys always carry the declaring addon's namespace (e.g. sale_stock.allow_returns). The declaring addon cannot declare keys prefixed with another addon. - **Dependency closure**: The target app specified in .app(...) must belong to the contributing addon's transitive dependencies (and be installed). Targeting an undeclared or uninstalled module is refused at registry publication, using the same checks that validate security policy groups. - **Section blocks**: .block(...) specifies the titled section inside the app page (e.g., "Operations", "Pricing", "Users"). Settings without an explicit block default to "General". - **Sequence ordering**: .sequence(...) specifies the sort order. Blocks are ordered by their minimum sequence (then title), and settings within each block are ordered by sequence (then key). Lower numbers display first. Native declarations are this delivery's scope. The WASM declaration mapping remains M2b and is not claimed as supported. addons/acceptance_notes contains the linked boolean example acceptance_notes.enabled, visible only after real installation. Its stored flag does not gate CRUD.

A block can show read-only values (a count, a company's name and address) and arrow links to a list, next to its settings (ADR 0174). These are not settings: they have no default, no write groups and no stored value, so they are a sibling declaration, PanelItemDecl, registered with its resolver: use erp_sdk::prelude::*; use erp_sdk::settings::{PanelItemDecl, PanelItemValue, SettingsScope}; fn items() -> Result<Vec<PanelItemDecl>> { Ok(vec![ PanelItemDecl::info("my_addon.open_orders", "Open Orders")? .block("Orders")? .sequence(10) .access(&["base.group_system"])?, PanelItemDecl::action_link("my_addon.manage_orders", "Manage Orders", "my_addon.orders_action", false)? .block("Orders")? .sequence(20) .access(&["base.group_system"])?, ]) } fn resolve<'a>( env: &'a Env, tx: &'a mut Transaction, _scope: &'a SettingsScope, key: &'a str, ) -> erp_sdk::BoxFuture<'a, Result<PanelItemValue>> { Box::pin(async move { match key { "my_addon.open_orders" => { let domain = Domain::field("state")?.eq("open"); let open = env.records("my_addon.order")?.search_count(tx, &domain, None).await?; let label = if open == 1 { "Open Order" } else { "Open Orders" }; PanelItemValue::info(Value::Int(i64::try_from(open).map_err(|_| { Error::internal("count does not fit") })?))? .label(label) } _ => Err(Error::programming(format!("my_addon does not declare {key}"))), } }) } erp_sdk::settings_panel_items!(items, resolve); - **Kinds.** PanelItemDecl::info(key, label) is an information row; its resolver returns PanelItemValue::info(scalar) (boolean, text, integer or finite float), optionally with .label(..) (1 to 256 bytes, for example the singular form) and .detail(..) (at most 1024 bytes, line feeds allowed). action_link(key, label, action, record) opens a window action; with record = true the resolver returns PanelItemValue::record(id) and the link opens that record. menu_link(key, label, menu) opens a menu. A plain link calls no resolver. A value out of bounds is a programming error, never cut. - **Placement and audience.** Same rules as settings: the key carries your addon's prefix, .app(..) (default: the prefix), .block(..) (default "General"), .sequence(..) (default 100). .access(read) is required. An item shows in every scope unless you call .scope(ScopeKind::Company) or .scope(ScopeKind::Global). A key is unique across all settings and items. - **Links are checked when the registry is published.** The action or menu identity must name exactly one ir.actions.act_window or ir.ui.menu row of an addon in your dependency closure (your own data included). Otherwise installing or upgrading fails at ir.config.setting._register_hook with "Setting item references an unavailable action or menu.". A release that adds a link to a new action needs the addon upgrade that loads that action. - **Values use the caller's rights.** The resolver gets the caller's own environment, never an elevated one: count with env.records(..) so access rules and record rules apply. Each call runs in a savepoint. Return an Access error to leave the item out for that caller; any other error fails the whole description. The scope tells you which company a company-scope page describes. - **Wire.** ir.config.setting.erp_describe(scope) returns the rows in items, sorted by key, beside declarations. erp_read_values and erp_write_values refuse an item key like an unknown key. The web client renders information and link rows alongside declarations. Base declares the General section this way (addons/base/src/settings_general.rs, SPEC-SETGEN): Users, Languages and Companies blocks with the active internal users, the active languages, the company's name and address with an "Update Info" record link, the number of companies, and links to the lists that manage them. Add your own rows to those blocks by targeting app base and the block title.

The native theme_office_blue addon demonstrates a global selection with internal-user read and system-administrator write policy. Install it explicitly; it is not auto-installed. Its theme_office_blue.appearance key offers default and office-blue. Settings saves use the same CAS and audit API as any declared setting. Refresh the application after saving; other open browsers see the database-wide choice on their next refresh. Uninstall removes the declaration, and fresh clients use Default without reading any orphaned value. Its CSS is declared as an installed tenant asset, not a browser preference.

The web client decodes erp_describe.items separately from scalar declarations. Only declaration keys enter erp_read_values and erp_write_values; information and links never enter the edit baseline or CAS changes. Rows share app/block placement and sequence/key ordering. An item-only app is visible, and base opens first unless the service widget explicitly selects an app. Information values and multiline detail are rendered as text. Search includes them without interpreting markup. Links use the shell-provided ServiceEnvironment.settingsNavigation capability (ADR 0184, Proposed). roots contains authorized root-menu presentation snapshots in server order; openTarget accepts the generated SettingsLinkTarget union and runs the normal action/record/menu route with departure checks. A matching module is provenance only. If several roots match, the first wins independently of a personal home-menu order. A child menu never supplies an app identity. Base keeps the General Settings content heading while its rail uses the root-menu name. A custom Settings host may pass { navigation: { roots, openTarget } } as settingsView's final options object. A description with links requires this capability. Scalar-only and information-only standalone hosts need none. A custom dispatcher must preserve authorization, dirty-state decisions and operation guards; it must not mark the service busy before asking the shell to leave, because departure may need to save that service.

Scalar setting keys may contain nested identifier segments, such as base.jobs.chunk.default.lock_ms; the first segment still owns the key. Policy group and menu/action external IDs retain their existing grammar. Use .help(text) for bounded plain-text units and range explanations. Help-bearing boolean, text and numeric controls offer **Use default**, which edits the field normally; Save persists that value with the same CAS and audit. Register interdependent values with erp_sdk::setting_groups!(factory). The factory returns validated SettingGroupDecl::new(identity, member_keys, validator) declarations. A validator is a synchronous fn(&BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<()>; it receives complete typed members and no environment, transaction or mutable values. Membership is unique, bounded, owned by the declaring addon and of one scope. Publication validates default snapshots. Overlapping groups expand to a bounded complete member closure. The Settings service checks authorization for expanded reads, locks the exact scope, compares the observed revision, and validates the complete proposed snapshot before any value/audit write. Unchanged members and restored defaults participate. A native callback cannot broaden read or write authority. Corrupt rows fail rather than becoming defaults. Keep predicates pure and return errors naming the relevant setting. Base registers the Shared jobs catalogue as the base.jobs group. Its numeric defaults and bounds come from erp_sdk::jobs::Setting; is_shared() distinguishes database policy from node capacity. Native composition injects DatabaseJobSettingsSource; each admission reads committed policy and each claimed run retains its snapshot. Settings changes publish an empty jobs wake only with their commit. Polling recovers missed hints; a failed policy read refuses new admission.

A technical value (a limit, bound, timeout, size, batch, retry or interval) is not a Settings page row. Declare it as a system parameter: it lives in ir.config_parameter under its key and shows in Technical, System Parameters (ADR 0227). Use a SettingDecl for a business choice an administrator makes on the Settings page; one key is either a setting or a parameter, never both. use erp_sdk::settings::{ParameterDecl, SettingGroupDecl}; use erp_sdk::Value; fn parameters() -> erp_sdk::Result<Vec<ParameterDecl>> { Ok(vec![ // key, label, default, (floor, hard bound) ParameterDecl::integer("my_addon.import_batch", "Import batch", 500, (1, 10_000))?, ParameterDecl::integer("my_addon.retry_base_secs", "Retry base (seconds)", 5, (1, 600))?, ParameterDecl::integer("my_addon.retry_cap_secs", "Retry cap (seconds)", 300, (1, 3_600))?, ParameterDecl::boolean("my_addon.strict_import", "Strict import", true)?, ParameterDecl::string("my_addon.partner_token", "Partner API token", "", 256)?.secret(), ]) } fn groups() -> erp_sdk::Result<Vec<SettingGroupDecl>> { Ok(vec![SettingGroupDecl::new( "my_addon.retry", &["my_addon.retry_base_secs", "my_addon.retry_cap_secs"], |values| match (&values["my_addon.retry_base_secs"], &values["my_addon.retry_cap_secs"]) { (Value::Int(base), Value::Int(cap)) if base <= cap => Ok(()), _ => Err(erp_sdk::Error::validation( "my_addon.retry_base_secs must not exceed my_addon.retry_cap_secs.", )), }, )?]) } erp_sdk::system_parameters!(parameters, groups); // or system_parameters!(parameters) The constructors are boolean, string (bound 1 to 65,536 bytes), integer and float (floor and hard bound, inclusive), and selection. Add .validator(fn) for a pure check beyond the bounds (it must accept the default), .secret() for a credential and .without_default_row() (below). A constructor refuses a bad declaration with a message naming the key: - the default must lie between the floor and the hard bound; - every number needs a floor of at least 1, whatever its key is called. Zero never means "unlimited", and an empty value means the default. A number whose 0 or fraction has a meaning (a switch-off threshold, a ratio) is declared with integer_floor_below_one or float_floor_below_one, which take the reason as their last argument. For example: ParameterDecl::integer_floor_below_one( "my_addon.warn_after", "Warn after failures (0: never warn)", 3, (0, 100), "0 turns the warning off", )? At registry publication (install, upgrade, server start) the key must start with your addon's name, and must not be declared twice by any addon, setting or Settings page item (Parameter <key> has more than one declaration.). A group may only name parameters of the same addon, and its validator must accept the defaults. What the framework does with the declaration: - **Default row.** Each declared key without a row gets one holding its default, so it is visible in System Parameters from install. An existing row is never overwritten. Do not also ship a data record for a declared key: the declaration is its default row. Use .without_default_row() when the absent value follows something a stored row would freeze: another key (base's per-login cooldown is four times the per-address one) or a floor a later release raises (the password hashing costs). - **Stored rows are checked at publication.** Install, upgrade and server start read every declared key's row: stored text outside its declaration or a group it breaks stops the publication with Stored parameter <key> is invalid. or the group's message. A migration that moves a value onto a parameter checks the same. - **Every write is checked.** The System Parameters form, ORM writes, set_str/set_int and data files all go through the declaration: <key> takes <bounds>. for a value of the wrong kind or out of bounds (the value is not echoed), then your validator and the groups the key belongs to. The whole batch rolls back. Emptying a row resets the key to its default. - **Audited.** An administrator's change takes the global Settings lock, advances the global Settings revision and writes an ir.config.setting.audit row (key, old and new value, actor) in the same transaction, only when the effective value changes (writing the default's text into an empty row changes nothing). A secret's row records (secret) for both values. Superuser-mode writes of framework code (install, default rows) are not audited, and a migration writes its own rows with actor migration:<addon>@<version>. - **Protected.** A declared key's row cannot be deleted or renamed, in any mode; the refusal is a validation error naming the key. - **Secrets.** A .secret() parameter is hidden from every caller outside superuser mode: no search, count, read, group or domain on value returns or matches its row, and get_str, set_str, a create or a rename onto the key are refused naming erp_replace_secret. The row stays hidden after your addon is uninstalled (while its code is linked). Administrators replace the value with ir.config_parameter.erp_replace_secret(key, value), which runs the same checks and returns nothing. Your addon still reads it with the typed reads below. Base also hides a closed list of credentials Odoo addons keep as parameters (erp_addon_base::ir_config_parameter::SECRET_KEYS, database.secret and database.uuid among them). - **Typos are refused.** Once your addon declares a parameter, a write of an undeclared key under your prefix is refused (Parameter <key> is not declared by an installed addon.). Keys outside every declaring addon's prefix stay free text for integrators, as in Odoo. When your addon is uninstalled its rows become plain text again. - **Typed reads.** Read with erp_sdk::params::{get_int, get_float, get_bool, get_str}(tx, &crate::ADDON, key); pass your own crate::ADDON itself, a copy of a descriptor is refused. The read is elevated (your code reads its own configuration; the caller needs no group), sees pending writes of the transaction, and returns the declared default for a missing or empty row. Stored text that does not fit the declaration fails with Stored parameter <key> is invalid.; it never falls back to the default. You may read keys of your addon and of the addons it depends on; any other key, an undeclared key or a getter of the wrong kind is a programming error naming the key. let batch = erp_sdk::params::get_int(tx, &crate::ADDON, "my_addon.import_batch").await?; Base declares its own parameters the same way: the authentication and session keys (password.hashing.*, base.login_cooldown_*, sessions.*), attachments.*, base.partition_upkeep_interval_secs, base.default_max_email_size, the image limits base.image_max_pixels, base.image_max_bytes, base.image_jpeg_quality and base.image_decode_timeout_secs ([Binary and image fields](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/binary-image-fields.md#system-parameters)) and the programmatic API key switch and limit. Those keys keep the write-time checks and messages they had before. database.* keys are not declared; database.secret and database.uuid are secrets and cannot be replaced over RPC. Settings administrators (base.group_system) have full access to System Parameters; other users have none. The System Parameters screen does not yet show a declared key's label, bounds, a "reset to default" action or a "replace secret" action. Inventory declares its stock unit limits (stock.quant_*, with the group stock.quant_retry_backoff) the same way; see [Stock quant engine](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/stock-quant-engine.md#settings). **Moving a Settings value to a parameter.** Keep the key and its bounds, remove the SettingDecl, add the ParameterDecl, raise your addon's version and add a post migration for that version (it runs before the new registry is published, so before the default rows exist). Copy each stored global ir_config_setting_value row of the key into ir_config_parameter as canonical text, check it with the declaration's check_text (a refusal stops the upgrade naming the key; never clamp) and run the parameter groups on the final values. Do not advance the Settings revision: the effective value did not change. Leave the source rows in place for one release so a rollback still reads them. addons/stock/src/migrations.rs (quant_policy_parameters) is a worked example.

Inventory declares seven company values and a database-global barcode separator (its stock unit limits are system parameters, see above). Read them through ir.config.setting.erp_read_values with the explicit scope and use erp_write_values with the observed revision. There is no mirror on company rows or arbitrary parameter fallback. | Key | Scope | Default | Domain | |---|---|---|---| | stock.picking_policy | Company | direct | direct, one | | stock.horizon_days | Company | 365 | 1–3650 days | | stock.annual_inventory_month | Company | 12 | Month keys 1–12 | | stock.annual_inventory_day | Company | 31 | Valid day of the selected month, February at most 28 | | stock.stock_move_email_validation | Company | false | Boolean | | stock.stock_text_confirmation | Company | false | Boolean | | stock.stock_confirmation_type | Company | sms | sms | | stock.barcode_separator | Global | comma | 1–16 UTF-8 bytes, no control characters | The month and day form one native settings group. A partial change validates the stored or default sibling under the scope lock; an impossible date is refused rather than adjusted. A failed batch preserves the prior values, revision and audit. Inventory managers can read company values; only settings administrators can save. The global separator is administrator-only. An effective stock.picking_policy change updates the active operation types of that company in the same transaction. Compare-and-save behavior, the RPC response and existing Settings permissions are unchanged. The native _apply_value_changes hook receives the exact scoped company and only the changed effective values. Consumer failures roll back the batch. Key-level refusals have kind Access, HTTP status 403, and the sentence Setting <key> is unavailable or access is denied. The key comes from the request. Unknown, inaccessible, wrong-scope and information/link keys use the same refusal path and do not reveal which condition applied. A denied validation-group sibling is reported using an original request key, not its hidden identity. Scope and model-level authorization errors keep their conditions and kinds; an inaccessible Settings company asks you to choose a company available to your account. Feature controls shown as unavailable are information items, never scalar declarations. Read and save only the declaration keys returned for the scope. Module links target Inventory's own Addons service action; saving settings never installs a module. Operational consumers of these values are still being delivered; the page's help states where a saved value has no effect yet.

docs.title: Store wire: sending records to the client store

sections.text: The store wire is the generic format in which the server sends records and field values to the web client: inside an RPC answer, or as a bus frame after a commit. It is owned in Rust by the erp-store-wire crate (builders, strict decoder, snapshot descriptor) and read in TypeScript by @erpforall/store-wire (decoder and reference applier). The behavior is fixed by docs/specs/mail/messaging-store.md (cases SPEC-MSGSTORE-001 to 034) and ADR 0148 D2. The codec contains no mail code: it knows models and fields only through a schema it is given. Chatter itself is described in [Chatter storage](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/mail.md). An addon cannot depend on the wire crate: it reaches the builders, the schema types and the decoder as erp_sdk::store_wire (a re-export of erp-store-wire through erp-orm); the mail thread answers of [Call the thread from the client](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/mail.md#call-the-thread-from-the-client) are the first producer.

1. The producer (a fetch topic or a bus emitter) lists the records it wants the client to hold, grouped by model. 2. For each field it builds a typed value with FieldValue. The schema decides the allowed kind; a value of the wrong kind, an unknown model or field, or an id outside 1..2^53-1 is refused when the value is set, never when the payload is read. 3. An answer is built with AnswerBuilder::new(schema, asof), where asof is the snapshot descriptor of the transaction that read the data (Transaction::store_snapshot() in erp-orm). A frame is built with FrameBuilder::new(schema, cursor, asof) where cursor is (xid, event id) and asof.own equals the cursor's xid. 4. set(model, id, field, value) adds one field; delete(model, id) adds a delete marker (a delete and field values for the same record in one payload are refused); encode() returns the canonical bytes. 5. The client decodes the bytes against its schema with the strict decoder and applies the result to the reference table (below). A payload either decodes whole or is refused with a code and a path.

The kinds are bool, int, float, string, html (typed as markup by the schema, never by an in-band tag), date, datetime, selection, many2one, reference (a model and id pair), x2many and counter. The set is closed and part of the wire major. Each schema field has a sync class: | Class | Meaning | Where its values come from | |---|---|---| | state (default) | An absolute value; its writers are serialized on a row or unique key. | Answers and events. | | counter | An integer changed by deltas; an optional cap makes "the cap or more" a valid answer. | Answers carry the absolute value, frames carry inc. | | answer_only | A value the server never announces by event. | Answers only; an event may not carry it. | An x2many field is a set: an answer sends the full id list (replace), a frame sends add and remove lists. A frame never sends a replace.

The codec cannot check these. Every producer must keep them, and each producing slice tests its part. - **A1, one snapshot per answer.** The store data and the descriptor of an answer come from one REPEATABLE READ transaction on the primary, with the descriptor read after the transaction's last write. A writing answer may mark the state fields its transaction wrote with mark_written; counters cannot be marked. - **A2, nested snapshots.** Snapshots taken on the primary have nested completed sets. This is a PostgreSQL property that the design relies on and has not been proved here (see the specification, open question 2). - **A3, serialized writers.** Every state coordinate is backed by a row or unique key that each of its writers writes, so the later of two committed writers saw the earlier one. - **A4, complete and exact events.** A commit that changes a coordinate the client may hold emits, in the same transaction, an event for exactly the coordinates it wrote: the final value for state, inc deltas that sum to the net change for counter, add and remove for x2many elements it changed, a delete marker for records it deleted. An event for a coordinate the transaction did not write breaks convergence (the negative control in convergence-property.test.ts shows it). - **A5, ids are not reused** within a model.

Answers must be read on the primary. A snapshot taken on a hot standby is not shown to nest with primary snapshots, so the fetch topics and any read routing (decision D-4 of the slice plan) must keep store answers off standbys until that is shown. Transaction::store_snapshot enforces it: a transaction routed to the read pool (effect = read RPC methods can be) is refused with a Programming error naming A2, so a producer that answers on a deployment with a read pool fails loudly until read routing can pin a method to the primary.

- The **wire major** (WireMajor::CURRENT, currently 1) covers the payload shape, the field kinds and the operations. Adding a kind or an operation bumps it on both sides together. accept_client_major refuses any other major, older or newer, with client_outdated; the transport decides the status or close code. - The **schema generation** is an opaque token on every payload and on the schema. A payload with a generation the client does not hold decodes to needs_schema: the client fetches the schema and decodes again. Change the token whenever a model, field, kind, target, sync class or cap changes.

StoreTable in @erpforall/store-wire implements the coordinate rules of spec section 4.4 and is what the client store wraps. The host decodes with Decoder, then calls one of: - applyAnswer(payload, request?) for an answer; - applyFrame(payload) for a bus frame, in the order the bus delivers them. Both return { resync }: counter coordinates that went stale (log overflow, or a decrement of a capped value) and must be fetched again. A stale counter shows no value until an answer from a request sent after the last dropped delta arrives. Requests are tracked so that a deleted record cannot be brought back by an older answer: const request = table.beginRequest();      // when the fetch is sent // ... the answer arrives and was decoded ... table.applyAnswer(payload, request); table.settleRequest(request);              // also when the fetch is given up beginRequest() returns an id; a tombstone made while the request is outstanding is kept until it settles. settleRequest(id) ends a request and releases tombstones that no longer wait for any request; an id that is not outstanding throws ApplyError. A host that never calls beginRequest gets no tombstone protection and must not apply answers that could predate a delete. Applying a payload twice changes nothing, and within one payload every upsert applies before every delete.
- Specification: docs/specs/mail/messaging-store.md. - Generated declarations and fixtures: docs/dev-setup.md, section "Store wire generated files".

docs.title: Client templates (QWeb for the web client)

sections.text: Status: implemented (erp-ui-compiler, trusted mode, base directives, rejection table, IR, codegen, coarse root source maps, limits, injection protection, native/WASM identity). Implements: ADR 0030 (Elang), design notes docs/design/m4-ui0-compiler.md (docs/design/m4-ui0-compiler.md, not part of the published documentation) and docs/design/m4-ui2.md (docs/design/m4-ui2.md, not part of the published documentation). Specs: docs/specs/ui/templates.md (SPEC-UI-003, 004, 009, 010, 015, 091, 096, 098, 100, 101, 102, 105, 106, 109, 110 whole; 007, 011, 013, 018, 024, 030, 092, 097 compile-time half). See [declared UI assets](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/ui-assets.md) for the client manifest and publication APIs. An addon's client templates live in static/src/**/*.xml, written in OWL's QWeb dialect as in Odoo. ERPForAll does not ship them to the browser as XML: at install and upgrade they are compiled on the server into one ES module per template, so the browser never parses a template or evaluates code built from strings. A mistake in a template is reported when the addon is installed. Unique original nodes and inheritance operations carry their addon, file, line, column, template and applicable spec ordinal. When changed attributes prevent a verified literal attribution, the diagnostic clears the location and lists explicit source candidates; it does not attribute an extending addon's expression to the root addon. A declaration has spec n/a.

A template file holds templates under a root <templates> (Odoo also accepts <template> and <odoo>, and so do we; any other root element is itself the file's only template). Under the root: template elements, whitespace and comments; text there is an error. DTDs, processing instructions and namespaces are refused, except xml:space on the root and the SVG namespace on <svg>. <templates xml:space="preserve"> <t t-name="my_addon.Counter"> <button class="btn" t-on-click="() => this.state.count++"> Clicked <t t-out="this.state.count"/> times </button> </t> </templates> Template names use [A-Za-z0-9_.:-], up to 256 bytes, and are unique in the whole set (all installed addons).

Expressions are JavaScript expressions with QWeb's word operators (and, or, gt, gte, lt, lte). Every name must be one of: - this and its members: the component (this.props.record, this.state.open, this.onClick); - a template local: a t-foreach variable (row, row_index, row_value, row_first, row_last), a t-set name after its declaration, the t-slot-scope object, an arrow-function parameter; - an allowed global: Math, JSON, Number, String, Boolean, Array, Object, Date, RegExp, NaN, Infinity, undefined (and console in dev builds). luxon is not a template global: Odoo templates never read it, and a component that formats dates exposes the value or a method. A bare name that is none of these is an install error (`unknown identifier 'label' … use this.label for a component member). window, document` and other browser globals are not available in templates: expose what you need from the component. A template called with t-call may read its caller's locals; the compiler checks every call site statically. Subtemplate contexts are passed via t-call-context, caller body content is accessed via 0 (<t t-out="0"/>), and recursive calls are limited to 64 levels. Refused in expressions, each with a reason: function/class expressions, new, await, yield, comma sequences, eval, instanceof, delete, void, tagged templates, regular expressions, getters and methods in object literals, a __proto__ key, comments, and any assignment or update evaluated while rendering. Assignments are allowed in t-on-* handlers and inside arrow functions.

| Directive | Notes | |---|---| | t-if / t-elif / t-else | OWL's structural rules and messages (branch order, no text between branches, one per node) | | t-foreach + t-as + t-key | t-key is required | | t-out (t-esc deprecated, a warning) | escaped text; markup(…) values as HTML; a body is the fallback for null/undefined | | t-att-, t-attf-, t-att | class/style merge with the static value; IDL properties (value, checked, …) are set as properties | | t-on-[.stop.prevent.self.capture.synthetic.passive] | a method reference or an arrow function | | Components | props are expressions; an empty value is undefined | | t-set-slot, t-slot / t-call-slot, t-slot-scope | named and default slots | | t-set, t-call, t-ref, t-model, t-portal, t-tag, t-component | base directives compiled into fine-grained reactive DOM operations and helper ABI bindings | | t-custom- | the name must be registered by an installed addon (click and portal by web); runs in a later delivery | | t-translation="off", t-translation-context | Source compilation validates declarations; explicit localized compiler APIs are described below. Assembly integration is planned. | | t-debug, t-log | stripped from production builds | Refused on purpose: t-raw (removed in OWL 2; use t-out with markup), t-call-block (OWL-internal), and t-valuef, which Odoo's OWL silently ignores (BUG-063 in docs/compare/odoo-bugs.md: write t-value="'…'"). Any other t-* attribute is Unknown QWeb directive. A plain attribute on a node is an error: a renders no element to carry it, so class or style there would be lost (Odoo's OWL drops it without a word, BUG-065). Put it on an element. The markers Odoo's templates carry on (owl, name, id, data-id) are accepted with a warning and ignored. Warnings (the template still compiles, the output is what OWL renders): the markers above, t-esc (deprecated, use t-out), and t-set-slot outside a component, whose content renders in place. Markup the browser's HTML parser would restructure (a directly in a , a
or
  • inside a

    , text directly in a

    • , or move the element. HTML element names are lowercase (

Template inheritance runs on the same engine as server views (erp-views, [views.md](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/views.md)): t-inherit="parent" with t-inherit-mode="primary" (the default: a new template built on the parent, with its own t-name) or "extension" (modifies the parent in place, no t-name). Extensions apply in install order (addon dependency order, then file order, then position in the file); a primary child sees every extension of its parent, also those installed after it. A missing parent, an unknown mode or an XPath outside the engine's subset (ADR 0027: no .., following-sibling:: or contains()) is an install error naming the template. A primary child keeps the parent's combined content, changes the root tag to the child's tag, and overlays the child's root attributes (including its own t-name), except t-inherit and t-inherit-mode. Inheritance specs run before that child's root overlay; a later extension or primary descendant can select the merged root. Ordinary server-view primary inheritance keeps its existing behavior; the template adapter opts into root merging explicitly. Use t-anchor="row.actions" on an element to declare a stable extension target, then <anchor name="row.actions" position="after"><i/></anchor> in an inheriting template. The shorthand uses the same positions and limits as XPath, including nested moves; it becomes an XPath selecting the unique t-anchor. Names contain 1–128 bytes from [a-z0-9_.@-]. A missing name, unknown shorthand attribute, invalid operation or duplicate anchor fails compilation. Anchor uniqueness is local to one complete template, including all inherited nodes; separate templates can reuse a name. A combined-duplicate diagnostic identifies both node tags and their source entries, and points to the entry that introduced the duplicate. Development output includes data-t-anchor; production output strips it. In template position="replace" operations, an exact $0 text node is replaced at its position by a copy of the target. Thus <section>$0<i/></section> keeps the target before <i/>; the target's following text stays with its original parent rather than being copied. Copies still occur after moves, retaining ADR 0027's duplicate-move prevention. This template policy is explicitly selected by the adapter; the server-view engine's existing append policy is unchanged.

This matrix describes implemented behavior and executable test coverage, not a blanket parity verdict. The numbered behavior and its historical evidence are in the template specification (docs/specs/ui/templates.md). In this authoring task, the local Community reference read for primary-root and $0 behavior was commit 98f53af0148cd4801de7c1342657573ddd005dac (templates.js:63–72, template_inheritance.js:268–278). It was not refreshed in this subtask; this does not replace the specification's historical pins or establish current upstream parity. | Case | Implemented behavior / test pointers | Partial or remaining evidence | |---|---|---| | SPEC-UI-018 | Primary/extension roles and invalid inherit mode: compiler inherit_modes | Compiler role coverage; whole browser case is not claimed | | SPEC-UI-019 | Root tag/attribute merge and descendant selectors: primary_root_tag_and_attributes_are_merged, primary_root_merge_is_visible_to_grandchildren; engine opt-in leaves server views unchanged | Final rendered-source evidence is recorded separately | | SPEC-UI-020 | Extensions change the parent without adding a named template: inherit_modes | Compiler output coverage; final browser case is separate | | SPEC-UI-021 | Inside/before/after use the existing bounded engine; inside and anchor-after run through compiler tests | Complete operation/render matrix is broader than these compiler fixtures | | SPEC-UI-022 | Outer $0 copies occupy their text position; following text and ordinary server behavior are isolated: inherited_replace_wraps_the_target_with_dollar_zero, engine template_dollar_zero_keeps_its_text_position_and_server_views_keep_append | Inner replace and moves retain engine tests; no whole-case browser parity claim | | SPEC-UI-023 | Attribute operations use the engine; joined t-if compiles: inherited_condition_attributes_compile_as_conjunction | Full token/separator and rendered condition combinations remain separate evidence | | SPEC-UI-024 | Missing parents fail at assembly and retain declaration metadata: missing_parent_fails_at_assembly, declaration_errors_keep_template_and_source_metadata | The typed compiler kind is MissingTemplate; no browser-runtime failure is substituted for install refusal | | SPEC-UI-025 | A primary child sees later parent extensions: primary_child_sees_later_addon_extensions; adapter synthetic_ids_give_load_order fixes applied IDs | Browser rendering and final exact-source execution are recorded separately | | SPEC-UI-026 | Anchor shorthand, validation, per-template uniqueness, duplicate origins and dev/prod metadata: compiler anchor tests | Locator lint and anchor API diff are UI3-DONE; generated-range source maps remain partial | | SPEC-UI-103 | Unmatched operations preserve the leaf error, original source location and BFS spec ordinal: unmatched_xpath_reports_the_offending_spec_source, engine ui_spec_errors_retain_operation_context_and_underlying_kind | XPath remains the explicit ADR 0027 subset; non-element target parity is not claimed | | SPEC-UI-104 | Invalid positions/modes fail loudly; compiler shorthand and existing engine error tests cover these paths | Final combined-suite execution is required; no whole-case UI parity claim | | SPEC-UI-110 | Invalid extensions fail the set and dependent templates; declaration and combined-expression diagnostics identify source/spec where proven | Transactional previous-bundle preservation is integration evidence, not established by a compiler unit test | | SPEC-UI-113 | Compiler outputs are deterministic and authority is outside this pure crate | Two-process serving, compatible generation and node loss require the slice's integration receipts | Source-node ordinals survive imports, moves and copies. The diagnostic mapper checks unchanged original tag/attributes before assigning a literal source. Mutated nodes use at most 16 visible candidates with an explicit omitted count. Original position tables are computed in one UTF-8 pass per file. Their index, combined mapping rows and diagnostic labels have a cumulative portable charged-byte admission budget of min(input_bytes, 64 MiB); overflow is an explicit inheritance-provenance storage refusal. This is a safety limit, not measured allocation or performance acceptance. Generated JavaScript source maps currently attribute generated lines to the root file at line 1. They are coarse maps: the precise diagnostic mapping above does not establish per-generated-range inherited source-map attribution. Full generated-range maps remain partial and must not be used as proof of an extending addon's precise generated-code location.

Per file: 4 MiB, 200 000 XML nodes, 64 levels of element nesting (Odoo's deepest client template has 19), 256 attributes per element. Per expression: 4096 bytes, 64 levels of bracket nesting. Per template: 4096 locals, 512 reactive effects, 64 recursive t-call depth levels. Per set: 20 000 files and 128 MiB of input (both checked before any file is parsed), 20 000 templates; per generated module 2 MiB, all modules 128 MiB. At most 256 custom directives (MAX_CUSTOM_DIRECTIVES). A limit hit is an error naming the limit, its maximum and the actual value.

erp-ui-compile reads a framed request on stdin and writes the canonical result on stdout; its wasm32-wasip1 build gives byte-identical output and the same exit status (the CI step ui-compiler-wasm-identity proves it). It exits 0 when the result has no error, 1 when it carries errors (the result is still on stdout), 2 for a malformed or oversized request. The framing (tagged records: operation, mode, custom directives, lowered limits, files) is documented in the erp-ui-compiler-cli crate. From Rust: use erp_ui_compiler::{ AddonName, BuildMode, CompileOptions, TemplatePath, TemplateSet, TemplateSource, analyze, compile, }; let mut set = TemplateSet::new(); set.push(TemplateSource::addon_file( AddonName::new("my_addon")?, TemplatePath::new("static/src/counter.xml")?, "<templates><t t-name=\"my_addon.Counter\"><b t-out=\"this.state.count\"/></t></templates>", )); let options = CompileOptions::new(BuildMode::Prod).with_custom_directive("click")?; let analysis = analyze(&set, &options); // every template's verdict and diagnostics, never fails assert!(analysis.is_clean()); let compiled = compile(&set, &options).map_err(|e| format!("{:?}", e.errors()))?; assert_eq!(compiled.modules()[0].name().as_str(), "my_addon.Counter");

ADR 0129 supplies two explicit pure library operations through the native SDK's ui_compiler facade. Normal compile still emits source literals and its existing translation-skipped diagnostic. compile_localized consumes a validated immutable catalogue; extract_translations uses the same literal selection rules and returns sorted module/source groups with original source occurrences. These library APIs do not install a language or select a different served bundle. use erp_ui_compiler::{ AddonName, BuildMode, CompileOptions, TemplatePath, TemplateSet, TemplateSource, TranslationCatalogue, compile_localized, extract_translations, }; // Native addon hosts may use the equivalent erp_sdk::ui_compiler facade. let mut templates = TemplateSet::new(); templates.push(TemplateSource::addon_file( AddonName::new("my_addon")?, TemplatePath::new("static/src/hello.xml")?, r#"

Hello

"#, )); let catalogue = TranslationCatalogue::new("fr_FR")? .with_term(AddonName::new("my_addon")?, "Hello", "Bonjour")?; let options = CompileOptions::new(BuildMode::Prod); let localized = compile_localized(&templates, &options, &catalogue)?; let terms = extract_translations(&templates, &options)?; assert!(localized.modules()[0].code().contains("Bonjour")); assert_eq!(terms.terms()[0].source(), "Hello");

Static text uses XML whitespace at its lookup boundaries and preserves surrounding whitespace in the emitted text. Nonbreaking spaces remain significant. DOM translation covers alt, aria-label, aria-placeholder, aria-roledescription, aria-valuetext, label, placeholder, title and data-tooltip. Component and call properties are expressions unless declared with .translate; those expressions are never rewritten as translated text. Lexical t-translation-context="my_addon" selects a module, and t-translation="off" excludes a subtree. A DOM attribute may select its own module with t-translation-context-title="my_addon" (and the corresponding allowlisted attribute names). Lookup is module, global catalogue, then source text. A catalogue language is an identity, not proof that the database has installed it. Wrong language syntax, conflicting entries and size/count limits return typed errors. Values remain literal data through HTML/JavaScript escaping; never treat catalogue values as executable templates. Ambiguous inherited source ownership is an error rather than attribution to the root addon. Both APIs validate the untranslated source through semantic and HTML/codegen admission before selection/substitution. Empty or blank translations cannot hide source errors; extraction also rejects source constructs whose codegen is deferred. Localized output still obeys its own compiler limits. Ordinary blank translations remain valid where the source structure is valid. Original element identity cannot establish the owner of text merged by inheritance. When an applied operation has nonblank raw text/tails, replacement, move or $0, A conservatively refuses selected text throughout that combined template with an Inheritance diagnostic that says the case is not integrated yet and lists the candidate sources. This may include unchanged text in the same template. Element-only insertions without raw operation text/tails remain supported; ordinary source compilation is unchanged. Do not use these APIs to claim complete inheritance/localization parity. Selected inherited attributes also refuse after an applied attribute mutation, even if its final value equals the original or is restored by a later extension. The conservative check covers DOM attributes and literal .translate properties, and may include untouched attributes elsewhere in that combined template. Original element identity alone does not prove an unwritten attribute. Ordinary callee and slot literals retain declaration ownership. Caller-context or translation-off propagation requiring a separately compiled callee specialization is explicitly refused until that integration is delivered. The broad translation case therefore remains partial. Context-preserving PO/POT and erp ui extract are planned; language-specific publication is planned too. Localized compilation must not enter assembly before its key carries catalogue content, as required by ADR 0129. Catalogue source keys and values reject NUL bytes with TranslationError::Nul, which identifies source or value and the first UTF-8 byte offset. HTML parsing can remove or replace NUL, so the catalogue rejects it before duplicate lookup or storage rather than silently changing the literal. Both module and global term builders enforce this admission; ordinary Unicode and blank translations retain their documented behavior.

A field declared tracking has its changes captured by the ORM, so the mail addon can write a chatter message at commit.
