The ORM side produces raw old and new values; display names, formatting, the user's time zone and the messages are the mail addon's. Design: docs/design/m3-tracking-capture.md. Behavior: SPEC-MAIL-049..062 (every case keeps a mail-side half).
pub name: Option<Arc<str>>,

pub state: Option<Arc<str>>, tracking = <sequence> orders a record's changes (sequence, then field name). tracking = false switches tracking off when an extension re-declares a field. fields_get carries tracking and tracking_sequence for tracked fields only. The registry refuses, with the field named: tracking = 0; a field that is not stored; a one2many; a translated or company-dependent field (not supported yet); a database-generated field; a stored computed or related field (see below); a secret field (its value would land in the history and the chatter); a field of a type the history cannot store and show (json, binary and images, uuid, xid8, timestamptz, date_range, datetime_range); and more than 800 tracked fields on a model (PostgreSQL limits the RETURNING list of the flush UPDATE, which carries the old and new value of each tracked column). A WebAssembly addon cannot declare tracking yet (its loader refuses the attribute).

- Scalar columns: the flush UPDATE returns old and new values of the tracked columns it writes (RETURNING WITH (OLD AS ..., NEW AS ...)), so capture costs no extra statement. A write that touches no tracked column keeps its statement. - Many2many: the id sets before and after, taken from the relation write in memory. - Only prepared records count. A write() of a model with tracked fields prepares its records. Records created in the transaction (including upsert inserts) or deleted in it never report changes. A write under the context key tracking_disable or mail_notrack prepares nothing; if such a write is still waiting for the flush when a tracked write of the same record follows, it is flushed first (one extra statement). Both keys are set by server-side code only (the data loader, an addon method): an RPC client cannot send them, the call is refused with context key '<key>' cannot be set by the caller (they are in the RPC's server-only context keys). - An upsert that updates a row is a tracked write. - Changes are compared when taken: first old value, last new value; A -> B -> A is no change, and falsy values (NULL, false, 0, empty text, empty set) are equal. - Computed and related fields: tracking on a stored computed (or related) field is refused when the registry is built, because only write, create and upsert prepare records; a recompute prepares nothing, so the change would be silently lost. Tracking recomputed fields (Odoo prepares them on recompute) belongs to a later slice; its follow-up task must be created. - _inherits: a child model's delegated copy of a tracked parent field is not itself tracked (describe shows it untracked); the change is captured and reported under the parent model. - The log is savepoint-scoped: a rolled back savepoint reports nothing.

for record in tx.take_tracked_changes().await? { for c in record.changes() { /* c.field(), c.old(), c.new_value(), c.sequence() */ } } take_tracked_changes flushes, drains and clears the log; it is a Programming error while a savepoint is open. The ORM runs registered precommit hooks at commit, after the flush and before COMMIT (OrmBuilder::precommit_hook, PrecommitHook::new(name, fn)); they run again while tracked changes are still pending, at most max_flush_rounds rounds, then the commit fails with a Programming error. Hooks run again only when one of them drained in that round; when none does, the loop ends and the pending changes stay unreported (as with no hook registered). A hook error is returned as precommit hook '<name>': <message> with the hook's kind.

The history messages, display names and field-level filtering are written by the mail addon (docs/addon-guide/mail.md, Record history); a status written by an addon's own statement is reported with Transaction::track_external. Still open: monetary display with its currency, _track_add and cross-model tracking (064, 065), tracking of translated or company-dependent fields, tracking of stored computed fields, a monetary-field fixture, properties fields (the registry has no properties type, so there is no properties refusal and no properties ordering), and _track_discard (SPEC-MAIL-054: not implemented in this slice; a record deleted in the transaction reports nothing, which is tested under SPEC-MAIL-052). Known follow-ups: the log is kept in memory until a drain or the end of the transaction, so a transaction that writes very many tracked records with no consuming hook holds one entry per written tracked field.

Char, Text and Html declarations accept .translate(true) or #[field(translate = true)]. Stored values use JSONB language maps. A translated field cannot also be company-dependent; computed and related translated fields remain refused by ORM construction. Scalar reads (value, values, read, web_read, exports and grouped reads) project the context language with en_US fallback. Unset/empty language selects en_US. Non-default languages must be active. Search filters and ordering use the same language projection, including a many2one comodel's order in grouped reads. Malformed or oversized language codes are refused before query shapes are cached or SQL is generated. prefetch_langs=true keeps scalar reads as strings. The transaction cache already retains the whole stored map, allowing subsequent language reads from that cache. Use the explicit typed Records::get_field_translations(tx, field) accessor to obtain erp_fields::FieldTranslations: get(lang) returns the stored entry without fallback; iter, len, is_empty and into_inner provide ordinary map access. NULL returns an empty map. Model, field and record access checks still apply. Corrupt maps fail with a Programming error naming the model and field. Records::update_field_translations(tx, field, entries) updates named translations and returns whether it changed the value. Strings set entries; Value::False, Value::Bool(false) and Value::Json(JSON null) remove named non-English entries. Falsy English updates are ignored, even for required fields; an empty string remains a real update and is allowed only on an optional English base. Other values are refused. The final duplicate entry determines the request; a final falsy English entry cancels an earlier English update in that request. Empty input changes nothing. The English no-op follows the designated lead's correction to SEARCH r1 M2. A scalar write of False clears the whole field. A scalar string writes the context language; when English is inactive, the base stays synchronized with the written language. Copy preserves the whole translation map. Required translated fields require a non-empty English base. The check runs when the record is saved (create and write). An onchange works on a draft, so a new record's first onchange succeeds while a required translated field is still empty.

Static selection fields store untranslated key strings on business records, but their human-readable labels can be translated per language via ir.model.fields.selection (ADR 0002, SPEC-FIELD-105). 1. **Reflection & Registration**: Static selection fields declared on models are automatically reflected into ir_model_fields_selection during registry reflection (erp_orm::reflection::reflect_models). Each selection value creates an external ID in ir_model_data formatted as <module>.selection__<model_ident>__<field>__<value_ident>. 2. **PO Catalog Format**: Translations in PO files target the selection label using standard model references: #: model:ir.model.fields.selection,name:<module>.selection__<model_ident>__<field>__<value_ident> msgid "Source Label" msgstr "Translated Label" 3. **Runtime Resolution**: - fields_get and describe project translated labels for context['lang'], falling back to en_US or source labels if untranslated. - Keys and item order remain immutable; only the display label is localized. - At the ORM API level, Transaction::selection_labels(model, field) and Transaction::selection_labels_for_lang(model, field, lang) resolve the localized pairs in order.

docs.title: Writing and extending addons: a two-addon tutorial

sections.text: Status: verified against the integration suite crates/erp-test-models/tests/two_addon_lifecycle.rs. Implements: ADR 0001 (addon mechanism), ADR 0005 (workspace and crate map), ADR 0009 (addon platform runtime). This tutorial walks through building, extending, installing, upgrading, and uninstalling two native ERPForAll addons: 1. **test_addon_a (Base Addon)**: Declares a new model test_addon.book, provides XML seed records, defines form and list views, and implements a custom method describe(). 2. **test_addon_b (Extension Addon)**: Declares a dependency on test_addon_a, extends test_addon.book with new fields (isbn, rating), overrides describe() using Super chaining, and injects the new fields into the base form view via XPath. ---

In ERPForAll, native addons are Rust crates that integrate into the unified ORM and view registries: crates/erp-test-models/addons/ ├── test_addon_a/                   # Base addon │   ├── Cargo.toml │   ├── manifest.toml │   ├── src/ │   │   ├── lib.rs                  # erp_sdk::addon!(name = "test_addon_a") │   │   └── models.rs               # #[model] struct Book │   ├── data/ │   │   └── books.xml               # Seed data records │   └── views/ │       └── book_views.xml          # List and form view architectures │ └── test_addon_b/                   # Extension addon ├── Cargo.toml                  # Depends on erp-addon-test_addon_a ├── manifest.toml               # depends = ["base", "test_addon_a"] ├── src/ │   ├── lib.rs                  # erp_sdk::addon!(name = "test_addon_b", depends = ["test_addon_a"]) │   └── models.rs               # #[extend(Book)] struct BookExtension └── views/ └── book_views.xml          # XPath inheritance patching test_addon_a.view_book_form ---

The base addon declares the core business entity and its default views. The snippets follow the fixtures in crates/erp-test-models/addons/test_addon_a and test_addon_b, abbreviated: the real Cargo.toml files take their versions and lints from the workspace (.workspace = true), which needs a Cargo workspace.
[package] name = "erp-addon-test_addon_a" version = "1.0.0" edition = "2021" description = "Fixture addon test_addon_a: two-addon suite base" [dependencies] erp-sdk = { workspace = true }
name = "Test Addon A" summary = "Fixture: defines test_addon.book (two-addon suite)" version = "1.0.0" depends = ["base"] data = [ "data/books.xml", "views/book_views.xml", ]
//! Fixture addon test_addon_a: defines test_addon.book, views, data and describe method. pub mod models; pub use models::*; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "test_addon_a");
use erp_sdk::prelude::*; /// test_addon.book.

pub struct Book { /// Book title. #[field(char, required = true)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, /// Author name. #[field(char)] pub author: Option<Arc<str>>, /// Publication year. #[field(integer)] pub published_year: i32, }

impl Book { /// describe(): returns title and author. #[method] pub async fn describe(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<String> { let name = this.get(tx, Book::NAME).await?; let author = this.get(tx, Book::AUTHOR).await?; Ok(format!( "{} by {}", name.as_deref().unwrap_or("?"), author.as_deref().unwrap_or("Anonymous") )) } }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <odoo> <record id="book_dune" model="test_addon.book"> <field name="name">Dune</field> <field name="author">Frank Herbert</field> <field name="published_year">1965</field> </record> <record id="book_foundation" model="test_addon.book"> <field name="name">Foundation</field> <field name="author">Isaac Asimov</field> <field name="published_year">1951</field> </record> </odoo>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <odoo> <record id="view_book_tree" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">test_addon.book.tree</field> <field name="model">test_addon.book</field> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <list string="Books"> <field name="name"/> <field name="author"/> <field name="published_year"/> </list> </field> </record> <record id="view_book_form" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">test_addon.book.form</field> <field name="model">test_addon.book</field> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <form string="Book"> <sheet> <group> <field name="name"/> <field name="author"/> <field name="published_year"/> </group> </sheet> </form> </field> </record> </odoo> ---
The extension addon enhances test_addon.book by adding fields, overriding behavior, and patching views.

[package] name = "erp-addon-test_addon_b" version = "1.0.0" edition = "2021" description = "Fixture addon test_addon_b: extends test_addon_a" [dependencies] erp-sdk = { workspace = true } erp-addon-test_addon_a = { workspace = true }
name = "Test Addon B" summary = "Fixture: extends test_addon.book with ISBN, rating and inherited view" version = "1.0.0" depends = ["base", "test_addon_a"] data = [ "views/book_views.xml", ]
//! Fixture addon test_addon_b: extends test_addon.book. pub mod models; pub use models::*; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "test_addon_b", depends = ["test_addon_a"]);
use erp_addon_test_addon_a::Book; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; /// test_addon_b's extension of test_addon.book.
pub struct BookExtension { /// ISBN. #[field(char, string = "ISBN")] pub isbn: Option<Arc<str>>, /// Rating. #[field(float, string = "Rating")] pub rating: f64, }

impl BookExtension { /// Appends the rating to the base description using Super chaining. #[method(override)] pub async fn describe( this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, sup: Super, ) -> Result<String> { let base_desc = sup.call(tx, this.as_records(), ()).await?; let rating = this.get(tx, BookExtension::RATING).await?; Ok(format!("{base_desc} (Rating: {rating:.1})")) } }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <odoo> <record id="view_book_form_inherit" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">test_addon.book.form.inherit</field> <field name="model">test_addon.book</field> <field name="inherit_id" ref="test_addon_a.view_book_form"/> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <xpath expr="//field[@name='published_year']" position="after"> <field name="isbn"/> <field name="rating"/> </xpath> </field> </record> </odoo> ---

Install both modules into your database with one command. --addons-path defaults to ./addons; the two fixture addons live in crates/erp-test-models/addons, so name that directory (or use your own addons directory): erp module install -d mydb --addons-path crates/erp-test-models/addons test_addon_a test_addon_b The dependency resolver orders the modules by their depends, so test_addon_a is loaded before test_addon_b.

The lifecycle test (crates/erp-test-models/tests/two_addon_lifecycle.rs) builds the module system from a database pool and the addon index, links the native code of the three addons, initializes the database and installs one addon at a time (abbreviated; the test also binds each fixture's artifact identity with .native_artifact_identities(...)): let system = ModuleSystem::builder(db.pool().clone(), index) .code([ &erp_addon_base::ADDON, &erp_addon_test_addon_a::ADDON, &erp_addon_test_addon_b::ADDON, ]) .build()?; let init = system .initialize(InitOptions::new().with_skip_auto_install(true)) .await?; // su gives a superuser environment on the given ORM; each install returns the updated ORM. let outcome_a = system .button_immediate_install(&su(&init.orm), &[n("test_addon_a")]) .await?; let outcome_b = system .button_immediate_install(&su(&outcome_a.orm), &[n("test_addon_b")]) .await?;

1. **Database Schema**: The table test_addon_book is created in PostgreSQL with both base and extended columns: - Base columns: id, name, author, published_year - Extension columns: isbn, rating - System audit columns: create_uid, create_date, write_uid, write_date 2. **Data Records**: Seed records from data/books.xml are inserted, and their external identifiers are recorded in ir_model_data: - test_addon_a.book_dune - test_addon_a.book_foundation 3. **Combined View Evaluation**: When the web client requests the form view via get_views, the view combination engine applies the XPath patch from test_addon_b.view_book_form_inherit: <form string="Book"> <sheet> <group> <field name="name"/> <field name="author"/> <field name="published_year"/> <field name="isbn"/> <field name="rating"/> </group> </sheet> </form> 4. **Method Override Chaining**: Calling book.describe(&mut tx) executes BookExtension::describe, which invokes sup.call(...) to get the base description before formatting the rating: Dune by Frank Herbert (Rating: 4.8) (after the test sets Dune's rating to 4.8; the override formats the rating with one decimal). ---

When upgrading an addon (e.g. after adding fields or updating seed data), run: erp module upgrade -d mydb test_addon_a The upgrade is one PostgreSQL transaction (ADR 0009 §2). The lifecycle test checks that both addons stay installed and that Dune keeps its rating across the upgrade. What an upgrade does with migrations, noupdate records and removed external ids is described in [modules](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/modules.md) and [data files](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/data-files.md). ---

Uninstalling test_addon_a while test_addon_b is installed also uninstalls test_addon_b, as in Odoo: a live run cascades to the installed dependents and reports them. To see the effect first, use --dry-run, which plans without database state and refuses when an available addon depends on the one you named: erp module uninstall -d mydb --addons-path crates/erp-test-models/addons --dry-run test_addon_a cannot uninstall module 'test_addon_a' because module 'test_addon_b' depends on it (conservative plan-only check on available addons; a live run cascades to the installed dependents)

To remove the functionality cleanly: 1. **Uninstall the dependent extension first**: erp module uninstall -d mydb test_addon_b - Extended columns isbn and rating are safely dropped from test_addon_book. - The inherited view patch view_book_form_inherit is deleted, restoring the original form view. - ir_model_data rows for test_addon_b are purged. 2. **Uninstall the base module**: erp module uninstall -d mydb test_addon_a - The table test_addon_book is dropped. - The base views, actions, menus, and external ID entries are purged from the database. - Module state in ir_module_module transitions to uninstalled. ---

- **One transaction per operation**: an install, upgrade or uninstall is one PostgreSQL transaction (ADR 0009 §2); when anything fails, nothing of the operation is kept. See [modules](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/modules.md#one-transaction-per-operation). - **Strongly Typed Extension**: Extensions use Rust's type system with #[extend(Model)] and explicit Super chaining instead of loose string dispatch. - **Fail loudly**: an unknown module is refused with an error that names it.

UI3 base compiles inherited templates on the server during addon installation or upgrade. The web addon owns publication. A failed declaration, inheritance operation or compile aborts that transaction and preserves the previously committed bundle. Requests fetch admitted bytes; they never repair or rebuild an addon.

Ship static/dist/manifest.json with every client-bearing addon. An absent manifest explicitly means no declared client assets. Unknown fields are errors. Every listed file must exist inside the addon; absolute paths, traversal, encoding tricks, symlinks and unsupported media fail admission. The current host runtime ABI is elang-1; a package must declare that exact ABI. { "schema": 1, "runtime_abi": "elang-1", "entry": "@example/client", "modules": [ {"path": "static/dist/client.js", "specifier": "@example/client"} ], "templates": ["static/src/templates/example.xml"], "static_files": ["static/description/icon.svg"] } entry is optional; if present it names a declared module exporting register(ctx). Modules arrive prebuilt as UTF-8 ES modules. The developer/CI build owns JavaScript syntax, module imports and the register-export contract. Assembly preserves their supplied legal comments. Production rejects source-map directives. Declaring XML requires a dist module for @erpforall/elang/abi in the same complete addon set; a monolithic client bundle is not that bare-module declaration. Compiled-template names retain their accepted colon syntax in the import map; all targets remain declared local content hashes. See [template inheritance](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/templates.md) for primary roots, anchors and diagnostics. Inputs follow dependency/load order, then declared file and document order. A primary child sees all parent extensions, including later addons. Keys include length-prefixed compiler identity, runtime ABI, canonical limits, mode, ordered source identities, language and group. This slice supports group main; other groups fail with an error saying lazy groups are not available yet. Language is part of identity; the host still uses source compilation. The explicit pure localized compiler API is documented in [client templates](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/templates.md#compiler-localization); wiring it into publication is planned and must include catalogue content in the bundle key. No language-serving parity is implied.

The native CLI registers the same asset admission and durable registry signal for generic module operations as for the server and package operations. Hosts register trusted erp_modules::LifecycleHook services with ModuleSystemBuilder::lifecycle_hook. Package/WASM admission runs first; services run afterward in registration order for initialization, install, upgrade, uninstall and reinitialization. LifecycleChange exposes the final active AddonEntry set in load order. All durable effects stay in the supplied transaction. A custom host using startup admission must configure the durable Signal on every module writer; native server, package and generic CLI composition do so. A callback failure rolls back the whole operation. Ordinary loads use separate startup compatibility admission. The CLI connects that seam to erp_cli::ui_assets::AssetLifecycle. Source collection and compiler/ compression work run on a blocking worker; the transaction stays in the async operation. Archive assets come from the separately retained, integrity-verified client-file map, never from an unverified filesystem or the data loader's file map. Keep the LoadOutcome or OperationOutcome when composing another host service. Both expose admitted_addons(): the final effective addon entries in the same dependency/load order used by the registry. A forced-update load retains its committed operation's entries. For filesystem addons, AddonEntry::admitted_files() borrows the exact immutable byte map captured during source admission. Package client bytes stay in the separate verified PackageData::client_files map. Neither accessor reopens a live source path. The CLI passes those retained entries directly from Node::load to startup asset admission. The host also passes an explicit durable Generations baseline read before the entire load, including source capture. After taking the module and asset locks, startup compares the current registry generation before assembling or publishing. A concurrent install, upgrade or uninstall returns a Concurrency error requiring a fresh load; startup cannot replace the newer committed addon bundle with its retained old snapshot. Native lifecycle writers use the shared signal so that their registry-generation bump commits atomically with their addon and asset changes. The asset collector uses an admitted snapshot whenever present, including when the live files have changed since admission. Host callbacks must not rediscover entries or replace captured bytes with a later directory read. A fresh load or lifecycle operation establishes its own source snapshot; the appropriate source and lifecycle checks apply there. These source accessors do not grant request access, enroll identity or change ordinary load's existing durable-receipt policy. Upgrade/uninstall still use ADR 0097's installed identity checks. An operator's explicit forward candidate supplies verified previous receipts through ModuleSystemBuilder::identity_previous; failed migration or asset assembly preserves those receipts alongside the previous bundle. See [installed addon identity administration](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/cli.md#installed-addon-identity). erp_addon_web::assets::assembly is the pure assembly API. Its validated result supplies blobs, imports, preload URLs, registration order and exact static-file mappings. Its register_module() exports an ordered registrations array of { id, register } entries retaining the original functions, for the existing runtime registerAddons consumer to supply per-addon contexts and validate synchronous return values. Assembly does not invoke addon JavaScript on the server. Durable manifests store metadata and content references; bytea blob rows hold identity, gzip and Brotli representations. The server's PublishedAssets is a verified snapshot selected from one database, independent of the disposable node content cache. Sharing cached bytes never grants another database a route. AssembledBundle::register_module() supplies an external ES module exporting an ordered registrations array of { id, register } entries. Each callback is the original imported addon function. A host consumer passes that array to Elang's existing `registerAddons(registrations, { registry })` API; it supplies each addon's context and patch ownership and refuses Promise or non-void/non-null returns. There is no asynchronous bundle wrapper and importing the module has no registration side effects. preloads() includes the registration module URL and declared module URLs. These getters are host integration APIs; activating addon entries in the current HumanApp is a separate client integration. Publication checks the compatible grace history inside the same transaction before success. Combined retained metadata is limited to 16 MiB and 40,001 content references, with at most 256 generations. Repeated artifact representations across generations are charged against a 384 MiB admission budget. Their combined serving URLs must fit the server's 40,001-URL / 128 MiB raw-byte protocol limits. A new bundle that exceeds these bounds refuses the transaction, preserving the prior committed bundle; history is not silently shortened. These are safety/admission limits, not measured performance results. Storage readers guard payload sizes before transferring them and verify exact manifest identity, media declarations and content references.

UI3 base owns transactional compilation/publication, primary roots/anchors, content identity, precompressed forms, exact declarations, nonce/CSP and runtime admission. Lazy groups, locator lint, anchor compatibility diffs and erp dev are planned. Translation integration is planned; product timings remain deferred to milestone end under ADR 0065. Optimized compressed-response transport is planned. Product performance evidence is DEFERRED_PERFORMANCE under ADR 0065; no size, latency or throughput result is claimed here.

docs.title: Links to users and company consistency

sections.text: A link to res.users is checked against that user's allowed companies (company_ids) when it is a stored many-to-many relation to res.company. The user's company_id selects its default company and does not override the allowed-company scope. Other models keep ADR 0044's usual field precedence. If the allowed-company field is absent, the usual shape-based selection applies. This correction changes registry metadata used by existing consistency checks, related-field company bounds and search-domain construction. It does not add a constraint ensuring that the default company belongs to the allowed companies. Reading users is company-restricted through the same field: res.users declares direct(field = "company_ids", branch = "exact", empty = "deny", escape = "share"). An internal user (share = false) is visible to every restricted user; a portal or public user is visible when one of its allowed companies is an active company of the reader (exactly: a parent or branch company is not enough). A reader whose active-company set is empty sees no user, internal users and itself included (SPEC-SEC-071), as for every company-scoped model. The user's contact follows the same idea through res.partner.partner_share (see [company consistency](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/company-consistency.md#the-escape-records-of-one-user-type-are-always-visible)). See the slice note (docs/design/m3-company-users-scope.md, not part of the published documentation) and [company consistency](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/company-consistency.md).

Some models have no company field of their own. They get company_id from a parent through _inherits delegation: a product variant reads its company from its product template. The registry records that delegation, but the model stays without a company scope of its own. Record rules, related fields and grouping keep treating it as a model without company, and its access is declared on the model itself (product.product declares parent(edge = "product_tmpl_id")). A link to such a model is checked only when it declares check_company = true, as stock.lot's product_id does. The check compares the linking record's company with the parent's company, read through the delegation. A change to the parent's company made earlier in the same transaction counts. The match is the parent's (exact unless the parent declares parent_of). A link that declares nothing is not checked: the usual default (ADR 0044 rule 2) does not yet reach these links. Three declarations are refused. The registry refuses the first two at build, with an error that names the delegate field and the parent model: - check_company = true toward a model whose company_ids come by delegation. A company list read through a delegation is not supported. - check_company = true on a field of the delegating model itself, and check_company_auto = true on it. That would need the delegating record's own company read through the delegation. Declare the check on the parent model instead. - At run time, a company-dependent field with check_company = true toward such a model is refused with a Programming error. A later change of the parent's company does not re-check links that already exist. The same holds for a model with its own company_id. The rule is ADR 0044 amendment A2 (docs/adr/0044-company-consistency-by-default.md); the case is SPEC-CRUD-067.

Status: view parsing, XPath inheritance, validation, and database records are complete (erp-views, crates/erp-data, addons/base). Implements: ADR 0005 (layer L7), ADR 0009 §12, ADR 0018, ADR 0019, ADR 0020. Specs: docs/specs/data/data-views-api.md (SPEC-DATA-042, 043, 044..059, SPEC-DATA-061). The erp-views crate provides the pure architecture parsing, locator, inheritance, and combination engine for ERPForAll. It operates completely in memory without database dependencies, converting XML view architectures into a structured DOM tree and applying inheritance patches with exact Odoo semantics. ---

In ERPForAll, view architectures are represented by the [ArchNode](#archnode) DOM tree, while views in the system are registered as [ViewDescriptor](#viewdescriptor-and-viewmode) values. use erp_views::{ArchNode, CombinedView, ViewDescriptor, ViewMode, combine_view, parse_xml}; let base_arch = r#" <form string="Partner"> <sheet> <field name="name"/> <field name="phone"/> </sheet> </form> "#; let base_view = ViewDescriptor::new(1, "base.partner.form", "res.partner", base_arch);

ArchNode implements the standard element tree model with text and tail semantics: - tag: The XML tag name (e.g., form, field, xpath). - attributes: An ordered mapping (IndexMap) preserving attribute declaration order. - text: Text content immediately preceding the first child element. - tail: Text content immediately following this element, before the next sibling. - children: Ordered vector of child ArchNode elements. use erp_views::parse_xml; let node = parse_xml(r#"
Hello World!
"#)?; assert_eq!(node.tag(), "div"); assert_eq!(node.attr("class"), Some("row")); assert_eq!(node.text(), Some("Hello ")); assert_eq!(node.children()[0].tag(), "b"); assert_eq!(node.children()[0].text(), Some("World")); assert_eq!(node.children()[0].tail(), Some("!"));

Views can be either Primary or Extension: - ViewMode::Primary: Defines a base view or a standalone derived view. - ViewMode::Extension: Extends a parent view (specified by inherit_id). use erp_views::{ViewDescriptor, ViewMode}; let ext_view = ViewDescriptor::new( 2, "addon.partner.form.inherit", "res.partner", r#"<xpath expr="//field[@name='phone']" position="after"><field name="email"/></xpath>"#, ) .with_inherit_id(1) .with_priority(16); assert_eq!(ext_view.mode, ViewMode::Extension); assert_eq!(ext_view.inherit_id, Some(1)); ---
Extension views locate an element in the parent view and apply modifications according to the position attribute.
Appends the specification's children to the inside of the target element: <sheet position="inside"> <field name="website"/> </sheet>

Inserts elements as siblings immediately after or before the target element. Any trailing tail text on the target element is properly preserved and transferred to the end of the newly inserted siblings: <field name="phone" position="after"> <field name="mobile"/> </field>

Replaces the target node: 1. **Outer replace** (mode="outer", default): Replaces the target element with the children of the specification. - If the specification has no children, the target node is removed. - $0 wrapping: If any inserted element has text $0, it is replaced with a deep clone of the original target element. - Root replacement: Replaces the entire root architecture (preserving t-name if present). 2. **Inner replace** (mode="inner"): Clears all text and children of the target element and inserts the specification's children, preserving the target's tag and attributes:

New Title

Modifies attributes on the target element without altering its children or text. Each child must be an <attribute> tag: <field name="name" position="attributes"> <attribute name="required">1</attribute> <attribute name="placeholder">e.g. John Doe</attribute> </field>
For attributes containing lists (e.g. class): <xpath expr="//sheet" position="attributes"> <attribute name="class" add="o_custom_sheet" remove="o_old_sheet" separator=" "/> </xpath>

Expression attributes combine with boolean logic using separator="and" (default) or separator="or": <field name="phone" position="attributes"> <attribute name="invisible" add="is_company == True" separator="or"/> </field> This wraps expressions with parentheses to preserve operator precedence: (existing) or (is_company == True).

Nodes can be moved from anywhere in the architecture to the target location: <sheet position="inside"> <xpath expr="//field[@name='old_location']" position="move"/> </sheet> ERPForAll enforces: - The moved node must exist in the architecture. - Moving the root element is forbidden (ViewError::MoveRootElement). - Moving the target node itself or an ancestor of the target is rejected (ViewError::MoveTargetOrAncestor). ---

ERPForAll supports a well-defined subset of XPath 1.0: - **Location steps**: Root /, absolute /form/sheet, descendant //field, child sheet/field. - **Per-parent indexing**: [n] uses 1-based indexing relative to direct sibling elements of the same tag. - **Attribute matching**: [@name='phone'], [@attr]. - **Text matching**: [text() = 'Overview']. - **Class matching**: hasclass('c1', 'c2') matches elements having all specified CSS classes in their whitespace-separated class attribute. - **Negation**: not(predicate). - **Boolean combinations**: predicate and predicate, predicate or predicate. Unrecognized or invalid XPath syntax fails loudly with ViewError::InvalidXpathExpr.

Extension views can also match elements without full XPath: - <field name="target_name" position="..."/>: Matches the first <field> element with attribute name="target_name". - <tag attr="val" position="..."/>: Matches the first <tag> element having exact matching attributes.

To ensure view stability across locales, using translated attributes as selectors is strictly forbidden: <!-- REJECTED: Translated attribute selector --> <button string="Save" position="after">...</button> <xpath expr="//button[@string='Save']" position="after">...</xpath> The system rejects string, help, placeholder, confirm, title, etc., and their t-attf-* variants, returning ViewError::TranslatedAttributeSelector. ---

Use [combine_view](#4-combining-views) or [combine_views_batch](#4-combining-views) to resolve view inheritance hierarchies: use erp_views::{ViewDescriptor, combine_view}; let catalogue = vec![ ViewDescriptor::new(1, "base", "res.partner", "<form><field name=\"name\"/></form>"), ViewDescriptor::new(2, "ext1", "res.partner", "<field name=\"name\" position=\"after\"><field name=\"phone\"/></field>") .with_inherit_id(1) .with_priority(10), ViewDescriptor::new(3, "ext2", "res.partner", "<field name=\"phone\" position=\"after\"><field name=\"email\"/></field>") .with_inherit_id(1) .with_priority(20), ]; let combined = combine_view(&catalogue, 1)?; assert_eq!(combined.applied_view_ids, vec![1, 2, 3]); assert_eq!( combined.to_xml(), "<form><field name=\"name\"/><field name=\"phone\"/><field name=\"email\"/></form>" );

1. **Hierarchy resolution**: Traverses inherit_id to the root primary view. 2. **Filtering**: Only active views (active = true) sharing the model with their parent (or explicitly on the inheritance path) are applied. 3. **Priority ordering**: Extension views are ordered by (priority, id). 4. **Pre-order application**: Extension views apply before primary children at the same level. 5. **Cycle detection**: Loops in inherit_id are detected and rejected with ViewError::CycleDetected. ---

Per ADR 0019 and ADR 0020, erp-views enforces strict bounds to defend against untrusted or malicious input: Every limit is a LimitKind of ViewLimits (full table in ADR 0027 §6); a host can only lower them (ViewLimits::default().lowered(kind, value)), and exceeding one is ViewError::LimitExceeded wrapped in ViewError::InView naming your view. - **Input size**: At most 10 MiB per view architecture (ArchBytes). - **Nesting depth**: At most 256 levels of XML depth (Depth), verified both at initial parse and after each inheritance step. - **Element and node limits**: At most 10,000 elements per arch (ArchElements) and 40,000 XML nodes counting text runs, comments and processing instructions too (ArchNodes). - **Attributes per element**: at most 256 (ElementAttributes), also after position="attributes" edits add some. - **Combined size**: At most 200,000 nodes and 32 MiB built while combining one view (CombinedNodes, CombinedBytes). - **XPath size**: expressions of at most 4,096 bytes, 64 steps and 32 levels of parentheses. - **Work per combination**: at most 20,000,000 evaluation steps (EvaluationSteps): nodes visited while locating and checking depth, comparisons (by their length), predicate tests, and the tokens of attribute edits (cost table in ADR 0027 §6). Real views use a tiny fraction (the 40-extension res.partner benchmark form uses about 12,000); CombinedView::evaluation_steps() shows what a combination used. Paths that start with // and have many steps cost a walk of the whole arch per step, so prefer short, anchored expressions such as //field[@name='email']. - **DTD rejection**: DTDs and external entity declarations are completely disabled. - **Null character rejection**: Raw \0 or entity-encoded � bytes fail immediately. - **Escaping**: Serializer escapes &, <, >, ", \n, \t, \r appropriately to avoid injection and malformed XML. ---

Views live in ir_ui_view, declared by the base addon with Odoo's field names, so the data files of a ported addon load unchanged (docs/design/m2-s3.md §3, §4). Addons ship views as <record model="ir.ui.view"> or <template> in their data files; they extend another addon's view with inherit_id, never by editing it. <!-- addon test_ext_b extends test_ext_a's form without touching test_ext_a --> <record id="view_book_form_pages" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="model">test_ext.book</field> <field name="inherit_id" ref="test_ext_a.view_book_form"/> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <field name="name" position="after"><field name="pages"/></field> </field> </record>

- mode: extension when inherit_id is set, primary otherwise; a write of inherit_id without mode makes a view primary when the parent is cleared and extension when a view that had none gets one, and a re-parented view keeps its mode. The rule is applied per record (BUG-074: Odoo decides once for a batch). mode = 'extension' without a parent is refused by the table ("The database refused the change: Invalid inheritance mode: ..."). - type: the parent's, else the arch's root tag (an unknown tag is refused with Odoo's "Invalid view type" message, which lists the types of the registry, selection_add included). - name: "<model> <type>" when missing; key: gen_key.<6 hex> for a QWeb view without one. - arch is stored in arch_db. Each data load of arch (install and upgrade) records arch_fs (<module>/<path> of the file it came from) and resets arch_updated to false; a write of arch outside a data load sets arch_updated. A write of arch_db itself changes neither, as in Odoo.

Every create, and every write of active, arch/arch_db or inherit_id, checks: 1. recursion of inherit_id ("You cannot create recursive inherited views."); 2. the combination of each written view, of its nearest primary ancestor and of every primary view built on that tree through extensions (deactivating an extension that another view needs fails; SPEC-DATA-057); 3. the arch of each written view: the root tag against the type, the model, <field> elements in document order with the create scope below, and the obsolete attrs/states (SPEC-DATA-058). QWeb views are combined only. Creating an extension checks field names in the elements it inserts and their descendants. Moving an old field into a newly inserted group, or inserting a field there through a later sibling extension, brings that field into the check. An unrelated stale field outside those subtrees does not block the create. The root/model checks, missing field names, group checks and obsolete attributes still run independently of this field-name scope. Creating a root view, or applying a replace or attributes spec, checks field names across the whole combined arch. XML character references are decoded before choosing that scope: position="replace" widens it just like position="replace". Ordinary writes also check the whole arch. Deferred x2many subviews remain excluded and produce the warning described below. An archived view is never combined (an inactive view on the path is an error of the engine), but writing one still checks it on its own: its arch must parse, and an archived root view's arch is validated as above. A malformed arch is never stored, active or not. Concurrent writes to one inheritance tree are serialized: each check locks the roots of the trees it reads (and a write of inherit_id the roots of the trees its views leave), so two transactions cannot both commit a cycle or a combination the other did not see; the second one fails with a serialization error and can be retried. A failure is a Validation error that names the view whose arch holds the faulty spec or node, its external id, its data file and the line in its arch: Error while validating view bad (test_ext_c.view_book_form_bad) in test_ext_c/data/views.xml, arch line 3: Field "no_such_field" does not exist in model "test_ext.book" The line counts in the view's arch as stored (the loader's arch starts with the <?xml version="1.0"?> line), not in the data file. The error's context holds name (the written view, BUG-071), xmlid, view.model, file and line; its source is the typed erp_sdk::views::record::ViewRecordError, whose Invalid variant carries an InvalidView (Combine(ViewError) or Arch(ArchIssue)). Not checked yet, and reported instead of skipped without a word: x2many sub-views inside a <field> (ArchWarning::SubViewNotValidated, until the web server delivers them), and groups that name no group (ArchWarning::UnknownGroup; such a reference never matches). The overrides post them to the transaction's notice channel (tx.notices(), tx.take_notices()) and log them on target erp::views with the view's name, external id and file: each unknown group on its own line, all sub-views of one check on one line. erp_addon_base::ir_ui_view::check_views returns them as values. The expression attributes of the elements it does read are checked (next section); the rest of the per-tag validation (buttons, labels, widget options) comes with the web server (planned). **Expression attributes and restricted fields (SPEC-DATA-104).** Write-time validation and get_view read the fields these attributes name: | Attribute | On | Read as | Names resolve on | |---|---|---|---| | invisible, readonly, required, column_invisible, decoration-* | any element | Python expression | the node's model | | context | any element | Python dict expression; its group_by (a string, or a list of strings, :interval stripped) is read as field names | the node's model | | domain | <field> | domain | left side (field path): the field's comodel; right side: the node's model | | domain | <filter> | domain | the view's model, both sides | | filter_domain | search <field> | domain (self is the typed value) | the view's model, both sides | | date, end_date | <filter> | a field name | the view's model | | default_order | <list>, <pivot> | field [asc\|desc], ... (a pivot has one measure; __count is the row count) | the view's model | t-if, t-elif, t-att-* and the widget options are not read. The list above is what this release reads, not everything Odoo's client reads: the kanban default_order, the default_group_by of list and kanban views and the pivot_measures, pivot_row_groupby and pivot_column_groupby keys of a <filter> context are not read yet (they come with the web server, planned). The operator of a domain leaf must be a string literal, and the right side of any, not any, any! and not any! must be a literal list of leaves; it is read as a domain on the comodel of the left path. A group_by of another type than string or list of strings, and a context key that is not a string literal, are refused. Only the root of an attribute chain is a field (partner_id.name reads partner_id), a short list of names the client provides (uid, context, today, bool, self, ...) is not a field (but a field of the model with one of those names is refused: the client would let the field override the name; so is parent.parent on a model with a field parent), and inside a relational field's sub-view parent.x reads the enclosing model while a bare name reads the sub-view's model. parent.x outside a sub-view is refused (Odoo drops it silently), and so is a bare parent (parent['x'], len(parent)). A name that is not a field is ArchIssue::UnknownFieldInExpression; an expression that does not parse, a value that is not a domain, a domain on a field that is not relational or a name the guard plan cannot hold is ArchIssue::InvalidExpression. The attribute is read only inside the validation scope of the write (the same rule as for unknown <field> names), and the content of a sub-view is not read at write time for now: get_view still reads it when it captures the bundle. *A visible node may not read a field it does not guard.* If a field's definition has groups, every node that reads it in one of these attributes must be shown only to users who may read the field: the node's effective guard (its own groups intersected with its enclosing nodes' and, for a <field> element, the field's own definition) must imply the field's groups. Otherwise the write is refused with ArchIssue::RestrictedFieldInExpression naming the attribute, field, model and groups. The rule is sound and not complete: repeat the field's groups on the node (or an enclosing node) and it passes. A group implies another through the group implication relation (implied_ids), a . guard implies everything, an unguarded node implies nothing, and a negated group (!x) in the field's groups must be excluded by the node (by !x or by the negation of a group that x implies). It is a divergence from Odoo (Parity: divergent — ADR 0060 D3.5). At serve time the same read is checked against the user's field masks: if the node survives the filter and a field it reads is unreadable for the user, get_view fails with Access naming view, line, attribute, model and field instead of dropping only the expression; a node that is removed by its own guard (or an enclosing one) raises nothing. Each notice carries a NoticeKind (UnknownGroup, SubViewNotValidated, Other; the enum is #[non_exhaustive], so match with a wildcard arm), a target and a message; do not match on the message text. **Notice lifetime and bounds (SPEC-DATA-082).** Notices belong to one transaction attempt. Commit, rollback and reset() clear them; a rollback to a savepoint drops the notices posted inside it and a release keeps them. With Orm::run, call tx.take_notices() inside the closure, before the commit: after the closure returns they are gone, and a retried attempt starts empty. A transaction keeps at most MAX_NOTICES_PER_TRANSACTION (256) notices and a message at most MAX_NOTICE_MESSAGE_BYTES (4096) bytes; a longer message is shortened and ends with ... [truncated: N bytes total]. A notice past the count cap is not stored: it is counted in tx.notices_overflowed() (a rollback to a savepoint does not decrease it; take_notices, clear_notices, commit and rollback reset it) and the first one of an attempt logs a warning on target erp::notices. An extension view may not have group_ids ("Inherited view cannot have 'groups' defined on the record. ..."); put groups attributes inside the arch instead (SPEC-DATA-059). During an install or upgrade, the primary views whose data has not loaded yet are not combined (they still hold their old archs): views of modules of the operation that come later, and views of the module loading now that it has not reached yet. A view written earlier in the same file counts as loaded, as in Odoo. After each upgraded module, its noupdate views are checked (ir.ui.view._validate_module_views, called by the module system; not after a reinit, which writes noupdate records too). The loader passes what is loaded in the context of every write that carries install_module, also when your model's create writes views (layout in erp_data::load::load_state). Code that sets install_module itself, outside the loader, gets a Programming error from a view write: the check would otherwise take "no load state" for "nothing loaded". For H18 module-data admission, XML and CSV operations additionally carry the loader-owned erp_sdk::load_state::DECLARING_MODULE key (__erp_data_module). It is stamped after authored context and reaches idless records and nested relational commands. A view or window mode outside list, form, search (and the separate qweb template kind) must belong to a dependency of that module and be published in the exact registry generation. These checks require an operation-managed System transaction with full elevation: setting context in ordinary CRUD does not establish lifecycle authority. The key grants no ACL or field-access permissions.

use erp_addon_base::ir_ui_view::select::{ViewRequest, ViewType, default_view, select_view}; let form = ViewType::new(&tx, "form")?; // the active primary view with the lowest (priority, name, id): one statement let default = default_view(&mut tx, "res.partner", &form).await?; // the context's form_view_ref, else the default let picked = select_view(&mut tx, &ViewRequest::new("res.partner", &form)).await?; for notice in picked.notices() { // RefNotQualified, RefNotFound, RefOtherModel, RefOtherType (BUG-073) println!("{notice}"); } A <type>_view_ref that is not a qualified external id, names no view, or names a view of another model or type is ignored, the default view is used, and the reason comes back as a ViewNotice (Odoo uses a view of another model; BUG-073). A ref longer than 256 bytes or not text is an error. A view given with ViewRequest::view_id is checked in one statement: a view that does not exist is Missing, one of another model or type is a Validation error. A type a request names that the registry does not have is "Unknown view type '<type>'. Allowed types are: ...". No view at all is a UserError ("No default view of type 'kanban' could be found! ..."); generated default views come with the web server (planned).

The web client fetches view architectures via get_view: use erp_addon_base::ir_ui_view::get_view; use erp_addon_base::ir_ui_view::select::{ViewRequest, ViewType}; let form = ViewType::new(&tx, "form")?; let req = ViewRequest::new("res.partner", &form); let resp = get_view(&mut tx, &env, &req).await?; println!("Filtered arch: {}", resp.arch()); get_view runs three steps: bundle, mint, filter (ADR 0060 D3). 1. **Bundle (shared, templates ormcache).** The inheritance tree is read read-only (fetch_trees_read_only, no row locks, works in read transactions) and combined. GuardedArch::capture(combined, model, &record_guards, &lookup, &ViewLimits::default()) then strips every groups attribute from the arch and records the guards it carried: the element's own groups intersected with the enclosing guard, and for a also the groups of the field definition. Equal effective guards share one index (numbered by first occurrence in document order). record_guards are (view id, group ids) of the applied primary views that have group_ids. The resulting bundle and its GuardPlan (host_access::plan_of(&guarded)) are cached across users and transactions. A groups value with no group reference at all or with a malformed non-empty term (empty terms beside a real reference are ignored; install-time validation refuses the same values), an unknown , an expression attribute that cannot be read or names a field its model does not have, or more than 64 references in one effective guard fail the capture with a ViewError::GuardCapture naming the view and line (Validation through get_view); too many distinct guards is ViewError::LimitExceeded. Nothing is served partly captured. 2. **Mint (per call).** get_view checks the caller can read the model, then calls tx.evaluate_guards(&env, &compiled.plan).await?. The transaction decides every guard of the plan for env's user once, from one snapshot of the user's groups, and returns a GuardEvaluation that borrows the transaction. Unknown group references never match (a negated unknown one never excludes), and a user in no group is refused by every guard. A model other than the view's own that the user may not read (the comodel of an x2many) is not an error: its fields count as unreadable, so the fields inside its sub-view are left out of the served arch; the relational field itself stays with an empty sub-view. The same holds for the expressions: inside such a sub-view a node whose decoration-*, invisible and the like read an unreadable field is removed, and a relational field whose own domain reads the comodel is removed, instead of failing the view (a relational field that holds a sub-view or a domain adds the probe .id to the plan for this). Only the view's own model refuses (Access). 3. **Filter (per call).** host_access::filter(&env, &compiled.guarded, &evaluation)?.to_xml() first checks that the evaluation was minted for this principal, that the bundle and the evaluation share a registry generation, that the evaluation's plan equals the bundle's own guard table, and that every record guard is satisfied. Then it writes the arch in one streaming pass. A subtree whose guard is false is omitted and keeps its parent's tail text (() -> ()); an attribute-less that had its own guard and passed is unwrapped so that enclosing layouts (, ) keep their structure. A mismatch is an Access error (another principal, another plan, an unsatisfied record guard) or Validation (another registry generation): the filter fails closed, it never returns an unfiltered arch. A warm call costs one database statement for view selection and none for the tree fetch, plus the guard evaluation (its resolved plan is cached per policy snapshot). **An addon never filters an arch itself.** GuardEvaluation and FilteredArch have private fields and no public constructor, so an addon cannot supply its own verdicts or build a filtered arch from booleans, and the filtered arch always matches the plan the evaluation decided. (Whether the plan is right depends on the host's GuardLookup answers and record guards; only base supplies them today.) the compile-fail cases of crates/erp-views/tests/compile_fail.rs pin this (forged literal, new, outliving the transaction, committing while a verdict is held). The only way to serve a filtered arch is get_view, or host_access::filter with an evaluation the transaction minted. Call get_view; if you hold a ViewResponse, do not re-process its arch. **GuardLookup contract.** capture asks the host for four answers about the registry, read once per capture: pub trait GuardLookup { fn registry_generation(&self) -> u64; // the registry state the answers belong to fn field_groups(&self, model: &str, field: &str) -> Option<&str>; // group spec text of the field definition fn comodel(&self, model: &str, field: &str) -> Option<&str>; // comodel of a relational field, else None fn has_field(&self, model: &str, field: &str) -> bool; } addons/base implements it over the transaction's registry (RegistryGuardLookup). A below a relational field's sub-view resolves against that field's comodel. A bundle captured under one registry_generation is refused under another. **A view limited to groups.** get_view refuses (Access) a primary view whose group_ids are non-empty and do not include the user; a view with no group_ids is never refused (SPEC-DATA-101, Parity: divergent — ADR 0060 D3, accepted by the lead: Odoo's _check_view_access is called only when rendering templates and by the website addon, never by get_view). Choosing the view without an id does not skip such a view: the lowest-priority primary is selected whatever its groups and then refused, it never falls through to the next primary; ask for a view by id (or a *_view_ref) to get another one. **Breaking change for addon code.** FilterDecision is no longer exported from erp_sdk::views and Arch::to_xml_filtered is now crate-private to erp-views (it was the callback filter get_view used); Transaction::group_spec_matches and the matching helper in erp-orm were removed. The only users found under addons/ were in base (get_view.rs), which now uses the flow above. erp_sdk::views exports GuardLookup, GuardedArch and host_access::{FilteredArch, filter, plan_of}. Design: docs/design/m2-s3-b-guarded-arch.md. **Breaking change for RegistryLookup implementors (GA-3).** erp_sdk::views::validate::RegistryLookup gained three required methods, field_groups(model, field), comodel(model, field) and implies(group, implied), because write-time validation now reads expression attributes (see above). ArchIssue gained InvalidExpression, UnknownFieldInExpression and RestrictedFieldInExpression (the enum is #[non_exhaustive]), and erp_sdk::views::validate::reads_fields(&Arch) tells whether an arch holds expressions that need the group implication data. addons/base implements the trait over the registry and the res.groups implication relation.

Every create, write and unlink of a view invalidates the named cache templates; with signals on, the commit bumps cache:templates and every other node clears it before its next transaction (MN-1). A migration that writes ir_ui_view with SQL bypasses that: it must call tx.invalidate_ormcache("templates") itself.

Uninstalling a module removes its own views with its other records, and with them every view built on them, the extensions of modules that stay included (as Odoo does). Then the views users copied from them: views keyed <module>.… that no module staying installed names by external id (an __export__ id is no module's), archived ones and the views built on them included. PurgeReport::copied_views_removed counts every view that went that way, copied_views_kept the keyed views a staying module names. The other records a module owns in base models go too: a group with its memberships (its users stay). A record of a staying module that still points at one of them through a restrict foreign key fails the uninstall with the ORM's error. A row left after the purge that holds a selection value the module added (a view of a type it added, ...) fails the uninstall until selection ondelete handling exists; the rows the purge deletes itself never count.

Arch size 10 MiB at write time even for an inactive view, the engine's limits at combination, 128 views on one inherit_id path (LimitKind::InheritanceDepth), 10,000 views in one inheritance tree (LimitKind::CatalogueViews), 64 references per groups attribute, 256 bytes per *_view_ref. View checks also bound all tree text (names, models and architectures) to 64 MiB before fetching; names and models count twice because the check retains two copies. An oversized value is refused without transferring its text. External-id aliases are limited to 10,000 and 64 MiB of text per lookup; filename diagnostics have a 64 MiB text bound. ViewCatalogue::combine_many shares both a work budget (BatchSteps) and a retained-storage budget (BatchBytes, 128 MiB by default). Roots and no-op primary views consume work too. The retained cap covers the parsed cache, returned architectures and their owned container capacities. The active combination and the spec being parsed also have their ordinary per-arch limits. These limits can only be lowered with ViewLimits::lowered. For pure validation, use validate::group_refs_with_limits(arch, catalogue.limits()) when a host lowers CheckGroupRefs; repeated mentions of the same group count once. A caller validating several arches also bounds their union before resolving group names. validate::group_refs uses the default limit of 4,096 distinct references; every individual groups attribute still allows at most 64.

A record form can display any authorized static selection field in its header: <form> <header> <field name="phase" widget="statusbar" statusbar_visible="draft,done" readonly="1"/> </header> <sheet><field name="name"/></sheet> </form> Declare the selection and its default using the normal model API. Labels and order come from model metadata; the widget does not require a field named state. Omit statusbar_visible to show all choices. A provided list must contain unique, nonempty known keys; the current record value remains visible even outside the list. readonly="1" displays state only. A writable occurrence uses normal draft edits, onchange and Save/Discard. It never calls an approval method or saves directly. Keep business transition checks on the model. Unknown options, many2one stages and placement outside a record header are refused. Use existing view inheritance to add/modify the header or its field. No approval or activity records are created by declaring this widget. See ADR 0102 for the bounded contract.

Native declarations use ViewTypeDecl constructors and an owner-bound ViewTypeContribution. A VIEW_TYPES link-time registration alone does not publish a serving contract. The native composition root passes the real addon descriptor and declarations to ModuleSystemBuilder::view_types; erp_addon_web::view_type_contributions() supplies the builtin list/form/search declarations. Composition produces PublishedViewTypes for that exact Arc<Registry>. Policy-bound serving ORMs must explicitly retain this attachment when they rebuild the same generation; a missing attachment or a different registry is an error, with no process-global registration fallback. Declarations specify a wire major, renderer, closed schema, validator, builder, metadata fields and exposed data methods. Bare compatibility keys belong to their designated owner; other addon keys use <addon>.<name>. An exposed method contributed by an unrelated addon does not satisfy an owner's method declaration. Selection additions must reconcile with the published owner. During module data loading, view/action keys require their owner's installed dependency closure; list/form/search and qweb have the framework record-admission exception described above. Serving still requires publication. Callbacks receive a borrowed CheckedViewInput<'_> from erp_addon_base::ir_ui_view::with_checked_view. The base adapter selects and combines the view, evaluates the actual caller's guards, and invokes the callback while that evaluation is alive. input.root() and CheckedNode traverse admitted nodes; denied descendants cannot be recovered through a raw arch accessor. input.model_spec() is descriptive metadata, not authority to expose a field. input.mobile() is the canonical presentation option. A borrowed with_mobile projection changes no principal, company, group decision, model or lifetime. Build directly through DescriptionValueBuilder; root.budget() provides the same request allowance for temporary work and every nested value. Do not serialize/reparse XML or construct an unbudgeted JSON payload before calling the builder. After construction the host independently walks the registered schema, checks every emitted model/field/relation segment through the caller's ORM, and applies the metadata predicates. Unreadable search fields/filters are pruned as complete items; a surviving prohibited layout or button expression refuses. Unknown paths remain errors. Field metadata reflects both read access and the effective readonly mask, including model/field write denial. The builtin adapter retains the existing client wire: list/form/search arenas, explicit nullable modifiers, form regions and object buttons, search expressions, and selection-panel descriptors. An arena must be a bounded tree with valid indexes and layout relationships. The list's implicit panel comes from the checked search tree directly; its caller context default and notices are added only after authorization. Other view families remain outside this builtin client contract. Builtin field, search_field and selection-panel handles name one direct field of the root model: a handle on another model, or a relation path such as company_id.name, is refused with a ValidationError that names the node kind and the handle (relation paths are planned), because the client resolves these handles in the root model's field catalogue. Relation paths stay valid inside expressions (domains, contexts, modifiers) and in the generic reference slots of non-builtin view types. A search filter or group whose unguarded domain or context reads a field the caller may not read is not pruned: the call is refused with an AccessError that names the view and line; guard the node by group to hide it from callers without the field.

Descriptions are uncached and transaction-bound. The base templates cache contains group-agnostic compiled architecture and guard plans; each request evaluates its own authority. PostgreSQL remains the source for views, groups and menus, so process loss discards reconstructible state. Existing multi-node invalidation and request-snapshot rules still apply; this slice adds no shared background quota.

- Request 1–16 [id|null, type] pairs with wire major 1. Duplicate types refuse; returned views retain request order and real resolved identities. - options may be absent. mobile, toolbar and load_filters are booleans with false defaults. Mobile reaches the registered callback; toolbar/load_filters true are refused with an error saying they are not available yet. - action_id, embedded_action_id, embedded_parent_res_id and studio are refused in this call. Unknown keys and wrong types are errors. The action-bundle RPC owns its model/view selection.

Expressions are typed versioned documents. Schema visitors derive references independently of builders: domain tuples, dotted relations, context group-by paths and modifiers all require authorization. Ordinary literal context data is not a domain. Search additionally includes every readable model field of a type the human client can render (others, such as a dynamic selection, are left out of the optional catalogue; a view that references one itself is refused) for custom filters; metadata predicates cannot widen access. Unsupported selection-panel features return an explicit descriptor. Unknown expression operators or fields fail loudly. Search-field operator has the current scalar consumer's explicit subset: ilike, =, !=, >, <, >=, <=. This slot is checked both during builtin lowering and independently on final custom-builder output. Filter-domain operators have their separate expression contract. Other search-field operator text fails with a located model/field/operator error saying the operator is not available yet. **Group By items of a list.** The list's search menu offers every <filter> of the model's default search view whose context evaluates to {'group_by': 'field'} as a Group By item (put them in a <group string="Group By"> as Odoo views do), for example <filter name="group_city" string="City" context="{'group_by': 'city'}"/>. The field must be one the server can group by (stored, readable) and of kind boolean, char, integer, selection or many2one. A field:interval item, a list of several fields, or another field kind is not offered yet; the menu names it under "Not offered here" with the reason. The list is grouped by one item at a time. Only the model's default search view is read; the action's own search_view_id is not consulted yet. Effective metadata readonly is a floor for every XML occurrence: readonly="0" cannot override model or field Write denial. With writable metadata, repeated occurrences still retain their own static readonly modifiers and combine to an editable record field when an occurrence is writable.

One DescriptionBudget spans a request's views, field catalogue, wire copies and serialization. Its 32 MiB construction ceiling accounts logical owned storage; it is not an allocator benchmark. Refusal is sticky. Expressions also share work and encoded-byte allowances. Dynamic source parsing uses erp_expr::source_preflight with the exact parsing limits, reserving before parser/admission allocation and retaining the reservation through both trees' lifetimes. Admitted-AST encoded length is checked before building another wire copy. The encoder limits output to 8 MiB, with a separate 2 MiB field-metadata preview ceiling. The final transport JSON copy and formatter/reservation scratch are admitted too. Requested architectures share a 4096-node cap and the current client tree depth is 32. Menus have a 4096-row cap. Limits can only be lowered by trusted host/test code; no RPC option changes admission. A conservative source preflight can refuse a valid large formatted string before parsing. This fail-closed limitation is accepted under ADR 0060 D7; tightening it is planned. The receipt retains the concrete fixture and raw safety output. This is an admission limitation, not a deferred performance assertion.

The former h18_checked_view_input() placeholder and its missing-bridge refusal are removed. Native H18 serving calls the real checked bridge and the generation's validator/builder. Pure erp-views consumers do not acquire ORM authority, and guest inputs cannot construct a checked view. Compile-fail fixtures cover direct construction and escaping nodes, evaluations and mobile projections.

The human-client producer admits object, action, URL and inert buttons in a record form's header and dialog footer. For type="object", name selects an exposed public model method; string is presentation data. A caption such as “Delete” does not select a built-in command, add an icon, change permissions or supply confirmation. <form> <header> <button name="submit" type="object" string="Submit" class="btn-primary" confirm="Submit this record?" invisible="phase != 'draft'"/> </header> <sheet><field name="name"/><field name="phase"/></sheet> </form> Declare the referenced fields and method in the addon. Keep authorization and business validation on that method: groups and invisible control whether a button is offered, and do not authorize its RPC. Dynamic visibility reads the record's admitted fields. Existing view inheritance applies before rendering, so extensions add or change declared actions rather than editing another addon. A header button confirms only when confirm is declared. After acceptance, the client saves a dirty or new record before calling its object method. Validation refusal stops that call. While execution is pending, affected controls are unavailable; an error is reported instead of repeating the write. An uncertain outcome keeps the existing read-only recovery policy. A danger appearance alone does not ask for confirmation. The served ranks are btn-primary (also oe_highlight), btn-secondary, btn-link, btn-success, btn-info, btn-warning and btn-danger. Omitting class selects secondary. A class declaration without a rank selects unstyled; a structural oe_stat_button retains the legacy secondary default. Conflicting ranks fail. rounded-circle selects the circular shape; remaining identifier tokens are addon CSS hooks. Class text has a 512-byte raw limit, at most eight distinct tokens and 64 bytes per token. Tokens match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*; only ASCII spaces separate them. Extra spaces canonicalize, preserving token order. Classes do not select an action. Header actions keep their declared visible order. On a phone, the first visible action remains direct and additional actions use a separate menu toggle; opening the toggle does not execute that action.

<header> <button name="submit" type="object" string="Submit" class="btn-success addon_submit" size="sm" icon="lucide:refresh-cw" title="Submit record" help="Checks the record first." confirm="Submit this record?" confirm-title="Review submission" confirm-label="Submit" cancel-label="Keep editing" data-hotkey="shift+s" debounce="300" block-ui="1" context="{'default_name': name}"/> <button name="7" type="action" string="Open related action"/> <button type="url" href="/documentation" string="Documentation" class="btn-link"/> <button string="Unavailable operation"/> </header> Here submit, name and action ID 7 are examples: declare the method/field and use the real installed action identity. The inert declaration has no type, name or URL and cannot execute. Action targets use a positive JSON-safe numeric identity; they never pass through object-method exposure. Loading/executing the action keeps its own access checks. URL text is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes: a single-slash absolute application route or an absolute HTTP(S) URL. Network-relative // URLs, backslashes, whitespace/control characters and every other scheme, including javascript: and data:, are refused. The browser repeats admission before navigation. | Attribute | Admitted declaration | |---|---| | size | sm, md, lg, mapping to small, normal and large; default normal | | icon | lucide:<name>, at most 256 bytes; must exist in the shipped client icon manifest; unknown names fail without fallback | | string, title, help | Plain text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes each. An empty/missing caption requires a nonempty title for an accessible name. Help uses a detailed tooltip; debug details describe the control and do not grant server diagnostics. | | confirm, confirm-title, confirm-label, cancel-label | Nonempty plain text, at most 4096 bytes each; overrides require confirm | | data-hotkey | One lowercase letter/digit, optionally prefixed by shift+; Alt is the access modifier. Only eligible controls in the active form/topmost dialog participate; repeated keydown does not activate. | | debounce | Integer milliseconds, 0..60000; immediate first activation, repeated activation resets the quiet window, no trailing call | | block-ui | Static boolean (0/1, false/true, False/True); scoped blocking is released on success, refusal or error | | context | Existing bounded expression document, evaluated after save against the saved record and current context; must produce a dictionary | Caller context is followed by evaluated button context. Protected company/session, identity and locale keys cannot be replaced. Button context also cannot supply active_model, active_id or active_ids. Object calls retain established caller context (including a wizard's parent context), while method ids use the saved record. Action-ID loading binds active model/record identities from its saved caller. The schema visitor independently derives context field references; an unreadable reference on a button refuses the description rather than publishing its value or pruning an authorization check. The wire retains the legacy button, stat_button and cancel_button shapes with optional details. Non-object targets use action_button and a closed action/URL/inert target. Absent details preserve legacy output; present details require size, circle, classes, debounce_ms and block_ui. Optional members are omitted when absent; unknown keys, explicit nulls in these new optional slots and wrong types fail. Custom builders pass the same host semantic checks and DescriptionBudget as builtin XML. These declarations follow ADR 0123's coordinated strict wire contract.

A form sheet may declare a button_box containing object-method statistic buttons. The statistic is a real authorized numeric field or a supported relation count; it is never inferred from a label. For example, after defining the count field and the exposed open_orders method:
The client preserves visible button order when space moves actions into **More**. The same controls and actual statistic values appear in that menu; overflowing an action does not create a second action or a second count request. An invisible button consumes no visible slot. A button box with no visible actions is omitted. The [human form layout guide](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/human-form-layout.md) describes the surrounding sheet structure.

Header/footer action, URL and inert targets do not extend the button-box grammar: statistic buttons remain object methods. List-row buttons, generic kanban/card compilation, multi-create toolbars and Enterprise approval gates retain their own view/backend owners. The full upstream pending-control lock set and independent circle interaction-state obligations retain their separate acceptance scope. A dialog cancel control keeps special="cancel", closes without saving or calling a method, and may declare presentation/hotkey/debounce/blocking details. It cannot combine with name/type/href, context, confirmation or confirmation overrides. See the [wizard guide](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/wizard-dialogs.md). Unsupported declarations fail explicitly.

<sheet> <widget name="web_ribbon" title="Archived" tooltip="Kept for reference" bg_color="bg-warning"/> <widget name="notification_alert"/> </sheet> These display leaves are admitted under record-form form/sheet/group/page/aside containers. They are distinct from Settings/Addons service widgets. They accept groups pruning and refuse expression modifiers and undeclared options.
