For a ribbon, nonempty title takes precedence over text; one is required. Caption and optional tooltip each have a 4096-byte limit. bg_color admits bg- or text-bg- plus info/success/warning/danger. The XML default is success; arbitrary styles fail. This does not change the direct client component's historical default. The notification alert has only its name and optional groups. Permission is read from the browser, refreshed on focus/visibility and supported permission-status changes, and listeners are disposed with the form. Guidance opens only on user action; the widget never requests permission or accepts a server permission value. This section describes source behavior. New live view/client checks and the complete parent acceptance evidence remain pending; it does not announce deployment.

A main-route form has three bands, each with one job. The control row holds New, the breadcrumb, the smart buttons and the pager. The action row heads the sheet column: the <header> buttons on the left, the statusbar ending on the sheet's right edge. The chatter column starts on the same row, so its button row and the action row share a top (32px controls everywhere). Nothing in the view changes for this: the layout is the client's. Inside the chatter column every block (button row, composer, planned activities, files, the error line, the thread) starts on the column's left edge and ends on its right edge, with one 8px gap between neighbours on a line and one 12px gap between blocks. The button row is Send message, Log note and Activity as three separate buttons, then the attachments and followers buttons with counts at the right; the composer shows the signed-in user's avatar (the userName of the chatter options; none without a name), and a message row is a 36px avatar beside the head and body. Addons style these through the erp-mail-* classes; the DOM order (head before body, field name first in a tracking line) is part of the accessible reading order, so reorder visually with CSS, never in the DOM. - <button_box> stat buttons render as one joined strip in the control row. Each shows an icon, the value and the label; icon in the button details picks the icon, otherwise a neutral one is shown. When the row is too narrow the strip keeps as many buttons as fit and moves the rest into a "More" menu. - Rows of fields sit on a 32px pitch. The label column of a group is as wide as its longest label (up to 11rem), so the values of a group start on one x. - A radio widget lays its choices in a row that wraps. Declare options="{'horizontal': false}" to keep a column. - The Copy button of CopyClipboard* widgets and the calendar button of a date appear on hover and focus on a mouse device; touch screens always show them. - The breadcrumb has two lines: the parent link above, the record name below with a compact record menu beside it. The menu lists Duplicate (the generic copy method of the model), Archive or Unarchive, Delete, a divider and Reload. The model's own bound actions would follow the divider; the form does not load them yet. - A boolean_favorite field declared inside the <title> block shows as a star left of the heading. A picture next to the title is an image widget on a binary field ([binary and image fields](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/binary-image-fields.md#views-and-bin-size)). - The addon's context line (the control panel's extension slot) is helper text under the title. - A notebook whose tabs do not fit keeps one row: the last tabs move into a "More" menu, the selected tab stays. - Tags (many2many chips) are small quiet pills in the form and in the list alike. - The aside (Record information) is a collapsed card, with or without a chatter above it. - An integer that is not a quantity, such as a year or sequence number, supports options="{'enable_formatting': False}" (or options="{'type': 'number'}"): the value shows without a thousands separator in both read and edit modes.

A <field> for a one2many without an inline <list>/<form> is shown with the comodel's own list and form views, as in Odoo (addons/web/static/src/client/x2many.ts, attachSubviews). The list hides the inverse field. The line form opened in a dialog gets the same treatment for its own one2many fields, so an author's book opened from the Books tab shows its Loans with the loan list's columns. This goes at most SUBVIEW_DEPTH (3) form levels deep. It stops at a model that is already open higher up, for example a partner's contacts inside a partner. Such a one2many shows only the lines' display names. An inline <list> or <form> inside the <field> is refused ("Field nodes cannot contain children."), and so is editable on a list root: the columns of a sub-list are the comodel's default list view (the lowest priority), and a line is edited in the comodel's default form, so give the line model both (addons/account/views/account_move_views.xml, view_move_line_lines). A field cannot name a different sub-list yet. A model without a name field (and no rec_name) shows the model,id display name, as in Odoo. Set rec_name in the model file when its lines need a readable title.

Both <list> and <form> view architectures support action control attributes matching Odoo behavior: - create: Set to "0" or "false" to disable creating new records from this view (hides the **New** button in the list or form view controls). - edit: Set to "0" or "false" to disable editing existing records (puts the form in read-only mode). - delete: Set to "0" or "false" to disable record deletion (removes the **Delete** action from the actions dropdown menu). Action context keys (e.g. {'create': False}, {'edit': False}, {'delete': False}) are also respected by the Elang client and combine with arch attributes.

A list column is sized by its field's kind unless the arch says otherwise: numbers, amounts and dates take their one-line content width within fixed bounds, check boxes at most 100 px, long text at most 600 px, and every other column flexes from 80 px (the record name column from 160 px) and shares the spare room. Set width on a <field> of a <list> to choose the width yourself, in pixels of content (the cell padding comes on top, as in Odoo): <list> <field name="sequence" widget="handle"/> <field name="name" width="[200px]"/>        <!-- at least 200 px, flexible above --> <field name="code" width="60px"/>           <!-- exactly 60 px --> <field name="note" width="[100px,400px]"/>  <!-- between 100 and 400 px --> </list> Values run from 1 to 2000 px; px may be left out. Anything else (100%, 12.5px, a maximum below the minimum) refuses the view by name when it loads, and width on a field outside a list view is refused too.

ADR 0124 extends the existing fieldWidgets registry and strict H18 descriptions. The selected base implementation is being verified; consult docs/design/behavior-matrix/field-widgets.md for actual tested scope. Registration alone is not server declaration admission. A field occurrence can declare shared placeholder, help and applicable family options. For example, `<field name="private_note" widget="password" placeholder="Private note" help="Visible only to permitted readers" autocomplete="new-password"/>` requests masked presentation. It does not grant read permission or make a readable value secret on the server. Unknown options and incompatible kinds fail admission. Authorized auxiliary fields are included in record reads; denied dependencies prune their owning field occurrence. Trusted adapters retain the object-based createFieldControl contract and disposable handles. They propose value changes to the record owner. Invalid drafts prevent save; adapters never write independently. Multi-field date changes use one changeValues callback so validation cannot observe a half-updated range. Dynamic modifiers use validated expression documents; evaluation errors block the affected operation. The server remains authoritative for access. Dynamic invisible, readonly and required expressions are admitted in record forms only. In a list view (which also supplies x2many columns) they fail admission, for example with Dynamic 'invisible' modifiers on list fields need per-row evaluation, which a later delivery adds.; literal values remain allowed there. Values a user can type never break rendering. A url value without an http(s):// or ftp(s):// prefix gets http:// (so localhost:3000 links to http://localhost:3000); a value that still has no safe link, such as javascript:…, is shown as plain text. search_threshold on many2one and many2many_tags is the number of typed characters before a relation search starts (0 to 4096, as admitted by the server); the result count stays the default. password columns of embedded x2many lists are masked like the main list. A tag created with quick-create has no colour until it is read again. The existing registry resolves js-class, view-specific and generic adapters in that order for a known identity. Form/list/card component behavior requires separate tests. A card adapter does not establish a served kanban renderer. Code/HTML editor wiring retains its separate ownership. Monetary presentation currently targets only amounts that round-trip through the existing JSON numeric contract and currency scale. Lossless Decimal transport remains a completion obligation; unsafe amounts must be refused visibly, never rounded or replaced with zero. An amount whose record has no currency is shown and edited as a plain number without a symbol. While the currency loads, or when the amount cannot be presented, the field shows a status message; that state never blocks saving the record, since nothing was edited. Relation domains use comodel criterion paths and root-record RHS expressions. Literal criterion structure is admitted; dynamic domain structure and nested any scopes are explicitly refused for now. Domain/context options never bypass the record RPC's ACL or field checks. Readonly ranges need both endpoint descriptions/values, but require no mutation capability. Editable ranges require one atomic changeValues callback; line forms forward that callback and the actual numeric locale. Parent line writes reevaluate occurrence policy in the line's own value scope. Explicit discard invalidates editor-local drafts; unrelated onchange does not discard invalid input. Numeric type='number' selects canonical decimal input; type='text' uses configured separators. enable_formatting (a boolean, True by default) on integer and float fields: False suppresses thousands grouping in both read and edit modes. It is the reference's option name; the percentage and monetary widgets do not take it, and a view that spells it format is refused by name. Write booleans as True/False, as everywhere in options. hide_trailing_zeros changes readonly formatting only, never the stored amount. Boolean icon_class accepts bounded class tokens. Unsupported family/option combinations fail declaration admission. Operations: this wire contract requires the server and generated client assets from the same release. Rebuild/generated-input checks must pass before activating either side. Reload clients after a coordinated update; roll back server and assets together. No database migration is introduced. Disposable field handles may expose captureDraft() and restoreDraft() for owner-driven rerenders. The snapshot contains editor text and its validation message, never a save command. An asynchronous adapter retains the snapshot until its inner control mounts; disposal suppresses late rendering. Record-owned discard and successful reload invalidate retained drafts. Failed reload preserves the current editor and its validation state. Placeholder fields are authorized text dependencies. A supplied false/null value means an empty placeholder; other non-text values are refused instead of being coerced. Selection, filterable selection and badge-choice overflow use the same dynamic placeholder precedence as text editors. Boolean and display-only badge/label widgets reject placeholder options because they have no placeholder editor surface. This is an invalid declaration, not a silently ignored setting.

Onchange is independent of the XML button/view grammar above. A native warning may carry validated className and sticky notification options using OnchangeWarning::with_options; see [model onchange documentation](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/models.md). ADR 0123 defines the bounded option contract. The client retains accepted field updates if warning presentation fails. These warning options do not change XML button or ribbon admission. A single normalized warning retains its options; distinct warnings combine into an ordered dialog without notification-only options. Deduplication includes class/sticky, and explicit false or an empty class string stays distinct from absence.

A Text field in a record form can use the code widget: <field name="arch_db" widget="code" options="{'mode': 'xml'}"/> The closed mode vocabulary is xml, python, javascript, json, qweb, scss, bash, and text. Omitted mode defaults to qweb; an explicit invalid mode fails validation. XML and QWeb are distinct presentation modes. The only admitted option is mode; unknown keys, duplicate keys, expressions and nonstring values fail rather than being evaluated. Options are a literal dictionary limited to 4096 UTF-8 source bytes and parser depth 8, within the shared description budget. See ADR 0125. The widget supports Text, not Html or Char. Effective required/readonly field modifiers apply. Draft changes update record dirty state immediately; blur or Save commits pending onchange before persistence. The form retains code-editor handles across identical value echoes so typing, cursor and history remain local. Save/readback, Discard and reload establish authoritative baselines. Code contents are ordinary untrusted text; highlighting does not authorize or execute source.

An Html field in a record form can use the html widget (or render by default when no widget attribute is specified): <field name="description" widget="html"/> In form view, the editor is a flat field (no box and no permanent toolbar) with a hint when empty. A formatting toolbar (role="toolbar": bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, undo, redo) floats over a non-collapsed text selection and a / command list (headings, lists, quote, code block) opens at the caret; both are described in [Reusable HTML editor](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/human-client-extensions.md#reusable-html-editor). Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+B / Meta+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U for formats, Ctrl+Z for undo, Ctrl+Y or Shift+Ctrl+Z for redo. Drafts are staged immediately, and immediate draft staging with onchange commit on blur or save. The form retains editor handles across identical value echoes so typing, cursor position, and undo/redo history remain local. In list cells, the field displays safe read-only plain text extracted via an inert template, preventing any script execution. When saved, the server is the sole trust authority: server-sanitized content is reflected back into the editor, and server-side refusals or sanitization errors surface directly as typed validation feedback. Required HTML fields prevent saving when empty or containing only empty scaffolding. Readonly HTML fields display formatted content with controls disabled and editing prevented. Trusted custom draft widgets may use WidgetEnvironment.draft and return the optional WidgetHandle.draft lifecycle: admit a replacement without mutation, flush accepted input, update an authoritative value/policy, validate the full document, focus, and disable the whole editing engine. RecordForm supplies staging/commit ownership, preserves stable occurrences and disposes them when removed. Ordinary widgets retain their existing change contract. RecordState admits one editor owner through bindEditorOwner; its disposer detaches only that owner and invalidates pending onchange reads. Incoming load, onchange and save values pass draft admission before replacing an accepted source. This ensures direct Save paths also await pending drafts. A standalone control must not invent persistence or bypass the record owner. The Technical Views form declares arch_db with explicit XML mode. Existing databases require the normal base addon data upgrade to receive that declaration. Invalid-locator overlays, general Html wiring and additional upstream adapter options remain outside this delivery; SPEC-WIDGET-030 is partial.

SchemaNode::ScopedDomain and DescriptionValueBuilder::scoped_domain carry a validated expression document with a descriptive target model. They grant no ORM or caller authority. The independent constructed-value and serialized visitors keep criterion fields in that model, and category variable names in the root scope, including otherwise special names such as uid. validate_panel_domain enforces the narrower panel grammar; general expression admission alone does not authorize a panel predicate. The native host independently checks that the target model matches the section relation and that RHS dependencies name declared categories. Builtin list/search declarations publish web.list_sections_v1 / web.search_sections_v1. The schema grammar revision remains 1. Closed sections payloads require these capability keys; the adapter and updated client still admit legacy shapes under old keys. Structural callbacks cannot populate default_values: the reserved adapter initializes empty arrays and the host's caller overlay is their only producer. Broader panel controls remain unavailable for now; metadata acceptance is not interactive parity. For H18 panel producers, with_checked_panel_view admits raw syntax before access filtering and removes complete denied sections and their dependents before the callback. The final host still rechecks emitted scopes and access. CheckedNode::source_child_count and source_sibling_ordinal preserve original numeric shape and IDs without exposing denied text. They prevent pruning from changing an extended declaration into the legacy selection contract. DescriptionReservation::grow admits additional retained capacity against the same sticky request allowance; it cannot raise or reset that allowance. Public examples are checked as Rust doctests.

The list-companion boundary converts only recognized unsupported panel syntax into a located unsupported descriptor; the list and its ordinary domain remain usable. Standalone search requests return the corresponding Validation error. Panel class, section icon_class and category depth are not accepted then ignored. Their values never appear in diagnostics. Unknown references, permission failures outside section pruning, exhausted budgets and database failures retain their errors. Whitespace-only domains are invalid; absent/empty source and canonical [] retain their existing meaning, while padded  []  remains a declared empty domain. A plain relational section also requires Read access on its comodel. Unreadable sections and filters depending on denied categories disappear together. Custom callbacks receive no exemption. Section wire IDs are positive NonZeroU32 values. PanelDomain::new is internal to the adapter. PanelSection::defaults() exposes a slice. The variant fields and PanelDefaults deserialization are still raw transport: code holding &mut PanelSection can replace them. The invariant comes from the host sequence, final-host refusal of structural defaults followed by the checked overlay. The native PanelCallerDefaults::checked factory checks the actual registry model/field, value type, count, selection keys and duplicates. Its private, non-deserializable value binds the section ID, model, field and kind; set_caller_defaults accepts only that value and refuses rebinding; reserve retained storage under the request budget first. Raw DTO deserialization remains untrusted and must pass final host admission.

docs.title: WASM addons: one source, a native crate and a sandboxed component

sections.text: Status: implemented (macros, dispatch, lifecycle, CLI, proof of concept, UI and override surfaces). The macros and erp-sdk compile the same addon source natively and for wasm32-wasip2; a component exports describe() and runs its methods in mixed native/WebAssembly override chains, overrides the core create, write and unlink, and contributes scalar computed fields and constraints; a package installs into a running server, brings views, window actions, menus and access rows, and its public methods are callable from the web client. Onchanges of a component come later. Contract: ADR 0081, wit/addon/. Design: docs/design/m2b-macros-wasm-backend.md. Every example is taken from code that builds in CI: crates/erp-test-models/addons/test_wasm_dual_a and test_wasm_dual_b and test_wasm_dual_c, tested by crates/erp-test-models/tests/wasm_dual_describe.rs, wasm_dispatch_chain.rs and wasm_dispatch_component.rs (CI step wasm-dual-describe).

You write #[model], #[extend], #[methods] with #[method], #[method(override)], #[compute], #[constrains], #[onchange] and addon! exactly as for a native addon (see models.md, cross-addon-extension.md). No cfg appears in business code. erp_sdk selects its backend by target: the native one links the ORM, registry and database crates; for WebAssembly it is a small facade over erp-fields and the guest bindings, with no ORM or database dependency. use erp_sdk::prelude::*; erp_sdk::addon!(name = "test_wasm_dual_a", depends = ["base"]);

pub struct Dual { #[field(char, required = true)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(integer, default = 1)] pub qty: i32, } An addon that extends another does so as on native: depend on the other crate and #[extend(Dual)]. Both crates end up in one component.

The crate you compile to the component (the leaf: test_wasm_dual_b above) writes one line: erp_sdk::export_component!(); Natively it expands to nothing. On WebAssembly it exports the addon world. Two build requirements: Model company_access declarations use the same #[model] and #[extend] syntax in both targets. The package loader reads all four forms from the component descriptor and passes them to registry validation (ADR 0093). A malformed or unsupported declaration refuses the package operation. Omission has the same meaning as an absent native declaration; it does not imply unrestricted. The encoded company_access expression is limited to 8,192 bytes; the decoded unrestricted reason remains limited to 512 bytes. For an existing package, deploy a server that understands this descriptor first, upgrade the package with its explicit decisions, and verify it reloads before enabling mandatory company access declarations for the registry. 1. **Lints.** The export glue is the component ABI's unsafe code, which the workspace's unsafe_code = "forbid" cannot allow. In the leaf crate's Cargo.toml replace [lints] workspace = true with `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny" plus the workspace's clippy denies (see test_wasm_dual_b/Cargo.toml`). The glue is allowed on that one expansion; nothing you write is unsafe. 2. **Fat LTO.** Build with lto = "fat" (CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat). Without it the linker may drop the registrations of a dependency addon that no code references, and describe() would then miss that addon. CI builds the fixture this way and compares the result with the native build, which fails on a missing addon. CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat cargo rustc --release -p erp-addon-test_wasm_dual_b \ --crate-type cdylib --target wasm32-wasip2 erp addon build --target wasm does this for you: erp addon build my_addon --target wasm --addons-path ./addons erp addon package my_addon --addons-path ./addons -o my_addon-1.0.0.erpaddon build compiles the crate in the addon directory as a cdylib for wasm32-wasip2 with fat LTO (set for that build only), loads the result with the WASM host under its CPU and memory limits, and checks that describe() lists the addon and every dependency of its manifest that has a [wasm] section; a missing one is an error naming it. The component is then written to <addon>/wasm/<name>.wasm. The manifest needs a [wasm] section (sdk_version = "1.0"); a dependency that is a native addon, or that is not in the search paths, is listed in the output as not expected. package writes the .erpaddon (manifest, the files data/demo name, i18n/, migrations/, static/dist/, the component, SHA256SUMS), reads it back from disk with the installer's reader, and prints the archive sha256 and the capabilities the manifest requests. Both commands need the target once: rustup target add wasm32-wasip2; if it is missing they stop with that command before building. Details: docs/design/m2b-cli.md.

A component's describe() returns what erp_sdk::describe() returns in a native program that links the same addons: compact JSON, {"schema":1,"contributions":[...]}, one entry per addon, model, extension, method, override, compute, constraint and onchange, sorted by (addon, model, kind, name, detail). An entry has addon, kind (addon, model, extend, method, override, compute, compute_override, constraint, onchange), model (empty for addon), name and a detail object. Models and extensions carry their arguments and fields (name, kind, attrs); methods their arguments and result type; computes depends, reads, depends_context; constraints and onchanges their field lists. Values are the source text you wrote ("1", "\"Note\""), not resolved types. The text is produced by the macros at compile time, so the native and the WASM build of one source cannot differ.

A component runs the methods its addon registered (#[method], #[method(override)]) inside the same override chains as native addons: a WebAssembly layer sits between native layers in the order of the addons, and super crosses in both directions. A chain that mixes native and WebAssembly layers needs the wire form of the native method: every native #[method] whose arguments and result implement `Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static` has it without any attribute (WASM.WIRE-NATIVE). When the types of a native method are not serialisable, or the method is sealed (below), the registry build refuses the chain and names each native implementation with the type that blocks it (for example Vec<RawVals>, argument vals_list) or the place that seals it. #[method(wire)] (or #[method(override, wire)]) is still accepted: it asserts at compile time that the method has a wire form, and the compile error names the method and the type. Arguments travel as the JSON of the tuple (["x"]; no arguments is null), the result as JSON.

async fn label(this: &RecordSet<Dual>, tx: &mut Transaction, prefix: String, sup: Super) -> Result<String> { let inner = sup.call(tx, this, (prefix,)).await?;   // the layer below, native or WebAssembly Ok(format!("{inner}{MARK}")) }

#[method(sealed)] (or #[method(override, sealed)]) keeps a native method out of every chain that has a WebAssembly layer: a package that overrides it is refused when the registry is built, with the method and the place that seals it, whatever its types. One sealed implementation seals the chain. Seal what a package must never wrap or skip: credentials, sessions, API keys, access rows, groups and membership, company access, record rules, validation of stored definitions (views), and the schema and registry hooks (init, _register_hook). sealed and wire contradict each other and are refused together. Base and mail seal their methods of that kind; the list is in docs/design/WASM.WIRE-NATIVE-plan.md, section "Sealed methods". Three more seals need no attribute: - Every #[constrains] method is sealed as a constraint and every #[onchange] method as an onchange: the ORM runs them through their chains while it checks a write or answers a form, and a package layer that does not call super would skip the check. Package overrides of constraints come with WASM.COMPUTE-REL, of onchange methods with WASM.ONCHANGE. wire on such a method is a compile error. - The core seals its record-level methods (action_archive, action_unarchive, create, write, unlink, copy, copy_data, default_get, name_create, upsert, exists, filtered_domain) on res.users, res.groups, ir.access, res.users.apikeys and ir.config_parameter (the list SEALED_ON_MODEL in crates/erp-orm/src/method_wire.rs), whatever the native entries of the chain say; the refusal names the model, the method and the list's line. - A native entry with no wire record at all (a core method without a codec yet, a selection hook, an implementation registered by hand) refuses every chain that crosses into a package, naming that entry. A seal limits overriding, not calling. Native code and RPC call a sealed method as before. What a package may call is decided separately (the methods exposed over RPC and the addon's own, CallableMethods in crates/erp-wasm-host/src/dispatch.rs). A sealed implementation contributes no wire codec, so a package's call in the wire form reaches a sealed method only when another native implementation of its chain has one; otherwise the call is refused, naming what blocks it.

async fn _set_password(this: &RecordSet<ResUsers>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<()> { /* … */ } What a body may do in a component today: this.ensure_one(), this.get(tx, Field) and this.set(tx, Field, value) for boolean, integer, float, decimal (read), char, text, html, selection, date, datetime, many2one and x2many fields; sup.call(tx, this, args); the typed <Type>Methods call of another method (this.shout(tx, text).await); tx.search_json(domain_json, limit, order); and creating, writing several fields at once and following a relation (next section). Each is an orm-host import made as the calling user and company and through the ORM's access rules; the host refuses what the administrator did not approve (orm:read, orm:write, orm:create, orm:unlink, orm:call-method) with access-denied. A body must not wait on anything but those calls. One call has a time budget (Limits::cpu, default 500 ms) that covers the guest and every host call it waits for; a runaway or overdue call fails the method and poisons the transaction. The same source runs natively: get, set, ensure_one, sup.call and the <Type>Methods calls have the native signatures. search_json is the one guest-only call (the typed Domain is not in a component yet). A component has no source of randomness: std::collections::HashMap and HashSet trap on first use with wasi:random/insecure-seed ... has not been defined. Use BTreeMap/BTreeSet or a Vec.

A component creates records, writes several fields at once, takes an empty recordset of another model and follows a many2one to its records with the native API (crates/erp-test-models/addons/test_wasm_refs is the same source in both modes; tests/wasm_refs_flow.rs runs it natively and as a component and expects the same answers): let loans = this.env().model::<Loan>()?;                 // empty RecordSet<Loan>; env().model is the native call let vals = loans.vals()                                  // Vals<Loan>: only Loan fields (or those of models it inherits) .set(Loan::BOOK_ID, book.rec_ids()[0])               // Many2one<Book> takes a RecId .set(Loan::BORROWER_ID, partner_id) .set(Loan::LOAN_DATE, today)                         // Option<Date> takes a Date .set(Loan::STATE, "out");                            // Option<Arc<str>> takes &str let loan = loans.create(tx, vec![vals]).await?;          // RecordSet<Loan> of the new records book.write(tx, book.vals().set(Book::AVAILABLE, false)).await?;   // several fields: one write let book = loan.related(tx, Loan::BOOK_ID).await?;       // Many2one<Book> -> RecordSet<Book> (x2many too) | Call | Signature in both backends | Goes through | |---|---|---| | this.env() / tx.env() | &Env / Env; Env::model::<M>() -> Result<RecordSet<M>> | nothing: an empty set. Whether the model exists is the host's to say, at the first call that uses it | | Vals::<M>::new(), rs.vals(), .set(field, value) | typed by the field handle; a handle of another model does not compile | nothing | | rs.create(tx, Vec<Vals<M>>) | Result<RecordSet<M>>, one create-batch for the list; an empty list is a no-op | the model's whole create chain: every addon's override runs (native and WebAssembly), then the core. Needs orm:create; a create layer that calls super also needs orm:unlink, because values may carry x2many removals | | rs.write(tx, Vals<M>) | Result<()>, one write-batch for all fields; nothing happens on an empty set or no value | the model's whole write chain. Needs orm:write | | rs.related(tx, field) | Result<RecordSet<Comodel>> for a Many2one<C> or X2many<C> handle, in order, each record once | one read-columns. Needs orm:read | | rs.browse(ids), rs.iter(), rs.rec_ids(), rs.len() | as native | nothing | Values cross with the host's own validation, field by field: a value that does not fit its field is a validation error naming the field, never a default. Not in a component yet: x2many command values in Vals (Vals::commands), new (in-memory) records, Records::create on untyped sets.

model_ref!(pub Loan = "sample_library.loan") names a model. Add a field list to also get typed Field handles for fields that the owner (a data-only addon's TOML, or a native addon) or another extending addon declared: erp_sdk::model_ref!( /// sample_library.loan, declared by the data-only addon sample_library. pub Loan = "sample_library.loan" { state: Option<Arc<str>>,        // selection (also char, text, html) book_id: Many2one<Book>,        // Book is another model_ref! borrower_id: Many2one<Partner>, loan_date: Option<Date>, due_date: Option<Date>, return_date: Option<Date>, } ); // Loan::STATE, Loan::BOOK_ID, ... are Field<Loan, T> constants (the field name in upper case); // Loan is also the model type of #[extend(Loan)] and #[methods(Loan)]. - The handle types are the field types of #[field]: bool, i32/Option<i32>, f64, Decimal, Option<Arc<str>> (char, text, html, selection), Option<Date>, Option<DateTime>, Option<serde_json::Value>, Many2one<C>, X2many<C> (one2many, many2many), Vec<RecId>. Any other type is a compile error (trait bound RefType). - The handle list goes into describe() (entry kind model_ref, with the kinds the Rust type can hold and the comodel of a relation). **When a package is installed or upgraded, the installer checks every handle against the registry of the module set it joins**: a model nobody declares, a field the model does not have, a field of a kind the Rust type cannot hold (Option<Arc<str>> on an integer field) or a Many2one<C> whose field points at another model refuses the install with WasmReason::ModelRef, naming the addon, the model and the field, and nothing is written. This was chosen over a first-use check because the guest has no field metadata, and a handle that cannot work should never reach a running database. - A native build of the same source has no installer: a wrong handle shows at first use, as the ORM's own error for an unknown field or a value of the wrong type. describe() carries the same entry natively, so a test can run the check (erp_modules::wasm_lifecycle::check_refs_in_registry, used by wasm_refs_flow.rs). - The handles do not make this addon the owner of the fields: they add no field, column or access rule. Declare the addon's own fields with #[extend] as before. Two addons may name the same fields independently.

The core methods are overridden from a component exactly as from a native addon, with the same signatures and super. No wire is needed on them: the core implementations ship their wire form. The same holds for name_create (["name"] in, [id, "display name"] out), action_archive and action_unarchive (null in and out) since WASM.WIRE-NATIVE. On res.users, res.groups, ir.access, res.users.apikeys and ir.config_parameter these core methods are sealed (above) and cannot be overridden from a component.

async fn write(this: &RecordSet<Loan>, tx: &mut Transaction, mut vals: RawVals, sup: Super) -> Result<()> { if vals.contains("due_date") && !vals.contains("renewal_note") { vals.insert("renewal_note".into(), Cell::Str("due date edited by hand".into())); } sup.call(tx, this.as_records(), (vals,)).await        // the core write, same user and company } - The override sits in the chain at the position of its addon, in the same (depth, order) order as native layers: a native layer above and one below it both run, in that order (wasm_override.rs). - super reaches the next layer or the core implementation with the environment of the records the method was invoked on (user, sudo, companies, context): access rights, record rules and the other checks of the core apply to what the override passes down, and a refusal comes back as the same error kind. An override cannot widen what its caller may do. - create takes Vec<RawVals> and returns Records (the new ids); write takes RawVals and the records are the ones being written; unlink takes nothing. Values travel as JSON and are converted again with the field's own type on the way down, so a value that does not fit its field is a validation error naming the field, never a default. - A component's RawVals has the scalar API of the native one (get, insert, remove, contains, iter). A selection is a Cell::Str; date/datetime text also stays Cell::Str, while an x2many command list or JSON document stays Cell::Json. An untouched value goes back unchanged; the host validates it against the field. - A create override must answer exactly the records its super() created, in order. The host records what the super-call of create returned and compares: any other answer (a dropped, repeated or foreign id) is a validation error and the transaction cannot commit. The answer must also have one record per input value; skipping super for a non-empty create is refused. - An unlink or write override that does not call super skips the layers below, the core included, and still reports success, as an override that does not call super() does in Odoo. Call super unless you mean to veto by returning an error. - In a sudo or System environment (module install, data load, sudo() callers) a guest asks the host for nothing but super-call: the elevation belongs to the caller, not to the guest. Test a method that reads or writes as an ordinary user. - An override that returns an error ends the call; the layers below do not run. A Validation error poisons the transaction as in a native override.

These six core methods are overridden from a component the same way since WASM.WIRE-NATIVE.CORE-CODECS: the same signature as in a native addon, super reaches the layer below or the core, and no wire is needed. Before, the registry build refused such an override. use erp_sdk::ValueMap;

async fn default_get(this: &RecordSet<Loan>, tx: &mut Transaction, fields: Vec<String>, sup: Super) -> Result<ValueMap> { let mut values = sup.call(tx, this.as_records(), (fields,)).await?;   // the core's defaults values.insert("renewal_note".to_owned(), Value::str("new loan")); Ok(values) } | Method | Arguments | Result | What crosses (the JSON of the argument tuple, the JSON of the result) | |---|---|---|---| | copy | Option<ValueMap> (the default) | Records | [default], a values object or null; the ids of the copies | | copy_data | Option<ValueMap> | Vec<Option<ValueMap>> | [default]; one values object (or null) per record | | default_get | Vec<String> (field names) | ValueMap | [[field, ...]]; a values object | | exists | none | Records | null; the ids that exist | | filtered_domain | Domain | Records | [domain] in list syntax; the matching ids | | upsert | UpsertCall | UpsertResult | [{"key", "rows", "update", "accumulate"}]; one [id, outcome, previous_version, version] per input row | - The types have the names and the methods of the native ones (erp_sdk::ValueMap, and Domain, UpsertCall, UpsertOutcome, UpsertResult in the prelude), so one source compiles in both backends. In a component a ValueMap is the same ordered map (insert, get, iter); a Domain is its list syntax (Domain::from_json(&json), to_json()), without the builder API; an UpsertCall has the builder and accessors of the native one. - Values are untyped on the way, as a client's, and the host checks each against its field when the call reaches the native implementation: a value that does not fit is a validation error naming the field. A field that has no form in this ABI (bigint, uuid, xid8, timestamptz, binary) is refused by name in a default and in an upsert row, as in create and write. - exists and filtered_domain are filters: an override answers a subset of the records it ran on, each at most once. An id that is not one of them, or that comes twice, is a validation error naming the id. - copy answers one record and copy_data one entry per record it ran on, and default_get answers only fields it was asked for; any other answer is a validation error naming the difference. - The result of an upsert has one entry per input row, in input order; an override that answers another count is refused, naming both counts. Leave the number of rows unchanged when you adjust rows_mut(). - A domain an override passes down is read as external input: the internal traversal operators of native framework code do not cross, so a native caller's domain that uses them is refused at the layer, by name. - Capabilities for the super of these methods (and for calling the exposed ones) follow what they do: copy and copy_data need orm:create, orm:unlink (their values may carry remove commands) and orm:read (they read the records), upsert needs orm:create, orm:write, orm:unlink and orm:read, default_get, exists and filtered_domain need orm:read. - An addon's own default_get or copy_data runs only when the addon holds orm:create and orm:unlink, even if it calls nothing: what it answers becomes the values of a create, and values for a create need those capabilities however they are supplied. Without them the call is an access error naming the capability. - On res.users, res.groups, ir.access, res.users.apikeys and ir.config_parameter all six are sealed. - Not checked at the boundary: the answers of copy and upsert overrides are not compared with what their super did (the host does that for create only). Access to the records they name is checked when they are used.

pub popular: bool,
fn compute_lending_summary(batch: &mut Batch<'_, Book>) -> Result<()> { /* batch.get / batch.set */ }

async fn check_renewals(this: &RecordSet<Loan>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<()> { /* Err(Error::validation(..)) */ } - A compute is a synchronous fn(batch) over plain fields of its own model listed in depends and reads. The host reads those fields as the invoking environment reads them (access rights, record rules and field groups apply), hands the values over as data and takes the assigned columns back. A compute asks the host for nothing (every orm-host request is refused), never runs elevated (compute_sudo = true is refused at install; the default is forced to false) and may not name a field restricted to groups. It also runs on records that are not in the database yet. Stored and non-stored computes use the ORM's own dependency tracking: a write to a dependency marks the field and it is recomputed on read or at flush. - A constraint is an async method that runs once on the whole recordset, in the environment that wrote, after a write or a create touched a field of its list. It is not elevated and its bridge is read-only: it may read (and search) with that user's rights, and any other request is refused. In a sudo or System environment it may ask for nothing, so the write fails closed. Its error, whatever kind the guest used, reaches the caller as a validation error; the transaction is poisoned and nothing is committed. - Batch::get/values/set/set_all and RecordSet::mapped have the native signatures. A computed or constrained field of a package may be boolean, integer, float, char, text or html; dates and relational fields are read as the follow-up lists below say. - Not available, refused by name when the package is installed (WasmReason::Unsupported), never skipped: async computes, #[compute(override)], a depends or reads path through a relation (line_ids.qty), #[onchange], inverse, related, precompute. A computed field must name a compute the addon declares on the same model, and every compute must fill a field (WasmReason::DescribeMismatch). - The first call of a compute after install also fills the stored field of rows that already exist.

Date values cross typed get/mapped/set as days since 1970-01-01; DateTime values cross as microseconds since midnight UTC. Null remains None. Dates are calendar days and datetimes mean naive UTC: caller timezone never shifts them. The native temporal types are reexported by the SDK prelude. Lifecycle create/write overrides use JSON server text: dates use YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes use YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (without microseconds). This seam has second precision even though WIT scalar/column transfers preserve microseconds. RawVals keeps incoming strings as Cell::Str; the host validates them against the target field, rather than guessing that arbitrary strings are dates. Typed date cells inserted into RawVals serialize with the same server-text precision. Range fields are outside this support.

this.context_today(tx)? is Odoo's fields.Date.context_today(record): today's date as a Date, in the time zone of the call (the context tz; UTC when the context has none or an unknown one, as in Odoo). The signature is the same in a component and natively, so one source compiles for both:

async fn lend(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<i32> { let loan_date = this.context_today(tx)?;                       // 2024-01-02 in Asia/Jakarta let due_date = Date::from_days(loan_date.days() + 14); Ok(due_date.days()) } Natively the zone comes from the recordset's own environment; in a component it comes from the call context, which the host built from the same environment. Without a recordset, Date::today() is today in UTC, Date::context_today("Asia/Jakarta") today in a named zone and Date::context_today_at(zone, timestamp) the date of a given naive-UTC datetime in a zone; an unknown zone name is a Validation error there. The component reads the clock through the host's wasi:clocks/wall-clock (what SystemTime::now() uses in the Rust standard library), reported to the microsecond. It is the only WASI import the host answers with real data; the monotonic clock, environment, randomness and the rest still trap when called (ADR 0081 amendment 2026-10-28). A component that uses time zones carries the bundled time-zone database (about 340 KB in the fixture, release build with fat LTO); one that does not use them does not.
