A WebAssembly addon is shipped as a .erpaddon package (the [wasm] section of manifest.toml and wasm/<name>.wasm). The administrator's program installs it into a database without changing other databases. Embedded library callers can adopt the returned registry directly. The native membership-bound server requires draining and restarting membership when package identity changes; see [Native membership and installed package identity](#native-membership-and-installed-package-identity). // once, at start-up: the package runtime goes to the module system, the lifecycle wraps both let packages = WasmPackages::new(Arc::new(HostLoader::new(host, Limits::default()))); let system = Arc::new(ModuleSystem::builder(pool, index).signal(signal).package_runtime(packages.clone()).build()?); let life = WasmLifecycle::new(system, packages); // the administrator approves what the package asks for, then installs it let package = ErpAddonPackage::from_bytes(&bytes)?.consent(&consent)?;   // capabilities, client-code digest let outcome = life.install(&env, package).await?;                          // switch to outcome.orm life.upgrade(&env, newer_package).await?; life.uninstall(&env, &ModuleName::new("my_addon")?).await?; // an authenticated administrator (a browser or API session) goes through the trusted authorizer life.install_authorized(&authorizer, package).await?;   // also upgrade_authorized, uninstall_authorized Who may call: install, upgrade and uninstall are the operator (CLI) entry points and accept only the System environment (uid 1) of the module system, as the native immediate operations do; any other caller is refused with AccessDenied before the package is looked at. The *_authorized forms take the same InstallAuthorizer the browser installation of native addons uses: it rechecks the session and the module-administration right inside the operation transaction, under the lifecycle lock. The audit row names the actor: the administrator's own uid and the session id (actor_kind = 'session'), or uid 1 ('operator') on the operator path. A package cannot take the name of a native addon: base, web, an installed addon and an addon of a development folder are refused. One package may contribute at most 4096 methods, 256 models and 4096 fields (WasmReason::TooLarge). What is checked before anything is written: the package digest and consent (by type: consent() is the only way to get the ConsentedPackage that install takes), that every dependency of the manifest is already installed (the lifecycle never installs dependencies for you), that describe() names your addon and the same dependencies as the manifest (a different name or dependency list fails), and that the addon uses only what this build can run: | In describe() | Now | |---|---| | models and extensions with boolean, integer, float, char (size), text, html, date, datetime fields and the attributes string, help, required, readonly, copy, store, translate | read into the registry; the schema is synced in the same transaction | | methods (method, override) | joined into the override chains | | compute and compute_sudo on a field; scalar compute (sync, plain-field depends/reads) and constraint contributions | read; the compute graph and the constraint list of the ORM are given the computes and constraints of the package | | model kind = "regular", "abstract" or "transient"; many2one fields with a nonempty comodel and optional ondelete = "set null", "restrict" or "cascade" | read into the registry; see [Wizard dialogs](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/wizard-dialogs.md) for the transient form flow | | on a transient model: transient_max_age_seconds and transient_max_count, plain decimal integers (0 disables a threshold) | read into the registry as the validated cleanup policy, the same as natively; declared only, no cleanup runs yet ([Wizard dialogs](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/wizard-dialogs.md#cleanup-policy)) | | selection fields (selection = [("value", "Label"), ...]), default, index, digits = (p, s) on float, groups; keys, parent_store and parent_name on a model the package creates | read into the registry, see [Field attributes, keys and a parent store](#field-attributes-keys-and-a-parent-store) | | selection_add, selection_method, default_fn, a named digits; keys, parent_store or parent_name on an extension; the raw SQL forms constraints, indexes, unique_indexes | refused by name (WasmReason::Unsupported) | | other relational field declarations, related; async or overriding compute, onchange contributions | refused by name (WasmReason::Unsupported), nothing is skipped | | manifest capabilities (network:outbound:, filesystem:temp:, migrations-sql) | refused (CapabilityUnavailable): this host cannot enforce them yet. The ORM access every addon has is bounded by the caller's own rights | Everything happens in the module system's own operation transaction: the package row (ir_module_package), one audit row (ir_module_wasm_audit: operation, versions, SHA-256, capabilities, acknowledged client-code digest, actor) and the registry-change signal other nodes wake on. Any error rolls all of it back and the registry you were using stays the only one. An operation that would change anything else (a dependent uninstalled with it, a dependency installed on the way) is refused. uninstall refuses while other installed addons depend on the package, and removes its models' data under the module system's uninstall rules. A restarted server, or a node whose registry generation moved because another node changed a package, calls life.load(): it reads the installed packages from ir_module_package, checks each stored archive again (content address, SHA256SUMS, capabilities and client-code digest against the row) and loads the module set.
A package model uses the same attribute syntax as a native #[model]; the installer reads the attribute text describe() carries (SPEC-WASM-030, SPEC-WASM-031, SPEC-WASM-032, SPEC-WASM-033):

name = "my_assets.asset", keys = [key(name = "_serial_uniq", fields = ["serial_no"], message = "The serial number must be unique.", nulls_distinct = true)] )] pub struct Asset { #[field(char, index)]                                   // index, index = true, index = "trigram" pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(char)] pub serial_no: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(selection, selection = [("draft", "Draft"), ("done", "Done")], default = "draft")] pub state: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(float, digits = (16, 2), default = 1.5)] pub amount: Decimal, #[field(char, groups = "base.group_system")] pub secret: Option<Arc<str>>, }

pub struct Node { #[field(char)] pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, #[field(many2one, comodel = "my_assets.node")] pub parent_id: Option<RecId>, #[field(char, index)]                                   // the path the ORM maintains pub parent_path: Option<Arc<str>>, } - **Defaults** are literals: a string, a number (negative too) or true/false. false on a field that is not boolean means "no value", as in a model file. default_fn names a Rust function and is refused. - **Selection**: a static list of string pairs. selection_add (extending another addon's list) and selection_method are refused; selection_add follows in a later slice. A list is bounded by MAX_SELECTION_ENTRIES; a longer one is refused, not cut. - **digits** is (precision, scale) on a float only; a named precision (digits = "price") is refused. - **index** with a named kind ("trigram", "brin", "gin") follows the native rules for the field type. - **Keys** are the typed key(name, fields, message, nulls_distinct) only, never SQL: the registry checks the fields. A duplicate create fails with the key's message. nulls_distinct = true is a plain UNIQUE (rows with an empty part do not conflict, Odoo's unique(field)); without it two rows with empty parts conflict. A temporal key (without_overlaps) and the raw SQL forms constraints, indexes and unique_indexes are refused: raw SQL is native only. Keys and parent_store belong to models the package **creates**; on an extend entry they are refused, since a key on a native table could make native inserts fail. - **Upgrading** to a version that adds a key over rows that already break it fails, names the key (cannot add key '_serial_uniq' to 'my_assets.asset': existing records conflict) and rolls back. An upgrade that turns parent_store on for a model the installed version has without it is refused (WasmReason::State, naming the model): nothing fills the paths of existing rows. Declare parent_store from the first version of the model. - **An extend entry only adds fields.** Redeclaring a field another addon introduced, with any attribute (string, sanitize, comodel, an index, ...), is refused at install, upgrade and load, naming the model, the field and the addon that declared it first. Changing the type of such a field is refused when the registry is composed. - **Value shapes are fixed.** selection, digits, default, keys and company_access are read by a flat reader that accepts only the forms shown above (string literals, numbers, true/false, ( ) [ ] , = -); any other expression, a call, an index, a method chain, a cast, however it is repeated, is refused naming the attribute. Each value has a byte cap. digits needs a precision of at least 1 and a scale not above it; a key may not name a field twice, and may not take a name the ORM generates (primary key, foreign key, not-null, field index, the parent path index, the id sequence). - **Upgrading** parent_name (or the model the parent field points to) while parent_store stays on is refused, naming the model. - **groups** restricts a field to a group. A package may set groups only on a field it introduces: when the registry is composed, a runtime declaration (package or model file) that sets groups on a field an earlier addon declared is refused, naming the model, the field and the addon that declared it first. The group applies to reads the same way as for a native field; a compute of a package reads with the caller's rights.

A model declared in a data-only addon (models/*.toml) has no Rust type. Name it with erp_sdk::model_ref!, then extend it and add methods as for any model; the fields of the model stay with its owner and the extension adds its own. From examples/wasm/sample_library_wasm/src/lib.rs (tested by crates/erp-cli/tests/wasm_addon_poc.rs): erp_sdk::addon!(name = "sample_library_wasm", depends = ["sample_library"]); erp_sdk::model_ref!(pub Loan = "sample_library.loan");   // add { field: Type, .. } for typed handles, see above
pub struct LoanRenewals { #[field(integer, string = "Renewals")] pub renewals: i32, }

impl LoanRenewals { #[method(wire)] async fn renew(this: &RecordSet<Loan>, tx: &mut Transaction, note: String) -> Result<i32> { let loan = this.ensure_one()?; let renewals = loan.get(tx, LoanRenewals::RENEWALS).await? + 1; loan.set(tx, LoanRenewals::RENEWALS, renewals).await?; Ok(renewals) } } A second package overrides it with super, from its own package, without editing the first (examples/wasm/sample_library_wasm_policy): #[method(override, wire)] async fn renew(..., sup: Super) refuses with Error::validation(..) or calls sup.call(tx, this, (note,)). When one addon is both the leaf of its own package and the dependency of another package's leaf, export the component behind a default feature and let the dependent turn it off, because a component exports once:
[features]                                              erp-addon-sample_library_wasm = { path = "..", default-features = false } default = ["component"] component = []

erp_sdk::export_component!(); The sample also shows the inherit/override surface: computed lending_summary (not stored) and popular (stored) on a book, a constraint limiting a loan's renewals, a write override with super on a loan, a create override on a book and an unlink override on a loan. Date and datetime fields support get/mapped/set. See docs/design/m2b-poc.md and docs/design/m2b-k-override.md. Screens, menus and RPC of a package are in the next two sections.

A package ships screens the way a data-only addon does: list the files under data in manifest.toml, put them in views/, data/ or security/, and erp addon package carries them (and SHA256SUMS covers them, so the archive is refused if one changes). They load in the install transaction through the same data loader as native addons: a failure rolls the whole install back, the records get external ids owned by the package, an upgrade reloads them, and uninstall removes them with the module's other data. A native dependency upgrade leaves the package version, archive and lifecycle audit unchanged. Before committing, it validates the installed package views against the final native views. If an inherited XPath no longer applies, the native upgrade rolls back and reports the package view that failed. Repair the native view or upgrade the package to a compatible extension before retrying; a native upgrade does not reapply the package's data files. Native-install and post-init-hook paths have not been validated by this task; this paragraph describes native upgrades only. From examples/wasm/sample_library_wasm: depends = ["sample_library"] data = ["views/sample_library_wasm_views.xml"] <erp> <!-- extend the form of another addon in place; nothing of sample_library is edited --> <record id="book_form_lend" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">sample_library.book.form.lend</field> <field name="model">sample_library.book</field> <field name="inherit_id" ref="sample_library.book_form"/> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <xpath expr="//field[@name='available']" position="after"> <field name="times_lent"/> <field name="last_borrower"/> </xpath> </field> </record> </erp> What a package's data files may declare (anything else fails the install, naming the file, the line and the rule): | Allowed | Notes | |---|---| | ir.ui.view records, also inherited views of any view of a dependency | the view's model must be a model the package declares or extends (#[model], #[extend], model_ref!). On a model it only **extends**: extension views only (inherit_id required, mode absent or extension), no priority. No type=qweb, no key | | ir.actions.act_window records | res_model must be a model the package declares or extends; binding_model_id only on an action for a model the package declares, as ref="<package>.model_..." | | <menuitem> and ir.ui.menu records | a menu may sit under another addon's menu (parent) and point at another addon's action | | access rows, in a CSV file named ir.access.csv (the platform's access model, see addons/base/security/ir.access.csv) | columns only id, name, model_id/id, group_id/id, operation (crud, r, …), active (no .id, no domain); only for models the package declares itself (model_id/id is <package>.model_...) | An addon that only extends (#[extend]) a model of another addon must add at least one field or method to it; an empty extension is refused at install. erp addon install|upgrade prints extended_models, next to rpc_methods. Rules that apply to every record: - **Ids are the package's own.** Every record id, menu item id and access-CSV id is unqualified or qualified with the package's own name; a record needs an id. A package cannot update base.* menus, another addon's views or actions or access rows (they would not be restored on uninstall). inherit_id, parent, action and ref() may point anywhere. - **A <field> name is given once per record**, and context and uid are not allowed on any element (<data>, <record>, <menuitem>). - **Values are checked by field type.** A one2many gets no value (no child records, no links). A many2many takes ref() or a list of 3-element commands whose code is a bare integer literal: (4, ref('x'), 0) link, (5, 0, 0) clear, (6, 0, [ref('x')]) set; lists and tuples are read alike, and (0, ...), (1, ...), (2, ...), (3, ...), dicts, +2, Command.* are refused. Any other field takes text, numbers, ref() and eval of literals, ref('...') and lists and tuples of them; search= lookups and file-valued fields are refused. The field must exist in the registry being installed. Refused by name: .sql files, demo data, <function>, <delete>, <template>, <asset>, records of any other model (for example res.users, ir.cron, record rules), and an access record written in XML. Data files live in views/, data/ or security/ and are .xml or .csv. A form view may carry a <header> with <button type="object"> (the rest of the header grammar is planned). The header must be the first child of <form>, so an inherited view adds it with <xpath expr="//sheet" position="before">. A button's name must be a method exposed on the form's model (see the next section): the form is refused when it is built otherwise. The sample adds a Lend button to the book form and a Renew button to the loan form. A wizard field that the opening action fills from its context (default_<field>, such as the Lend wizard's book_id) is declared readonly = true, as in Odoo: the form shows it but cannot change it, the web client does not send read-only fields when it saves, and create takes the value from the context default. The sample does this since version 1.3.2. Starting with version 1.3.3, the book form and list show both popular and lending_summary.
A method is callable from the web client and over call_kw/JSON-2 on a record only when you say so, as for a native method (#[rpc], ADR 0038): add rpc to the method attribute.

async fn lend(this: &RecordSet<Book>, tx: &mut Transaction, borrower: Option<String>) -> Result<i32> { /* ... */ } POST /erp/json/2/sample_library.book/lend      {"ids": [7], "borrower": "Reader"}   ->  2 rpc is carried in describe() ("rpc": true). Natively it is a no-op (#[rpc] is the native marker); the dual source stays one source. rpc on an override or on a name that starts with _ is a compile error. Nothing is exposed by default: a method without the marker, an override, a name that starts with _ and a method with an argument that is not a plain name are never callable from a client. - erp addon install and erp addon upgrade print rpc_methods: the model.method names the package opens to clients. Read it before you trust a package: the capability consent does not cover it. - Arguments are the method's arguments after this and tx, by name. Option<T> ones are optional (absent is null). A required one must be present and not null (422 before the method runs), and an integer, boolean, number or string argument is checked against its Rust type. Other types are accepted as any JSON value and the method's own deserialisation refuses a wrong shape (the guest reports it as an invalid argument, which is a 422). A button passes no arguments, so give the arguments it should be able to omit the type Option<T>. - The call runs as the signed-in user: the method's own reads and writes go through the ORM's access rules and record rules, so a user without write rights on the model is refused (403, access error) and nothing is stored. - Effect class is write: the transaction is a writing one, read-only API keys are refused, and the gates of the RPC service (scopes, idempotency keys) apply. A component cannot declare a read-only method yet. - The call reaches the top of the override chain, so an override from another package (the policy package in the sample) applies to a button press as well.

You need the server's deployment file (the one erp server --config reads), the .erpaddon, and the addons its dependencies come from already installed (for the sample: sample_library, installed from the Addons screen or erp module install). erp addon build sample_library_wasm --target wasm --addons-path addons,examples/wasm     # developer, once erp addon package sample_library_wasm --addons-path addons,examples/wasm -o sample_library_wasm.erpaddon erp addon install sample_library_wasm.erpaddon -d erpforall --config /etc/erpforall/server.toml --approve none erp addon upgrade sample_library_wasm-1.4.0.erpaddon -d erpforall --config /etc/erpforall/server.toml --approve none erp addon uninstall sample_library_wasm -d erpforall --config /etc/erpforall/server.toml - --approve is required (an empty element or a capitalised NONE is refused). List exactly the capabilities the package requests (comma-separated), or none. Approving more or less than the package asks for is refused. (This host cannot enforce any capability yet, so a package that requests one is refused at install.) - A package with client code (static/dist/) needs --ack-client-digest <sha256> of the code you reviewed (printed by erp addon package); a wrong digest, or a digest for a package without client code, is refused. - -d must be the database the configuration names. - On success one JSON line is printed: operation, addon, version, archive_sha256, database, installed, upgraded, uninstalled, rpc_methods, runtime_grants. Exit codes: 1 refused (nothing written), 3 another module operation is running (retry), 4 rolled back, 5 committed but the post-commit phase did not finish, 2 system error. - Package operations bump the registry generation. A native membership-bound server refuses publication if loading changes its immutable catalogue; drain and restart membership after install, upgrade or removal. A fresh server verifies the stored packages before registration. Embedded library callers manage their own registry replacement. Nothing is written to a server's addon directory. - Keep the Rust source of an addon you install as a package out of the server's addons_path (the samples live in examples/wasm, not addons/). If it is there anyway, the folder is refused as a native addon (its manifest has a [wasm] section) and the installed package wins. - If the output ends with the operation COMMITTED, but publishing the runtime grants failed, the package is installed. Fix the cause (usually the runtime role in the configuration) and run erp db publish-grants --config <file> before restarting native membership for the changed catalogue. Do not repeat the install: it would say the addon is already installed. - A server whose registry rebuild fails (a stored package that does not verify) keeps answering with maintenance and tries again after 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... up to 60 s between attempts, not on every request; the error is in the server log. - The command acts as the System principal; the audit table ir_module_wasm_audit records every operation, the package SHA-256 and the approved capabilities. Both tables are core tables created and owned by the schema owner, not by the runtime role. The audit table is insert-only (a trigger refuses row changes, removals and truncation even for the owner), the release grants give the runtime role nothing on it and only SELECT on ir_module_package (revoke_wasm_lifecycle_runtime_writes, called by grant_runtime). load() loads a stored package only when an install or upgrade audit row records the same archive with the same capabilities and client-code digest; a row written outside the lifecycle is refused. After the first package operation on a database, run the runtime grants publication so the runtime role can read the package store.

The native membership-bound server includes installed packages in its startup catalogue even when no corresponding source folder is shipped. It verifies archives and lifecycle consent before registration, then validates the loaded catalogue again before publishing authentication, RPC and assets (login-admission ADR 0126, docs/adr/0126-login-rollout-admission.md). Earlier native hot-update demonstrations in wasm_addon_poc.rs predate this membership boundary and remain historical, optional demonstrations; this repair does not certify them. Library lifecycle examples show registry loading, not native serving admission. For the native server, an install, upgrade or removal that changes the catalogue requires draining and restarting membership; keeping the same addon name does not permit different archive bytes under the old identity. Registry refresh with an unchanged catalogue remains supported. See the [operator procedure](/en/next/developer/installation/login-selection-rollout.md). The required wasm-startup-catalogue CI stage builds the actual sample WASM packages and runs native readiness, login and package-RPC checks with their sources outside the configured addon paths. The test is fixture-dependent and runs explicitly through scripts/wasm-poc.sh --startup-catalogue; an ordinary nextest run alone does not certify it.

A wizard is a record form opened over its caller by an exposed object method. Use a transient model for its temporary input and ordinary models for durable business results. Native and WASM methods share the server action-result normalizer and the human client's dialog controller (ADR 0088). This page describes the merged authoring contract. Installed native/WASM checks cover the sample lending flow, including confirmation, cancellation and access denial. They do not establish complete behavior parity; the limitations below still apply.

The existing sample at examples/wasm/sample_library_wasm/src/lib.rs uses #[model(name = "sample_library.lend.wizard", kind = "transient", ...)], required Many2one<Book> and Many2one<Partner> fields, and a required Option<Date> due date. This is the shared erp-sdk declaration surface for native and component targets. A WASM method opts into client calls with #[method(wire, rpc)]; use the native method exposure described in [RPC](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/rpc.md) for native-only addons. Declare ordinary access rows for the wizard and every business model it uses. A transient declaration or window action grants no elevated access. The normalizer checks read access to the target model; the subsequent reads, saves and object method still run with the caller's authority. Package the form with the addon data files. A direct, last <footer> holds the object method button and a cancel button with no method: <form string="Lend Book"> <group> <field name="book_id"/> <field name="borrower_id"/> <field name="due_date"/> </group> <footer> <button name="action_confirm" type="object" string="Lend" class="btn-primary"/> <button special="cancel" string="Cancel" class="btn-secondary"/> </footer> </form> The sample defines requiredness on the model, with no contradictory field-node modifiers. book_id is also readonly = true on the model (since 1.3.2): the Lend button sets it through default_book_id, the form shows it read-only, and create takes it from the context because the client does not send read-only fields. A footer is omitted on the main-route form. Load each added view through get_views in a test as a user who opens it; method tests alone do not establish that the form can render.

The sample's lend method returns this shape, filling the book id and calendar date from its own authorized record and date calculation: { "type": "ir.actions.act_window", "name": "Lend Book", "res_model": "sample_library.lend.wizard", "target": "new", "views": [[false, "form"]], "context": {"default_book_id": 1, "default_due_date": "2026-11-11"} } The id and date above are illustrative, not measured output. Return literal default_<field> values only, naming actual target fields. Do not return active_*, session, language or company selectors: the client composes those from its authenticated caller binding. Exactly one form selection is admitted; use views or view_id/view_mode, never both. An optional res_id must be positive and JSON-safe. Main-route actions and other view types are refused. The complete result is limited to 16 KiB serialized and depth 6. Context has at most 64 keys, model names at most 256 bytes, notification messages at most 4096 bytes and titles at most 256 bytes. Unknown members and wrong types fail by name. After validation/save, the sample's action_confirm reads the saved borrower and due date, creates a durable loan and marks the book unavailable. It returns ir.actions.client with tag display_notification, text params.message, optional params.title, params.type = "success", and params.next = {"type":"ir.actions.act_window_close"}. Levels also admit info, warning and danger. HTML rendering, links, sticky notifications and arbitrary action chains are outside this contract. An explicit close admits no additional members. Scalar results (null, booleans, numbers, strings) mean no action; arrays are refused.

Confirm validates and saves before the exposed method. Cancel does neither. Dismissal through Escape, close, replacement or navigation discards wizard edits without a prompt; a pending or uncertain write cannot be blindly dismissed. Close/no-action ends the dialog and refreshes its caller once without changing the caller route. Notification content is text. If the method response or its presentation is uncertain, do not retry the method: readback does not establish whether another business write is safe. The client keeps that operation read-only. An ambiguous save of an existing record has a separate readback recovery path; new-record defaults cannot prove that creation committed. Component onchange contributions remain unsupported; sharing the form's initial onchange transport does not add guest onchange support. WASM field declarations currently admit many2one, date and datetime alongside the scalar kinds listed in [WASM addons](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/wasm-addons.md); other relational field declarations remain refused. Transient expiry, vacuum and cleanup takeover are planned. No cleanup guarantee follows from closing a dialog.

A transient model can declare how long its rows may live. Two optional model parameters carry the policy (ADR 0092); the same names work in #[model] / #[extend], in the TOML of a data-only addon (transient_max_age_seconds = 7200) and in a WASM addon, which declares them through the same macro: | Parameter | Meaning | Default | |---|---|---| | transient_max_age_seconds | rows older than this may be removed | 3,600 (one hour) | | transient_max_count | the most rows the model keeps; the oldest surplus may be removed | not limited |

name = "sample_library.lend.wizard", kind = "transient", transient_max_age_seconds = 7_200, transient_max_count = 500 )] Rules, checked when the registry is built (a wrong declaration fails the addon load; nothing is defaulted silently): - 0 disables that threshold. Disabling both is allowed; the registry reports it (TransientPolicy::is_cleanup_disabled). - Values are plain non-negative integers: the age is at most 315,360,000 seconds (ten 365-day years), the count at most i64::MAX. Negative numbers, floats, strings, suffixes (3600u64), hex literals and overflow are refused with the model and the parameter named. - Only a transient model may declare them. A regular or abstract model that does is refused, naming the model and the parameter. - An in-place extension (#[extend], extend = "…") inherits the policy of the model it extends; a parameter it states itself overrides the inherited one, a parameter it leaves out is kept. - Native and WASM declarations compose the same validated policy (ModelSpec::transient_policy). **The cleanup is inactive until an operator runs or schedules it.** The ORM has a cleanup engine for transient models, Orm::vacuum_transient(model, VacuumOptions) (ADR 0092). It is a host-only library call: it opens its own system-principal transactions, takes no principal or context, and is not an RPC method, a model method or a WASM import, so an addon cannot call it. The operator entry point is the command erp db vacuum-transient (see [Running the transient cleanup](/en/next/developer/installation/transient-vacuum.md)). No scheduler, worker or request starts a cleanup, so a deployment removes no transient row until an operator runs the command or schedules it. Until then, treat transient rows as permanent for operational purposes.

erp db vacuum-transient --config /etc/erpforall/server.toml --model sample_library.lend.wizard --max-rows 5000 erp db vacuum-transient --config /etc/erpforall/server.toml --all Host code that already holds an Orm (a test, or the operator tooling) calls the engine directly. The block below only illustrates the engine's options (it is not compiled); the CLI argument example that is compiled as a doc test is on VacuumTransientArgs::options in erp-cli. use erp_orm::{VacuumOptions, VacuumOutcome}; let options = VacuumOptions::default().max_batch_rows(200)?.max_rows(5_000)?; assert_eq!((options.batch_rows(), options.rows()), (200, 5_000)); // the hard caps cannot be raised or disabled assert!(VacuumOptions::default().max_rows(0).is_err()); assert_ne!(VacuumOutcome::Completed, VacuumOutcome::Pending);

Write your unlink overrides so that they can fail only for a reason an operator can fix: a failing override on the oldest rows blocks every later call (the operations page describes the remedy). What a call does, once a host invokes it: - It removes rows through the normal unlink chain, so your unlink overrides, relation effects and errors behave as for any deletion (under the system principal). An error in your override rolls that batch back and is returned unchanged. - *Age*: rows whose last write (write_date, else create_date) is strictly before the cycle start minus the age (never less than 300 seconds). *Count*, after age: when the table holds more rows than the limit, every row older than 300 seconds goes, not just enough to get under the limit. A row written in the last 300 seconds is never removed. - It is safe on several replicas: a lease row in the tenant database (erp_transient_vacuum_state, created by sync_schema) decides who works. The report says Busy, NotDue, LostLease, Completed, Pending (stopped early or rows are locked by others: call again), BudgetExhausted, PolicyChanged or Disabled, with the committed row and batch counts. - Bounds: 1,000 rows per batch, 100 batches and 100,000 rows per cycle (persisted, a takeover does not reset them), a new cycle at most every 300 seconds. VacuumOptions can lower the caps of one call, never raise them. The caps bound the rows selected directly; an unlink override or cascade may touch more. - Rollback and backup: deleted rows cannot be restored by restoring an old executable. Disable the invocation first, then change the schema or policy.

The queue (ADR 0150) lives in three tables of the tenant database: erp_job (pending, running, held and dead jobs), erp_job_run (history) and erp_job_item_failure (items that failed alone). Any worker may claim any job of a kind its binary registers; there is no scheduler process and no leader. A job's lease is measured on the database clock, so clock skew between nodes cannot make two workers own one job. **Configuration delivery boundary.** The server has optional in-app job composition. Whether a particular dev/testing deployment has enabled it is not established by this guide. The declared database settings below govern new enqueues and claims on database-backed nodes. Running jobs retain their admitted limits.

Every setting has a default, a floor and a hard bound. A value outside them is refused by name the setting (jobs.poll_interval_secs = 0 is outside 1..=300); zero never means unlimited. jobs.wake_slack_ms = 0 wakes only exactly-due work; it is a threshold, never unlimited capacity. Capacity settings belong to the node; Shared policy comes from the tenant database. Node admission checks provider/catalogue compatibility while allowing saved policy to change without a restart. | Setting | Default | Allowed | |---|---|---| | jobs.workers (node) | 4 | 1 to 256 | | jobs.workers_per_db (node) | 2 | 1 to jobs.workers | | jobs.max_running_per_db | 16 | 1 to 4,096, divided by the live workers | | jobs.claim_batch (node) | 8 | 1 to 256 | | jobs.lease_secs | 90 | 15 to 3,600 | | jobs.reap_interval_secs | 15 | 1 to 300 | | jobs.poll_interval_secs | 5 | 1 to 300 | | jobs.notify_interval_ms | 1,000 | 50 to 60,000 | | jobs.wake_slack_ms | 1,000 | 0 to 60,000 | | jobs.max_chunks_per_run | 10 | 1 to 10,000 | | jobs.run_budget_secs | 120 | 1 to 3,600 | | jobs.job_deadline_secs | 900 | 10 to 86,400 | | jobs.chunk.default.{lock,statement,transaction}_ms | 5,000 / 30,000 / 60,000 | lock below statement below transaction | | jobs.chunk.maintenance.* | 5,000 / 300,000 / 600,000 | same | | jobs.backoff_base_secs, jobs.backoff_cap_secs | 10, 3,600 | 1 to 3,600; base to 86,400 | | jobs.max_attempts | 10 | 1 to 100 | | jobs.payload_max_bytes | 65,536 | 1,024 to 65,536 | | jobs.progress_max_bytes | 1,048,576 | 4,096 to 1,048,576 | | jobs.max_item_failures_per_job | 10,000 | 1 to 100,000 | | jobs.history_days | 7 | 1 to 3,650 | | jobs.dead_retention_days | 30 | 1 to 3,650 | A job's lease is max(jobs.lease_secs, its class's transaction timeout + 10 s), so a running chunk cannot outlive its lease unnoticed.

Settings administrators open **Technical > Automation > Background Job Settings** and find the **Background Jobs** block. These values are Global within the current tenant database, never per company. Each Shared internal key maps to base. plus its complete name, preserving nested timeout segments. Defaults and ranges are shown with units. **Use default** edits the field; **Save** audits the ordinary value write, while **Discard** reloads stored values. Defaults are returned for absent rows without seeding fake values or audit history. Installation/upgrade preserves saved choices. A save validates the entire resulting group, including unchanged members. Both timeout classes require lock < statement < transaction; backoff base must not exceed cap. Invalid batches, stale revisions and audit failures persist no prefix. A conflict requires reloading and reviewing the other writer's changes. Corrupt stored values fail by setting name; they never silently restore defaults. Saved values govern new enqueues and claims without restart. Active runs keep their admitted snapshot. The served request ORM, isolated owner runner and attachment recovery use the same database authority. Node workers/workers_per_db/claim_batch/run_in_app are excluded from the database editor because they describe local capacity and placement. Generic queue/history CRUD remains refused.

Per process and database a runner uses up to jobs.workers_per_db pool connections for claims and chunks plus the one shared signal-listener connection. Worker connections are processes x databases x workers_per_db (plus one listener each); count them next to the connection budget of the server. Database-backed policy adds a separate read pool of up to workers_per_db connections per process/database. The owner runner shares that reader pool; an operator recovery command uses one separate read connection. Enqueues send at most one payload-free NOTIFY erp_jobs per jobs.notify_interval_ms per process and database, and none when this process is the only node. The cluster-wide budget of notifying commits is shared with the signal, outbox and bus channels, so keep the interval at its default unless you have measured the cost. A lost or suppressed notification costs latency, never a job: every runner also polls every jobs.poll_interval_secs.

A job that fails for good stays in erp_job with state = 'dead', an error code and a bounded message (no payload text). An administrator holding the jobs.admin capability can requeue or discard it. Dead letters older than jobs.dead_retention_days move to history as dead_expired (the move is logged at warn with the count), history older than jobs.history_days is deleted in batches of at most 10,000 rows. Both run as core schedules once a runner is up. **Attachment schedules.** Installing or upgrading base, and every erp server start, creates the recurring rows of the attachment maintenance kinds (base.attachment_gc, base.attachment_clean_staging, base.attachment_reconcile) that are missing; existing rows keep their next run time. With jobs_run_in_app = true the in-app runner excludes the elevated attachment kinds (ADR 0165 D5, ADR 0185): their rows stay ready and are never claimed. Discard old attachment dead letters instead of requeueing them (a requeue collides with the live row on the dedup index). They show up in the job list as ready and run only where the isolated maintenance runner is enabled with attachment_maintenance_run_in_app = true ([attachment store](/en/next/developer/installation/attachment-store.md#garbage-collection)).

The native server maintains every installed partitioned model at startup and on an owner-role timer. This work runs independently of the ordinary job runner and its enable switch. It has no queue execution row yet. The closed audit/outbox event-table timer remains independent, including each node's audit-store readiness refresh. The database-wide system parameter base.partition_upkeep_interval_secs has default 3600 seconds and an allowed range of 60 through 3600. The Technical parameter form displays the range; administrator access to that screen remains unavailable until the separate parameter-access security work is delivered. An operator can use the trusted owner path meanwhile. Invalid edits are refused by name. Absent or empty values restore the default. Startup refuses invalid stored policy or incomplete upkeep. Later policy corruption skips that tick and emits a named error; recovery is retried at the last valid cadence. Committed changes are read at the next scheduled wake. There is currently no general event-maintenance health screen; inspect operator logs for failed steps and deferred drops. Budget one additional owner connection per serving process and tenant database. The fixed one-slot pool serves this serial operation only; requests retain their existing runtime role and receive no DDL privileges. Each run uses the database's UTC time, the current installed registry, and the partition engine's existing per-table locks. Multiple nodes can attempt upkeep safely. A lost connection releases locks; later runs recover interrupted work. Missing partitions continue to refuse inserts instead of routing them to a catch-all table.

Administrators holding the jobs.admin capability (granted to base.group_system by default) manage jobs and inspect runs through the technical views: - **Technical > Automation > Background Jobs** (ir.job): list and form views showing kind, state, priority, attempts, scheduled time, next run, deadline, worker, and duration. Action buttons allow operators to Hold (pause ready job), Resume (unpause held job), Cancel (stop queued job), Requeue (retry dead job), and Discard (abandon dead job). Generic record modifications (create, write, unlink) are refused: queue rows are lifecycle-managed only. - **Technical > Automation > Job Runs** (ir.job.run): read-only execution history displaying job UUID, worker identifier, start and finished timestamps, duration, chunk count, and outcome.

The runtime role holds SELECT, INSERT, DELETE on the three tables and UPDATE only on the lifecycle columns of erp_job (never the identity, kind, payload, keys or stored principal) and on the error columns of erp_job_item_failure. erp db publish-grants sets this, and the server's start check verifies it as the runtime role. A single runtime role means the in-process runner can change leases; a dedicated worker role is a later hardening.

Before enabling the database source, inventory any custom embedding's Shared jobs.* process overrides. A Settings administrator must review those values and save them through the Global Background Jobs group (or the same audited ir.config.setting CAS service). Remove every explicit Shared process override, including values equal to defaults, before starting the database-backed node. Startup never imports values and never makes the first node the policy writer. The served TOML parser does not expose a general Shared jobs.* table; do not add one as a migration shortcut. Node workers, workers_per_db and claim_batch remain local. The existing jobs_run_in_app server option is the source of the effective run_in_app choice. Native composition allocates a separate bounded read pool sized from the node workers_per_db capacity; it is shared by policy readers for that served generation. Enqueue transactions cannot consume that pool's connections. Missing declarations/schema, invalid values or an unavailable reader refuse new admission and emit an error. Repairing committed policy lets bounded polling resume admission, even after a lost notification. Existing active leases are not shortened. Old attachment owner markers have no admitted deadline recorded. Recovery therefore waits the jobs deadline catalogue's hard envelope, plus the existing check for a live ownership-singleton lease. Lowering the current deadline cannot prove older work finished. This conservative recovery wait can exceed the current configured deadline; operators must still inspect and confirm recovery normally. The first database-authority deployment changes jobs compatibility identity. Use the existing controlled rollout window or drain and replace the previous binaries; keep build/addon/readiness admission enabled.

Status: implementation candidate; not a deployment record. Ship the field sanitizer with its transport reporting and model-field editor in the same reviewed release train. Deployment goes through the build host to the dev/testing deployment. The storage type stays text (JSONB for translated fields). This change does not rewrite existing rows or make previously stored HTML trusted. Every renderer must keep its own safe reconstruction or sandbox boundary. A newly written value is admitted under its resolved registry policy; merged translated values are also admitted. Raw fields remain untrusted text, with sanitized=false and html_render_mode=sandbox in their description. No new daemon, database extension, secret, permission or configuration flag is required. Do not bypass sanitation with sudo or user groups. Named email presets are unavailable for now; a refusal is not a reason to switch the field to raw HTML. The diagnostic channel is attempt-local and is cleared at commit/rollback/reset. An API, import or job must transfer its reports before commit, publish only after successful commit, and discard reports from failed retries. Reports contain removal names/counts and sample node ordinals, not removed text or URLs. Excess diagnostic storage refuses the write explicitly. Do not enable a new consumer until its report delivery is verified. On a validation refusal, keep the input draft or failed import row for correction outside logs; do not log the rejected body. Retry only after correcting the input or changing an explicit supported policy. A database/unknown commit outcome follows the existing recovery protocol, never a blind write replay. Rolling the application back does not restore content removed by an already committed write; use the ordinary data backup/recovery procedure if restoration is required. Before release, test a clean edit, a removal with its diagnostic, strict refusal, required translated content removed to empty, savepoint rollback and raw-field display. Existing historical engine logs certify only their pinned source; focused host logs are kept with the release evidence. Product performance evidence remains deferred to milestone end under ADR 0065.

This procedure prepares digest-bound admission for custom login selection and describes its rollback. Apply it to a compatible candidate release. Release documentation and isolated tests do not prove that an installation has completed enrollment or activation: the responsible operator must retain actual installation-specific evidence and authorize cutover. The repository user page docs/user/login-selection.md describes sign-in behavior. A source inventory distinguishes inspected tests from runtime evidence and records remaining acceptance work. Publishing these pages does not enable the feature or certify a deployment.

Load operator credentials into DATABASE_URL through the installation's protected environment. Never put a connection string, password, cookie or signing secret in a command, issue or receipt. The cluster commands use those credentials and the database selected by -d. Converge schema using the release's supported module upgrade/schema procedure **before starting its native server**. Core DDL installs the feature tables and capability column; authentication inserts auth.login_principal, version 1, disabled only when absent. Repeated synchronization preserves activation, enrollment, approvals, counters and trust. Initial schema migration can require table locks and belongs before serving; repeated converged node DDL checks catalogs before column changes and leaves the membership and feature tables unlocked. Validation examines the actual principal CHECK/index definitions and helper identities, rather than trusting a version setting. The candidate needs explicit first helper provisioning/publication before serving, including when selection stays disabled. Ordinary runtime grants alone are insufficient. The supported release and clone preparation paths call the shared deployment helper. Schema migration must finish first. For an installation managed separately from these scripts, the equivalent explicit DBA sequence below remains available. Provision an isolated maintenance role through the database administrator: CREATE ROLE erp_node_feature_maint NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS; It must not own the tables, reach the database owner, or have business/session data privileges. Request and heartbeat roles must not reach it through INHERIT, SET or ADMIN paths. Keep those roles distinct. Do not substitute a LOGIN/operator role if publication fails. The trusted application owner needs one-way maintenance-role membership for repeat ownership management; the maintenance role must never inherit the application owner. Publish ordinary runtime/heartbeat grants, then the narrow feature helpers: erp cluster login-selection publish -d <db> --maintenance-role <maint> --request-role <runtime> Publication validates fixed helper bodies and execution attributes, grants request EXECUTE, transfers ownership to the maintenance role, and installs an ALWAYS INSERT/UPDATE row trigger. Request receives no node/feature relation rights. Heartbeat receives no feature-state or auth data rights. Re-publish after role-policy changes; inherited or column grants crossing these boundaries need explicit reconciliation. The deployment-only sidecar login-selection-publication.toml has exactly these keys: database = "tenant_database" maintenance_role = "tenant_login_helpers" provisioner_role = "tenant_role_provisioner" operator_database_url_file = "login-publication-operator-url" Keep both files private (mode 600 regular files, no symlinks), outside git and outside the serving container's mounts. The operator URL must name that database at the same endpoint as the owner/runtime/heartbeat credentials. The application owner remains NOCREATEROLE. The shared release preparation will create an absent safe role or validate an existing role, then use the candidate's ordinary and feature publication commands before switching or clone startup. Clone preparation must rewrite every credential binding to its isolated tenant and use a clone-specific maintenance role. The original tenant is never an implicit fallback. Use a dedicated non-superuser CREATEROLE provisioner with CONNECT to this tenant. Its URL is read only for first provisioning/publication. After a valid maintenance role and owner membership exist, the file can be removed: repeat publication probes and uses only the application owner. PostgreSQL gives the creator an ADMIN-only membership in a created role, without INHERIT or SET, issued by the bootstrap superuser. The limited creator cannot revoke that grant. This residual is allowed only for the dedicated CREATEROLE administrator. The application owner gets INHERIT+SET without ADMIN. An extra owner grant carrying ADMIN is refused even if a separate safe owner grant exists; reconcile it explicitly rather than expecting publication to repair it. Request/heartbeat roles cannot reach creator, owner or maintenance through any membership path. Never grant runtime roles membership in the provisioner. A failed or timed-out preparation never authorizes switching. Earlier steps may have committed; inspect the protected login-selection-publication.log (written by the helper command and by the release preparation, and named in the error message; its first line is a UTC timestamp so a stale log is recognizable), reconcile catalog state, and repeat the same policy. Do not drop roles or reset counters, approvals, enrollment, generation or trust. Every publication re-checks that no feature is enabled and no digest is approved after each publication step, not only on the version-1 rollback path. This step never enables selection. Version-1 rollback remains supported with a known recovery limit: its publisher and startup require broad runtime access, so the runtime role can write retained feature tables during that period. Disable features and remove digest approvals before rollback. Restore, grant reassertion and activation of a v1 artifact over active v2 save the exact bounded feature and digest rows in the mode-600 login-selection-rollback.json before invoking v1 grants. Keep this file outside runtime mounts. Roll-forward compares it before publication, revokes broad grants, republishes helpers as owner, and checks state again before switching. Changed state refuses with Login feature state changed during v1 rollback; operator reconciliation required. Do not delete or overwrite a damaged/mismatched guard to bypass this refusal. Reconcile changes with the responsible operator. Every publication, including repeats and guarded roll-forward, requires disabled, unapproved feature state. Even an exact fingerprint cannot admit enabled or approved rows in this rollout. Preserve the guard until successful narrowing; publication clears it afterward. --activate also refuses, before anything is published or switched, a candidate whose runtime grant contract is older than the active release's (for example v2 over v3 or v4) and a pre-contract candidate over a release that declares a contract. Use --rollback to a recorded previous release, or reconcile with the operator. For a return to the identical already-migrated v2 artifact after v1 rollback, retain its verified package and original successful forward-migration receipt, then use python3 -I scripts/human-release.py <same-40-hex-source> --activate. This repeats publication and identity validation without rerunning migrations or rewriting installed receipts. A fresh candidate still uses the normal clone/migration gates. Do not rerun the first-upgrade wrapper against an OLD preimage after candidate receipts have already been stamped. Missing or changed artifacts, receipt, source kind, migration witnesses or registry state require reconciliation. The clone migration gate creates separate clone LOGIN roles and credential files, restores under its own owner, and records a clone-specific publication policy. The coordinated/package clone steps reuse those bindings. No dev/testing serving role is granted clone membership. The trusted provisioner retains PostgreSQL's ADMIN-only creation grants on its newly created clone roles. No source tenant is a fallback. Each clone keeps all of its private files in its own directory, STATE/clones/CLONE/ (mode 0700, created exclusively): server.toml, login-selection-publication.toml, the owner, request and node URL files, operator-url, and the clone's own rollback guard and login-selection-publication.log. A clone therefore never reads or writes the dev/testing guard or log, and a second creation for the same clone name refuses until the directory is removed. The clone's operator-url (the role-creation credential) is consumed by the first helper publication on the clone, which in the deployment chain is the human-clone-start.py --phase pre startup rehearsal (the package and coordinated clone steps do the same when they publish first; that rehearsal also writes a failed publication's diagnostic to the clone's login-selection-publication.log): it is removed once first provisioning commits, and only when it lives in that clone directory (the dev/testing credential is never touched by this path). A failed provisioning keeps it so the step can be retried. human-clone-upgrade.py SHA --drop and --replace remove the clone's database, its four roles (owner, request, node, maintenance) and its directory, plus any file of the earlier STATE/clone-SHA8-* layout. Dropping the roles needs the dev/testing provisioner credential. When the credential is missing, the files are still removed, the command prints the roles that remain and exits nonzero (`Clone database dropped; clone roles remain (...); the provisioner credential is unavailable: restore it and rerun --drop`). When the credential is present but the drop fails, the exit message says so and names the protected diagnostic clone-cleanup-SHA8.log in the state directory; the remaining roles hold passwords nobody knows, so rerun --drop after reconciling. A file that cannot be removed is reported the same way after the JSON record is printed. A leftover clone directory refuses new clone steps with Clone directory exists; run human-clone-upgrade.py SHA --drop or --replace; after a role-creation failure whose outcome is unknown (roles may exist) a plain rerun is refused or fails on the existing roles, so rerun with --replace or --drop. A clone left in the earlier layout makes the new clone steps refuse with `Legacy clone layout found; run human-clone-upgrade.py SHA --drop first. If the final --drop of human-deploy-host.sh` fails, the release is already active: the script prints `release SHA is active; gate clone cleanup incomplete; rerun human-clone-upgrade.py SHA --drop` and exits nonzero. The coordinated path keeps its clone for validation and recovery; run --drop when done. The package grants step prints a JSON record (clone-grants or grants) like every other step. Operational limits, accepted for the dev/testing cluster: - Role passwords are created with CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD '<hex>'. With log_statement=ddl the cluster's server log can contain them. Clone roles are short-lived and removed by --drop; a client-side SCRAM verifier would need a native login proof and is a possible follow-up. Child diagnostics are scrubbed of password literals (also truncated ones) and 64-hex tokens. - The helper strips PGSSLMODE and the other libpq variables, and every endpoint is loopback. A TLS requirement needs a reviewed policy key; until then the helper is for loopback endpoints. - The rollback guard fingerprints the feature and digest rows, not catalog objects. The pinned v1 publisher grants no TRIGGER or ALL PRIVILEGES (a test checks the fixture), and rules and policies need ownership; privileges issued by the v1 helper functions that the fixture does not extract are unverified.

Membership cannot discover an older standalone Auth service. Before confirmation, inventory all serving processes and endpoints, drain/retire old endpoints, fence legacy LOGIN roles and every inherited credential path, and close their existing database sessions. A password rotation alone does not close existing sessions. Retain actual evidence. An empty erp_node listing proves nothing about standalone clients. The isolated role-fencing test is a rehearsal of this procedure, not proof that an installation has completed it. Start compatible binaries with selection disabled. The native binary contributes the fixed capability to its combined digest; a runtime flag cannot manufacture support. Native registration precedes Auth composition; readiness follows composition. Startup failure shuts down its new membership with a bounded cleanup. Registry refresh creates a fresh binding; a changed local addon catalogue requires draining and restarting membership. Installed package archives are part of that catalogue even when their source directories are absent from the release's addons paths. Startup verifies the stored packages against their lifecycle audit, capabilities and component declarations before registering membership. Composition rechecks the catalogue after loading the registry, before publishing authentication, RPC or assets. Install, upgrade or removal that changes package identity requires draining and restarting the native membership; a same-name archive replacement is also an identity change. Ordinary registry refresh with unchanged package identity remains supported. Never bypass this refusal by approving an unverified digest or disabling the registry coverage check. Before deploying a startup-admission change, rehearse readiness and login on an isolated clone with the installation's actual installed addons and packages. A migration-only clone check does not establish startup acceptance. Preserve the existing private rollback guard for roll-forward; this catalogue correction does not enable login selection. A bound credential override currently refuses authentication/identity verification with a SESSION message, including while disabled. The legacy unbound base constructor remains available for its existing use. Selection plus credential composition remains unsupported until SESSION. Account for this native compatibility limit when choosing addons for the candidate release.

erp cluster login-selection status -d <db> erp cluster nodes -d <db> erp cluster login-selection approve -d <db> --digest <exact-combined-digest> erp cluster login-selection enable -d <db> --confirm-legacy-drained-and-fenced Status reports enabled state, generation, required version, approved digests and the count of incompatible fresh/recent non-stopped memberships in one observation. Missing or malformed state is an error. Activation names an offending node/digest when membership is incompatible. Approve only a fresh registered candidate with the exact required capability. Approval is idempotent while disabled; disable before changing approvals. There are at most 32 approvals per feature and eight registered feature keys per database. Activation requires an approval and rejects incompatible starting, ready, unready, dev and stopping peers, including recently expired rows within their own lease horizon. Draining alone does not establish quiescence. Ordinary cluster rollout windows remain necessary for distinct compatible digests and cannot authorize this feature themselves. The confirmation flag records the operator's external drain/fencing acknowledgement. The command cannot perform or attest that inventory automatically. After enable, verify each service's serving admission, alias-to-canonical session behavior and shared principal budget using actual endpoints. Retain exact source/artifact identities, commands and raw output. An old-statement test is SQL emulation; only an actual retained executable can support an old-binary claim.

erp cluster login-selection disable -d <db> erp cluster login-selection status -d <db> Await confirmed disable. It holds exclusive feature protection and waits for earlier protected finalizations. A hash still in flight cannot subsequently publish a session against the old generation, even after re-enable. Already committed sessions retain their normal semantics. Completed failed guesses retain authoritative accounting after disable or caller cancellation. A caller that disconnects after its password was accepted does not cancel the login: the verdict runs to completion in its own task (the session is written once and the table guard is released), so a cancelled request can still leave a valid session that nobody received. Disabling does not rewrite an addon's selection hooks into base hooks. Custom-selection services refuse new sign-ins while disabled; arrange compatible base-login services before promising users that ordinary stored-login sign-in has resumed. If helper publication returns a COMMIT/store error, its outcome is not a success acknowledgement. Inspect catalog ownership/attributes through the supported startup validation and re-publish the same isolated role policy before serving; do not infer rollback from a lost acknowledgement. An actual enabled-state change increments generation once; repeated enable/disable is idempotent. A lost COMMIT acknowledgement is **unknown**, never success or confirmed rollback. Reconcile status before acting again. Store failures retain their internal cause; public login responses use the existing safe error mapping. Then drain/replace custom-selection services before admitting an older release. Use that release's own compatible grant publication and startup checks. Keep the feature schema, counters and trust rows. Do not reset security data or invent historical alias-to-uid backfill. Keep actual rollback results separate from plans, and verify the restored release before it serves.

Principal counters and trust are tenant-local PostgreSQL state. While active, bound canonical base login and aliases share the selected uid budget across services. Disabling and successful login clear no counters. GC and secret-rotation semantics remain those of the existing auth system; this procedure introduces no retention or rotation schedule. The database gate protects the supported binary/role protocol. It does not attest hostile native code or retrofit undiscovered old clients. The database owner remains trusted. Product latency, allocation, memory and throughput evidence is DEFERRED_PERFORMANCE under ADR 0065. Functional security, admission bounds and semantic query/flight contracts remain required. The sidecar pins the nonsecret provisioner_role name. Repeat policy validation allows the ADMIN-only creation grant only for that exact role, even after its URL file is removed; an unrelated CREATEROLE member is refused. The supplied first-use URL must match that name. Creating a new clone requires role-creation authority again, and so does dropping its roles (--drop, --replace). If the provisioner URL was removed after live first publication, restore it temporarily through the protected operator procedure for clone provisioning and cleanup, then remove it again. The normal repeat publication path still requires no creation credential. Clone backup/restore needs PostgreSQL 18 clients matching the supported server; do not silently use an older pg_dump.

ERPForAll requires **PostgreSQL 18** as its foundation (ADR 0028 (docs/adr/0028-postgresql-feature-baseline.md, not part of the published documentation)). This document provides requirements, connection pooler architecture, and provider verification details. ---

- **Minimum Version**: PostgreSQL 18.0 (server_version_num >= 180000). - **Connection Gate** (in review): enforced on every physical connection via the pool's connection hook (ADR 0028 (docs/adr/0028-postgresql-feature-baseline.md, not part of the published documentation) §1). Any connection to a server with server_version_num < 180000 is refused with a typed error naming the found and required versions. - **PostgreSQL 19 Compatibility**: Servers reporting server_version_num >= 190000 are accepted and logged once per pool as "untested" until a compatibility check passes following 19's GA. - **Core PG 18 Primitives**: The ORM relies on native PG 18 capabilities including RETURNING OLD/NEW (for atomic upsert, tracking, and the transactional outbox without pre-reads), uuidv7(), WITHOUT OVERLAPS temporal constraints, btree skip scan, and asynchronous I/O. ---

Per ADR 0028 §2, optional extensions and server features are **probed, recorded, and reported at startup**, **NOT required for server startup**: - **No Startup Exits**: The server never exits on startup merely because an extension is absent. - **Probed Extensions**: At pool initialization, the ORM records the presence of pg_trgm, btree_gist, unaccent, and pg_stat_statements, along with settings for wal_level, io_method, and max_locks_per_transaction. - **Feature-Specific Enforcement**: - pg_trgm: Installed when a database is created, as Odoo does (the create path is in review). If an addon declares a trigram index (index = "trigram") on a database where pg_trgm is missing, the operation returns an error naming the field and the missing extension. - btree_gist: Installed automatically by schema sync when a model declares an exclusion or temporal constraint requiring equality GiST indexing. - pg_stat_statements: Recommended for production observability and query cost monitoring; optional in operation. - io_method: Recorded in telemetry and benchmarks. Values such as sync or worker are valid across providers; io_uring is never mandatory. ---

When placing PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL: - **PgBouncer Version**: ≥ 1.21 (required for prepared statement support). - **Prepared Statement Limit**: max_prepared_statements must be **explicitly configured** to at least 1024 (to match the ORM connection statement cache limit). The default of 200 introduced in PgBouncer 1.24 is too small for active ERP workloads. - **Transaction Pooling**: Transaction-level pooling (pool_mode = transaction) is fully supported for standard ORM operations, batch updates, and transaction-scoped advisory locks.

> [!IMPORTANT] > The LISTEN connection of the cross-process signal must bypass transaction-mode PgBouncer (ADR 0028 §3.1 (docs/adr/0028-postgresql-feature-baseline.md, not part of the published documentation), > pg-features.md:213 (docs/design/pg-features.md, not part of the published documentation), > m3-signal.md:356 (docs/design/m3-signal.md, not part of the published documentation)). - **Reason**: PostgreSQL LISTEN requires a dedicated, persistent session. In transaction-mode pooling, backend connections are released after each transaction commit, terminating or misrouting asynchronous notifications. - **Architecture**: The long-running LISTEN connection (responsible for registry invalidation, policy generation bumps, and realtime bus notifications) must connect: 1. **Directly** to the PostgreSQL primary instance; or 2. Through a dedicated **session-mode pool** (pool_mode = session). - **All other traffic** (regular request transactions, CRUD, background job execution) continues through the standard transaction-mode pool. ---
